I mentioned the media or attorney out of frustration because the owner's contact information was not provided, preventing me from appealing to her directly about the cleanliness of the area and the need to clean or paint the columbarium. The neglected state of the older area that is hidden from view has been an ongoing issue for years, but we decided to voice our complaints after growing tired of it. Unfortunately, the person I spoke to never acknowledged the possibility of cleaning it up.

Regarding the vases, I did not demand a replacement specifically for my Dad's niche. Instead, I suggested that the person in charge should replace the cheap plastic vases on ALL the niches as they were falling off and deteriorating. The number of vases needing replacement is relatively small. My intention was simply to emphasize that it would be the right thing to do.

Throughout our conversation, I did not perceive any empathy from the person I spoke with.

input:
From the second you walk in the door, you're greeted by the adorable woman at the counter. It seems if you come in here more than once a week, she'll know you're name but I haven't been so lucky since my visits are a bit more sporadic.

My most recent discovery are the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are served all day! I particularly enjoy veg. sausage w/ havarti on an everything bagel. I could actually go for one right about now... I've also had the veggie club sandwich and my other half has enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. Everything always taste fresh, they are priced really well  (I think my favorite bagel sandwich I mentioned is $2.09-2.99- cheaper than wawa!). The people at the deli are super helpful, offering menus if you can't read the one on the wall and will make great suggestions and accommodations to your needs and want.

Don't forget to grab a really great snack too while you're there- they have amazing chocolate bars, an incredible drink case, tons of chip varieties and those addictive hi-chew candies in every flavor.

I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?
Refine this for me please:
From the moment you step through the door, you'll be greeted by the lovely woman at the counter. If you become a regular, she'll remember your name, although I haven't been fortunate enough to experience that since I visit sporadically.

Recently, I stumbled upon the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are available all day long! My personal favorite is the veggie sausage with havarti on an everything bagel. It's truly mouthwatering, and I could definitely go for one right now. Additionally, the veggie club sandwich is delightful, while my significant other enjoys the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. The best part is that everything tastes incredibly fresh, and the prices are very reasonable (my favorite bagel sandwich, as mentioned before, is only $2.09-2.99, cheaper than wawa!). Moreover, the staff at the deli is extremely helpful. They provide menus if you're unable to read the one on the wall and gladly offer great suggestions and accommodations based on your preferences.

While you're there, don't forget to indulge in their fantastic snacks. They have an impressive selection of chocolate bars, an incredible assortment of beverages, a wide variety of chips, and those addictive hi-chew candies available in every flavor.

It goes without saying that I'll definitely be returning here. Who doesn't appreciate fast, delicious, and attentive service?

input: We stopped in for brunch and we weren't expecting the food to be so delicious.  The 3 meat hash was amazing, as was the turkey sandwich and bagel/salmon.  The employees were very friendly and accommodating.  A little pricey, but well worth.  We will visit again if in the area.
Refine this for me please: We were pleasantly surprised by the delicious food when we decided to stop in for brunch. The 3 meat hash was absolutely amazing, and we also thoroughly enjoyed the turkey sandwich and the bagel with salmon. In addition to the fantastic food, the employees were exceptionally friendly and accommodating. While it was a little pricey, the experience was well worth it. We will definitely make a point to visit again if we find ourselves in the area.

input: Nice little bar located at the very far end of Terminal E and Tampa International. The airport recently added several new restaurants with a "local vibe" and this is one of them. There isn't a ton of seating but it also isn't close to the TSA area so it's a bit hidden. Hey have TVs if you wanna catch a game while you wait for your flight. Food is very reasonably price for the portion size. Appetizers run from $5-$10 and majority of sandwiches are $12. I didn't order any food but it looked amazing! Drinks are tasty and Prices are not terrible. Think 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. You cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (Columbia does this I think). I had a Manhattan for $11 and it was very tasty. Staff is attentive and friendly. I know my new spot when I'm waiting on a Delta flight!
Refine this for me please:
This hidden gem is a charming little bar tucked away at the end of Terminal E in Tampa International Airport. Recently, the airport has introduced a selection of restaurants with a local vibe, and this bar is one of those fantastic additions. Although the seating is limited, the location offers a respite from the hustle and bustle of the TSA area.

For sports enthusiasts, the bar provides TV screens, allowing you to catch a game while waiting for your flight. The menu offers a range of mouthwatering appetizers priced between $5 and $10, while most sandwiches are reasonably priced at $12. Although I didn't have the chance to try any food myself, the presentations of the dishes were impressive.

The drinks at this establishment are delicious, and the prices won't break the bank. You can enjoy a refreshing 22oz Jai Alai for just $8.50. It is worth noting that alcoholic beverages cannot be taken into the terminal, unlike some other establishments such as Columbia. Personally, I couldn't resist trying their Manhattan, which was expertly crafted and priced at $11.

The staff at this bar are attentive and friendly, adding to the overall positive experience. I have unquestionably found my go-to spot when waiting on a Delta flight.

input: The depot burger is so delicious along with the shishito peppers! Perfect food, perfect atmosphere, perfect drinks!
Refine this for me please: The Depot burger and shishito peppers are exceptionally delicious! The combination of their flavors is simply perfect. Furthermore, the overall atmosphere, accompanied by the delectable food and refreshing drinks, creates an absolute perfection for a delightful culinary experience.

input: Quality of this store has gone downhill over the past few years. In the past,  I was able to easily choose from a wide selection of food at reasonable prices any time of day. I have noticed recently that the produce is not as fresh, but more expensive,  and the prices of the organic foods are more expensive than Whole Foods. This morning I debated on going to Wegmans or going to this store. I only had to get a few items so I decided on this Giant since it was closer. Big mistake. I have seen on average at least 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m. In the past but today just me. They had all of the store roped off where it was impossible to get to certain aisles and very difficult to get to the register. In my frustration I went under a rope to get soup.  I was then berated by a number of people who were supposed to be cleaning the floors but some were just standing around doing nothing. I couldn't even walk out of the closest door because that was blocked off. If they needed to clean the floor they should have closed the store for a few hours. It would have taken less time at Wegmans which is where I will shop for now on.
Refine this for me please:
The quality of this store has significantly declined in recent years. Previously, the store offered a wide selection of food at reasonable prices throughout the day. However, I have recently observed that the produce is not as fresh and is more expensive. Additionally, the prices of organic foods are even higher than those at Whole Foods. This morning, I had to choose between shopping at Wegmans or this store, and despite needing only a few items, I decided to go to this Giant due to its proximity. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a major mistake.

Unlike in the past, where I would often see around 3 or 4 early-morning shoppers, today I was the only one present. The entire store was divided by ropes, making it impossible to access certain aisles and extremely difficult to reach the checkout counter. In my frustration, I went under one of the ropes to grab some soup. To my surprise, I was met with the disapproval of several individuals who were supposedly employed to clean the floors, although some appeared to be standing around idly. Moreover, I found myself unable to exit through the nearest door as it was blocked off as well. If the intention was to clean the floors, it would have been more sensible for the store to be closed for a few hours. In light of this experience, I have decided to permanently switch my grocery shopping to Wegmans.

input: This place is a hidden gem.  It is located in a strip mall, but this restaurant is anything but a strip mall restaurant.   My husband took me here for my birthday and I was blown away with the whole experience.  It's a very modern, romantic atmosphere.  The food is excellent.  I was shocked by the Fois gras-amazing.  I had the prix fixe menu and I loved ordering 3 courses.  The short ribs were great, but I want to try something new next time.  The desserts were awesome.  I usually take caramel, but there was a caramel tart that was to die for.  Can't wait to go back!!!!
Refine this for me please: This place is truly a hidden gem, tucked away in a strip mall. Don't let its location deceive you, as it surpasses the typical expectations of a strip mall restaurant. My husband surprised me by bringing me here for my birthday, and I was completely blown away by the entire experience. The atmosphere is sleek and contemporary, exuding romance. But what impressed me the most was the outstanding food. The Fois gras dish was truly exceptional, leaving me in awe. Opting for the prix fixe menu allowed me to savor three delightful courses. Although the short ribs were delicious, I'm already eager to explore different options on my next visit. The desserts were beyond words. While I usually gravitate towards caramel, the caramel tart offered here was simply divine. I am eagerly counting down the days until I can return to this remarkable establishment!

input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.
Refine this for me please:
--------DINNER REVIEW - Hugely Disappointing Experience----------

I seldom take the time to write reviews, but this dining experience was truly one of the worst I have ever had. In fact, even without considering the hype surrounding this place, it was objectively terrible and completely ruined what should have been a lovely birthday dinner celebration. 

We had made a reservation well in advance for our party of 8. The wait time was relatively short, which wasn't too bad considering it was a normal Friday night and the restaurant wasn't overly busy or at capacity.

Since it was a birthday dinner, I informed the hostesses about the occasion and asked if they could arrange something special for her at the end of the meal. They acknowledged it, which is something I would expect anywhere, whether at a casual chain restaurant or a high-end establishment. Oddly enough, despite being seated right next to the Maitre D' stand and the wait staff's station, we still received barely any attention.

After being served water, it took an uncomfortably long time for anyone to come over and acknowledge us. Even after ordering wine, it took another good 15-20 minutes before it was brought to our table, and there was no check-in from the staff at all! (Hint: If you run a restaurant, wine is a major source of profit and requires minimal effort, simply taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. It should be brought out promptly).

The same situation continued with our food order. There was a significant wait for our meals to be served, and no one bothered to check on us throughout the entire time. We finished the bottles of wine we ordered and had to physically get up and hunt down a waiter to place another wine order. Some of us even had to remind them, multiple times during the meal, to bring out something special for the birthday girl at the end.

After our plates were cleared, we were given dessert menus and our server disappeared yet again for an infuriating 10-15 minutes. Once he returned, he finally took our dessert order, so we requested some coffees as well. However, we were left waiting and waiting, with no sign of our desserts or coffees. Eventually, we had to approach the server and inquire about the delay, expressing our frustration and asking if they were going to honor our previous requests.

Finally, after what felt like an eternity, they brought out a few cookies, accompanied by a solitary candle...

In summary, the food itself was a mixed bag, with some dishes displaying mediocrity considering the price point. The whipped feta, as other reviews have mentioned, was outstanding, and the braised lamb was genuinely enjoyable. However, the sirloin was disappointingly chewy and lacking in flavor, and the grilled Caesar tasted like a sad, soggy, lukewarm, wilted mess (two orders were left virtually untouched by our party of 8). The atmosphere was pleasant and trendy, but the service, which is a crucial aspect of a dining experience, was utterly horrendous.

I genuinely love the experience of dining at popular, trendy restaurants and having a memorable time. It's unfortunate that I have to write such a negative review, but I felt compelled to share my experience, particularly for a restaurant that seems to be receiving an undeserved amount of hype.

input:
Great food for the price. 
Tender steak and perfectly cooked shrimp. 
Would certainly come back.
Refine this for me please: Exceptional value for the quality of food. The steak was incredibly tender and the shrimp cooked to perfection. I would definitely return for another meal.

input:
We stopped at Tako due to the positive reviews on yelp. We brought a bottle of white wine with us, the staff did not bring a ice or a chill bucket for us. It took 45 minutes for our appetizers to come out. The edamame was over cooked and mushy while the spring roll did not look appetizing almost like it was frozen. I could buy better spring rolls from trader joes.
Next we moved on to our sushi which was sat on the sushi bar for 15 minutes before it was brought to us. The sushi it self was good, but not the best I have ever had,
If I came here again I would not buy any appetizers. The service was slow
Refine this for me please:
, the staff was not attentive to our needs, and the quality of the appetizers was subpar. Additionally, the lack of proper accommodations for our wine, such as an ice or chill bucket, was disappointing. The wait time for our appetizers was excessively long, and when they finally arrived, the edamame was overcooked and mushy while the spring roll appeared unappetizing, almost as if it had been frozen. Comparatively, I could easily find better quality spring rolls at Trader Joe's.

Moving on to the sushi, although it was satisfactory, it did not exceed my expectations or rank among the best sushi I have ever had. If I were to revisit Tako in the future, I would skip ordering any appetizers entirely due to the slow service and lackluster quality, as they did not enhance our dining experience at all.

input: The catfish, chicken, gumbo and mac &a cheese are all to die for. We are the lunch buffet and everything was piping hot and fresh. This place was recommended by a local in the neighborhood we are staying in and it was so worth it!
Refine this for me please: The catfish, chicken, gumbo, and mac & cheese at this place are absolutely exceptional. We decided to try their lunch buffet and were delighted to find that everything was served piping hot and fresh. This hidden gem was recommended to us by a local in the neighborhood we're staying in, and it definitely lived up to the hype!

input:
See's candies is California base bakery reach Florida. I know about this candies when my wife living in California. Their chocolate is very soft and tasty. 

In Tampa, the International Plaza Mall has this temporary store from Thanksgiving to Easter. They located very close to H&M clothing store. You can have samples before you buy it. I got the lollipop candies. I also bought one assorted chocolate candies. They are very good. The store clerk was kind enough to let us try their assorted chocolate other their typical sample candies. 

You can go with chocolate with nut, mint, toffee, milk, white or dark chocolate. All are good. Guilty pleasure with a touch at sweet side. Mail order through the web also available. If you close to the mall, just go to buy one without shipping.
Refine this for me please:
Please refine:

Located in California, See's Candies is a renowned bakery that has expanded its reach to Florida. I first discovered these delectable treats when my wife lived in California, and I must say, their chocolates are incredibly soft and flavorsome.

In Tampa, at the International Plaza Mall, a temporary See's Candies store opens from Thanksgiving to Easter. Conveniently positioned near the H&M clothing store, this store allows customers to sample their products before making a purchase. During my visit, I tried their lollipop candies and also indulged in assorted chocolate candies, which were absolutely delightful. The store clerk even kindly allowed us to sample their other chocolates, aside from their usual samples.

When it comes to chocolate flavors, See's Candies offers a variety ranging from nutty to minty, and everything in-between, including toffee, milk, white, and dark chocolate. All options are heavenly and provide a touch of guilty pleasure with their sweetness. If you're in close proximity to the mall, it's worth a trip to purchase these treats in person, eliminating the need for shipping. Alternatively, you can also conveniently order them online through their website.

input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Refine this for me please:
For our second stop during Center City Restaurant Week, we decided to try out R2L. Located on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place, this restaurant/lounge offers breathtaking views of the city. Despite not getting a table by the window, we still enjoyed the stunning sunset and the cityscape at night. 

R2L offers a diverse menu with multiple choices for each course. I started off with the delicious crisp peas, ham, and garlic risotto balls. For the main course, I opted for the hearty Butcher's Filet, which featured braised short rib, Steuben bean chili, potato and farm veg slaw, along with basil. The dish was quite substantial, considering the addition of meat in the chili. 

To end the meal on a high note, I indulged in the mind-blowing milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel. To enhance the flavor, I enjoyed a cup of coffee that melted the chocolate, accompanied by delectable candied almonds on the side. Complementing our dinner, we also had a bottle of wine for the table. 

Overall, R2L provided a classy dining experience with exceptional food. The waiter went above and beyond, ensuring I was aware that the risotto came in ball form rather than a traditional bowl. I highly recommend visiting R2L for its stunning views, delicious cuisine, and top-notch service.

input: Becca is an awesome bartender. They have awesome happy hour specials including land shark. The food menu is somewhat limited but the service at the bar is great. We hope they can keep up the business and attract more locals.
Refine this for me please: Becca's exceptional bartending skills make her an outstanding bartender. The bar proudly offers sensational happy hour specials, notably including the highly sought-after Land Shark. While the food menu may be slightly limited, the bar excels in delivering remarkable service. We eagerly anticipate Becca's continued success in attracting and retaining a larger base of local patrons.

input: Bummer, just moved to this area and this was my first visit to this location.  I didn't receive my change or receipt,  it was just change but I asked for it and she said she gave it to me, um no. Was in a hurry so I didn't wanna argue.  And no spoon for my chili. Cheese on my burger was old, which means my burger wasn't freshly made. Tasted ok but won't return.

Although it was just a small amount, I specifically requested it and was told that it had already been provided to me, which was not the case. Due to time constraints, I decided against arguing the matter further. Additionally, I was disheartened to find that there was no spoon provided for my chili. Furthermore, the cheese on my burger appeared to be old, indicating that my burger was not freshly made. Although the taste was acceptable, I do not intend to revisit this establishment.

input: They have great prices if you order family style. We tried the pot roast and it was just as good carry out as it would have been at the restaurant. They packaged everything nicely and it stayed warm after the 30 min car ride. There was definitely enough for a family of 4. The green beans were amazing! I would definitely recommend. It's nothing special, just a good family restaurant

We recently tried their pot roast, and we were impressed that it tasted just as delicious as if we had dined in. The packaging was neat, ensuring the food remained warm during the 30-minute car ride. The portion size was generous enough for a family of four. Their green beans were a standout, simply amazing! input:
This place is amazing! The pizza cookies are a must. It came hot, soft, and crazy delicious. 

We tried the Peanut butter pizza cookie and the Oreo cookies, and both were perfection. I'm very eager to try other flavors. Also, being open until 3am is the smartest decision of any bakery in America. 

The only reason I'm not giving a 5 is because of the prices. But, to be honest, those late nights when all I want is a fresh baked cookie pizza, I'd be willing to pay $50.
Refine this for me please:
This place is absolutely incredible! The pizza cookies here are an absolute must-try. They arrived at our table piping hot, irresistibly soft, and bursting with insane flavor.

We indulged in both the Peanut Butter Pizza Cookie and the Oreo Cookies, and let me tell you, they were sheer perfection. We couldn't help but be tempted by their other flavors, and can't wait to explore more options on our next visit.

What sets this bakery apart is its genius decision to stay open until 3am. It's hands down the smartest move any bakery in America could make. Late-night cravings for a fresh-baked cookie pizza can now be satisfied without any time restrictions.

The only slight drawback preventing me from giving it a perfect 5-star rating is the prices. However, truth be told, on those nights when all I crave is a mouthwatering cookie pizza straight out of the oven, I would willingly shell out $50 without any hesitation.

input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Refine this for me please:
I relocated from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago and have found that while everyone here raves about the restaurants, I have yet to come across many that deserve a high rating. However, I must say that this particular restaurant stands out as the best I have experienced in Philadelphia.

To start the meal, tahini and bread were brought to the table. At first, I found them plain but satisfying due to my hunger. However, I soon realized that there was something addictive about the tahini, as I couldn't resist wanting to devour it like an uncivilized dog. The bread was also excellent and paired well with the tahini.

One aspect I appreciate about this restaurant is their diverse selection of organic meat options. How often does one come across an organic beef shishkabob? The dish was beyond superb - the meat cooked to perfection and the onions having a slight caramelization, providing a satisfying crunch. The purslane salad tasted like a fresh garden in my mouth, a rare occurrence for me to dream about a salad, yet this one manages to do so.

My husband opted for a chicken dish accompanied by black-eyed peas, green peas, and fantastic rice. Describing the flavoring would be a challenge, as it surpasses my culinary vocabulary. We inquired about the spices used, and apart from traditional zatar, they incorporate their own spice blend. The exact composition may be unknown to us, but the fact that we can return and order this dish repeatedly is enough for us.

Despite feeling full, I couldn't resist indulging in dessert, something I rarely do. However, with the exceptional quality of this restaurant, I had a strong feeling that the desserts would be equally impressive. I decided to try the pistachio creme brulee, which exceeded my expectations. The delicate custard was both light and rich, infused with the heavenly taste of pistachio. It was truly a taste of paradise.

The service we received was impeccable. Despite squeezing us in for a last-minute Friday night reservation with a time constraint of an hour and 15 minutes, the staff ensured that we never felt rushed and perfectly timed each course. Additionally, while my husband was away, the waiter even took the time to neatly refold his napkin. Though I don't particularly care about the positioning of a napkin during a meal, it served as a clear indication of the attentive and well-trained waitstaff.

Considering my experience at this restaurant, I may choose to forgo dining elsewhere in Philadelphia most of the time in order to frequent this slightly expensive yet appropriately priced establishment. Kudos to the talented chef behind these remarkable dishes.

input: They served me a frozen pizza and skunked beer.  'Nuff said.
Refine this for me please: They served me an unappetizing frozen pizza along with a beer that tasted like skunk. Need I say more?

input: Whole family got sick after eating here. The frozen yogurt was pretty but did not taste good. Would not go here again or recommend it.
Refine this for me please: The entire family fell ill after dining at this establishment. Although the frozen yogurt appeared visually appealing, its taste was unpleasant. I will not consider returning to this place and do not recommend it to others.

input:
This is the place for authentic Indian street food. I've been here multiple times ordering different things ranging from bhel puri, pav bhaji, vada pav, deconstructed samosa and aloo tikki, dabeli, kulfi and more. Everything was made exceptionally well.

I regret not having found this place sooner.
Refine this for me please:
This place is an absolute gem for those seeking authentic Indian street food. I have visited multiple times and have tried a variety of dishes including bhel puri, pav bhaji, vada pav, deconstructed samosa and aloo tikki, dabeli, kulfi, and more. Without fail, every item I ordered was prepared to perfection.

I can't help but feel a sense of regret for not discovering this place sooner.

input:
Uhhhhh.... Not sure how to quantify or qualify my experience here. Let's start with back story: 

My sister was visiting for the weekend, so I wanted to show her a solid night on the town that lasted till the wee hours of the morning. We started on Frenchmen, but for whatever reason it was dead. 
Deciding to adventure Uptown we proceeded on a respectable bar crawl, including Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes, however, at 3 AM the usual Uptown culprits start to raise their heads. A summary of the following dialogue:

Friends "Let's go to FMs" 
Me: "No, too much broken glass"
Friends: "Let's go to Snake and Jake's"
Me: "Eh...."
Friends: "Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling"
Friends: "The Saint!!"
Me: "I suppose I haven't been there before, I'm curious."

After entering the Saint the look on my sisters face was priceless, akin to a deer in headlights look. I kept my countenance, and we ordered a round. Things proceeded as expected ... unwanted dance grinding advances, check! uber drunk guy talking your ear off, check! Big Buck Hunter, CHECK!!! Overall I'm glad I moderately traumatized my sister and sated my curiosity in the same night. 

Helpful hint: They have outdoor seating, surprisingly, which is very good to escape the smoke
Refine this for me please:
Let me refine that for you:

I recently had an interesting night out with my sister and wanted to share the details. We started our evening on Frenchmen Street, but unfortunately, it was quite quiet. To make the most of our night, we decided to venture uptown and went on a bar crawl to places like Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes. However, as it got later, we were faced with the usual Uptown spots that weren't too appealing.

Here's a summary of the conversation that followed:

Friends: "Let's go to FMs."
Me: "No, there's too much broken glass."
Friends: "How about Snake and Jake's?"
Me: "Eh, not feeling it."
Friends: "What about Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling."
Friends: "What about The Saint?"
Me: "Well, I've never been there before, so I suppose I'm curious."

Upon entering The Saint, my sister's reaction was priceless - she had a look on her face like a deer caught in headlights. I kept a straight face and we decided to order some drinks. As expected, the night unfolded with unwanted dance grinding advances and an overly drunk guy talking our ears off. But the highlight was definitely playing Big Buck Hunter - it was a check on our list!

Overall, I'm glad I managed to give my sister a memorable experience and satisfy my own curiosity in one night. Here's a helpful tip: The Saint surprisingly offers outdoor seating, which is great to escape the smoke.

input: The food here is so great and fresh. I don't shy away from my kids favorite Wonton Soup because i know they take the time to cook it.
Refine this for me please: The food offered here is excellent, as it is prepared using fresh ingredients. I have no hesitation in ordering my kids' favorite dish, Wonton Soup, as I am confident that it is carefully cooked to perfection.

input: Food was great. But very disappointed with the hospitality. We  entered the restaurant at 9:15 pm but was denied dine in and was told that though the  restaurant closes at 10 pm they won't let us dine in and can give only to go. They saw that there were two pregnant women and a kid with us and I explained that our home is a hour drive from there and yet they denied for no reason. I had to drive back to home and make everyone eat. Very disappointed with such attitude towards customers. Never going back here. Let them try to forgive them self for denying dining for pregnant women.
Refine this for me please: The food was excellent, however, our experience was greatly marred by the disappointing hospitality. Despite arriving at the restaurant at 9:15 pm, we were denied the opportunity to dine in. We were informed that even though the restaurant closes at 10 pm, they would only offer take-out service. To add to our frustration, the staff noticed that two of us were pregnant and we had a young child with us. I explained the inconvenience of having to drive an hour back home to eat, yet our request was denied without any apparent reason. This treatment towards customers is deeply disheartening. We will not be returning to this establishment again. It is difficult to forgive such a thoughtless decision to deny dining to pregnant women.

input: This place surpassed our expectations!  The steak is far superior to any steak house I have been too.  The staff flows together like a well trained team, the hostess Mallory, our waiter Max, and the busboy all keep things moving smoothly and leave you never wanting for anything.  Honestly the whole experience was amazing and we will be back for more. Love this place!
Refine this for me please: This place exceeded our expectations! The quality of the steak surpasses any other steak house I have been to. The staff works seamlessly as a well-trained team, with Mallory, the hostess, Max, our waiter, and the busboy ensuring everything runs smoothly and leaving us wanting for nothing. The overall experience was truly incredible and we can't wait to come back for more. We absolutely love this place!

input: The service is super friendly! During my exam, Dr. Dinh was very kind and addressed my concerns. input: When I ordered my pizza for me and my friends , he pizza was so small and this delivery girl took forever and she was rude and didn't want to give me my change back and she said she thought I gave her a tip no ! And she didn't even give me the right change and it was all coins ! This place sucks ! DONT EAT HERE !!!!!!
Refine this for me please: When I placed an order for pizza for my friends and me, the pizza we received was considerably smaller than expected. input: I was told this place is a must for a Sonoran hot dog. I was visiting from out of town and had never had one. It was good, but the whole Sonoran hot dog isn't really my thing (too many components for me) so I can't say it was great. The guacamole on the other hand, was great! I also had the taco combo - the chicken and carne asada were very good but the cabeza was slimy. BK has a salsa bar that allows you to help yourself to your own toppings and I appreciated that. Service was good, food arrived quickly. It was pretty packed during lunch on a weekday.
Refine this for me please: I was recommended this place as a must-visit for trying a Sonoran hot dog. As someone visiting from out of town, I had never tried one before. While I found it to be good, I personally felt that the combination of ingredients in the Sonoran hot dog was a bit overwhelming for my taste. Hence, I cannot claim it was exceptional. However, I must say that the guacamole was absolutely delicious! Additionally, I ordered the taco combo which consisted of chicken, carne asada, and cabeza. The chicken and carne asada were both very tasty, but unfortunately, the cabeza was quite slimy. I appreciated the fact that BK has a salsa bar which allowed me to customize my own toppings, adding to the overall experience. The service was efficient and my food arrived promptly. It is worth mentioning that the place was quite busy, especially during lunch on a weekday.

input:
Walked into the restaurant, with reservations, and many open tables.  I asked the manager for a window table and was responded with "they are all reserved."  Two hours later, when we left, still many open tables next to the windows.

Overall food was good.
I had the filet and she had the salmon.
The bottle of wine that was recommended was $75 and was not told prior to ordering it, just that it was the last bottle.
Refine this for me please:
When we arrived at the restaurant with our reservations, there were numerous unoccupied tables. I politely requested a window table from the manager, who informed me that they were all reserved. Surprisingly, upon leaving two hours later, we noticed that there were still many empty tables by the windows.

In terms of the food, we were generally satisfied. I opted for the filet while my companion chose the salmon. The dish recommendations were adequate, except for the fact that we were not informed about the price of the recommended $75 bottle of wine prior to ordering. We were only told that it was the last bottle available.

input: Best Indian I have ever had! The food was fresh and delicious. Staff are very friendly and attentive and restaurant is clean and welcoming. The paleek paneer and briyani were amazing!
Refine this for me please: This is the best Indian food I have ever had! The dishes tasted exceptionally fresh and delicious. input: Best smoothies in the whole world. And fresh bread is amazing. Very knowledgeable staff.
Refine this for me please: Indulge in the most exceptional smoothie experience worldwide, featuring the finest and most delectable blends available. Prepare to be astonished by the extraordinary quality and taste. In addition, relish the incredible pleasure of savoring freshly baked bread that surpasses all expectations. The level of expertise possessed by our staff is truly remarkable, ensuring an unmatched level of service and guidance.

input:
I stopped by Bell Meade during a recent visit to Nashville. The best way for me to describe my experience is to say that the next time I go to Nashville I will go out of my way to make sure I return to Bell Meade.

On my travels, I tend to stop from time to time to see if I can find specific bourbons that may be out locally. At this time of year, I did not expect any great finds because many of the items for which I look have their annual release later in the year so it's a surprise to find any of them on the shelf. For example, Elmer T Lee is a favorite of mine so it was one that I asked about.

Despite the fact that I walked away without Elmer T, I still had a great time. I enjoyed a few tastes at the tasting bar and even better I had a great conversation with Max. He is one of the reasons I will return.

I did walk out with a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream that is not sold locally and there was a bottle on the shelf that I have not seen locally that I need to investigate. As I said I will return and a five star rating from me should say at all.
Refine this for me please:
During my recent visit to Nashville, I made a stop at Bell Meade and I must say that my experience was truly exceptional. I was so impressed that I have already decided to make it a priority to return to Bell Meade the next time I visit Nashville.

As a bourbon enthusiast, I often make it a point to search for rare and unique bourbons during my travels. Although I wasn't expecting to find any remarkable discoveries during this time of year, as most of the bourbon releases happen later in the year, I was pleasantly surprised to come across a few hidden gems on the shelf. I specifically inquired about Elmer T Lee, one of my personal favorites, but unfortunately, they didn't have it in stock. However, I didn't let that dampen my experience.

What made my visit truly memorable was the opportunity to indulge in a few samples at the tasting bar and, even better, the engaging conversation I had with Max. His knowledge and passion for whiskey were truly captivating, and it was clear that he was an integral part of what makes Bell Meade so special. Max's genuine enthusiasm and expertise were one of the main reasons I am eager to return.

Before leaving, I couldn't resist purchasing a bottle of their exclusive Tennessee whiskey cream which isn't available locally. Additionally, there was another bottle on the shelf that caught my eye, and I am eager to further explore its unique flavors. With this in mind, it's safe to say that a five-star rating from me is well-deserved and speaks volumes about my exceptional experience at Bell Meade.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.
Refine this for me please:
I thoroughly enjoy sampling fresh seafood at piers, wharfs, and seaside markets. Unfortunately, many times I have been disappointed with my experience. However, this particular place exceeded my expectations. The food is genuinely fresh and expertly prepared. The stunning view adds to the already delightful experience. Although I have been here before, I made the mistake of ordering the wrong dish, cioppino, a couple of years ago and found it underwhelming.

On this occasion, we arrived for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Surprisingly, even at 4pm, there was a wait. We patiently waited for about 25 minutes and were eventually seated outdoors. While it was not ideal to be exposed to the sun without any shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the breathtaking view made up for it.

We decided to try the local crab special, which consisted of a steamed 3-pound crab served with a salad and soup, all for $26. I found this to be a great deal as the crab was enormous, scrumptious, and filled with meat. The garden salad was refreshingly simple and fresh. We also ordered the lobster bisque, which was quite enjoyable. Other options included a Caesar salad and clam chowder. To complement the crab, they served a couple of onion rings and provided cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. It was a delectable feast!

In addition, we opted for the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari, and scallops, priced at $12.95. This dish came with a side of coleslaw, onion rings, tartar sauce, and cocktail sauce. Although this meal was on the greasier side, it was one of the best fried platters I have had the pleasure of enjoying. The seafood was incredibly fresh, including the usually apprehensive fried oyster.

Due to the scorching sun, the ice in our iced teas melted quickly. Our waitress was amazing and went above and beyond by promptly bringing us ample amounts of extra ice and even an additional iced tea. Her friendly nature and great service warranted a five-star rating.

By the time we departed at around 6pm, there was a substantial crowd waiting for tables. I highly recommend signing up on the clipboard for a seat as soon as you arrive. The restaurant is located at the very end of the pier. Free parking is available for 90 minutes on the pier, although it may be rough on your tires. I chose to park in a large lot south of the pier and took a 15-minute walk to reach it, which was free during the late afternoon on a Monday.

input:
What a disappointment. This place was not good I would suggest you think twice before selecting this option. The manager and wait staff may possibly be the worst I have ever encountered, rude and definitely not focused on customer service.  The manager is a very angry hostile fella I asked if I could get brown rice instead of white and he blasted me...I offered to pay extra and he stormed off? Do not know what the deal was but this is just plain unprofessional and creepy behavior. The waitresses will smack into you while you are eating...man what a mess this place is from top to bottom.
The food just OK at best! I am seriously complimenting them here... you can do better at home than here. Seriously I am not going to go into you have been warned just yuk...OK? these other folks with the positive reviews for this place must burn off their taste buds with adult beverages. (Didn't try the sake it may be the high point of the joint...but why would I want to expose my taste buds to a substandard meal to enjoy some rice wine? I can do this at home.
 Here is something I am not sure of, I have only lived here a few months now, is it customary to charge for each soda every time you get a refill here? I was charged for each I asked why they said "This is how we do it here." So at $2 bucks per 6-8 ounces of beverage you may want to go with water at this place...but smarter yet! Go elsewhere.
I will not be returning to this establishment.

Worst yet.
Refine this for me please:
This place was a huge disappointment and I strongly advise against selecting this option. The manager and wait staff were incredibly rude and showed no focus on customer service. The manager, in particular, was hostile and angry. I simply asked if I could have brown rice instead of white and he completely overreacted, storming off when I offered to pay extra. This unprofessional and creepy behavior is unacceptable. Additionally, the waitresses would bump into customers while they were eating, making the experience even worse.

The food was mediocre at best. Even when trying to find something positive to say, I could only come up with a mediocre assessment. Honestly, you can make better food at home than what they offer here. I don't understand how anyone can leave positive reviews for this place—unless they have numbed their taste buds with alcohol. I didn't try the sake, but it may be the only decent thing in the establishment. However, why would I want to subject myself to a substandard meal just to enjoy some rice wine? I can do that at home.

Another issue I had was with their charging policy. I'm not sure if it's customary in this area, but they charged for each soda refill. When I asked about it, their response was, "This is how we do it here." At $2 per 6-8 ounces of beverage, it might be more reasonable to just stick with water or, better yet, find another place to dine.

I will definitely not be returning to this establishment. It was the worst experience yet.

input: I was happy his was my first experience with Nola food and not my last, started on a low point. First, I understand it was Sunday night before Fat Tuesday and our waitress was working back to back 12 shifts. However, my drink order was forgotten, and my friends plate was mixed up. For my food, I had the po'boy shrimp and was underwhelmed, there was a hardy serving of shrimp but there was minimal lettuce or sauce and the fries were weak, many soggy. Needless to say, we didn't go back. From other reviews seems like we caught them on an off-day but unfortunately the result is a lack luster review.
Refine this for me please: Despite starting on a low note, I was still able to enjoy my first experience with Nola food. It was unfortunate that our waitress was overwhelmed with back-to-back 12-hour shifts on a Sunday night before Fat Tuesday, which may have contributed to some mishaps. My drink order was forgotten, and my friend's plate got mixed up. As for my food, I ordered the po'boy shrimp, but it left me underwhelmed. Although there was a generous serving of shrimp, there was minimal lettuce or sauce, and the fries were disappointing, with many being soggy. Regrettably, this experience left us with no desire to return. It appears that we might have caught them on an off-day, as other reviews suggest, but the end result is still a lackluster review.

input:
Let's be honest, this place needs a face lift. It's starting to feel shady, I wouldn't even feel comfortable taking my small children here (if I had any, which I don't). The service is mediocre and everything looks tired. The comedy club doesn't feel cheerful or fun, it just feels like the back hallway of a banquet room.

Great parking and good location though. Please owners, please put some money into this place. It really needs it.
Refine this for me please:
To be frank, it's time for a major renovation in this place. The current atmosphere feels questionable, and to be honest, I wouldn't even consider bringing my hypothetical small children here. The service is average at best, and the overall appearance gives off a worn-out vibe. The comedy club lacks the liveliness and joy one would expect, resembling more of a gloomy back hallway of a banquet room.

On the positive side, the parking facility is excellent, and the location is convenient. However, I earnestly implore the owners to invest in this establishment. It desperately requires a significant financial infusion to revitalize its appeal.

input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Refine this for me please:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday and had a great experience overall. Here are the details:

Arrival: Before my arrival, I had read some reviews mentioning the lack of signs marking the location, so I used Starbucks as a point of reference. I found parking in front of the multi-business complex and entered to find a guard at a desk. The guard informed me that they were contracted to hand guests their keys and room numbers only. He pointed out a phone on the wall in case I needed to make any calls. He also mentioned that the few parking spots in front were free on the weekend.

The Room: I was pleasantly surprised to find that the accommodation was not just a room, but an apartment. It was incredibly spacious and had everything I needed for the weekend. The fully stocked kitchen, desk, ample space, king bed, large table, and comfortable living room were exactly what I was looking for. The only downside was that the windows couldn't be opened as they were sealed shut. However, the room came with a small welcome bag filled with cookies, water, and information about nearby food delivery options.

Maid Service: This accommodation seems to be more suited for long-term stays, as there wasn't any maid service during my short visit. That being said, I was perfectly fine with that since I was only there for three days. I went grocery shopping at Shoprite and stocked up on supplies for the weekend.

Overall: I absolutely loved staying at this location. The apartment offered a spacious living room where I could entertain my guests, as well as a comfortable desk for studying. One of the best aspects was how quiet it was; I felt as if I were the only one there. This made it perfect for focusing on my studies, especially on Sunday. Additionally, having two TVs allowed me to enjoy watching The Walking Dead. I would definitely choose to stay here again in the future. The apartment was spacious, updated, and overall, a great place to stay.

input: Awesome location, good service is why I have been eating there for the past 15 years off and on. Mostly the excuses about the steak is why I have to write the review. I am happy to pay more for good quality steak but don't blame the poor guy that sold it to you !
Refine this for me please: I have frequented this establishment for the past 15 years due to its incredible location and commendable service. However, I feel compelled to leave this review primarily because of the recurring issues regarding the steak. While I am willing to pay a higher price for a quality steak, it is unfair to place blame solely on the unfortunate individual who sold it to you.

input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon.  By Sunday after review of my budget I realized I was unable to afford the car.  I called the salesman and tried to explain my situation at 11:30am.  He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!
Refine this for me please:
I had a terrible experience recently, and unfortunately, it's not over yet. On a Friday afternoon, I made a mistake by purchasing a vehicle that is beyond my budget. It wasn't until Sunday, after reviewing my budget, that I realized I couldn't afford the car. I immediately contacted the salesman at 11:30am to explain my situation. He promised to speak with his manager and call me back. However, by 3:30pm, I still hadn't received a return call, so I called him again but he didn't answer. I left a voicemail and even after closing time, he never got back to me.

Feeling frustrated, I decided to visit the dealership early Monday morning when they opened. I approached Stephen, the salesman, to inquire about the outcome. He asked me to wait and said he would discuss the matter with his management team. Unfortunately, I had to wait for over an hour before being called into a cubicle. There, I was informed that my loan had been funded and the title had already been changed. This meant that if I wanted to return the car, I would have to sell it back as a used vehicle, resulting in a significant loss of money.

To my surprise, this morning, Bill, the head of finance, informed me that the bank had questions regarding the loan funding. I received a call from the bank stating that the loan had not been funded, and they could not approve it. Despite leaving numerous messages with the dealership, I have yet to receive a callback. Frustrated and seeking guidance, I contacted an attorney. Based on their review, I called the dealership again, requesting a specific time to return the vehicle and retrieve my trade. However, I still haven't received a response from them. The lack of communication and the lies from this dealership have been extremely disappointing. I strongly advise avoiding them at all costs.

input:
I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.
Refine this for me please:
I have been a loyal customer of Desi Village in West Philly for several years. Recently, after moving to the suburbs, my family and I decided to give the KOP Desi Village a try. Initially, we had some reservations due to our experience with Mood Cafe, another restaurant owned by the same people in West Philly that did not meet our expectations. However, to our surprise, the KOP location turned out to be quite comparable to its West Philly counterpart.

The atmosphere and ambiance at this location are lacking. It is situated in a rather dull strip mall, with Desi Village seemingly being the only active store there. The interior decor is outdated and unimpressive. Although they have a large space and appear to offer a lunch buffet, it is uncertain if it ever gets crowded. Therefore, I would not recommend visiting this place for its ambiance.

On the other hand, the food at Desi Village is excellent. We ordered Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani, and everything was delicious. The flavors were just right, not overly greasy, and appropriately spicy. As someone with a nut allergy, I made them aware of my dietary restriction, and they successfully accommodated it, which is not always the case at other Indian restaurants. Because of the quality of their food, we will definitely be returning. It would certainly be a bonus if they were to relocate to a more appealing establishment, but ultimately, the food is what matters most.

input:
What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.

I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,

We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.
Refine this for me please:
What an incredible turn of events! After being disappointed by another barbecue place running out of food, we stumbled upon this gem in Mid City. We were warmly welcomed by a friendly woman at the counter who explained the ordering process.

Opting for a one-meat plate, I chose the "wet" pulled pork accompanied by delectable sides of grits and potato salad. Feeling adventurous, I also ordered a medium mac and cheese. My boyfriend went for the two-meat plate, savoring the brisket and pulled chicken with sides of potato salad and fries. From the very first bite, we were blown away by the flavors of the food. The pulled pork was perfectly sauced, striking a wonderful balance without being overly drenched. Even without the wet option, I could tell it would have been equally delicious. The mac and cheese was divine and quickly became my favorite part of the meal after the pork. The stone ground grits had a unique, almost smoky flavor that I thoroughly enjoyed, while the potato salad provided a refreshing crunch.

Both of us agreed that not only was the food fantastic, but it was also reasonably priced. We were so impressed that we will definitely make the trip back to Earhart just to experience more of this mouthwatering barbecue. The owner himself went above and beyond, personally serving the food and ensuring our satisfaction. It's always a delight when owners take the time to connect with their customers. The casual and comfortable atmosphere made the whole dining experience a breeze. LA Smokehouse has definitely earned a spot on my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.

input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!
