Without a doubt, I will return here on my next visit to St. Louis.

input:
After a long hiatus from reviewing I have awaken from my 6 mouth yelp hibernation and my tummies a grumbles with an insatiable hunger for the cacophonous symphony of flavor that is Indian food. Like an all too familiar pattern, I go back to Mohammad Butt, my main man for marsala.
But whats this? 
There are whispers that he no longer cooks for "Best Taste of Asia," that he is gone, never to return; some sort of falling out.

No.
No, it can't be! 
I need to score - one .. final .. hit..

Life ceases to have meaning, existential murmurings dog the mind. Who am I?
Why am I here?
What is Cheeze Wiz?
Its done, over, a round falls into the chamber and just as I prepare to end it all and pull the trigger- steps in ZAIKA.

Zaika - meaning the art of taste -  stays to to its name. This is a place where the Paneer (cheese) is made fresh in house, resulting in a cheese that's silky in texture. Especially when in contrast to the prepackaged rubbery bone-white LEGO blocks most small Indo-Pak places purchase from Indian Grocers in attempts to reduce prep-times. While at Zaika such shortcuts are not taken,  the Chef takes the extra steps needed to ensure a dish comes together as a whole. For example, the Chicken Makhani uses Smokey Tandoori Chicken, which I have never seen done before but it certainly aids the chicken to cut though the rich buttery tomato sauce and elevates the dish as a whole. Even entrées like Dall Fray or  Palak Paneer  have so much flavor that they will leave you not missing animal protein in the least should you choose to go the vegetarian route. 

Zaika 's appetizers, like the Veggie Samosa and Aloo Tikki, (spiced potato patties) are generally large, peppery and well spiced - the latter of which remind me of something my own mother would make. Though I must warn others to avoid the items that occasionally pop-up as specials like the potato stuffed chili peppers, unless they have a iron stomach or are a gluten for punishment. These peppers are spicy, not deveined or even seeded. Further, I find the fish pakora to be far too fishy.
 
I've become rather taken by Zaikia. Even the simply things such as the naan are good there. Just right in elasticity, the bread does not have too much give and yet isn't too soft. It's nothing elaborate, just properly risen with a light texture and  no egg or yeast flavor. The only complaint being that it lacked that signature faint sweetness naan has. But hey, I use it mostly for mopping up the other good stuff on the plate anyway and the sweetness gets lost in the mix, so I don't mind at all.

The menu has nearly 120 different items, all numbered to order by, making take-out phone orders convenient and should eliminate any fears anyone should have of a language barrier problem. Furthermore, it has short descriptions of each dish - something all ethnic places like this should have.
Though some items like Lassie (a frothy yogurt drink) do not appear on the menu, that too is offered - both a salty and sweet mango verities. 
The head chef speaks English quite well and should be easy to deal with should you want to inquire more or want to setup large orders.

I have already noticed parties negotiating catering for Ramadan as I anxiously awaited my own order.

The bottom line here is this, Mohammad Butt has expanded on the menu he once created for "Best taste of Asia," and taken an all HALAL meat approach. 

Only good things can come of this, only good things.

P.S.
ZAIKA is right behind Nifty Fifties on Grant Ave., so you are all set for dessert should you want a milkshake. 
However, I would suggest getting the Ras Malai if available. These riccotta cheese dumplings flouting in soaked in sweetened, thickened milk are delicately flavored with cardamom, a very some amount of rose water and then garnished with pistachios. They are ungodly good.
Refine this for me please:
After a long break from reviewing, I have finally emerged from my six-month Yelp hibernation with an intense craving for the vibrant flavors of Indian cuisine. In my search for the perfect spot to satisfy my appetite, I sadly discovered that my go-to chef, Mohammad Butt, is no longer cooking at "Best Taste of Asia." There were rumors of a falling out, and I felt a sense of loss.

But then, a glimmer of hope emerged - Zaika. True to its name, Zaika, meaning the art of taste, lives up to its reputation. The restaurant takes pride in making fresh paneer (cheese) in-house, resulting in a silky texture that surpasses the rubbery prepackaged blocks commonly found in other Indo-Pak establishments. Chef at Zaika goes the extra mile to ensure each dish is a harmonious masterpiece. For example, the Chicken Makhani incorporates Smokey Tandoori Chicken, a unique touch that enhances the rich buttery tomato sauce. Even vegetarian options like Dall Fray and Palak Paneer boast so much flavor that you won't miss animal protein.

Zaika's appetizers, such as Veggie Samosa and Aloo Tikki (spiced potato patties), are generously sized, flavorful, and reminiscent of my mother's homemade recipes. However, caution is advised when approaching the occasional specials, like potato-stuffed chili peppers, as they may be too spicy for some or overpoweringly fishy, like the fish pakora.

I have fallen in love with Zaika, even their humble naan bread impresses me. Perfect in elasticity, neither too soft nor too firm, it serves as the ideal accompaniment to their delectable dishes. While it may lack the faint sweetness typical of naan, it doesn't deter from its role as a plate mopper.

With a menu boasting around 120 different items, Zaika makes ordering take-out over the phone a breeze, alleviating any concerns of a language barrier. The menu also includes brief descriptions of each dish, a thoughtful addition most ethnic restaurants should adopt. Even though some items like Lassie (a yogurt drink) are not listed on the menu, they are available, with both salty and sweet mango varieties on offer. The head chef is proficient in English and approachable for any inquiries or assistance with larger orders.

I've noticed that Zaika is already starting to cater for Ramadan, further highlighting their commitment to providing a variety of options for all dietary preferences.

In summary, Mohammad Butt has expanded upon his previous menu at "Best Taste of Asia" with a focus on offering all-Halal meat. This promising change is sure to bring nothing but positive developments for Zaika.

P.S. Zaika is conveniently located behind Nifty Fifties on Grant Ave., making it the perfect spot for dessert, such as a milkshake. However, if available, I highly recommend trying the Ras Malai. These delicate ricotta cheese dumplings soaked in sweetened, thickened milk, accented with cardamom and a hint of rose water, and garnished with pistachios are simply divine.

input: Busy place, but we were offered extra- special coffee while we waited. No sooner than it was ready, so was our table. The server was welcoming and offered suggestions for us after we made her aware of some dietary restrictions. My daughter and I shared a salad, entree, and Special grits. Every bite was delicious, beautifully presented, and reasonably priced as downtown prices go. We like this restaurant a lot.
Refine this for me please: At this bustling establishment, we were pleasantly surprised to be offered a premium coffee while we patiently waited. Almost instantly, our table was prepared and we were greeted warmly by our server who graciously accommodated our dietary restrictions by providing helpful recommendations. Opting to share a salad, entree, and their signature Special grits, we found each bite to be mouthwatering, elegantly displayed, and reasonably priced for a downtown eatery. It's safe to say that we thoroughly enjoy dining at this restaurant.

input: I love this place. Super friendly staff. Great with kids. And the food is amazing. Especially the hash browns. You can also get tomatoes and grits on the side. Yum! And on top of it all it's not hard on the wallet.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore this place. The staff is incredibly friendly and they go above and beyond, especially when it comes to kids. The food is absolutely outstanding, with a personal favorite being their incredibly delicious hash browns. Additionally, they offer tasty options like tomatoes and grits as side dishes. Simply delightful! What's even better is that this place doesn't break the bank, making it all the more perfect.

input: Similar experience at this place ..gelato is great...service sucks.a friend from out of town came to visit and we decided it would be cool to go here since they never had gelato..boy what a mistake..day staff cool..night staff not so much..they acted like we were an annoyance then a customer then whispering and laughing ..made my friend feels uncomfortable..so the young manager pops out from the back and I'm thinking cool though s guy will make them act more respectable,again wrong..he actually joined in.this place had great service not even a year ago..don't know what happened
Refine this for me please: We had a similar experience at this place where the gelato is great, but unfortunately, the service was very poor. A friend from out of town came to visit, and we thought it would be a good idea to take them here since they had never tried gelato before. However, it turned out to be a mistake. The day staff was fine, but the night staff was not pleasant at all. They treated us as if we were annoying and seemed to be whispering and laughing about us, which made my friend feel uncomfortable. We were hoping that the young manager would step in and improve the situation, but to our disappointment, he actually joined in. It is unfortunate because this place used to have great service less than a year ago, and I am not sure what has caused the decline.

input: Great hiking, biking, running spot. Lots of well maintained paths. Beautiful views and spots with shade which is great when you're hiking in the heat. Only complaint is that people don't follow the dogs on leash rule and I came across at least 6 dogs off leash and away from their owners. Just follow the rules or they will make it a no dog spot!!!!
Refine this for me please: This location is an ideal spot for hiking, biking, and running enthusiasts. It offers an extensive network of well-maintained paths, ensuring a pleasant outdoor experience. The picturesque views and conveniently shaded areas are particularly enjoyable during hot weather hikes. However, it is regrettable to note that some individuals choose not to adhere to the leash requirement for dogs. During my visit, I encountered at least six dogs freely roaming off-leash and away from their owners. It is crucial for everyone to respect and follow the designated rules to preserve this spot as a welcoming destination for canines. Failure to comply might lead authorities to enforce a strict no-dog policy.

input:
Like many other reviewers I passed by this place a number of times before looking it up on Yelp and realizing that I really did need to give it a shot...
Wow... I was not disappointed!
We started out with the crab cake appetizer- it was very well portioned (2 large crab cakes) and the sauce with it had an interesting hint of dill (just lovely and refreshing and a little different).
We were feeling like comfort food and had the chicken tenders-  The portions were very generous and the food was just solid.  Not fussy or stuffy or trying hard... just good, wholesome and good to eat.
The service was fine- however there is only one waitress for the tables and the bar, so i can imagine that if it is full that would cause some delays.  Overall it was just a lovely meal and the prices were unbelievably reasonable (most places have crabcakes 1/2 that size for twice that price)...
The ambiance is nice, nothing crazy but it is just a very nice option with reasonable prices and lovely food!
Refine this for me please:
After passing by this place multiple times, I finally looked it up on Yelp and decided it was time to give it a try. And let me tell you, it did not disappoint! Initially, we ordered the crab cake appetizer, which was generously portioned with two large crab cakes. The accompanying sauce had a delightful touch of dill, adding a refreshing and unique flavor to the dish.

Craving some comfort food, we opted for the chicken tenders. The portions were more than satisfying, and the food itself was simply delicious. It didn't try too hard or come off as pretentious - just good, hearty food that hit the spot.

While the service was decent, it's worth noting that there is only one waitress serving both the tables and the bar. This could lead to some delays if the place is crowded. Nevertheless, overall, it was a delightful dining experience, especially considering the unbelievably reasonable prices. In comparison, most other establishments charge twice as much for crab cakes half the size.

As for the ambiance, it wasn't anything extravagant, but it provided a pleasant atmosphere. With reasonable prices and delightful food, this place makes for a fantastic dining option.

input: Always excellent service and amazing food. The staff is is always friendly and there are many promotions that always keep us coming back. The quality of the fish is amazing and the perfect portion size of the rolls allows you to try many different kinds. Out favorite sushi in town!
Refine this for me please: The service at this establishment is consistently excellent, and their food is truly amazing. The staff is always friendly and welcoming, and they offer numerous promotions that make us keep returning. The quality of their fish is outstanding, and the rolls are perfectly portioned, allowing for the opportunity to savor a variety of flavors. Without a doubt, this is our go-to place for the best sushi in town.

input:
My boyfriend and I both decided to try Jesse's for the first time after we'd both grown up in the Brandon area and neither of us had ever been, and really hadn't heard much about the restaurant. 

We dined on a Saturday night and even though the parking lot and restaurant was packed, we were sat right away at a 2-top next to a window facing SR-60. 

Our server, Nikki, greeted us in a reasonable amount of time. We ordered our beverages and she brought them shortly after that. Something I did not like was there was not a drink menu on the table, but Nikki was able to tell us what beers were on draft and non-alcoholic drinks. She took our appetizer and entree order all at once. 

We ordered crab stuffed mushrooms and a French onion soup to share. These items came out together. The crab stuffed mushroom was basically a giant thing of crab stuffing on a TINY mushroom, which was almost laughable, but had a good flavor nonetheless. The French onion soup had a great flavor and wasn't scalding hot, which was super nice to eat right away. 

After our appetizer came out and we finished it, our Caesar salads came out as well as a loaf of bread and some butter. This was also really great pacing of our meal! Nikki never let empty plates sit on our table, was very attentive, and always made sure we had drinks in front of us. The Caesar salads were good. I gave the bread two chances... once dipped in the French onion soup and once just with butter on it... the bread could have definitely been better - it just didn't have a good flavor to it. 

I ordered the 6 oz filet and he ordered the 16 oz Delmonico - both cooked medium rare. The steaks are served with sautéed mushrooms, your choice of side, and a salad or soup of the day, which isn't mentioned anywhere on the menu. I got broccoli as my side and my boyfriend got a sweet potato with all the fixings. I saw three tables sat after us receive their entrees before us - I don't know if it was a kitchen issue or something else, but we were sat at least five minutes before each of those tables - I tried to make sense of the delay, but it honestly wasn't a big deal to me. Our steaks came out on hot metal plates that were inserted into a cooler outer shell. My filet was nice and thick and cooked perfectly and the broccoli was steamed very tenderly, but there were not enough sautéed mushrooms on the plate, in my opinion. If I had known it would have been like five mushrooms with the steak, I totally would have gotten them as a side. My boyfriend's steak was cooked perfectly as well, but being on the hot metal dish led the steak to cook more at the table, which he wasn't particularly pleased with. He enjoyed his sweet potato with butter, but it didn't come out with cinnamon on it like he requested. 

Anyway, I am sure we will return! Our server, Nikki, was fabulous. She was extremely attentive, had a great attitude, and was knowledgeable!
Refine this for me please:
After growing up in the Brandon area and hearing little about Jesse's, my boyfriend and I decided to try the restaurant for the first time. Despite the busy parking lot and packed restaurant, we were seated promptly at a 2-top table by a window facing SR-60 on a Saturday night.

Our server, Nikki, greeted us without much delay and took our drink orders. Unfortunately, there was no drink menu on the table, but Nikki was able to provide us with information on the draft beers and non-alcoholic options. Taking both our appetizer and entree orders simultaneously, she efficiently managed our dining experience.

For our shared appetizer, we chose the crab stuffed mushrooms and French onion soup. These two dishes arrived together. The crab stuffed mushroom appeared comically oversized compared to the tiny mushroom itself, but it had a pleasing flavor. On the other hand, the French onion soup had a delightful taste and was served at a temperature that allowed us to dig into it right away.

Following the appetizers, our Caesar salads were served along with a loaf of bread and butter. The timing was well-paced and our server, Nikki, was attentive, ensuring that our table remained free of empty plates and that our drinks were continuously refreshed. The Caesar salads were satisfactory, but the bread fell short, lacking the desired flavor despite being sampled both dipped in the French onion soup and with butter.

As for the entrees, I ordered the 6 oz filet while my boyfriend opted for the 16 oz Delmonico, both cooked to a medium rare. The steaks were accompanied by sautéed mushrooms, a choice of side, and a salad or soup of the day, which was unfortunately not mentioned on the menu. I selected broccoli as my side, while my boyfriend requested a sweet potato with all the fixings. Strangely, we noticed that three tables seated after us received their entrees before us, despite arriving at the restaurant earlier. Though we couldn't determine the cause of the delay, it didn't bother us much. When our steaks did arrive, they were presented on hot metal plates nestled within a cooler outer shell. My filet was beautifully thick and impeccably cooked, and the broccoli was perfectly tender. However, the plate lacked an adequate amount of sautéed mushrooms in my opinion; had I known, I would have ordered them as a side. My boyfriend's steak was also cooked to perfection, but the hot metal plate caused it to continue cooking at the table, which he found slightly disappointing. Nevertheless, he enjoyed his sweet potato with butter, although it arrived without the requested cinnamon.

Despite these minor shortcomings, we plan to return to Jesse's. Our server, Nikki, was exceptional, displaying a high level of attentiveness, a positive attitude, and extensive knowledge.

input: Friendly staff, good selection, fair prices.
Refine this for me please: The staff is friendly and accommodating, offering helpful assistance. The selection of products is extensive and diverse, catering to various needs and preferences. The prices are reasonable and fair, providing good value for the quality of the goods.

input:
This was my very 1st time in New Orleans. It's been an amazing experience and so far, every single place I've eaten at has been AMAZING. So... I took a chance with The Praline Connection and walked in. Why? The ambiance and the restaurant, overall, looked nice. 
However... I would NEVER return to this place again, nor would I Ever RECOMMEND it to Anyone. 

APPETIZERS:
I ordered the BBQ Oysters and..wow.. fucking wow...1st of all the oysters not in their shells. Instead they placed in a soup cup filled with  "BBQ sauce" that tasted like cheap Ketchup and Chef Boyarde! Disgusting! The oysters themselves were gooey.

The garlic bread was God awful! It tasted like stale frozen garlic bread. To make matters worse, when I received these appetizers, they were cold.. It tasted and looked like they had been microwaved and left out.  

I also ordered the Chicken wings. They were under cooked, cold and the sauce was nasty.  

The other members of our party ordered entrees. They all said, "This Sucks!"

PROS: The service was great. The servers were all very polite and attentive. 
Restaurant was clean, nice tables, nice ambiance.
Refine this for me please:
This was my first time in New Orleans and it has been an amazing experience so far. I have tried many incredible restaurants, but unfortunately, The Praline Connection was not one of them. Despite its appealing ambiance and overall appearance, I would never return to this restaurant and I cannot recommend it to anyone.

When it came to the appetizers, the BBQ Oysters were a major disappointment. Instead of being served in their shells, they were placed in a soup cup with a "BBQ sauce" that tasted like cheap Ketchup and Chef Boyardee. The texture of the oysters was gooey and unpleasant. The garlic bread was equally terrible, tasting like stale frozen garlic bread. On top of that, both appetizers were served cold, as if they had been microwaved and left out.

I also ordered the Chicken wings, which were undercooked, cold, and had a nasty sauce.

The other members of our party also ordered entrees, and they all shared the sentiment that the food was subpar.

On the positive side, the service at The Praline Connection was excellent. The servers were polite and attentive, and the restaurant itself was clean with nice tables and ambiance.

input: This is the McDonalds closest to my home, but I will forever drive any distance to find another bc it's a terrible restaurant. Even though it's not politically correct to say "I love McDonalds", every now and again and during lent we go to McDonalds and this one is really bad. Bad food, always cold or wrong items.  Bad service, and no offense to anyone but I cannot even communicate with most employees bc they don't speak any ENGLISH!!  I do not know much Spanish either but when I'm trying to spend my money in Fishers Indiana at a business I at least expect to be able to communicate in some way! Refine this for me please: This is the McDonald's closest to my home, but I am willing to drive any distance to find another because it is not a good restaurant. While it may not be socially acceptable to openly express love for McDonald's, occasionally, during lent, we still visit this restaurant. Unfortunately, this particular location is quite disappointing. The food is bad, often served cold or with incorrect items. The service is subpar and, without intending to offend anyone, most of the employees do not speak English, making communication difficult. I do not speak much Spanish either, but when spending money at a business in Fishers, Indiana, I expect to at least be able to communicate in some way. Additionally, the service at this location is notably slow compared to other nearby McDonald's restaurants. My advice would be to avoid this location unless you have plenty of time on your hands and can communicate in Spanish.

input: Very good breakfast. Within walking distance of our hotel. Had the crepes with fruit. Would get again for sure. Not sure about the tea. Had a hint of fennel seed to it.
Refine this for me please: Excellent breakfast option located conveniently within walking distance of our hotel. The crepes with fruit were delightful and definitely worth ordering again. However, the tea had a subtle touch of fennel seed which may not be to everyone's liking.

input:
Holy Mole!

Enjoyed a wonderful evening here as part of a Yelp Elite event. Got to sample a wide variety of their food, and each dish was better than the next. Refine this for me please:

Throughout the evening, I had the opportunity to try a wide range of dishes, and let me tell you, each one was better than the last. The flavors were superb, and there was no shortage of variety. input:
Ick.  That sums up my experience at Dinardo's in one "word."  Dinardo's gave me that "Ick" vibe the minute I set my foot in the door. THough we were greeted by a very friendly hostess, the place looked like a run down diner on the interior--and it wasn't very clean or charming.  This would have been fine because a lot of times the "run down" places have the best "authentic food," but this was not the case at Dinardo's.  At Dinardo's you do not get what you pay for as the prices are rather high and the food quality is rather low.    Our server hated his life and made snarky, mean comments throughout our time there which, though entertaining, was kind of unwelcome and unpleasant.  My friend had the mussels which were puny and in an unimpressive sauce--unimpressive being the general adjective I would use to describe any given dish my party ordered.  I had a soup which was extremely salty and bland beyond that and the broiled flounder and "seafood imperial" dishes were OK at best. 

I'd say if you're looking for good seafood you'd be better off at any BYOB; little fish, audrey claire, ANYWHERE but Dinardo's.  I don't understand how this place is still in business, to be honest.
Refine this for me please:
My experience at Dinardo's can be summed up with just one word: "Ick." From the moment I stepped foot in the door, I got an immediate sense of unease. Despite the friendly hostess, the interior looked like a rundown diner and lacked cleanliness and charm. While I understand that sometimes these types of places have the best authentic food, that was not the case at Dinardo's.

The prices at Dinardo's are high, yet the quality of the food is disappointingly low. Our server seemed to have a negative attitude, consistently making snarky and mean comments throughout our time there. Though it provided some entertainment, it was ultimately unwelcome and unpleasant.

One of my friends ordered mussels, which were small and accompanied by an unimpressive sauce. In fact, "unimpressive" is the best word to describe any dish we ordered. The soup I had was extremely salty and lacked any flavor beyond that, while the broiled flounder and "seafood imperial" dishes were mediocre at best.

If you're in the mood for good seafood, I would suggest going to any BYOB or trying out other restaurants like Little Fish or Audrey Claire. Anywhere but Dinardo's will provide a better dining experience. Frankly, I'm baffled as to how this place manages to stay in business.

input:
Drum-roll please! Review #100 coming right up! 

I chose to review Starbucks as my 100th review because it is a guilty pleasure. Something that I only allow myself once a week. But something that I crave everyday!

Refine this for me please:
Drum-roll please! Here comes review #100!

Starbucks takes the spotlight as my chosen 100th review, being my indulgent guilty pleasure. Though I limit myself to once a week, the crave for it lingers on a daily basis!

input: My wife and I loved everything about this diner. The decor is lovely & the food was great. I had the cheese steak and it was much better than Geno's.  Our server was awesome
Refine this for me please: My wife and I absolutely adored every aspect of this diner. The decor is absolutely lovely, creating a charming atmosphere that adds to the overall experience. Moreover, the food was outstanding, leaving us truly satisfied. I ordered the cheese steak, and it exceeded all expectations, surpassing even the renowned Geno's in quality. All aspects combined, our server was truly remarkable, providing superb service throughout our visit.

input:
Don't judge a book by it's cover.  Looked like a any similar bar food type chain like Friday's, Bennigan's, or Ruby Tuesdays... JB Dawson's is far better.
Awesome experience from the second we stepped in, hostess greeted us with a smile and time to table waiting expectation.  We were promptly seated, and tended to right away with a smile and good attitude by a server, Nancy, who helped us with a beverage and app order.  

For our app we shared the twisted shrimp as it was Twisted Tuesday.  Nancy told us this dish far surpassed Bone Fish's Bang Bang Shrimp, to our surprise, it clearly did.  Our beverage and app shortly followed. 

Shortly there after another server stopped by, Kyle, who was our designated server.  Boy, smile, great greeting, great attitude, engaging.  We talked a bit, figured our way through the menu and placed our order.

For our dishes, my wife selected the Four Cheese Mac & Cheese side -- Sharp Cheddar, Pepperjack, Mozzarella & Reggiano dusted with bread crumbs with cornbread as she had large lunch.  Very good.  Unexpected, light, not overly creamy, not burnt, just right.  And the corn bread with maple butter..... ahhhhhh that was really nice.

 I ordered the fish tacos-- 3 Flour tortillas, seasoned tilapia, chimichurri sauce, mango cilantro salsa & a lime cream drizzle.  Passed on starch sides and had their asparagus that was cooked to perfection.  To my surprise the they were filling, nice size portion (see photo)  not a two bite app.  Very moist and super fresh fish.

Great first experience all around expect one key aspect.  Their so called craft beer menu was really limited and did not contain a variety of types; focused more on IPAs.  Limited thinking for the bar manager I must say.  Kyle our waiter also bar-tends.  We got to talking and he offered with no questions to swap out my beer for another option --- Stoudts Scarlet, which is a reddish beer.  For my beer palette it was better then the others limited options had a nice taste at the swallow then waned off.   Kyle informed us that they buy for all 4 restaurants and try to find a middling that works across the 4 guest demographics.  Not a great decision honestly.  There are so many great craft brewers in the Bucks County region and even Bristol area that should be showed cased and tested through.  For me a bad or poor beer selection stunts the overall experience.

We'll be back but I may need to sneak in my own beer selections from my craft collection.
Refine this for me please:
Don't judge a book by its cover - JB Dawson's may resemble other bar food chains, but it far exceeds expectations. From the moment we walked in, the hostess greeted us warmly and estimated our wait time accurately. We were promptly seated and our server, Nancy, took care of us right away with a smile and positive attitude. She helped us order drinks and an appetizer, recommending the twisted shrimp which proved to be superior to Bone Fish's Bang Bang Shrimp.

Shortly after, our designated server Kyle approached our table. He had a great attitude, a welcoming smile, and engaged with us in conversation. He helped us navigate the menu and took our order. My wife opted for the Four Cheese Mac & Cheese side with cornbread, and it was unexpectedly light, perfectly cooked, and accompanied by delightful maple butter.

I chose the fish tacos, which came with seasoned tilapia, chimichurri sauce, mango cilantro salsa, and a lime cream drizzle. I skipped the starch sides and ordered asparagus, which was cooked to perfection. The tacos were satisfying with a generous portion of moist and fresh fish - not the small, appetizer-sized tacos you might expect. Overall, it was a great first experience.

However, the craft beer menu was disappointingly limited, mostly consisting of IPAs. This was a missed opportunity, as the bar manager should have considered incorporating a variety of beer types to cater to a wider range of tastes. Fortunately, our waiter Kyle, who also tended the bar, offered to swap my beer for another option - Stoudts Scarlet, a reddish beer. It had a better taste and improved my overall beer experience. Kyle explained that their beer selection aimed to cater to all four restaurants, which, in my opinion, was not a wise decision. There are numerous outstanding craft brewers in the Bucks County and Bristol area that should be showcased and tested. Personal preference aside, a limited beer selection can hinder the overall dining experience.

Despite this, we plan to return to JB Dawson's, possibly with my own selection of craft beers in tow.

input:
Stopped here for lunch on the way to drop some people off at the airport. It's a bit unexpected and a tiny bit off the beaten path on a residential street just behind a business district.

I chose the vegetarian plate and a Greek salad. The salad was the absolute best I've ever had. The cheese was absolutely fresh, the vegetables were fresh and chopped just for the salad, and the dressing and seasoning was perfect. The salad was quite large on its own and could easily make a light lunch by itself.

The vegetarian plate came along with their fresh pita-like bread that is baked fresh every morning, seasoned, pan fried vegetables, rice, and a tzatziki-like sauce drizzled on top. The flavors were astounding, and despite a lack of desire to stuff myself silly, I did anyway. Plenty of food for lunch and very reasonably priced.
Refine this for me please:
We made an unexpected stop for lunch while en route to drop some people off at the airport. The place we found was a hidden gem, tucked away on a residential street just behind a busy business district.

I opted for the vegetarian plate and a Greek salad. To my delight, the salad turned out to be the best I've ever had. Every component was top-notch - the cheese was incredibly fresh, the vegetables were crisp and perfectly chopped for the salad, and the dressing and seasoning were spot-on. The salad itself was quite generous in size and could easily be enjoyed as a light lunch on its own.

As for the vegetarian plate, it was accompanied by their freshly baked pita-like bread, which is made every morning. The bread was seasoned and pan-fried vegetables, rice, and a delectable tzatziki-like sauce were all part of the dish. The flavors were simply astounding, and despite not initially having the intention of overindulging, I couldn't resist and ended up eating to my heart's desire. The portion was more than satisfactory for a fulfilling lunch, and the prices were very reasonable.

input:

input: Great food love the atmosphere in the place. . .  the carne asada tacos are just like back home !!!

input:

input: My friend and I came here around 2pm on a Monday. It happened by default, as most of the restaurants on Main Street were closed. We sat ourselves down at the bar and got to drinking. input:
Wow!!  That really sums up, in a very good way, my interactions with Delicious Designs and Leigh Anne!  Our wedding was only planned two months out and was supposed to be very very small so no cake was needed.  As the weeks went by, the guest list increased, so I decided I wanted a cake.  With probably less than a weeks notice, Leigh Anne stepped up and made the exact cake I had in my head.  I asked for a simple two tier lemon cake with no decorations.  Not only did she make this happen beautifully, she made chocolate vegan cupcakes for my daughter at the last minute.    I'm attaching a picture of the cake "table".  My daughter did the decorating and I must say, for someone with not much in the decorating department, everything came out better than I could ever imagine.  And not only was the cake perfect, it was yummy delicious.  I can't wait for my one year anniversary to dig in to that top layer! 

If you are in need of any bakery needs in Reno and you don't use Leigh Anne with Delicious Designs, well then all I can say is I'm sorry!
Refine this for me please:
I am extremely pleased with my experience with Delicious Designs and Leigh Anne. Initially, our wedding was intended to be very small and we didn't plan to have a cake. However, as the guest list grew, I decided to have one. Despite giving Leigh Anne less than a week's notice, she exceeded my expectations by creating the exact two-tier lemon cake I had envisioned, without any decorations. Additionally, she went the extra mile by making last-minute chocolate vegan cupcakes for my daughter. I have attached a picture of the cake table, where my daughter did the decorating herself. Even though she isn't skilled in this area, everything turned out better than I could have imagined. Not only was the cake visually perfect, but it also tasted absolutely delicious. I am eagerly looking forward to indulging in the top layer on our one-year anniversary.

If you are in need of any bakery services in Reno, I highly recommend Leigh Anne with Delicious Designs. Trust me, you won't be disappointed if you choose her.

input: I have been going to this nail salon for years off and on. I came here back when it was called Tropical Nails and Tom was the owner. Now its Grant Nails and has a different owner. When I started getting my nails done again I lucked out and found an experienced technician named Amy. I stuck with her because she did good nails. Then about 2 months ago Amy left. So I let the owner Angela do my nails. The first time was ok. Then the second time she did them the gel polish (which she talked me into getting instead of regular polish) started to chip within a day. I called and complained, she redid the polish and again within one or two days it was chipping. Now my nails look at mess. I don't trust her to correct the problem. Unfortunately, I'm going to have to find a new nail place. Very upsetting and disappointing.
Refine this for me please:
I have been a customer at this nail salon for several years, with some breaks in between. I initially started coming here when it was called Tropical Nails and owned by Tom. However, it is now known as Grant Nails and under new ownership. 

Upon returning to get my nails done, I was fortunate to find an experienced technician named Amy. Her skills were excellent, so I became a regular customer. Unfortunately, Amy left around two months ago, leaving me to try out the services of the owner, Angela. 

My first experience with Angela was satisfactory. However, the second time she did my nails using gel polish (which she convinced me to try instead of regular polish), the polish began chipping within a day. I reached out to Angela to voice my dissatisfaction, and she agreed to redo the polish. Disappointingly, the chipping issue persisted just days later. Consequently, my nails currently look messy. I have lost confidence in Angela's ability to address this problem effectively. 

Regrettably, I am now in the unfortunate position of having to search for a new nail salon. This situation is deeply upsetting and disappointing to me.

input:
Awefull!!!! 
If I could give zero or negative stars I would!
I've never wrote a review before, but I am going out of my way to say that I had the absolute worst dining experience at the Sake House!! 
And esp families, stay clear! 
So first off, I decided to take my 15 month old son out on a sushi date. We arrive at the Sake House at 4pm. There is only one other table and they were closing out. We sit down, and I immediately ask for a simple ice water with lemon. Waiter comes back 20 minutes later (no water). I order a simple roll for my son, to get him started  and a cold Sake. I said I will wait to order mine to get him settled. Another 30 min later, still no water, no food. Waiter comes back with hot Sake, instead of cold. 20 minutes later, the roll for my son (not how I asked) finally some cold Sake, then I have to request water, and then only one cup for my son, no lemon. When I see 2 going on a third table had come in and ordered, and a "to go" order is being placed, all with food and water, I became perturbed. The waiter never came back to see what I wanted. Never came back to check on the order. Finally after  nearly 2 hours of waiting and trying to deal with my antsy son, who waited so long to be served, and seeing one chef trying to make everyone's order I decided it was time to go. Finally after waiting another 5/10 minutes I had to walk up and ask for my check , which was only a $6 drink. Which I reluctantly paid. After being in the hospitality industry for years, I know what to expect, and I know what to forgive. I also know that English being a second language must be tough...BUT since he was able to wait in other tables i know that wasn't the issue. After 2 hours of waiting, and dealing with a fussy/hungry toddler as a single mother I feel like the least they could have done is offer a free drink, to say "we understand we couldn't accommodate you, but we tried." It's principal above all else. ...I just waisted 2 hours! And had to leave and take my baby somewhere else. Time is money! And I waisted 2 hours here! 
Time that is rare and I had to plan being a busy mother.
I should have listened to the other reviews about the shitty service here. 
Don't waste your time or money!!!
Stay away! Any other place is better than here!
Refine this for me please:
Terrible Experience at Sake House!

I am extremely disappointed with my dining experience at Sake House and would give it zero or negative stars if possible. This is my first-ever review, but I feel compelled to share my terrible encounter here.

I decided to take my 15-month-old son out for a sushi date, and we arrived at Sake House around 4pm. To begin with, there was only one other table occupied, which was close to closing time. I promptly requested a simple ice water with lemon, but it took the waiter 20 minutes to return without the water. I proceeded to order a basic roll for my son and a cold sake for myself, mentioning that I would wait to order my own food. 

Another 30 minutes passed, and we still had not received any water or food. When the waiter finally returned, he brought me hot sake instead of the cold one I requested. After waiting for 20 more minutes, my son's roll arrived (not as I had requested), followed by the cold sake. I then had to specifically request water, but only one cup was brought for my son, without any lemon. My frustration grew when I noticed that two more tables had arrived and were promptly served with food and water, even a "to go" order was processed efficiently. The waiter did not bother to come back and check on my order or attend to my requests.

Finally, after nearly 2 hours of waiting and struggling to keep my restless and hungry son settled, I observed that only one chef was managing all the orders. That's when I decided to leave. After waiting another 5 to 10 minutes, I approached the counter to request my check, which amounted to a mere $6 for the drink. Reluctantly, I paid it.

Having worked in the hospitality industry for several years, I understand what is expected and what can be forgiven. While I acknowledge that English may be a second language for the staff, as they were able to cater to other tables, it was clear that language wasn't the issue. After enduring a two-hour wait and dealing with an impatient toddler as a single mother, I believe that the least they could have done was offer me a free drink as a gesture to acknowledge their inability to accommodate my needs. It's a matter of principle.

I wasted valuable and rare time planning this outing as a busy mother, and I should have heeded the warnings from other negative reviews about the poor service at this place. I strongly advise against wasting your time and money here. There are plenty of better options available. Stay away!

input:
The only good part.... 

Their stage is really cool! Raised up, lights that move around, good sound system, a fog machine, and a pretty big dance floor. 


But their food service.... crappy both times Ive been there. 

The last time I was there I walked in, hadn't been greeted by anyone at the empty front podium, and just found a table. I figured once I sat down Id wait for an employee to get back to the menus and go up and ask for one. So I saw a lady working up at the front and went up and asked her.  She said that they stopped serving food at...... I cant remember if it was 9 or 10 pm.... but she gave me a certain time that the kitchen closed. I went back to my table and looked at the time. It was 10 minutes before the time she told me the kitchen closed. I thought that was kinda dumb, but oh well.... maybe they stopped taking orders 10 minutes ahead or something. The next thing I see the SAME EXACT LADY seat four people RIGHT NEXT to our table and give them menus. Then she takes their order, and brings out their food. All I wanted were some freakin french fries and I had to sit there and watch the people who got there long after me eating french fries instead. RUDE!
Refine this for me please:
The only positive aspect of their establishment is their impressive stage setup. It features a raised platform, dynamic lighting, an excellent sound system, a fog machine, and a sizeable dance floor. 

However, I must express my disappointment with their food service. On both occasions I visited, it was subpar. During my most recent visit, I entered the venue and found no one at the front podium to greet me. Therefore, I took it upon myself to locate a suitable table. I assumed that once seated, an employee would attend to me, provide menus, and take my order. Eventually, I noticed a woman working at the front and approached her to request a menu. Surprisingly, she informed me that the kitchen had stopped serving food at a specific time, which I cannot recall precisely if it was 9 or 10 pm. However, I realized I still had 10 minutes before the said closing time. I found this rather illogical but decided to let it go, assuming perhaps they stopped accepting orders 10 minutes before the official closure time. To my dismay, moments later, the very same woman seated four individuals right next to our table and promptly served them with menus and took their orders. Witnessing other patrons who arrived much later than I did enjoy their french fries while I sat there waiting for my order was incredibly rude and frustrating.

input: My hair is a work in progress. I have been trying to get an A-line bob for a bit over a year now with little success until today! Jenna Moore was referred by a friend and on my god I'm so glad she did. Jenna is amazing. She listen to everything I had to say and told me what she was going to do to make sure we were both on the same page. Not only did she listen but she delivered too! I know my hair needs some healing, Jenna doing the healing, and growing to get where I want to be but I actually see it in the future now thanks to Jenna. HIGHLY HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!
Refine this for me please: My hair has been a project that I have been working on for quite some time. The A-line bob hairstyle has been my goal for over a year, but I have struggled to achieve it until today. Thankfully, a friend recommended Jenna Moore to me, and I am beyond grateful. Jenna is truly exceptional. She attentively listened to all my hair concerns and desires, ensuring that we were both on the same page. Not only did she listen, but she also successfully delivered outstanding results. I am aware that my hair requires some healing, growth, and time to reach my desired look, but thanks to Jenna, I can now envision it in the future. I wholeheartedly and enthusiastically recommend Jenna Moore. She is truly amazing!

input: Fast.  Fresh.  The carne was very good.  So was the guacamole.  Wish there was the ability to customize taco toppings.  The tortilla chips were too thick.  The dulche de leche  soft serve ice cream was amazingly delicious.  Wish that there was more seating.  Wish that table clean ups were more timely and more thorough.
Refine this for me please: Fast and Fresh: The carne was excellent, and so was the guacamole. However, it would be great to have the option to customize taco toppings. Additionally, the tortilla chips were a bit too thick. On the bright side, the dulce de leche soft serve ice cream was incredibly delicious. It would be even better if there was more seating available. Lastly, the table clean ups could be more timely and thorough.

input:
Would it be weird if I wanted to move in and permanently live here!? The style of this salon is impeccable. The color palette and decor they chose makes it feel like you're in a Restoration Hardware magazine...in France...surrounded by heirloom antiques. I didn't know what to expect when arriving but I was pleasantly surprised with their upscale polish options like Chanel and many others I actually didn't know I needed in my life until I arrived. 
Service was prompt and I especially enjoyed the extended massage. Most importantly the tools she used were brand new/ had been sterilized. I watched her open the fresh package up, that made me feel good about cleanliness and safety. I don't know if all nail salons have cute gold tips on their nail trimmer tools but now I want them for my own collection. 

I picked a gray color for my toes and did OPI Funny Bunny gel on my nails. So far I'm loving both! 
So nice to see a high end nail salon finally making its way to Nashville. I've gone to others in Nashville that seem to be high end, but it just ends up like a VIP club on the Vegas strip with loud music and sparkles just waiting for a Justin Bieber song to come on. 
CURED was not only high end, but it was classic. Like The Hamptons type of classic but with a comfortable low key brunch with girlfriends mimosa type of vibe. I think it would be amazing for a bridal party with so many photo opportunities. I felt comfortable with their prices, competitive to anywhere else I've gone in Nashville worth mentioning. 

I didn't know where to park so I parked on the side in a random parking lot. Looks like there's a lot of up and coming businesses beside them under construction. So I'm assuming once those are complete, parking will be pretty straight forward? 

When my Mom & Sister come into town next I'm going to take them here & go to Local Honey for lunch since it's so close. 

Can't wait to go back. Welcome to the neighborhood!
Refine this for me please:
Is it strange that I have the desire to move in and permanently reside at this salon? The aesthetic of this place is absolutely flawless. The chosen color scheme and decor give off a vibe reminiscent of a Restoration Hardware magazine...but in France...surrounded by beautiful heirloom antiques. I wasn't sure what to expect upon arriving, but I was pleasantly surprised by the upscale polish options they offer, including Chanel and other brands that I never knew I needed in my life until now.

The service was prompt and I particularly enjoyed the extended massage. Most importantly, I was pleased to see that the tools used were either brand new or properly sterilized. I witnessed the technician opening a fresh package, which made me feel confident about the salon's cleanliness and safety practices. I've never seen cute gold tips on nail trimming tools at other salons, but now I find myself wanting them for my own collection.

For my nails, I chose an OPI Funny Bunny gel color and went with a gray shade for my toes. So far, I'm absolutely loving both choices! It's refreshing to finally have a high-end nail salon in Nashville. I've been to others in the area that claim to be high-end, but they often turn out to be more like a VIP club on the Vegas strip, complete with loud music and excessive glitter, just waiting for a Justin Bieber song to start playing. CURED, on the other hand, exudes a sense of elegance and timelessness. It's reminiscent of The Hamptons, but with a relaxed, comfortable atmosphere perfect for a low-key brunch with friends and mimosas. I can imagine it being an amazing venue for a bridal party, with numerous photo opportunities. The prices were also reasonable and comparable to other places I've been to in Nashville that are worth mentioning.

Parking was a bit confusing for me, so I ended up parking in a random lot on the side. It appears that there are many upcoming businesses nearby currently under construction, so I'm assuming that once they're completed, parking will become much more straightforward.

When my mom and sister visit next, I plan on bringing them here and then heading to Local Honey for lunch, since it's conveniently close by.

I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit and I'm excited to welcome CURED to the neighborhood!

input: I've been coming to this place for years now, and even though I now live in Colorado, I come back here every time I'm in Philadelphia for work (which is often). I've tried many items on the menu and many were great, portions are generous, and prices are low. My go to item - Indian Mee Goreng, I can eat that every day of the week if I could, it's that good. Maybe one day I can get the recipe from the manager so I can actually do that on days I'm in CO.
Refine this for me please:
I have been consistently visiting this establishment for several years now. Despite currently residing in Colorado, I make it a priority to return each time I am in Philadelphia for work, which happens frequently. Throughout my visits, I have sampled numerous items from the menu and have found many of them to be exceptional. The portions served are notably generous, yet the prices remain remarkably affordable.

One particular dish that stands out for me is the Indian Mee Goreng. I am so enamored with its flavor that I could easily consume it daily if given the chance. In fact, I aspire to acquire the recipe from the manager one day so that I can enjoy it at home during my stays in Colorado.

input: not impressed!..... the service was great but the pizza i ordered was not good. i love Stella and Trenos pizza so i wast expecting the same type. no desire to return again
Refine this for me please: Not impressed at all! Although the service was great, the pizza I ordered was disappointing. I'm a huge fan of Stella and Trenos pizza, so I was expecting something similar, but it didn't live up to my expectations. I have no intention of returning in the future.

input: Stayed for one week post Christmas. Unless you take adjoining rooms as a family, strangers conversations/coughs/clearing throats/fights/dogs barking etc feel as if they are in your bed with you. Only slept two out of seven nights after hotel cleared out after New Years. Connecting doors are very poorly insulated. Staff at hotel is superior...really excellent but Starwood needs to do something about insulating those doors. Have stayed many places with connecting doors and never experienced anything as bad. Poor materials used????
Refine this for me please: During our one-week stay after Christmas, we unfortunately had a challenging experience due to the lack of insulation in the connecting doors. Unless you opt for adjoining rooms as a family, you can hear strangers' conversations, coughs, throat clearing, arguments, and even dogs barking as if they are right beside you in bed. This resulted in only two nights of restful sleep out of the seven nights we stayed, and it was only after the hotel cleared out after New Year's. We must highlight that the hotel's staff was exceptional, providing excellent service. However, we believe that Starwood, the hotel management, should address this insulation issue, as we have stayed in many places with connecting doors and never encountered such poor soundproofing. Perhaps better materials or insulation methods could greatly improve the situation.

input: I didn't really like my sandwich I got here. I got the jalapeño cheese bread and it was tasteless and dry. I could tell it was old. Also I got tomatoes and cucumbers which were mush because they were overripe. Usually they're a lot better than this but today wasn't it. The staff is very friendly though.
Refine this for me please: I was not satisfied with the sandwich I had here. The jalapeño cheese bread I ordered lacked flavor and was dry, indicating that it was old. Additionally, the tomatoes and cucumbers in the sandwich were overripe and mushy. Normally, the quality of the ingredients is much better, but today's experience fell short. On a positive note, the staff was very friendly.

input: We love this movie theater/ bar/ restaurant. Great drinks, friendly service and good food.  We can only recommend this place!!
Refine this for me please: We absolutely adore this movie theater/bar/restaurant. The drinks are fantastic, the service is consistently friendly, and the food is exceptional. We cannot recommend this place highly enough!

input: Ordered an iced mocha  and an iced white chocolate mocha and they were both was awful.  They  had NO coffee flavor or chocolate flavor at all, very watered down.  Even went back and asked the girl to add another shot and why.  I think she remade them, instead of just adding another shot.  Still had NO flavor.  Not even sure how you could make it that bad.  We both ended up throwing them away on the way out.  So sad, not even worth drinking.
Refine this for me please: I had a disappointing experience when I ordered an iced mocha and an iced white chocolate mocha. Unfortunately, both drinks lacked any coffee or chocolate flavor and were extremely watered down. In an attempt to improve the situation, I returned to the counter and requested an additional shot of coffee. I suspected that the barista remade the drinks instead of simply adding another shot, but even then, they still lacked any flavor. It was truly surprising how poorly they were made. Ultimately, my companion and I were so dissatisfied that we decided to throw the drinks away before leaving. It's unfortunate that they were not worth consuming.

input: This has fast become one of my favorite New Orleans gems! Enter over at the bridge on Peters near Elysian Fields or a little way up on Piety, either way, if you like breezes and city views, your efforts will be rewarded. The path stretches about a 1.25 miles from close to Elysian Fields over to the area near the old Navy installation. Along the way are various art installations, a dog park, and a wonderful walk along the mighty Mississippi River. If you time it just right, you might catch one of the spectacular sunsets. A beautiful way to end any day in NOLA!
Refine this for me please: This has quickly become one of my absolute favorite hidden gems in New Orleans! You can enter this stunning spot either at the bridge on Peters near Elysian Fields or a little further up on Piety. Regardless of your path, if you enjoy gentle breezes and captivating city views, you will be pleasantly rewarded. Meandering for approximately 1.25 miles from the vicinity of Elysian Fields to the area near the old Navy installation, this pathway offers an array of delightful experiences. You'll come across various captivating art installations, a welcoming dog park, and an enchanting stroll along the magnificent Mississippi River. If you time your visit just right, you might even have the chance to witness one of the most breathtaking sunsets imaginable. Undeniably, it's a stunning way to conclude any day during your stay in NOLA!

input: Yelp doesn't allow to leave 0 star review, so that is why you see one star. Me and my wife are moving from NY to South California, and we contacted 5 different moving companies. I sent my initial email to United Van Lines on 05/02/2018, and soon I got email back with Virtual Survey confirmation for 05/10. The lady that did virtual survey was very meticulous and professional and we "screened" through the whole apartment in 15 minutes. No one contacted me after that, so I sent a second email almost a month after, on 06/05 asking if everything is ok, and if I can get the quote. I don't need to mention that other 4 companies sent their quotes in less than 48 hours. Since no one replied til today, I called the direct phone and I left the message on the answering machine. No one called me back. I hope everything is ok, and that no one is hurt, because I don't see any other reasonable explanation why they are avoiding me. Very, very unprofessional.
Refine this for me please: Yelp has a policy where they don't allow users to leave a 0-star review, hence the one-star rating. My wife and I recently made the decision to move from NY to Southern California and reached out to 5 different moving companies for quotes. I initially contacted United Van Lines on 05/02/2018 and received a confirmation email for a Virtual Survey to be conducted on 05/10. The person conducting the survey was extremely meticulous and professional, efficiently going through our entire apartment in just 15 minutes. However, after that point, there was no further communication from their end. Growing concerned, I sent a follow-up email almost a month later on 06/05 inquiring about the progress and requesting a quote. It is worth noting that the other 4 companies provided their quotes within 48 hours. Despite this, I haven't received any response from United Van Lines to date. In an attempt to resolve the situation, I called their direct phone line and left a message on their answering machine, but no one has returned my call. As a customer, I hope that everything is well and that nobody has encountered any unfortunate circumstances, as there seems to be no other reasonable explanation for their lack of responsiveness. This level of unprofessionalism is highly disappointing.

input: Excellent price for sushi and I love their specialties sushi menu. Snow mountain and Volcano sushi are remarkable sushi!
Refine this for me please: Their sushi menu offers excellent prices and a fantastic selection of specialty rolls. The Snow Mountain and Volcano sushi rolls are particularly outstanding.

input:
THE BEST place to go for gyros! The quality of their food is amazing. I always get chicken gyros here but they have all kinds of goodies. My daughter loves their burgers. And the thick, perfectly seasoned steak fries are the bomb! Always hot and fresh. 

The only thing I did not care for was the baklava. They make it with pistacios.
Refine this for me please:
The absolute top destination for gyros! Their food is of exceptional quality, truly outstanding. Personally, I always go for their mouthwatering chicken gyros, but they offer a splendid variety of delights. My daughter is particularly fond of their delectable burgers. Additionally, the thick-cut, flawlessly seasoned steak fries are absolutely phenomenal, unfailingly served hot and fresh.

The only aspect I wasn't particularly fond of was their baklava, which unfortunately incorporates pistachios.

input:
In Reno for the night. Was a bit skeptical because well..it's Reno, but this place far exceeded expectations. Very good Taiwanese food compared to most places I've tried in different cities. My recommendations: 三杯鸡, oyster omlet, and scallion pancake. 

There are many other dishes I wish I could try. Will definitely miss this place once I leave.
Refine this for me please: I had the pleasure of staying in Reno for the night and to be honest, I had some doubts about the food scene here. However, this place has completely surpassed my expectations. Their Taiwanese cuisine stands out, even when compared to numerous other cities I've visited. I highly recommend trying their 三杯鸡, oyster omlet, and scallion pancake – they were absolutely delicious. I only wish I had more time to sample their other enticing dishes. I know for sure that I will really miss this place once I have to leave.

input: Good, authentic food. Nice, clean environment. Good service. Not a significant beer selection but all in all a great first experience. We will return.
Refine this for me please: Excellent, genuine cuisine paired with a delightful, immaculate ambiance. The service was commendable, although the beer selection was somewhat limited. However, these minor shortcomings did not overshadow the overall fantastic initial experience, making us eager to revisit.

input: Came here for lunch with my fiancee and friend, found a small table by the window.  they have a great and varied wine selection.  I got a bubbly and my fiancee got some Italian orange soda.  We got the lamb sausage, potato chips, and crab stuffed peppers as "snacks" then i got the mozzarella with prosciutto bacon bits sandwich which was delicious and savory while being light and healthy. service was prompt and polite.  rustic, intimate, and cozy wine lounge atmosphere with low to medium noise level.  bathroom door lock and handle are kind of confusing to use at first. would definitely recommend for lunch!
Refine this for me please: My fiancee, friend, and I came to this restaurant for lunch and easily found a small table by the window. Their wine selection is extensive and varied, offering something for everyone. I opted for a bubbly, while my fiancee enjoyed an Italian orange soda. As for snacks, we indulged in the lamb sausage, potato chips, and crab-stuffed peppers, which were all delectable. For my main, I ordered the mozzarella with prosciutto bacon bits sandwich, which was both delicious and surprisingly light and healthy. The service was prompt and courteous, enhancing the overall dining experience. The rustic, intimate, and cozy wine lounge atmosphere created a pleasant ambiance with a moderate noise level. The only downside was the slightly confusing lock and handle on the bathroom door. Despite this minor inconvenience, we highly recommend this place for a satisfying lunch.

input: This is my first choice whenever we decide to go out to dinner! They have a huge selection of foods that will fit any type of person who will be dining there. Their staff is super nice and will accommodate to whatever your needs may be! The restaurant itself is beautiful and very relaxing. In my opinion, Fellinis of media has the best Italian cuisine around.
Refine this for me please: Fellinis of Media is always my top pick for a dinner outing. With its extensive array of delectable dishes, there is something to satisfy every palate. The staff is exceptionally friendly, providing personalized service that caters to your specific requirements. The elegantly designed ambiance of the restaurant creates a serene and calming atmosphere. In my perspective, Fellinis of Media stands out for offering the finest Italian cuisine in the area.

input:

I think this place is exactly  what the neighborhood needed!
Refine this for me please: This place is a total game changer for the neighborhood! We decided to try their take-out tonight, and let me tell you, the food was beyond delicious. I'm absolutely thrilled that they've joined our community, and I've fallen head over heels for their incredible Southern Latin cuisine. On top of that, the family who owns it couldn't be any sweeter. I truly believe this place is exactly what our neighborhood was missing!

input:

 I see no FUTURE for this place or in MY FUTURE.  Don't waste your time or money. This is the Lehigh Acres location.

input:
was here twice -- first for a nightcap at the bar -- the drinks really were some good stuff and i tried a the lemon hummus and pita -- that was the best hummus ive ever had!

the next morning we came in for brunch, which was pretty much terrible. first of all, it took us 45 minutes to get our food for brunch....and it came out cold and we found a hair. the manager did comp our check though. overall, the bar is great, but i would skip breakfast. what a disappointment for a kimpton restaurant.
Refine this for me please:
I visited this place on two occasions. The first time was for a nightcap at the bar where I had some amazing drinks and tried the lemon hummus and pita, which turned out to be the best hummus I've ever had.

The following morning, we decided to have brunch there, but it was a disappointing experience. Firstly, it took us a frustrating 45 minutes to receive our food, which was served cold and even had a hair in it. However, the manager was kind enough to comp our bill. Overall, while the bar is great, I would advise skipping breakfast as it was a letdown, especially for a Kimpton restaurant.

input: I really enjoy this theater! It is always clean and the staff is always friendly. the reason I am giving them for star in that V is because they haven't done some of the necessary updates that other theaters have done by updating the seating offering wait staff service excetera. You can go to the Roadhouse theater for $11 with a student discount or 12 bucks, which is all required liners and heated seats and they have wait staff with a chef. The pricing is nearly the same at this theater but it doesn't have all the same perks. I believe they may have one or two theaters with upgraded seats but they really need to go through the entire theater and update it.
Refine this for me please: I really enjoy this theater due to its consistently clean environment and friendly staff. However, I am giving them a lower rating because they have not implemented necessary updates that other theaters have adopted, such as updated seating options and wait staff service. For instance, at Roadhouse theater, you can enjoy added comforts like heated seats, wait staff service, and a chef, all for a student discount of $11 or $12 otherwise. Although the pricing is similar at this theater, it lacks these additional perks. Although it may have upgraded seats in one or two theaters, I believe a comprehensive update of the entire theater is needed.

input:
4-5 stars, this is just after one visit so far, worth a try if you're a thai fan. I liked the food, but you always have to have the first visit to see "how they do things" and figure out what your preferences will need to be.

I did use their living social deal so I brought my dad in when he came in from out of town to try it out with me. I like the set up, the quaint house is cute (and well, quaint), but I can see how it wouldn't be ideal it if was jam packed. I imagine you could potentially do family style for some of the pub height tabletops. I did call ahead to make sure that I didn't need to print out the coupon and it could be used from my ipod and to make sure they were open, as the website said to just double check.

We started with shrimp spring rolls, probably the best I've had, the ingredients seemed fresher, and crispier. No shredded lettuce here. Simple and loosely wrapped, but you could taste the individual components. The peanut sauce was tasty too, though they don't have sirracha (spelling?) to add to it, just dried pepper flakes. 

We then got the tom yum (gai?) with shrimp. I know it is hot (because of the name, duh), I usually prefer it a little less spicy (I am white), though I still got a good sour flavor (for instance at Thai chili it's too hot for me, I don't taste any sour). I usually get my tom yum without meat or seafood because I feel the meat gets dried out, but the server assured me the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they weren't. I think they are making sure to use fresh ingredients, but I do prefer straw mushrooms (I think they are usually canned) over the button mushrooms they used. Next time I am probably going to try out a veggie version (i love the soup with the cabbage, and broccoli). The owner did tell me they are trying to be authentic and so maybe button mushrooms and less veggies is more authentic?

We then got shrimp pad thai and chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodle) minus the red pepper. Both were tasty, the portions were probably a little less than other places in Reno (not sure if just lunch sized portion now that I think about it).

Like Ernie said, the pad thai noodles were a little soft, overdone, and its not the 'orange-y' sauce like other pad thai's, but there was still flavor there. The shrimp were also tasty in this dish. The drunken noodles was done exactly how I like them, lots of baby corns and the noodles covered in the sauce and of course spicy. 

My dad and I talked outside for a while and the husband did come out and talk with me about the food, and asked if I was happy (we were outside a while). I hope the living social deals bring in some business, and I do plan on coming back, it is just hard because I don't live in the area. I also asked about the cooking classes (they are a steal at $65), and on facebook it said they are looking to improve and give some focus to that side of the business. The owner did say that they use just a regular kitchen so no woks or anything like that (meaning what they teach us can actually be done at home), I wonder if that is why the pad thai noodles are that way? Regardless, they seem to pride themselves on authentic and quality food and service.

I did include pictures. Oh I did try a thai iced tea for the first time too, pretty tasty, reminded me of chai tea. 

I didn't get to see the bill closely, but it was $24 and some change after the living social deal (takes $20 off), I didn't think that was too bad for 2 for lunch (the total cost), with an appetizer and soup and a drink.
Refine this for me please:
Overall, I would give this restaurant a 4-5 star rating based on my first visit. It's worth trying if you're a fan of Thai food. The food was delicious, but keep in mind that the first visit is important to understand how they do things and adjust your preferences accordingly.

I used a living social deal to bring my dad, and we enjoyed the cute and quaint atmosphere of the restaurant, which is located in a house. It might not be ideal if it gets crowded, but I think you could potentially do family-style dining at their pub height tabletops. I called ahead to make sure I could use the coupon from my iPod and to confirm their opening hours.

We started with their shrimp spring rolls, which were the best I've had so far. The ingredients tasted fresh and crispy, and I appreciated that they didn't include shredded lettuce. The simple and loose wrapping allowed the individual flavors to shine. The peanut sauce was also delicious, although they don't offer sriracha, only dried pepper flakes.

Next, we tried the tom yum soup with shrimp. It was hot, as expected, but I prefer it a little less spicy. Nevertheless, it still had a good sour flavor. The server assured me that the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they were right. They seem to prioritize using fresh ingredients, but I personally prefer straw mushrooms over the button mushrooms they use. Perhaps the use of button mushrooms and fewer vegetables is more authentic? I plan on trying their vegetable version next time, as I love the soup with cabbage and broccoli.

For our main dishes, we ordered shrimp pad Thai and chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodle) without red pepper. Both dishes were tasty, but the portions seemed smaller compared to other restaurants in Reno. The pad Thai noodles were slightly overdone and lacked the orange-y sauce typically found in other pad Thai dishes, but there was still plenty of flavor. The shrimp in this dish were especially delicious. The drunken noodle dish was cooked exactly how I like it, with lots of baby corn and a generous amount of sauce, and of course, it was spicy.

My dad and I had a conversation outside the restaurant, and the husband came out to talk with me about the food. He asked if I was satisfied with my experience. I hope the living social deals bring in more business for them. I'm planning on returning, although it's difficult since I don't live in the area. I also inquired about their cooking classes, which are priced at an affordable $65. They mentioned on Facebook that they are looking to improve and focus on that aspect of their business. The owner mentioned that they cook using a regular kitchen, so what they teach in the cooking classes can be replicated at home. I wonder if that's why the pad Thai noodles are prepared that way. Regardless, the restaurant takes pride in serving authentic and high-quality food with great service.

I included pictures in my review. I also tried a Thai iced tea for the first time, and it was quite tasty, reminding me of chai tea.

Unfortunately, I didn't closely examine the bill, but after applying the living social deal, the total came to around $24, which I thought was reasonable for two people having lunch with an appetizer, soup, and a drink.

input:
Sometimes I just head on over to Kingsway if I need a little shopping fix, instead of battling the crowds at West Ed. They've got lululemon, Jacob, Danier, Gap, Club Monaco, American Eagle, and a variety of other shops that work for me, and it's never so busy you have to brush past people in the halls. 

I sometimes just go for the food -they've got New York Fries, Orange Julius, Poppin' pop corn, Booster Juice, Extreme Pita, Bad Ass Jack's and other choices. 

The food court has a ton of seating. It's never completely full. There's a Zellers and a dollar store and a Sears. I just wish they had a Bay and a movie theatre to round it out a bit. Otherwise, Kingsway is as good a mall as I need.
Refine this for me please:
Sometimes when I want to go shopping but don't want to deal with the crowds at West Ed, I like to head over to Kingsway. They have a great selection of stores like lululemon, Jacob, Danier, Gap, Club Monaco, American Eagle, and more that suit my style. Plus, it's never too crowded, so you don't have to squeeze past people in the hallways. 

Another reason I enjoy going to Kingsway is for the food options. They have New York Fries, Orange Julius, Poppin' pop corn, Booster Juice, Extreme Pita, Bad Ass Jack's, and many other eateries to choose from. The food court also has plenty of seating available, so it's never completely full. 

Although Kingsway has a Zellers, a dollar store, and a Sears, I do wish they had a Bay and a movie theater to complete the mall experience. But overall, Kingsway is still a great mall that meets all my needs.

input:
So my favourite Indian in St Louis is still Spice and Grill on Olive, Husband said lets have a change so we tried out Indias Kitchen this evening and ordered a portion of the goat curry.

Sorry to say this curry was not great, the sauce was very heavy on the salt and tomato and the goat was tough as an old boot, the naan bread was below mediocre. Only nice thing was the rice.  Very Very dissapointed
Refine this for me please: I must say, my favorite Indian restaurant in St. Louis is still Spice and Grill on Olive. However, my husband suggested that we try something different, so we decided to give Indias Kitchen a chance this evening. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing. We ordered a portion of goat curry, but it fell short of our expectations. The sauce was overly laden with salt and tomato, and the goat meat itself was incredibly tough. Additionally, the naan bread was far from being satisfactory. The only saving grace was the rice. All in all, we were extremely disappointed with our meal.

input:
Yes, it's a little pricey, but it was darned near worth it. 
It certainly didn't seem a priority to get us our menus, but once they did, the service was pretty on point. The bread was good. I ordered a chopped salad and a crab cake, and the hub got a crab cake sandwich with fries. We had water to drink, no appetizers-walked out for $45 with tip. The food came quickly.  My food was great-and I'm no salad eater. The crab cake was quality, fries were good.
