Another drawback is that we had to sit in the bar area bc it was after 9. The table was the size of a chair, 3 plates were too much.

P.S. i used my bank card, and noticed that I was charged significantly more than I agreed to, so I called the restaurant. The manager said it's a banking glitch, and should correct itself before the money comes out of my account... It better.
Refine this for me please:
Yes, it was a bit expensive, but I would say it was definitely worth the price. Initially, the waitstaff seemed indifferent about serving us, as it took some time to receive our menus. However, once they did attend to us, the service was quite impressive. The bread provided was enjoyable. For our meals, I ordered a chopped salad and a crab cake, while my companion opted for a crab cake sandwich with fries. We only had water and skipped appetizers. In the end, our bill, including tip, came to $45. To my surprise, the food was promptly served. I was particularly impressed with my salad, considering I don't typically enjoy them. The crab cake was of high quality and the fries were tasty. 
One downside was that we were seated in the bar area due to the late hour, and the table was small, barely accommodating the three plates we had. 
Additionally, I paid with my bank card and noticed an unexpectedly higher charge. I promptly contacted the restaurant and was informed by the manager that it was a banking error, which should be rectified before the amount is deducted from my account. I certainly hope so.

input:
I am sort of a sushi snob. 

I'm going to be honest. This was literally the worst sushi Ive ever had.  It was warm... WARM! (and NO! it wasn't tempura).

I also paid $3 for a side salad which was literally iceberg lettuce. 

Nope... no spring mix...no romaine...no iceberg with slivers of carrots or even purple cabbage... LITERALLY just iceberg. I was puzzled and then angry and then i had to smirk and whisper, "well played my friend... well played".

I will never be back..

Check and Mate.
Refine this for me please:
I have very refined taste when it comes to sushi, and unfortunately, the sushi I just had was the absolute worst. Surprisingly, it was served warm, and it wasn't even tempura.

To make matters worse, I paid $3 for a side salad that consisted solely of iceberg lettuce. No spring mix, no romaine, not even carrots or purple cabbage to add some flavor and variety. It was just plain iceberg lettuce. I was perplexed at first, then frustrated, and eventually found myself smirking and whispering, "You got me there, my friend. Well played."

Needless to say, I will never visit that place again.

Game over.

input: My partner and I split the vegetarian platter and left stuffed! Delicious food, very kind and attentive staff.  Will help you make decisions on ordering and certainly won't take advantage of you. Will definitely be back.
Refine this for me please: My partner and I thoroughly enjoyed sharing the vegetarian platter and left feeling completely satisfied! The food was absolutely delicious, and the staff was incredibly friendly and attentive. They were more than happy to assist us in making choices when ordering and treated us with utmost fairness, ensuring that we were not taken advantage of. We are definitely planning on returning in the future.

input: I have never stayed at a hotel so ghetto. Sure the atmosphere is great and very classy looking. However the staff is the opposite. First of all, my friend booked us a suite for the bachelorette party she was planning. They gave us two separate rooms and my friend had to beg for them to be at least next door to each other since they ran out of suites. Then to make up for it, they threw in free valet. The next day her car had been keyed on her door when the valet brought it from the parking garage. Seriously? Worst experience and I certainly won't ever be back.
Refine this for me please: I had an extremely unsatisfactory experience staying at a hotel that was beyond low-standard. Although the ambiance and appearance of the hotel were upscale and stylish, the behavior and attitude of the staff were the complete opposite. Let me elaborate on the series of disappointments. Initially, my friend had made a reservation for a suite to celebrate a bachelorette party, but we were assigned two separate rooms instead. It took considerable effort and pleading on her part to have them at least allocated next to each other, as they claimed to have run out of available suites. As a compensation, they offered complimentary valet service. However, when her car was brought back from the parking garage, it was found to have been scratched on her door. Can you believe it? This entire experience has been absolutely terrible, and I can confidently say that I will never choose to stay at this hotel again.

input: I've been to this place in numerous occasions and I have never been disappointed! My friend and I are traveling to Puerto Rico and my mother in law wanted Tamales! They were very accommodating and gave us free samples and offer to cook them and pack them for us! Great place and very friendly staff!
Refine this for me please: I have visited this place on multiple occasions and it has never failed to impress me! Recently, my friend and I traveled to Puerto Rico and my mother-in-law had a craving for Tamales. To our delight, the staff at this establishment were incredibly accommodating. They provided us with free samples and even offered to cook and pack the Tamales for us to take away! Not only is this place great, but the staff is also exceptionally friendly.

input:
Wish I had read the reviews before we stopped for dinner.  When we arrived there were only two other tables of patrons and a handful of people at the bar.   They promptly took our food order, but we waited 50 minutes for it to be delivered.   It was only a burger and a pork tenderloin sandwich.   Not sure why we didn't leave other than the fact we were watching football.  Food was just ok.

The people at the bar were so loud, offensive and obnoxious that I felt uncomfortable for an older couple that was dining.    What kind of management allows this kind of behavior?   

This place won't last.
Refine this for me please:
I wish I had taken the time to read the reviews prior to deciding to stop for dinner. Upon our arrival, we discovered that there were only two other occupied tables and a few individuals at the bar. Although our food order was promptly taken, it took an excruciating 50 minutes for our meals, which consisted of a burger and a pork tenderloin sandwich, to finally be served. Despite contemplating leaving, we stayed due to our engagement in watching a football game. The quality of the food was average at best.

My discomfort arose from the offensive and obnoxious behavior exhibited by the individuals at the bar, causing me to feel empathetic towards an older couple who were also dining. I found myself questioning the management's tolerance of such conduct.

Based on my experience, I believe that this establishment is unlikely to thrive in the long run.

input:
i enjoyed the experience eating here and will definitely go back.

first of all, there are vegetarian options on the menu. we started with the veggie spring rolls which were hot, crisp, and delicious. my husband had the duck and rice vermicelli soup which we both agreed was great in a yummy, savory broth. i had the beef pho which i didn't care for because the meat was a bit grisly and i'm not a fan of tripe. i've not eaten a lot of pho and wasn't sure what to order, though. they offer several different beef cuts and i should have picked a different one. next time. also, the regular serving size was way more than enough. i don't think either of us could have come close to finishing the largest bowls.

the restaurant was clean and quiet with a sparse, yet very 80s decor. the server was quick and attentive.
Refine this for me please:
I thoroughly enjoyed my dining experience at this restaurant and I am already looking forward to returning. One aspect I particularly appreciated was the availability of vegetarian options on the menu. To start, we ordered the veggie spring rolls, which exceeded our expectations with their hot, crisp, and delicious taste. My husband opted for the duck and rice vermicelli soup, which we both agreed was exceptional, especially due to its flavorful savory broth. On the other hand, I ordered the beef pho, but unfortunately, I did not enjoy it as much since the meat was a bit tough and I am not a fan of tripe. However, considering my limited knowledge of pho and lack of previous experience with it, I should have made a different beef selection. Nonetheless, I appreciate that the regular serving size was incredibly generous, as neither of us even came close to finishing the largest bowl.

In terms of ambiance, the restaurant was impeccably clean and provided a quiet atmosphere. The decor had a minimalist 80s style, which some may find spartan, but it added to the unique charm of the place. The server was prompt and attentive, providing excellent service throughout our meal.

input:
3.5 stars.

Chickie's and Pete's is a friendly sports bar, particularly for women, and it has lots of seating for Sunday games. I appreciate the sound booth in the sky, as it means that (admittedly bad) music is played during the commercials, along with special themes for Eagles fans. And, the place seems to be smoke free.

But, I am not impressed by the famous crab fries, which are crinkled, lightly fried, and seasoned with garlic, chili pepper, and salt. Something about the congealed cheese sauce detracts from the entire experience, and I also prefer my fries to be piping hot. However, there are towers of beer available (complete with taps), which is pleasantly tacky. 

With loads of space, booming sound, cute servers, and rowdy fans, Chickie's and Pete's is a perfect place to catch a game.
Refine this for me please:
I would give Chickie's and Pete's a rating of 3.5 stars. It is a friendly sports bar with a lot of seating, making it great for watching Sunday games. The sound booth in the sky adds a unique touch, playing music during commercials and offering special themes for Eagles fans. Moreover, the fact that the place is smoke free is a definite plus.

However, I was not impressed with the famous crab fries. While they are crinkled, lightly fried, and seasoned with garlic, chili pepper, and salt, the congealed cheese sauce detracts from the overall experience. Additionally, I personally prefer my fries to be piping hot. On the bright side, there are towers of beer available, complete with taps, which adds a fun and slightly tacky element.

Overall, with its spacious interior, booming sound system, attractive servers, and energetic fans, Chickie's and Pete's is a perfect spot to catch a game.

input: Pancake Pantry is an institution in Nashville. A place to see country stars and have a great breakfast. Pancakes are good. It's a thing to do in Nashville. Plan to stand in line and enjoy the conversation.
Refine this for me please: Pancake Pantry is an iconic institution in Nashville, known for its celebrity sightings and exceptional breakfast offerings. The pancakes are undeniably delicious, making it a must-visit destination in the city. Standing in line is part of the experience, allowing you to soak in the lively conversations happening around you. Don't miss out on this renowned Nashville tradition, where you can enjoy a fabulous breakfast while potentially spotting some country music stars.

input: I have been a loyal customer at Magasin Cafe for years, it's what made me fall in love with Vietnamese food. Since Magasin Cafe has closerd for renovations I came to Magasin Kitcheb to curb my weekly pho cravings. The food and service were good- even the chopped was seasoned better than the other location. However, paying more money for the same meal and the restaurants atmosphere deters the ranking. Quality food and service will continue to keep me a loyal customer.
Refine this for me please: I have been a devoted patron of Magasin Cafe for several years, as their amazing Vietnamese cuisine won my heart. Unfortunately, since Magasin Cafe closed down for renovations, I have been visiting Magasin Kitchen to satisfy my weekly pho cravings. While I found the food and service to be commendable - with the chopped dish even better seasoned compared to the other location - the higher price for the same meal and the ambience of the restaurant hindered its overall rating. Nevertheless, as long as they maintain their standard of quality food and service, I will remain a loyal customer.

input: I love this place...stop whenever I can; either at this location or the Philadelphia one. I could eat the cumin style lamb every day of the week. But honestly, all of their food is good. I'm definitely a fan of their rabbit appetizer. People can argue about how authentically Sichuan it is...whatever. The only place I've actually had Sichuan food taste exactly like they serve in Sichuan Province was when I went to Chengdu. This place is well worth eating at.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore this place. I make it a point to stop here whenever I can, be it at this location or the one in Philadelphia. The cumin style lamb they serve is so incredibly delicious that I could easily have it every single day of the week. However, to be fair, all of their dishes are outstanding. Personally, I'm a huge fan of their rabbit appetizer. Some may argue about its authenticity to Sichuan cuisine, but honestly, I couldn't care less. I've only experienced the exact taste of Sichuan food as it's served in Sichuan Province during my visit to Chengdu. Nonetheless, this eatery is definitely a must-try.

input:
A quasi political rant and a store review all wrapped in one, so enjoy. 

Ever since Target hit the scene I really have to ask, "Who even goes to Kmart anymore?" I asked this to myself out loud the other day as I had to get my meds filled due to a sinus infection. No one looked at me odd, as there seemed to be several people talking to themselves. I now go here because of the stolid contractual war between Express Scripts and Walgreens. Thanks you two....idiots.....qausi-political rant over.

This store is harshly bright, rather dingy, and the selections, especially in the electronic section, are on the cheaper end.  On top of that, I've found the mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are overpriced.  I laughed at the men's area, especially the young man's department, as they had a tv with music videos playing. I laughed because it just seemed a lame attempt to be cool and creating a shopping experience that you will find at a department store like Macy's or Dillard's. This is hard to create when everything is whitewashed. You will feel like you are in that August Burns Red's "Whitewashed."  The best WTF moment is discovering the opportunity to purchase Joe Boxer male thongs. Who knew that Kmart cared about male panty line?

One great tip is you can find patio furniture cheap during the off season and clearance days. I bought a great patio table for under $50. So, keep that in mind.

The extra star is for the pharmacy, as they filled my prescription out efficiently and with the greatest of ease. The hours are little later than Target.  No problems there and credit when credit is due!

The later 80s quote, "K-Mart sucks", remains as true as ever and who knows, you may even bump into someone who still dresses from that Tom Cruise era who cares about male panty line. One never knows?
Refine this for me please:
A combination of a quasi-political rant and a store review, here's my take:

Since the emergence of Target, it begs the question - who even bothers going to Kmart anymore? This thought echoed in my mind one day as I reluctantly had to visit Kmart to fill my prescribed medications for a sinus infection. Surprisingly, no one paid attention to me as there appeared to be many individuals engaged in sporadic conversations with themselves. The only reason I find myself at Kmart these days is due to the never-ending battle between Express Scripts and Walgreens. Thank you, both...for nothing. Rant over.

Let me begin by saying that this store gives off a harshly bright yet dingy atmosphere, and the product selection, especially in the electronics section, leans towards the cheaper side. Additionally, the prices for mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are completely unreasonable. The men's department, particularly the young men's section, struck me as comical with its attempt to incorporate a TV playing music videos. It seemed like a feeble effort to emulate the shopping experience found in high-end department stores like Macy's or Dillard's. However, this illusion quickly fades when everything is whitewashed, leaving customers feeling like they stepped right into August Burns Red's "Whitewashed" music video. The pinnacle of bizarre discoveries here was the availability of Joe Boxer male thongs. Who knew Kmart was so invested in resolving male panty lines?

On a positive note, one can find cheap patio furniture during the off season and clearance sales. I managed to snag a great patio table for under $50. So, keep that in mind if you're in need of outdoor furniture.

A bonus star goes to the pharmacy department, as they efficiently filled my prescription without any issues. Their operating hours are also more accommodating than Target's. Credit where credit is due!

It's safe to say that the sentiment from the late 80s still rings true - "K-Mart sucks." And who knows, you may even encounter someone who still dresses like they're from the Tom Cruise era, someone who truly appreciates the importance of male panty lines. One can never be too sure, right?

input: The Tuck Special. So good I would drive all the way back out to Nashville from TX just to have it again. It's a mix of strange ingredients- brisket, egg, pimento cheese but combined they are an amazing flavor combination. My husband didn't care for the BBQ sauce on the table, but meat was pretty good. I can see how this place gets crowded, but if you have patience and look up the menu ahead of time, it should be manageable.
Refine this for me please:
Please refine this text:

"The Tuck Special is absolutely mouthwatering. It's so delicious that I would gladly drive all the way from Texas back to Nashville just to have it again. This unique sandwich combines unexpected ingredients like brisket, egg, and pimento cheese, resulting in an incredible blend of flavors. While my husband didn't particularly enjoy the BBQ sauce provided on the table, the meat itself was quite good. It's easy to see why this place gets crowded, but with a little patience and by checking out the menu in advance, it should be a manageable experience."

input: The restaurant smelled like a toilet.  I couldn't stand it.  My daughter and I got the meals to go and the guy put them in the same box.  She doesn't eat fish and that is what I got.  I know it's a sushi restaurant but she likes the California rolls.  I got the spicy tuna roll.  It was mediocre.  My daughter did enjoyed hers.  Will not be going back.
Refine this for me please: The restaurant had a strong odor resembling a toilet, which made it unbearable for me. Consequently, my daughter and I decided to order our meals for takeout. Unfortunately, the employee placed both our orders in a single container, despite my daughter not eating fish, which is what I ended up getting. While I understand it is a sushi restaurant, my daughter usually prefers California rolls, while I ended up with a spicy tuna roll, which turned out to be quite average. On the other hand, my daughter seemed to enjoy her meal. Overall, based on this experience, I have decided not to return to this restaurant.

input:
Love the food. Big portions, interesting and ever changing menue. The only issues i have are that the seating is cramped, too loud for conversation and the coffe is not as good as Sabrina's.

The latkas are always perfect and the bacon is the best I ahve had in Philly.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore the food here. The portions are generously large, and the menu is constantly evolving, keeping things interesting. However, I do have a couple of minor concerns. Firstly, the seating is quite cramped, making it a bit uncomfortable. Additionally, the noise level is often too loud, making it difficult to have a proper conversation. Lastly, I must admit that the coffee here does not quite match up to the quality of Sabrina's. On a brighter note, the latkas are consistently flawless, and I must say that the bacon surpasses any I've had in Philadelphia.

input: This is a must get when you come to Reno is Yellow Subs. Ask for the sprouts on your sub and you won't regret it. It is way better then  anywhere I've ever been. The people are totally down to earth and always are nice and Stack your sub with only the best. Only the best and I recommend this to anyone who loves subs and loves food. Oh and there Tank Tops and T-shirts, priceless, I have a tank myself and represent it anywhere I go. Will be going there again in the future. 5 stars because the service was fast, people were nice, food was amazing, seating made you feel closer to your peers with more conversation movement back and forth and a great environment.
Refine this for me please: When visiting Reno, make sure to check out Yellow Subs - it's a must-try. Don't forget to add sprouts to your sub; you won't be disappointed. The quality surpasses any other place I've been to. The staff is friendly and genuine, creating a welcoming atmosphere. Their subs are stacked with only the best ingredients. I highly recommend Yellow Subs to any sub and food enthusiasts. Additionally, their Tank Tops and T-shirts are worth owning - I proudly wear mine everywhere. I'll definitely be returning in the future. I give it 5 stars for its fast service, friendly staff, amazing food, conversation-inducing seating arrangement, and overall great environment.

input: Tina I believe was our waitress.. I'm not sure if I want to give 3 or 4 stars. Its just that the initial wait was kinda long. But it was my first time eating the food and I thought it was pretty good. I liked my side salad too!
Refine this for me please: I believe Tina was our waitress at the restaurant. However, I am unsure whether to give 3 or 4 stars to the overall experience. The reason being that the initial wait time was quite long. On the other hand, it was my first time trying their food and I found it to be quite enjoyable. Additionally, I really liked the side salad that I ordered.

input: Love!! Our new favorite local spot. We've gone a few times since they opened and it's always a good ambiance, and great food. The drinks are great, the salsa is super yummy, and the salads are very much entree sized. Bring your friends, sit outside, grab a margarita and enjoy!
Refine this for me please: Love!! Our new favorite local spot is absolutely amazing. We have visited multiple times since their grand opening and have been consistently impressed with the incredible ambiance and delightful food. Not to mention, their drinks are top-notch and their salsa is simply irresistible. The salads they serve are generously portioned and feel like a complete meal on their own. Additionally, we highly recommend visiting with your friends, especially for an outdoor seating experience. Soak up the refreshing atmosphere while sipping on a margarita - it's the perfect recipe for a truly enjoyable time!

input:
Great service, food was ok..  Wish the soups were served warmer, and my steak was cooked well done, when requested medium. 

However the service was excellent.
Refine this for me please: The service provided was excellent, but there were some areas that could be improved upon. The food quality was satisfactory, although there were a few aspects that fell short of expectations. Specifically, the soups could have been served at a warmer temperature, and the steak was overcooked, as I had requested it to be prepared medium.

input:
Despite it's great reviews by other Yelpers, I was not that blown away by Nippon Tei. 

My roommate and I were craving sushi and were recommended to come here by Yelp and a friend so we decided to give it a shot. 

First off, they get bonus points for serving FREE edemame as an appetizer. I usually pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi restaurants. The mango sake drink I have was alright, but not worth the price I paid for it. 

On to the main event...SUSHI! We had the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. They were all yummy, but I would have to say I have had better. Actually, out of the hand-full of sushi restaurants I have tried, this was the worst sushi I have tried, but I cannot say the sushi was bad by any means. Don't get me wrong, it was still tasty. 

The other big thing was that the rolls were actually falling apart. I have never had this happen. Therefore, I can say that the presentation and the ability to get the sushi from the plate to my mouth without falling apart did make me unhappy. 

I am willing to come back to Nippon Tei, but I have to say I already have my other favorites. The prices were average compared to other sushi bars, so that won't really help them out either when it comes to bringing me back. We will see!
Refine this for me please:
Despite its positive reviews from other Yelpers, Nippon Tei didn't impress me as much as I had hoped. My roommate and I were in the mood for sushi and after hearing recommendations from both Yelp and a friend, we decided to give it a try.

To give credit where it's due, they deserve bonus points for offering complimentary edamame as an appetizer. Typically, I would have to pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi restaurants. On the other hand, the mango sake drink I ordered was average and not worth the price.

Now onto the main event, the sushi. We tried the Philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and California roll. While they were all tasty, I must admit that I've had better. In fact, out of the handful of sushi restaurants I've visited, Nippon Tei had the least impressive sushi. That being said, the sushi wasn't necessarily bad, it just didn't surpass my expectations. 

One major issue we experienced was that the rolls kept falling apart. This was a first for me and it definitely affected my overall satisfaction with the presentation and the ability to eat the rolls without them falling apart.

I am open to giving Nippon Tei another chance, but I already have my favorite sushi spots in mind. Additionally, the prices were average compared to other sushi bars, so that won't be a determining factor in whether I return or not. Only time will tell!

input: Went to see Star Wars Rogue One yesterday in 3D.  Buying the tickets was a breeze, and the atmosphere was inviting.  Found the comfortable seats with no problem and ordered right away before the movie began.  I ordered pretzel sticks - food was hot, prompt & delicious.  I was excited for the movie to begin.  Once the advertisements were done and the movie started, that's when I noticed something wasn't right.  The entire screen was so dark that I was not able to make out the faces of the actors on the screen.  I kept lifting up the 3D glasses to see if it made a difference - nope.  The two people seated next to me were noticing the same and complaining.  I thought that maybe this is how the movie was filmed?  Then it got worse.  Even with the 3D glasses on, the shadows in the background on the screen were double and there was no discerning most actors' faces at all.  I got up and went to the lobby and asked for the manager.  The gentleman wore a blue shirt, middle age with a beard, said that this was the 3D experience, it was a "closed-system" and there was nothing he could do.  I simply asked him to come with me into the theater to see with his own eyes how dark it was.  He would not and did not.  I suspect this wasn't the first time he's heard this from a customer.  I've seen normal movies at this location before, but this was my first, and last experience with their 3D in room #1.
Refine this for me please:
Yesterday, I went to see Star Wars Rogue One in 3D and had an overall positive experience. Buying the tickets was a breeze and the atmosphere of the theater was inviting. I easily found comfortable seats and promptly ordered some pretzel sticks before the movie began. The food was hot, delivered promptly, and delicious, enhancing my excitement for the movie.

Unfortunately, as the movie started, I realized that something was off. The entire screen was too dark for me to make out the faces of the actors, even when I lifted my 3D glasses. I wasn't the only one to experience this issue, as the people seated next to me were also complaining. Initially, I wondered if the darkness was intentional and part of the movie's filming style. However, the problem worsened when the shadows in the background appeared double, making it impossible to discern the faces of most actors.

Frustrated, I decided to address the issue and went to the lobby to speak to the manager. The manager, a middle-aged man with a beard wearing a blue shirt, unfortunately, seemed dismissive of my concerns. He claimed that this was simply the way the 3D experience was meant to be and there was nothing he could do. Seeking a resolution, I requested that he accompany me to the theater room and witness firsthand how dark the screen was. However, he refused to do so, leaving me with the impression that he may have previously encountered similar complaints.

While I have previously enjoyed watching regular movies at this location, this disappointing and unsatisfactory 3D experience in room #1 will be my final one there.

input: Overpriced for average food served warm (not hot) by servers who had trouble saying the names of the dishes and seemed in a rush to give us our bill when the place was more than half empty (on a Saturday night). When one of the servers came over to check on the $23 pork chop (which was not listed in the menu - $18 price was), my spouse commented there was a lot of fat....she seemed baffled by his comment, then walked away! The "ropa vieja" dish was good, but overpriced for being served in moderate portion. The menu prices did not reflect the ambiance (random plastic container boxes placed on a nearby table nor the sagging knitted item hanging over our table - it looks like there should've been a lamp in it).
Refine this for me please: The restaurant is significantly overpriced considering the average quality of the food, which was served warm instead of hot. The servers struggled to pronounce the dish names and appeared hurried to present us with the bill, despite the restaurant being more than half empty on a Saturday night. When one server checked on the $23 pork chop (not listed on the menu, with a listed price of $18), my spouse mentioned that it contained a lot of fat. She seemed confused by his comment and hastily left. Although the "ropa vieja" dish was satisfactory, it was still overpriced given the portion size. The menu prices did not align with the overall ambiance of the restaurant, evident by the presence of random plastic containers on a nearby table and a sagging knitted item hanging over our table, presumably meant for a lamp.

input: Should have listened to other reviews--we were kind of disappointed.  The layout of the restaurant is interesting in that it's made to look sort of like the inside of a chicken coop (made for people).  However, the food was overpriced and underwhelming.  We ate from the Sunday brunch menu--only decent value on the menu is the chicken strips and fries.  My wife ordered the seasonal salad, which was comically small and was way short on the actual lettuce (and not cheap either).  Chicken was good, but nothing better than Raising Canes in my opinion.  Service and food seemed on the slow side, especially with the small crowd.
Refine this for me please: We should have taken heed of other reviews as our experience left us feeling somewhat disappointed. While the layout of the restaurant was intriguing, designed to resemble the inside of a chicken coop, our overall impression was marred by the overpriced and underwhelming food. Opting for the Sunday brunch menu, we found that the only item offering reasonable value was the chicken strips and fries. Unfortunately, the seasonal salad my wife ordered was comically small, lacking in lettuce and far from reasonably priced. While the chicken itself was satisfactory, we felt it didn't surpass the quality of Raising Canes. Moreover, both the service and food were notably slow, particularly given the small number of customers present.

input: Wow. I am not a vegetarian, nor am I a health-food nut (except for my random "diet" binges) but this place is awesome. A co-worker talked me into trying it out one day (by going there and getting me something and putting it in front of me) and she created a monster. I may not order every day but I sure do think about them. And their delicious salads! Every time I go there I am greeted with a smile and there are tons of other people waiting for their food, as well. Good company =)
Refine this for me please: I'm not a vegetarian or health enthusiast (except for occasional "diet" phases), but I have to admit, this place is absolutely amazing. One day, a co-worker convinced me to give it a try by bringing me a meal and placing it in front of me. Little did I know, she had just created a monster. Although I don't necessarily order from here every day, I find myself constantly thinking about their mouthwatering dishes, especially their delightful salads. Whenever I visit, I'm welcomed with friendly smiles and it's always bustling with other satisfied customers. It truly is a great place to be.

input:
Only giving a 1 because there is nothing lower!!! Angie
Gave me the worst haircut I've ever had!!! I came in with 2 photos of the cut I wanted came out with my hair looking NOTHING like the photos!!  Even when pointed out to her she didn't not pay attention to what she was doing.  Came out basically having a mans flattop!  Would never go to this place again!!! Nothing like going into the Holidays with a crappie haircut. Thank you!! Angie and Regis Hair salon!!
Refine this for me please: I am extremely disappointed with the haircut I received from Angie at Regis Hair salon. I had shown her two photos of the desired cut, but my hair ended up looking completely different from the pictures. Even when I pointed out the discrepancies, Angie seemed uninterested and continued to work without paying attention. The result was a disastrous, masculine flattop haircut. I would never consider going back to this salon again. It's truly disheartening to start the holiday season with such a subpar haircut. Thank you, Angie and Regis Hair salon, for the awful experience.

input: Perfect place for a date night. The sweet potato nachos and the "breakfast" we're to die for! Really everything we tried was delicious...I can't wait to go back again.
Refine this for me please: This place is the perfect spot for a memorable date night. The sweet potato nachos and the "breakfast" were absolutely divine. In fact, every dish we tried was incredibly delicious. I am eagerly looking forward to returning here again soon.

input: We had dinner at Convivio right after it opened and we will definitely go back. There were a few minor quirks with the service and with wine being out of stock, but I'm chalking it up to the fact that it just opened and they were working out the kinks. The owner visited our table and he could not have been nicer or more gracious. The food was excellent...nothing to change there! I had the tortelloni pansotti, and i think it was the best pasta I've ever had. I'm sure we will be frequent diners .
Refine this for me please: We recently had dinner at Convivio shortly after its opening, and we are certainly planning on returning. Although there were a few minor quirks with the service and wine availability, we understand that these are common issues that arise when a new restaurant opens, and they appeared to be working on resolving them. The owner personally came to our table and displayed exceptional kindness and hospitality. As for the food, it was truly outstanding - we wouldn't change a thing! The tortelloni pansotti that I had was possibly the best pasta I have ever tasted. With such a memorable dining experience, we anticipate becoming regular patrons of Convivio.

input: After driving pass all the seafood restaurants around Clearwater Beach, I knew wanted seafood right there and then. I wasn't familiar with the area and did not do any yelping before hand, so was pretty hesitant to just blindly pick a restaurant.  Finally, after a long day at the beach, we made a quick walk across the street to all the restaurants and thats when we stumbled into Crabby Bill's. We ordered the $25 bucket of steamed seafood. It was decent, not necessarily the best fresh seafood. This was just a quick snack that I shared with one other person to keep us going before our big dinner at Bern's Steak House that we had reservation for a couple hours later.
Refine this for me please: After driving past numerous seafood restaurants around Clearwater Beach, my craving for seafood was at its peak. However, being unfamiliar with the area and having not done any prior research, I was hesitant to blindly select a restaurant. Exhausted from a day at the beach, we finally decided to take a chance and crossed the street to find ourselves at Crabby Bill's. Opting for the $25 bucket of steamed seafood, we found the meal to be decent, though falls short of the freshest seafood options. This quick snack served as a temporary fix to sustain us until our much-anticipated dinner reservation at Bern's Steak House, scheduled a couple of hours later.

input:
Just finished a State Street Kitchen, Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss and Honey Mustard Sub.  To kick it up a notch I stuffed in Jalapeno Chips for a spicy crunch. 
It was great on an afternoon when autumn is starting to assert itself with bluster.  

This excellent local establishment continues to turn out first rate creative dishes thanks to the ever-present Micha, and her friendly staff.  It has become my most constant breakfast companion, and often my lunch date, as well.  

If you have not been in for a taste of home cooking with a Korean flare, you don't know what you are missing. 

Find a way to get there.  Sit down and become part of the family.
Refine this for me please:
Just recently devoured a phenomenal State Street Kitchen creation: a Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss, and Honey Mustard Sub. To add an extra kick, I decided to stuff it with Jalapeno Chips for a delightful spicy crunch. It was the perfect choice for an autumn afternoon, as the season began to make its presence known with gusts of wind.

This wonderful local establishment, helmed by the ever-present Micha and her friendly staff, consistently delivers exceptional and inventive dishes. It has become a staple in my breakfast routine and is often my go-to spot for lunch as well.

If you have yet to experience the comforting flavors of home cooking infused with a Korean twist, you truly don't know what you're missing. Make it a priority to visit this place and immerse yourself in the warm and inviting atmosphere that feels just like family.

input: awesome place.  good food. nice people.  rotating specials.  all home made.  what else do you want?  Chicken salad is a great pickup to make sandwiches at home.
Refine this for me please: Experience the ultimate dining destination - an awesome place with good food and nice people. Indulge in our delectable dishes, featuring a variety of rotating specials, all expertly handcrafted with love. What more could you ask for? Don't miss out on our incredible chicken salad, a perfect choice for a delightful sandwich at home.

input: I'm rating this based on the service and not the food. I am a sales administrator at a hotel. Typically, many places offer a hospitality discount because we do refer guests different places. Front desk told me I should try this place as they give a decent discount. I called to place my order and wasn't really able to say what I liked b/c the girl who answered would cut me off to finish my statement.(she wasn't in the best mood) We get to the end of the order and she asks me am I a guest or an employee. I told her an employee. She asked my title. I told her. She gives me a total and I asked her about the discount. She says it's only for front desk. I'm shocked that this is a departmental thing 1 and 2 I'm thinking to myself, "I'm in sales. I get groups of people here. They ALWAYS asked for recommendations." I said well should I hang up and have front desk place my order? She huffed and puffed and then said "well i'll give it to you this time but please dont abuse it." I was so shocked at how rude she was. So when I finally got my food, I tipped the driver and gave him their menus back and said we will no longer be doing business with you guys. She didnt know SALES is in charge of who the front desk can recommend. Her name was Neisha.The food was good though.
Refine this for me please: I am evaluating this experience solely based on the service and not the quality of the food. As a sales administrator at a hotel, it is common for us to receive hospitality discounts from various establishments due to the referrals we provide. The front desk recommended a particular place to me, mentioning that they offer a decent discount. Subsequently, I phoned the restaurant to place my order. However, I encountered difficulties expressing my preferences as the staff member who answered seemed uninterested and frequently interrupted me. Towards the end of the order, the staff member inquired whether I was a guest or an employee. I responded by stating that I am an employee and disclosed my job title. After providing me with the total cost of the order, I asked about the discount mentioned by the front desk. To my surprise, the staff member informed me that the discount only applies to front desk personnel. I was both taken aback by this department-specific policy and frustrated as I contemplated the fact that, in my sales role, I frequently provide recommendations to groups of people. I inquired whether I should hang up and ask the front desk to place the order for me. The staff member reluctantly agreed but emphasized that I should not take advantage of the situation. I found her rudeness to be quite shocking. Nevertheless, when my food finally arrived, I compensated the driver accordingly and returned the menus, informing him that our business relationship would no longer continue. It seems that she was unaware that the responsibility of recommending establishments lies with the sales department and not solely the front desk. The staff member I interacted with was named Neisha. Despite the unpleasant service, I must admit that the food itself was satisfactory.

input: Always the sweetest ladies! Appointments never take forever and barely any wait time!
Refine this for me please: These ladies are always the sweetest! Appointments are quick and there's hardly any wait time!

input: We won't be back. We got the Brussel sprouts and they tasted like pure salt. Our server sent them back and we got another batch and they tasted exactly the same. My husband got the burger and it was okay but the fries that came with it tasted like pure salt also. Maybe the cook working this night was just a little heavy handed on the salt, I don't know. I got the flank steak and it was okay. I wouldn't rave about it or ever get it again. Our cocktails were good and the atmosphere was nice, but we were really disappointed with the food :(
Refine this for me please: We will not be returning to this restaurant. The Brussel sprouts we ordered were excessively salty in taste. Despite sending them back to the kitchen and receiving a new batch, they were still equally as salty. My husband ordered the burger which was decent, but the accompanying fries were overly salted as well. It seems that the cook on duty that night may have been too heavy-handed with the salt. As for my flank steak, it was just average and I would not choose it again in the future. On a positive note, our cocktails were delicious and the ambiance of the restaurant was pleasant. However, overall, we were greatly disappointed with the quality of the food.

input: I love going to Phillies games sooo much and this stadium definitely adds to the experience. I was never a big baseball fan until about a couple of years ago, when my bf introduced me to the wonder that is the Phils- instant love. Sure,my first Phils game was the 10, 000 loss but whatever. The places has a open feeling, and never feels clausterphobic. The only time i've felt that I had bad seats was when we sat right under neath the scoreboard, and I had to keep on looking up.  I like how you can wander about and watch the game from the lower levels, and that despite it's a sold out game, it never feels cramped or you're really aching to get around the stadium. They have a lot of great food (lots of variety) and the facilities are always clean- both are numerous, so I'm never waiting in line.  I am missing baseball season and I cannot wait until April! Go Phillies!
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore going to Phillies games, and the stadium itself truly enhances the whole experience. Although I wasn't initially a huge baseball fan, my perspective completely changed a couple of years ago when my boyfriend introduced me to the magic of the Phils – it was love at first game. Even though my first Phils game was during the 10,000th loss, that didn't diminish my enthusiasm one bit. The stadium has such an open atmosphere, never making me feel claustrophobic. The only time I had less than ideal seats was when we were situated right beneath the scoreboard, requiring me to constantly look up. However, I appreciate the option to wander around and catch glimpses of the game from the lower levels. Even during sold-out games, it never feels overcrowded or impossible to navigate through the stadium. The wide variety of delicious food options and the cleanliness of the facilities only enhance the overall experience. With numerous food stands and restrooms available, I never have to wait in line. I am eagerly awaiting the start of baseball season in April – I miss it dearly! Go Phillies!

input: My boyfriend and I decided to stop by for lunch yesterday, and I am so glad we did. I ordered a side of beans, chips and salsa, and guacamole. He ordered two steak tacos and a side of rice. The beans are hands down my favorite I've had from a mexican restaurant.  My only complaint is that, unfortunately you do not get a very big portion. The salsa is so fresh tasting and delicious-very cilantro forward, and the chips were nice, thick and crunchy without being oily at all. Take note though, chips and salsa are not included with your purchase and must be bought separately. Now let me get to the best part-the made to order, chunky guacamole. The hardy chips would definitely withstand this heavy duty guac, but I opted instead for tortillas as my vessel to stuff it with along with my beans and salsa. The hot sauces were anything but, though admittedly my tolerance to spices may be higher than the average persons. While I had a great eating experience, my boyfriend did not. He said the meat was of low quality and quite flavorless. He did say he would give it another shot though!
Refine this for me please: Yesterday, my boyfriend and I decided to have lunch at a Mexican restaurant, and I'm thrilled that we did. For my meal, I ordered a side of beans, along with chips and salsa, and guacamole. Meanwhile, my boyfriend opted for two steak tacos and a side of rice. Without a doubt, the beans were the best I've ever had at a Mexican restaurant. However, my only complaint is that the portion size was disappointingly small. On the other hand, the salsa was incredibly fresh and delicious, with a prominent cilantro flavor. The chips were equally impressive, being thick, crunchy, and not at all greasy. It's worth noting that chips and salsa are not included with your purchase; they have to be purchased separately. Now, here's the best part: the made-to-order, chunky guacamole. The sturdy chips could definitely handle its heaviness, but I decided to go with tortillas to stuff it with, along with my beans and salsa. As for the hot sauces, they weren't really "hot," but this could be because I have a higher tolerance for spices compared to others. While I thoroughly enjoyed my meal, my boyfriend didn't have the same experience. He found the meat to be of low quality and lacking in flavor. However, he did mention that he would be willing to give the restaurant another chance.

input: I love this place. It's been in La Cumbre Plaza for I don't know how long now. If you are looking for a good sandwich look no further. All of the ingredients taste fresh, and their bread rolls are amazing. They are nice and soft, not with that cut the roof of your mouth crust. Being born and raise in Santa Barbara, actually just down the street, I have been coming here for some years now. I've tried probably over half of their sandwiches and all have been good, so good it's hard to pick a favorite.  In addition, I cannot forget to mention their awesome soda selection, so awesome I cannot hesitate to try something different with every visit. You won't find anything super fancy or exotic, like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich here, but if you're a local or just passing through and feel like having a great sandwich with good fresh ingredients swing by Plaza Deli and grab a bite.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore this place located in La Cumbre Plaza. Its enduring presence in the neighborhood has always amazed me. If you're on the hunt for a superb sandwich, look no further. The freshness of all the ingredients is remarkable, and their bread rolls are simply divine. They are wonderfully tender, unlike those crusty ones that might scrape the roof of your mouth. Having grown up in Santa Barbara, just a stone's throw away, I have been a loyal customer for years now. I've had the pleasure of trying more than half of their sandwich offerings, and each one has been consistently exceptional. It's nearly impossible for me to choose a favorite because they are all that good. I must also mention their impressive soda selection, which never fails to impress me. The variety is so extensive that I always feel compelled to try something new with every visit. While you won't find any overly fancy or exotic options like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich here, if you're a local or simply passing through and crave a phenomenal sandwich made with fresh, quality ingredients, make sure to swing by Plaza Deli for an unforgettable dining experience.

input: I think this Nordstrom's shoe department is better than other locations.  There was a lot of variety and they carry some higher end lines here.  The sales professionals were very good.  A gentleman named Erwin helped me locate two pairs of shoes throughout the Nordstrom's network AND price matched them to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price.  And no charge for shipping and handling.  Nordstrom's has won my loyalty due to the very high level of customer service!
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend the shoe department at Nordstrom's. Compared to other locations, it truly stands out. The wide range of options available, including some high-end lines, is impressive. The sales professionals are exceptional, and I had the pleasure of being assisted by Erwin. He went above and beyond to help me find two pairs of shoes by searching throughout the Nordstrom's network. Not only did he locate the shoes, but he also ensured that they were price matched to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price. Additionally, I was pleasantly surprised that there were no charges for shipping and handling. The outstanding level of customer service I experienced has solidified my loyalty to Nordstrom's.

input: A small aquarium that is interesting mainly for kids.  They have a shark feeding show and stingrays that you can pet and buy food to feed.  It is not the first place i would go in Tarpon Springa, but it is ok, small children seem to like it.
Refine this for me please: A fascinating and interactive small aquarium perfect for kids! Here, you'll find an exciting shark feeding show and an opportunity to pet stingrays while you also have the option to buy food and feed them. While it may not be the top attraction in Tarpon Springs, it still offers a fun time for young children who seem to thoroughly enjoy their visit.

input: Nothing extraordinary, but if you want some simple Chinese takeout, this is the best place around. The food seems less greasy than you sometimes find and the people are super nice.
Refine this for me please: If you're looking for a no-frills Chinese takeout spot, this is the top choice in the area. The food stands out for its relatively low grease content compared to other places, while the staff is exceptionally friendly.

input: Quaint place with great ambience, food and service. I had the Shrimp Po Boy. It was delicious. The fries and cole slaw were perfect side dishes. This was my first visit. Definitely not my last.
Refine this for me please: This charming establishment offers a delightful ambiance, exceptional cuisine, and impeccable service. During my visit, I had the pleasure of savoring the delicious Shrimp Po Boy, which exceeded my expectations. Accompanied by perfectly cooked fries and refreshing cole slaw, the meal was a true delight. This initial experience left a lasting impression, ensuring that it will not be my last visit to this extraordinary place.

input: Broussard's was pretty good when I went there a few weeks ago. I had a Groupon that was about to expire so I took my parents out to dinner.  I knew going in that Broussards is a very old skool New Orleans restaurant, and it is very nice when you walk in to see the old tile on the walls in the foyer of the building. The courtyard is beautiful and I just had to turn into a tourist and take a picture in front of the fountain with my mom. We were seated and very promptly greeted by the drink guy.  He brought us our water and told us about the extensive wine list, but they were of course out of the Pinot Grigio that I ordered.  He successfully suggested a Chardonnay for me instead and I was happy. The head waiter came out and explained with great detail the specials for the night, but I went for menu regulars, the maytag blue cheese salad and the pecan crusted drum. I wanted more salad, it was so good, I ate it up so fast. The drum was excellent too. It had this soy butter sauce on it that was so good and topped with crawfish. I was definitely happy with my meal and glad I had the experience. What makes me knock off two stars is that though the foyer's vintage appeal is nice and the courtyard is beautiful, I feel like the dining room needs an upgrade.  The chandeliers on the walls in the main dining room are very reminiscent of the hallways of my grandmother's assisted living home. I think its just one of those places I am glad to say I've been to, but I don't think I will choose to go there again.
Refine this for me please:
Broussard's provided a pleasant dining experience for me a few weeks ago. I had a Groupon that was close to expiring, so I decided to take my parents out for dinner. As a well-established New Orleans restaurant, Broussard's exuded charm and history as soon as we entered the building. The beautiful old tile on the walls in the foyer added to the ambiance. We couldn't resist capturing a touristy moment by taking a photo in front of the fountain in the courtyard with my mom.

Once seated, we were quickly attended to by the drink server who brought us water and informed us about their extensive wine list. Unfortunately, they were out of the Pinot Grigio I initially requested, but the server made a successful suggestion of a Chardonnay as a substitute, which made me happy. The head waiter then arrived, providing us with detailed explanations of the specials for the evening. However, I opted for their regular menu items: the Maytag blue cheese salad and the pecan-crusted drum. The salad was so delicious that I finished it quickly, and the drum was equally outstanding with its soy butter sauce and crawfish topping. Overall, I was pleased with my meal and grateful for the experience.

However, I deducted two stars from my review due to the outdated appearance of the dining room. While the vintage appeal of the foyer and the beauty of the courtyard were impressive, the main dining area could benefit from an upgrade. The chandeliers on the walls reminded me of the hallways in my grandmother's assisted living home. Broussard's is a place I am glad to have experienced, but I don't think I will personally choose to dine there again.

input:
Service is excellent. Atmosphere is great. The raw bar was fantastic. Those were the best Alaskan crab legs I've had. Well worth splurging for them. 

My friends were drawn in by the awesome looking burger they had, and indeed the burgers were all they hoped for. It came with a generous portion of crispy fries. But if you want anything else besides the $17 burgers, expect to spend over $30 for your entree. While the ambience feels and looks casual, it is fine dining.

Unfortunately, the waiter did sell the shrimp and grits with the additional crab as "heaven in his mouth", but that it was not. I've had better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and there is no reasonable way you should be paying $30 for shrimp and GRITS. Without the crab, it was still over $20.

But everything else was great. Drinks were delicious. Everything came out pretty quickly. Oh, when we mentioned we were visiting from out of town, the waiter was nice enough to give us a complimentary appetizer of the cool pizza to start. It was great but the name is hard to say or remember. And the rabbit and chicken liver pate was super worth since it comes in a huge mason jar.

I recommend sticking to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers and you'll be a pretty happy camper.
Refine this for me please:
The service at this restaurant is excellent and the atmosphere is great. We had a fantastic experience at the raw bar, especially with the Alaskan crab legs - they were the best I've ever had and definitely worth splurging on. My friends were lured in by the delicious-looking burgers, and they were not disappointed. The burgers came with a generous portion of crispy fries. However, be aware that if you want something other than the $17 burgers, you should expect to spend over $30 for your entree. Although the ambience may seem casual, the overall experience is that of fine dining.

Unfortunately, the shrimp and grits dish that the waiter raved about fell short of our expectations. I have had better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and it is unjustifiable to pay $30 for this dish, even with the addition of crab. Without the crab, it still cost over $20.

Despite this, everything else was great. The drinks were delicious and all of our meals arrived promptly. As a bonus, when we mentioned that we were visiting from out of town, the waiter kindly offered us a complimentary appetizer - a cool pizza. It was tasty, although its name was difficult to pronounce or remember. Additionally, I highly recommend trying the rabbit and chicken liver pate, as it comes in a huge mason jar and is worth the price.

To have a satisfying dining experience, I suggest sticking to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers.

input: I love Doan's. It's the kind of place you have a "usual" and every time you have it, it's just as good as the last time. They staff is friendly and speedy so if you don't have a long lunch it's a great place to go.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore Doan's. It's the kind of establishment where you can establish your own customary order, and each visit is consistently delightful. The staff here is exceptionally amiable and prompt, making it an ideal spot when you're pressed for time during lunch.

input: This amazing brick oven pizza joint gets better every time I go. The last I time I went I got a Rotolo and a prosciutto pizza. The Rotolo is dough wrapped around mortadella and ricotta cheese and topped with pistachios and oil. It is so good. I order it every time. It's about the size of a bun and cost $5. The pizza was amazing. The prosciutto was incredibly tasty. The dough is divine. The service is always great and the beer selection is good. Definitely one of the best pizza places in Philly.
Refine this for me please:
This exceptional brick oven pizza joint never fails to impress me with each visit. During my last visit, I ordered a delicious Rotolo and a mouth-watering prosciutto pizza. The Rotolo consists of dough wrapped around a delectable combination of mortadella and ricotta cheese, generously topped with pistachios and oil. It has become my go-to choice every time I visit, and priced at just $5, it is not only affordable but also satisfyingly sized, similar to a bun.

The pizza itself was extraordinary, with the prosciutto adding an incredibly tasty touch to the overall flavor. The dough deserves special mention as it is simply divine – perfectly cooked and irresistibly delicious. Moreover, the service at this place is consistently great, with a good selection of beers to complement the pizza. Without a doubt, it ranks among the best pizza establishments in Philly.

input:
Amazing pizza. AMAZING! After my first bite, I felt like that Oprah Winfrey meme, where her head is thrown back, her mouth is agape and her arms are open wide, and she's screaming, "You get a car!" Except it's not Oprah, it's me. And I don't get a car -- I get a pizza. But I felt that excited.  

This is basically the pizza I have been looking for since moving to the Indianapolis area. It's a whole lot of nothing: It's not cut into square pieces. It's not crispy and thin. It's not redolent of oregano. It's thick and chewy, cheesy, greasy, wonderful -- it tastes the way pizza is supposed to taste! I have found my new pizza home.
Refine this for me please: Incredible pizza. INCREDIBLE! With just one mouthful, I experienced the exact feeling depicted in the Oprah Winfrey meme: my head thrown back, mouth agape, arms wide open, and a scream of pure ecstasy — "You get a car!" Although I'm not Oprah, my excitement matched hers, just replace the car with a mouthwatering pizza. It was a sensation I've longed for since relocating to Indianapolis. This pizza is everything I've been searching for. It's unlike anything else: not sliced into squares, lacks the crispness and thinness, and doesn't overpower with oregano; instead, it boasts a satisfying thickness and chewiness, abundant cheese, and delightful grease. It embodies the perfect essence of pizza! I can confidently declare that I've discovered my new pizza haven.

input: Waited 27 minutes for three teas (no one else was in the store when we came in and ordered). NO tea is worth that long of a wait, especially in Chinatown.
Refine this for me please: We had to wait for a total of 27 minutes to receive three teas, even though there were no other customers in the store when we placed our orders. The waiting time was exceptionally long, especially considering that we were in Chinatown where prompt service is typically expected. In my opinion, no tea is worth such a lengthy wait.

input:
I grew up eating beef sandwiches in Chicago, and this place makes the best beef I've ever had outside of the city. 

Couple of suggestions: Offer a third sandwich size option (bigger!), get sweet peppers, serve fries(!!!), keep the main location off of Mass Ave open year-round, and have longer hours!
Refine this for me please:
During my upbringing in Chicago, beef sandwiches were a staple in my diet. Having tried various places across different locations, I can confidently say that this establishment serves the most exceptional beef I have ever tasted outside the city.

To enhance the dining experience further, I have a few suggestions. Firstly, consider offering a third sandwich size option, catering to those who have a hearty appetite. Additionally, incorporating sweet peppers as a topping would provide a delightful flavor contrast to the beef.

Furthermore, the addition of fries to the menu would undoubtedly be a welcomed accompaniment and add to the overall satisfaction of the meal.

To cater to a larger customer base, I recommend maintaining the main location off of Mass Ave open year-round. This would ensure that patrons can enjoy the exceptional beef sandwiches regardless of the season.

Lastly, extending the business hours would be greatly appreciated by customers who may wish to indulge in their extraordinary sandwiches later in the day or evening.

Implementing these suggestions would undoubtedly elevate the dining experience and solidify this establishment as a must-visit destination for beef sandwich enthusiasts.

input:
We came here for an early mothers day celebration as we were on the quest to find a nail salon that could accommodate 4 pedicures at the same time. They were very friendly and even though they didn't have 4 pedicurists on the schedule that day they added one to accommodate us. That was really nice of them as they could have easily told us no. 

The place itself is decorated very modern and offers a very clean, minimalist atmosphere. Upon walking in we were immediately greeted and after we checked in with the front desk we were asked what we wanted to drink. They had complimentary mimosas, wine and champagne, the perfect way to begin to unwind. Once we picked out our polish colors we were well on our way to getting our pedicures. Everyone was so nice and made us feel comfortable and welcomed. My polish never chipped the whole time I had it on. I will definitely be back. 

The only downside is that its street parking only, which isn't something that they can control. They told us most of their business comes from people who work in the CBD so parking probably isn't an issue for their regular customers. Aside from parking being an issue I would definitely go to Buff again.
Refine this for me please:
We visited this nail salon for an early Mother's Day celebration with the goal of finding a place that could accommodate four pedicures simultaneously. Despite not having four pedicurists scheduled that day, the staff went above and beyond by adding an additional one to accommodate us. Their generosity was greatly appreciated, as they could have easily turned us away.

The salon itself boasts a modern decor and offers a clean, minimalist atmosphere. Upon entering, we were promptly greeted and, after checking in at the front desk, offered a choice of beverages. Their complimentary mimosas, wine, and champagne were the perfect way to kickstart our relaxation. Once we had selected our polish colors, we began our pedicures. The staff were extremely friendly, making us feel comfortable and welcomed throughout the experience. I was particularly impressed that the polish on my toenails did not chip the entire time I had it on. I will definitely be returning to this salon in the future.

The only drawback I noticed was that the salon only offers street parking, which is beyond their control. However, they informed us that most of their regular customers are individuals who work in the CBD, so parking is likely not an issue for them. Despite the parking inconvenience, I would highly recommend giving Buff a try.

input: Great spot for pho! Broth is very good. I ordered No. 51 (small) and it was filling. Would definitely come back again when I'm in Philly.
Refine this for me please: This place is a fantastic spot to have pho! The broth is truly exceptional. I opted for the No. 51 in a small size, and it was surprisingly satisfying. I will definitely make a point to return whenever I find myself in Philly again.

input:
I love the concept of this place. One half of it a café that serves different types of coffees and teas, and breakfast type items, and the other world where it serves bar type apps, salads, and sandwiches,  Can't forget that they also serve a wide variety of beers that they serve on tap, bottled, or in can.  

This place is pretty darn casual, and one can hang out here for hours with their friends.  Reminds me of the good ol' college days when no time could pass especially on a chill out Sunday Fun day.

Bring your four legged friend too.  They are totally welcome.
Refine this for me please:
I absolutely adore the concept of this place. It's divided into two halves - a delightful café serving an array of coffees, teas, and delectable breakfast items, and a captivating world where they serve bar-style appetizers, fresh salads, and mouthwatering sandwiches. To top it off, they offer an extensive selection of beers, available on tap, bottled, or in cans.

The atmosphere is incredibly laid-back, making it the perfect spot to spend quality time with friends for hours on end. It evokes nostalgic memories of carefree college days, particularly on relaxing Sunday fundays.

Additionally, don't forget to bring along your furry companion, as this place warmly welcomes four-legged friends.

input: My husband reserved a Corolla-sized car over the internet ten days ahead of time. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car at the Reno airport I asked if the rental could be upgraded to a Camry-size vehicle. They offered us two different kinds of cars and finally we got the Camry we wanted. The man was very professional and in the end told us the rental would be $800.00 for five days. I felt the price was very high, however we had gone through most of the paperwork. I had already selected to get the $25.00 a day insurance which came to $150.00 with tax. We were very happy with the car and had no problems with it. During our vacation I decided to talk to an Avis representative when we dropped the car off. I asked her if a weekly rate would be less expensive. She said it would be $15.00 more. She said the upgrade cost an extra $20.00 a day. I will not rent from Avis any more. Next time I will go to Hertz or Dollar and make the reservation over the phone. Looking back, i would not have gotten the extra insurance. My personal insurance covers everything.
Refine this for me please:
My husband had made an online reservation for a Corolla-sized car ten days in advance. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car at the Reno airport, I requested an upgrade to a Camry-size vehicle. After considering two different options, we were finally given the Camry that we desired. The staff member assisting us was extremely professional and informed us that the rental would cost $800.00 for a five-day period. Although I found this price to be quite high, we had already completed most of the paperwork. Additionally, I had already opted for the $25.00 per day insurance, bringing the total cost of insurance to $150.00 including taxes. Despite the expensive rate, we were pleased with the car and encountered no issues during our vacation.

During our trip, I decided to inquire about the possibility of a weekly rental discount when returning the car. To my surprise, the Avis representative informed me that it would actually be $15.00 more expensive. Additionally, she explained that the upgrade itself incurred an extra charge of $20.00 per day. Disappointed by these revelations, I have decided not to rent from Avis in the future. Instead, I plan to make reservations over the phone with Hertz or Dollar. Reflecting on the experience, I realize that I would not have needed the additional insurance as my personal coverage already provides comprehensive protection.

input: Great customer service! Love my new car! Highly recommend to anyone who's trying to buy a new used car in good shape! Talk to Andy if you want some good help!
Refine this for me please: Exceptional customer service! Absolutely thrilled with my recent car purchase! I highly recommend this dealership to anyone in search of a well-maintained, pre-owned vehicle. For knowledgeable assistance, be sure to reach out to Andy!

input: After moving to the area, Jungle Prada Tavern was one of the first places a friend took me.  The bartender made a great recommendation based on a beer I told her I liked and I loved it!  Now for the food- I LOVE seafood, so I am leary of ordering from places that don't do it justice, but alas, they impressed me thoroughly with all the seafood options I chose!!  The scallops prosciutto app, del mar pizza with crab and scallops, and crab stuffed portabella app (comes with a crab and lobster bisque- YUM) are all delicious!!  I also love the roasted portabella app- for a vegetarian option, it is delicious and was recomended by someone who isn't. I've actually gone back several times since then just to eat (obviously, I also drank ;) and took my sister when she was in town visiting (and is a seafood fanatic).  So all in all, give this place a chance!!  You will not be disappointed with the options!
Refine this for me please: After recently relocating to the area, I was introduced to Jungle Prada Tavern by a friend. The first time I visited, the bartender impressed me with a fantastic recommendation based on my beer preference, which I thoroughly enjoyed. As a seafood lover, I typically approach ordering seafood from new places with caution, as some fail to meet my standards. However, Jungle Prada Tavern exceeded my expectations with their exceptional array of seafood options. The scallops prosciutto appetizer, the del mar pizza with crab and scallops, and the delectable crab stuffed portabella appetizer (served with a delightful crab and lobster bisque) all left a lasting impression on my taste buds. Additionally, their roasted portabella appetizer, recommended by a non-vegetarian, turned out to be an exceptional vegetarian option that I truly enjoyed. Since my initial visit, I have returned multiple times solely for their scrumptious food (and, of course, to indulge in their beverages). I even took my seafood-loving sister, who was visiting from out of town, to experience the delights of Jungle Prada Tavern. Trust me, you won't be disappointed with the variety of options available at this establishment. Give it a chance and prepare to be impressed!

input: This is one of my favorite bead stores in Nashville, walls and walls of seed beads and glass strands!
Refine this for me please: This is my absolute favorite bead store in Nashville, boasting an impressive collection of seed beads and glass strands that span across wall after wall!

input: Went here for dinner on opening day and was SO HAPPY I DID!! Great atmosphere, lovely staff, and food on fleek!! Green tea (PHO PHREE) was so satisfying, summer rolls and spicy peanut sauce were DELISH, and pho was PHONOMENAL! Definitely making this one of my regular hot spotz as I eat my way through Fairmount!
Refine this for me please: I visited this restaurant for dinner on their opening day and I couldn't have been happier that I did! The atmosphere was great, the staff was lovely, and the food was absolutely amazing. I highly recommend trying their green tea (PHO PHREE) - it was so satisfying. The summer rolls with spicy peanut sauce were incredibly tasty, and the pho was simply phenomenal. I will definitely be making this restaurant one of my regular spots as I continue to explore the culinary delights of Fairmount!

input:
Don't let the outside fool ya or even the initial impression when you walk in because they food here is really good! When ya walk in this place it's like stepping back into the 1950's.  It's kinda awesome.  Definitely a small-town, homey feel that serves good ole family cookin'.  They had a iceskates up on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner.  How precious.   
Don't come here expecting the best food in the whole wide world.  It is great for grandma's greasy cooking.  I've only eaten breakfast here but it's been amazing everytime.  I got pancakes and they are so fluffy and light and awesome (esp if you add a little butter).  The bacon was nice, thick, large slices; slightly overcooked maybe but super good cuz I love bacon! :)
The prices are reasonable and the service is great.  This is a great place for a quick delicious home cooked breakfast!
Refine this for me please:
Please disregard the unassuming exterior and initial impressions upon entering, as the quality of the food here is exceptional. Stepping into this establishment is like traveling back to the nostalgic ambiance of the 1950s, which is rather delightful. It undeniably emanates a charming small-town atmosphere that offers delicious, genuine, homemade meals. Decorations such as iceskates displayed on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner add a touch of endearing charm.

It is essential to have realistic expectations when visiting this place; while it may not offer the pinnacle of culinary excellence, it excels in delivering remarkable comfort food akin to one's grandmother's greasy home cooking. Although I have solely indulged in their breakfast offerings, each experience has been consistently outstanding.

The pancakes, in particular, are exceptionally fluffy, light, and delightful, especially when accompanied by a small amount of butter. The bacon slices are nicely thick and sizeable, albeit slightly overcooked, which does not detract from their irresistible taste given my fondness for bacon.

The prices are reasonable, and the service is exceptional. This is an ideal establishment to enjoy a quick, scrumptious, home-cooked breakfast.

input: Tried this place out after many suggestions from friends.  We went in one night about an hour or so before closing just to find that they were only serving a partial menu - we're not talking that late, it was like, 9:30 on a weekend.  There was no mention of going down to a bar menu on the website so I was a bit annoyed by that.  Something about 'surprise disappointments that could be totally avoided' really bother me.  So, the dish I had picked out online wasn't available and I ordered a burger instead.  The server seemed to have a very hard time understanding my burger and suggested that modifications couldn't be made?  I told him I'm sure removing a single topping wouldn't cause the kitchen staff any issues...  The rest of the meal we were generally ignored and the service wasn't great.  I found the food to be overpriced for the quality.  Unless there is a special reason to attend, I don't think we'll be going back.
Refine this for me please:
After receiving multiple recommendations from friends, I decided to try out this place. Unfortunately, when we arrived one night about an hour before closing time, we were disappointed to learn that they were only serving a partial menu. It was quite early, around 9:30 on a weekend, so this was unexpected and not mentioned on their website. I found this lack of communication to be quite bothersome, as such surprises can easily be avoided. 

Since the dish I had initially chosen was unavailable, I settled for a burger instead. However, the server had difficulty grasping my modifications request and claimed that no changes could be made. I politely explained that removing a single topping should not pose any issues for the kitchen staff.
