Let's discuss the broth now. While flavorful, the red chili broth was a bit too spicy for my taste and ended up overpowering the overall depth of the broth. Personally, I prefer the black garlic tonkotsu broth for its more balanced flavors.

In general, the food was delicious and reasonably priced. Additionally, the decor of the restaurant was very pleasing. However, the presence of loud and unruly children running around took away from the overall pleasantness of our dining experience.

input: Hands down best breakfast in Philly!  I've only been here for four months, but I have tried nearly every "Best of" spot in town.  I'm a breakfast fanatic so I get little over critical.  However, this small cafe has managed to create incredible flavor while keeping their dishes fresh and simplistic.  While the actual space is "cozy," this menu could easily keep a place as big as Parc overflowing with patrons.
Refine this for me please: Without a doubt, this small cafe in Philly serves the best breakfast in town! Despite having only lived here for four months, I have explored numerous acclaimed breakfast spots. As a self-proclaimed breakfast fanatic, I tend to be overly critical, but this cafe has surpassed all expectations. Their menu is simple yet bursting with amazing flavors, maintaining a refreshing and delightful taste. Although the cafe itself is cozy, its incredible menu could easily attract crowds comparable to the popular Parc.

input: If I could give this place 6 stars I would. Don't let the looks deceive you, great diner food. Biscuits and gravy were incredible. Portions were more than I could eat.
Refine this for me please: This place deserves 6 stars in my book. Despite its modest appearance, the diner serves fantastic food. The biscuits and gravy were absolutely incredible, and the portion sizes were so generous that I couldn't finish everything.

input:
This place is hip.  Perhaps too hip for many over 35 but if you can tolerate the boisterous and extremely casually attired youth--I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either but even 20 year olds should have something besides skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline obscene slogans in their closets--the food is worth it and the staff copes well.   

I had a 6:00 reservation (obtained the day before) but the sky seemed threatening a downpour so I came early to avoid it and was seated 20 minutes or so before the appointed time.  I often don't even make reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by being there when they open or, for those open all day, coming before the popular dinner hour, but that didn't work the day before at Lüke.  Even at 4:30 the place was packed so I did make one for the following day.

My meal started with the crispy Brussel Sprouts.  Even if you hate Brussels sprouts (I like them), don't be afraid to try this dish--if no one told you you might not know what you were eating.  They are in some sort of sweet/sour sauce/dressing and fried both slightly blackened and crispy as advertised . . . tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Then I had pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (that's shoestring fries to the Galliphobes).  It came with whitish gravy in a pitcher, I suppose to make it "Southern".  The gravy was good but I skipped eating it, doing that the usual way with a squeeze of lemon.  It was excellent and the fries were fine too.

I finished with some excellent decaf and a glass of Kahlua--I had had iced tea with the meal so some alcohol was not an excess.

A lady who was some sort of hostess dropped by my table while I was eating to make sure everything was OK and when told I needed ketchup (for the fries), went and got me some (in a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle).  My waiter also checked several times but didn't hover.

I am giving it 4 stars.  The 5th star is withheld because of the crowded dining room and noise level . . . nothing to do with the food which I greatly enjoyed.
Refine this for me please:
This place is trendy, perhaps too trendy for many over 35. However, if you can tolerate the loud and very casually dressed young crowd (I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either, but even 20 year olds should have something besides skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline obscene slogans in their closets), the food is worth it and the staff handles the chaos well.

I had made a 6:00 reservation (obtained the day before), but because the sky looked threatening a downpour, I arrived early to avoid it. Thankfully, I was seated about 20 minutes before my reservation time. Usually, I don't bother making reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by arriving when they open or coming before the popular dinner hour. However, that didn't work the day before at Lüke. Even at 4:30, the place was packed, so I made a reservation for the following day.

My meal began with the crispy Brussels Sprouts. Even if you dislike Brussels sprouts (I happen to like them), don't hesitate to try this dish. If no one told you, you might not even know what you were eating. The sprouts are coated in a sweet and sour sauce/dressing and fried until slightly blackened and crispy, as advertised. They are tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño, and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Next, I ordered the pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (shoestring fries for those who aren't familiar). It was served with a whitish gravy in a pitcher, presumably to give it a "Southern" touch. The gravy was good, but I personally skipped eating it and instead squeezed some lemon juice over the schnitzel, which was excellent. The fries were also satisfactory.

To finish off the meal, I had some excellent decaf coffee and a glass of Kahlua. Since I had iced tea during the meal, I didn't see having a bit of alcohol as excessive.

While I was eating, a lady who appeared to be a hostess stopped by my table to ensure everything was alright. When I mentioned that I needed ketchup for the fries, she promptly brought me a dainty little single-serve bottle of Heinz. My waiter also checked in on me several times without being too intrusive.

Overall, I would give this restaurant 4 stars. The fifth star is withheld due to the crowded dining room and high noise level. However, this has nothing to do with the exceptional food that I greatly enjoyed.

input: Beers were amazing! I got the porter, the double IPA and the table gutt and they were all fantastic. Food was also killer if you like Russian cuisine. They had a special when I went with a sausage and sauerkraut which was tasty. I also got the pickled everything appetizer, great choice. This place rules.
Refine this for me please: The beers at this place were absolutely incredible! I tried the porter, the double IPA, and the table gutt, and each one was fantastic. Furthermore, if you have a taste for Russian cuisine, you won't be disappointed by their food. During my visit, they had a special featuring a delicious sausage and sauerkraut dish that I really enjoyed. Additionally, I highly recommend trying their pickled everything appetizer, as it was an excellent choice. Overall, this place is undeniably amazing.

input: There are a ton of good sushi places in Reno and I have tried them all, but it always seems like Rickshaw has the freshest fish. I'm not a big fan of rolls and sauces, and opt mainly for Nigiri or sashimi. You can get some dressed up roll anywhere, hell you can buy them in the store, but if you are a true fan of sushi, just fish is where its at and Rickshaw has some of the freshest in town.
Refine this for me please: Reno boasts a multitude of exceptional sushi establishments, and having explored them extensively, I have personally found that Rickshaw stands out with its unparalleled freshness in fish. As someone who tends to steer clear of elaborate rolls and excessive sauces, favoring Nigiri and sashimi instead, I have often observed that many places offer dressed up rolls, which can even be purchased in stores. However, for sincere sushi aficionados who appreciate the true essence of sushi, the emphasis lies solely on the fish itself. In this regard, Rickshaw truly excels, consistently serving some of the freshest fish in town.

input: This was my 1st visit here.  Overall, not that impressed!  To start with parking was really bad!  There are good choices of beer on draft.  The food was ok.  We split a few appetizers.  The fried olives were very tasty & different!  The rest of the appetizers were ok: the blue cheese chips, calamari, & meat/cheese platter.  I would try this place again, but overall not thrilled!
Refine this for me please: This was my first visit to this place, and I have to say, I wasn't really impressed. The parking situation was really bad, which was a disappointing way to start. On a positive note, they did have a good selection of beers on draft. As for the food, it was just okay. We decided to split a few appetizers, and while the fried olives stood out as being tasty and unique, the rest were just average. The blue cheese chips, calamari, and meat/cheese platter were decent, but nothing exceptional. I might give this place another chance in the future, but overall, it didn't leave me feeling thrilled.

input: Really not sure what the hype was when it opened. It's fine, the ambiance was nice, but the menu is limited and food is nothing to write home about. They are in a nice location so at least if you decide to wait, then you have things to see...
Refine this for me please: I was quite underwhelmed by the hype surrounding its opening. While the ambiance was pleasant, the menu was disappointing in its limited offerings, and the food itself failed to impress. However, one redeeming factor is its favorable location, which at least provides distractions should you opt to wait.

input:
This place was amazing! I only tried their ice cream I really wanted to try the hot chocolate but didn't get a chance :(. Well the ice cream was great! The first night I came here I got a brownie sundae all for myself, brownie on the bottom and three scoops of ice cream topped with whipped cream and nuts. I finished it all happily! I chose pumpkin cake flavor which was delicious and smooth. I also got pralines and cream that was better than other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge was vanilla with fudge swirled it was good not too special. 

The next time I came I got nutter butter ice cream that was really good had cookie pieces in it! I got the hot fudge topping over it and that was a great combination. 

The service was great the workers were really nice and patient with me haha indecisive! They would joke around with me and let me sample all I wanted. Also no judgement for eating all the brownie sundae alone :) lol
Refine this for me please:
I had an incredible experience at this place! Although I regret not being able to try their hot chocolate, the ice cream itself was absolutely delicious. On my first visit, I treated myself to a delightful brownie sundae consisting of a brownie base topped with three scoops of ice cream, whipped cream, and nuts. I happily devoured every last bite! I opted for the pumpkin cake flavor, which was both scrumptious and velvety. Additionally, their pralines and cream flavor surpassed other interpretations of this classic. The Tennessee fudge variety, a combination of vanilla with fudge swirls, was good but not anything extraordinary.

During my subsequent visit, I indulged in the nutter butter ice cream, which was incredibly tasty with its generous cookie pieces. Adding the hot fudge topping was a brilliant decision, as the flavors complemented each other perfectly.

The service at this establishment was exceptional, with friendly and patient staff. They playfully engaged with me and willingly allowed me to sample as many flavors as I desired. Furthermore, they didn't pass any judgment when I devoured the entire brownie sundae by myself. It was a truly enjoyable experience!

input:
My dad and I were here for lunch and after reading some of the reviews, I was excited to check out this restaurant located where an O'Henry's once stood.

The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were lead upstairs. Honestly, there's not much going on up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stick it out. Everything on the menu looked great and I decided to get the Catfish Acadian, which is catfish topped with crawfish and sauce with a side of vegetables. My dad got the pork chop.

My dish was great! I have no idea what was in the sauce but it was delicious and it was a perfect pairing with the fish. The vegetables were also really good; they were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't overly blown away by his pork chop, so if you find yourself here you might want to stick to the seafood.

Bria was our waitress and she was wonderful! She was attentive, kept the fresh iced tea coming and she was extremely personable. She was probably the highlight of the visit.

I'm not sure if I would go back. The food was good, but the atmosphere left something to be desired and I feel like I can get good catfish at plenty of places without going out of my way. I might go back at dinner, when the weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony outside as Harry suggested.
Refine this for me please:
My dad and I visited this restaurant for lunch, intrigued by its location, once the site of an O'Henry's. Upon arriving, we found the place fairly empty at 1pm on a Friday and were directed upstairs. However, the upstairs seemed lackluster with minimal activity and a somewhat warm temperature. Despite this, we decided to stay and explore the menu options. Personally, I chose the Catfish Acadian, a dish consisting of catfish topped with crawfish and a delectable sauce, accompanied by a side of vegetables. Meanwhile, my dad opted for the pork chop.

Fortunately, my dish exceeded my expectations. The sauce, though its ingredients remain a mystery, was undeniably delicious and complemented the fish perfectly. The vegetables were also noteworthy, as they were skillfully prepared and served fresh. On the other hand, my dad found his pork chop to be underwhelming, leading me to believe that seafood options may be the restaurant's stronger suit.

Our waitress, Bria, deserves special recognition for her exceptional service. She was attentive, ensuring that our iced tea remained refilled and establishing a friendly, personable rapport. Undoubtedly, she was the highlight of our dining experience.

As for my overall thoughts on the restaurant, I am uncertain if I would return. The food was undeniably good, but the atmosphere left much to be desired. Considering the abundance of other places serving quality catfish, I question whether the effort to come here is worthwhile. However, I may consider giving it another chance for dinner, taking into account the suggestion made by Harry to sit on the cooler balcony outside.

input:
Well, well.... Where do I start with this place? First time experience, went in with my partner.

Walking in at about 7:30 on a Friday night (st paddys day weekend even)  and the  place had about 4 customers. That should have been my first clue as to what our experience was going to be like.

We seated ourselves and the waitress, an older gal maybe mid to late 40's who had greasy stringy unwashed hair and rotting teeth came up and took our drink order. My girlfriend got a Dr. Pepper and I got a water. She brought out Coke instead of DP. No biggie. We let it go, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes she returns and we order a 12 piece "jumbo" wing basket ($11.99), a 6 piece($7.99), and a beer batter sampler($11.99). 20 minutes pass and finally here comes our appetizer. The waitress throws the basket of appetizers on the table  and says "here's your food." Very flat with a big attitude and walks off. The beer battered mushrooms were doughy and undercooked. We had a single half full ranch cup to share between us for the big platter and she avoided our table when she saw we needed more.
***let me note that this waitress is giving the customers at the 3 tables surrounding us WAY better customer service. Even brought their food out in a timely manner with no attitude whatsoever.
I decide to let the mushrooms slide for the moment. I used to work in a restaurant and I understand that mistakes happen, however this far into the experience I'm being mighty generous since it's a first time experience.
We finish our appetizer and we wait and wait and wait and finally she comes by and takes the platter returning 10 minutes later with our wings. She makes no inquiry about the broken open, clearly undercooked, mushrooms still sitting on the platter.
I got the 12 piece with a single half full ranch. Again. Food on the table, doesn't ask if we need anything else which is something she is doing for other customers. at this point we have been here for about 40 minutes.

I got half regular and half thai flavor. The wings were NOT jumbo. They were puny. The flavor was good for the thai, and the waitress even stopped by to check up on us, though I wouldn't consider walking by quickly and saying in your flat attitude tone "youguysdoingalright?okaycool." Really all that helpful since she came and went so fast it took me a second to understand her. I had to reiterate for my girlfriend.  When I started on the regular I bit into my drumstick and had to fish a feather out of my mouth. DISGUSTING. It was that point that the entire experience was completely and thoroughly unacceptable.  The wings were soggy because they batter them or something on top of all that.  At first I had no plans other than to pay for the meal and leave the waitress 2 pennies and be on my merry way. But when the waitress came and asked if we needed a box I said no with 6 wings still on my plate, OBVIOUS SOMETHING WAS WRONG, again. She was going to take my stuff and make no inquiry to right the situation. I asked for the manager. Took a minute but finally the manager came over (mind you it is still pretty dead, what are these people doing I wonder?) I explained the food issues but blew off bringing up our treatment by the waitress. Normally I give the benefit of the doubt on this one but it was blatantly obvious that we were being treated differently with a different attitude than other patrons because we are a same-sex couple. Like our table had a contagious disease that prevented us from getting food in a timely manner, and getting drink and condiment refills too, regardless of the *empty* cups on the edge of the table. It wasn't like we were off in the distance. She had to walk by our table every time to communicate with the surrounding tables.

Anyways. The manager experience wasn't the greatest, but I wasn't going to pay for that meal after the feather thing, and she comped everything. BUT only after slightly arguing with us about the undercooked mushrooms, which by the way come frozen which  makes the fact that they weren't cooked all the way acceptable I guess? Don't know. Don't care. I WILL NOT BE GOING BACK!!!

2 stars because they did comp the meal, the waitress got lucky. If I would have had to pay for anything she wouldn't have gotten a tip due to the attitude but we left her $4 anyway since we didn't have to pay for the meal.  THAT IS THE ONLY REASON.
1 star though for the overall experience. Same-sex couples, steer clear. You aren't welcome there and it's obvious.
Refine this for me please:
Where do I even begin with this place? My partner and I went here for the first time and it was quite an experience.

We arrived at around 7:30 on a Friday night, which also happened to be St. Patrick's Day weekend, and the place was nearly empty with only about four customers. This should have been a sign of what was to come.

We found a table ourselves and a waitress in her mid to late 40s, with greasy stringy unwashed hair and rotting teeth, came over to take our drink order. My girlfriend ordered a Dr. Pepper but was given a Coke instead. We didn't make a fuss about it, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes, she returned to take our food order. We ordered a 12-piece "jumbo" wing basket for $11.99, a 6-piece for $7.99, and a beer batter sampler for $11.99.

After waiting for 20 minutes, our appetizer finally arrived. The waitress simply threw the basket of appetizers onto the table and said, "here's your food," with a rude attitude before walking away. The beer-battered mushrooms were doughy and undercooked, and we were only given a half-full ranch cup to share between us. When we tried to ask for more, she purposefully avoided our table.

It was clear that the customers at the other three tables surrounding us were receiving much better service. Even their food was served promptly and without any attitude from the waitress.

Despite these issues, we decided to let the undercooked mushrooms slide for the time being, understanding that mistakes can happen in a restaurant. However, as time went on, we became increasingly frustrated with the overall experience.

After we finished our appetizer, we waited and waited for our main wings to arrive. The waitress finally came by after what felt like an eternity, taking away the platter and returning 10 minutes later with the wings. She didn't even ask about the half-eaten and clearly undercooked mushrooms still on the platter.

Once again, I received a single half-full ranch cup for my 12-piece wings. The wings themselves were far from jumbo, more like puny. The Thai flavor was decent, and the waitress briefly checked up on us, although her rushed and uninterested manner made it difficult to understand her. When I bit into one of the regular wings, I discovered a feather in my mouth, which was absolutely disgusting. At that point, the entire experience became completely unacceptable.

The wings also tasted soggy, possibly because of the way they were prepared. Initially, I had planned to pay for the meal and leave the waitress a minimal tip, but when she asked if I wanted a box despite the obvious issues with the food, I requested to speak to the manager. After a short wait, the manager finally came over, though the interaction with them wasn't great either. I explained the food issues but chose not to bring up our treatment by the waitress, even though it was clear that we were being treated differently because we were a same-sex couple. It felt like she believed our table was contagious and needed to be avoided, even when it came to basic service, such as drink and condiment refills.

Ultimately, the manager decided to comp our entire meal, although there was some slight argument about the undercooked mushrooms. Apparently, the mushrooms come frozen, so the fact that they weren't cooked properly was somewhat acceptable, I suppose. I don't know, and I honestly don't care. What I do know is that I will never be going back to this place.

I'm giving it two stars because they did end up comping our meal, and the waitress got lucky with a $4 tip, even though she didn't deserve it due to her attitude. However, the overall experience warrants only one star. Same-sex couples should definitely steer clear of this place, as it is clear that they are not welcome and the discrimination is evident.

input: Why don't we have a Target?  I thought K-Mart was going out of business.  Well not this one, this miserable son of a bitch refuses to die.  They had the audacity to try to update it.  It reminds me of Jack Palance its old, tired, and smells funny, but it ain't going know where.    I wish a shiny new Target would come along and stab this relic of a store through the heart with its superior retail sword.  I have experienced on no less than 5 occasions of a product being labeled as on sale only to be charged full price at the counter.  Then I have to stop the line to back to the aisle and grab the sign to show it to the cashier.  Once I bought a beach chair here, well my wife saw the dopeness of said chair and wanted to copy me.  I return to the store the next day (happened to be 80 degrees and sunny) and those SOB's raised the price of the chair $10.  I was pissed yo.
Refine this for me please:
Why don't we have a Target nearby? I had heard that K-Mart was going out of business, but this particular store seems to be sticking around against all odds. They even attempted to update it, but it still feels old-fashioned and unappealing. It's like Jack Palance, worn out and giving off an unpleasant odor, but surprisingly resilient. I wish we had a shiny new Target that would come and put this ancient store out of its misery with its superior retail offerings. 

On multiple occasions, I've had the frustrating experience of finding a product labeled as on sale, only to be charged the full price at the checkout counter. It's incredibly inconvenient, as I have to halt the line, go back to the aisle, and retrieve the sign to prove the discounted price to the cashier. 

Another incident that angered me was when I purchased a beach chair here. My wife liked it so much that she wanted one too. When I returned to the store the next day (which happened to be a beautiful, sunny day), I discovered that those sneaky employees had raised the price of the chair by $10. This left me feeling furious and disappointed.

input:
Don't let the outside fool you-this place is much cuter and nicer inside than you would expect! 

Food is good and reasonably  priced. We ordered papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. Papaya salad is always refreshing, but this place overdoes it on the fish sauce. Anything triple flavor is always a safe but delicious choice. I would say their king soup, with choice of protein, is a winner. 

And also, BYO!
Refine this for me please: Don't be deceived by the exterior; this place is unexpectedly charming and inviting once you step inside. The food is both delicious and reasonably priced. We tried the papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. The papaya salad, although refreshing, was a bit heavy on the fish sauce. Anything labeled triple flavor on the menu is a reliable and enjoyable option. However, the real standout was their king soup, which allows you to choose your preferred protein. Don't forget, you can bring your own beverages!

input:
I feel so comfortable with the Mazzoni Center.  I, and many others, am incredibly lucky and grateful that these services exist.  Going through all sorts of life challenges can be painful and frightening when you know you're assumed to be a certain way.  Here, there are no assumptions.  They know who they're working with, and they are sensitive without the need to pry for information.  If you're in need of gynecology and you're not a woman, for example, they know exactly how to handle your needs while prioritizing respect for your identity.

My biggest concern is the physical space in which the Mazzoni Center clinic exists.  I feel sort of exposed in the waiting room.  I hope that they someday have the funds to upgrade to a larger, more private space.

If you visit during youth drop-in hours rather than making an appointment, you will probably wait a very long time to see someone.  This is completely understandable, in my opinion.  They'll advise you regarding what time you should show up if you call.

Occasionally, I've noticed lapses in communication; I have been kept waiting in the exam room before with no one around and no idea how much longer I would have to wait.  This is not a common issue, and I find that, overall, I receive more attentive service here than at any other clinic I've visited.

Be aware that the doctor you want to speak with may not always be available over the phone.  Don't be afraid to leave messages with reception.  You'll always receive quick assistance.
Refine this for me please:
I am incredibly fortunate and grateful to have the Mazzoni Center providing its services. During challenging times, it can be painful and daunting when society assumes we are a certain way. However, at the Mazzoni Center, there are no assumptions, and the staff is sensitive and respectful without prying for personal information. This inclusive approach extends even to non-traditional gynecology needs, such as those of individuals who do not identify as women.

One aspect that concerns me is the physical space of the Mazzoni Center clinic, particularly the waiting room. I often feel exposed there and hope that the center will eventually have the resources to upgrade to a larger and more private space.

If you choose to visit during youth drop-in hours instead of making an appointment, expect a potentially long wait time. However, this is understandable, and the center's staff can provide guidance on the best time to arrive if you call ahead.

On rare occasions, I've experienced lapses in communication, finding myself waiting alone in the exam room without any indication of when I would be attended to. Nonetheless, this is not a frequent issue. Overall, I receive attentive service at the Mazzoni Center, surpassing my experiences at other clinics.

Keep in mind that the specific doctor you want to speak with may not always be available over the phone. However, don't hesitate to leave a message with reception, as quick assistance is always provided.

input:
If I could give half a star I would, I'm from Tx, and anyone that thinks this is BBQ, I am willing to apologize to you for being led to believe that this is what BBQ is like.
I ordered the sample platter, horrific, the chicken looked and tasted like frozen pressed meat, the ribs.... All cartilage, the sausage, bland.... The sauce.... Walmart basic sauce with cups of sugar thrown in.... Extremely overpriced for ummm.... A child's plate (what it seemed like). I would never recommend this place to anyone.
Refine this for me please: I would not recommend this place even if I could give half a star. As a Texan, I feel compelled to apologize to anyone who was misled into thinking that this establishment serves authentic BBQ. My experience with the sample platter was horrendous. The chicken appeared and tasted like processed, frozen meat, while the ribs consisted mostly of cartilage. The sausage lacked flavor, and the sauce resembled a generic, store-bought variety with an excessive amount of sugar added. The prices were outrageously high for what felt like a child's portion. Overall, I am thoroughly disappointed and would not suggest this place to anyone.

input:
Really great place for wine!

Came here with my dining group, there was about 20 of us on a Friday, for their Happy Hour. Excellent wine happy hour where all glasses are $5 or you can take $5 off any bottle of wine, which is a great deal if you're sharing with a few people...great way to try a few bottles.

The food was also great! Cheese plates are the way to go here! Excellent selections! Several of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, which looked & smelled amazing! They all raved about them!

The ambiance is very warm and inviting! They do a great job decorating, especially around the holidays! My favorite space is the enclosed patio area, adjacent to the main dining area. Super warm and romantic on those cold winter evenings! 

The service is great as well!
Refine this for me please:
This place is a fantastic spot for wine! I recently visited with my dining group of about 20 people on a Friday and we had a wonderful time during their Happy Hour. The Happy Hour deal for wine is outstanding - all glasses are only $5 or you can enjoy a $5 discount on any bottle of wine. It's perfect if you're sharing with a few friends and want to experiment with multiple bottles.

The food at this place is also top-notch! I highly recommend their cheese plates, they offer an excellent selection. Some of my foodie friends opted for sandwiches, which not only looked amazing but smelled delicious too. They couldn't stop raving about them!

The ambiance of this place is incredibly cozy and inviting. The decorations, especially during the holidays, are done exceptionally well. My personal favorite area is the enclosed patio, right next to the main dining room. It creates a warm and romantic atmosphere, especially during those chilly winter evenings.

Lastly, the service here is excellent. The staff is attentive and friendly, ensuring that you have a great dining experience overall.

input: Rude staff. Can't even get a salad order right. Overpriced by the slice. When we sat down to wait for our food I thought wow this is taking a long time given the fact we were the only people in there. I guess it should stay that way. Don't waste your money.
Refine this for me please: The staff was extremely rude and they couldn't even manage to get a salad order correct. Additionally, the prices were excessively high for just a single slice. As we patiently sat down, we noticed that our food was taking an unusually long time to arrive despite being the only customers present. This experience truly reflected the overall poor quality of this establishment, so I would strongly advise against wasting your money here.

input: Really good, really authentic! This is some of the BEST Mexican cuisine I've tasted since my nana cooked for me; I'm from California so I would know. The enchiladas w/mole are awesome and the carne asada tacos remind me of Rosarito Beach, yummy!
Refine this for me please: This is an excellent and authentic Mexican cuisine that rivals even the exceptional flavors prepared by my nana back in California. The enchiladas with mole are simply outstanding, and the flavorful carne asada tacos take me back to the memories of indulging in them at Rosarito Beach. Absolutely delicious!

input:
You need a Cinnamon Roll from the bake house.  You probably need two; life would have just a little less happiness and light without their Cinnamon Rolls.
The coffee and salads are also excellent, a lovely Saturday morning breakfast treat.
Refine this for me please: Indulge yourself in the irresistible goodness of the Cinnamon Rolls at the bake house. In fact, I highly recommend getting two, as life would seem slightly duller and less enjoyable without these delectable treats. As an added bonus, the bake house also offers excellent coffee and salads, making it the perfect choice for a delightful Saturday morning breakfast.

input: I had the carrot cake.... Very disappointed tasted like licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's too bad because everything looks so delicious :( also didn't like the chocolate chips in it either.
Refine this for me please: I was extremely disappointed with the carrot cake I had because it tasted like a combination of licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's unfortunate because everything else looked so delicious. Additionally, I did not enjoy the presence of chocolate chips in the cake either.

input: You can't beat the prices for the unlimited food, but I've had better. The sushi is delicious, the salad was subpar and the crab Rangoon was probably the worst I've had. I've been twice and would definitely go again.
Refine this for me please: The prices for the unlimited food cannot be beaten, although I have experienced better quality. The sushi is delicious, while the salad falls a bit short, and the crab Rangoon was possibly the worst I've ever tasted. Despite this, I have visited twice and would still consider going again.

input: Best chicken you could ever hope for in bourbon st. The chicken is good. The sauce is good. Everything is goof
Refine this for me please: Experience the absolute pinnacle of chicken perfection on Bourbon Street. Prepare to embark on a culinary journey like no other as you indulge in the most delectable chicken dish known to humankind. The succulent tenderness of the chicken itself is unparalleled, complemented flawlessly by a sauce that will tantalize your taste buds and leave you craving for more. With every heavenly bite, you will be transported to a realm where everything is simply divine.

input:
Reviewing the food.
Hard to justify $16 for a burger and fries BUT wowow this burger was so delicious. I'm not sure if I was just starving but ordered the Lama burger and the patty size is quality. They also have random ingredients thrown in that you probably haven't seen before like gruyere stuffed in a pepper on your burger. Fries came out nice and crisp vs. soggy and the bun on that burger was great. You order inside by the Nook and then can sit around. They have tons of craft beer to choose from and I could see this place getting packed on the weekends.
Refine this for me please: Although the price of $16 for a burger and fries may seem steep, the taste of this particular burger makes it worth every penny. I ordered the Lama burger and was pleasantly surprised by the generous size of the patty. The addition of unique ingredients, such as gruyere stuffed in a pepper, adds a distinctive touch to the burger. The fries were perfectly crispy instead of soggy, and the bun complemented the burger well. The ordering process takes place inside the Nook, and there are ample seating options available. With an extensive selection of craft beer, it is likely that this place will be bustling on weekends.

input: Stopped in for breakfast on 12/2/17 I used to like it here for breakfast.  Service was slow coffee was not hot, grits were only warm and twenty minute wait for cinnamon biscuit after breakfast was brought to table then ten minutes to pay at counter to get out of the place there are better places to get breakfast in the area.  Should have went with my first choice instead of here.
Refine this for me please: I visited this restaurant for breakfast on 12/2/17, where I used to enjoy dining in the mornings. However, my recent experience was disappointing. The service was slow, and the coffee was not hot enough. Additionally, the grits served were only lukewarm. Moreover, it took a long twenty minutes to receive a cinnamon biscuit after my breakfast had already been brought to the table. Furthermore, when I finished my meal, I had to wait an additional ten minutes at the counter in order to pay and leave the establishment. In light of this experience, I believe there are better breakfast options available in the area. I regret not choosing my initial preferred restaurant instead of coming here.

input: simply the best! everything from here is good! I come from a very Italian family and whenever there is a family event, there is always Termini brothers dessert trays! Their cannolis are amazing! Highly recommend.
Refine this for me please: Simply the best! Everything here is excellent. Coming from a very Italian family, Termini Brothers dessert trays are always a staple at our family events. Their cannolis are absolutely amazing and I highly recommend them.

input: It's a nice place. Really nice! Great service and awesome restaurants in the hotel. Clean rooms
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely wonderful! The level of service provided is exceptional, and the range of dining options available within the hotel is simply awesome. On top of that, the rooms are impeccably clean.

input:
After our recent trip to New Orleans, I came back to Reno appreciating this place even more than before! 
The shrimp po boy is my favorite thing on the menu! And their corn bread is amazing as well!
Refine this for me please: Upon returning to Reno after our recent trip to New Orleans, I found a newfound appreciation for this place! The shrimp po boy, undoubtedly my favorite from the menu, never fails to impress. Moreover, their delectable cornbread is an absolute delight that cannot be missed!

input: People in this place are generally friendly, but do not make the mistake of going to Katie.  She went through my hair like a bulldozer-- slapped colour on it in less than 5 minutes and cut it in even less time.  I think she was in a rush to get out of there (it was late in the day), but then she shouldn't have agreed to take me on.  The whole thing cost me close to $200, and I was shaken up by the experience.
Refine this for me please: Overall, the people in this place are usually quite friendly, but I strongly advise against visiting Katie. My encounter with her was highly disappointing as she handled my hair carelessly, resembling a bulldozer rather than a skilled stylist. In a hasty fashion, she applied color to my hair in under 5 minutes and even spent less time cutting it. It was evident that she was in a rush to finish her work, possibly because it was late in the day. However, if she wasn't able to dedicate sufficient time to my appointment, she should not have accepted it in the first place. To make matters worse, this subpar experience cost me nearly $200, leaving me feeling unsettled and discontented.

input: Favorite place in Nashville for breakfast!! This is a must go to spot!! Near Vandy and always busy...park in the back lot and be sure to get the parking ticket from the machine so you won't be charged...its free parking for a specified amount of time. My favorite is banana pancakes...think banana bread only in a pancake!! Perfection!!!! I don't leave Nashville until I go here to eat my pancakes!
Refine this for me please: One of the best breakfast spots in Nashville, conveniently located near Vanderbilt University, is an absolute must-visit! Be prepared for a bustling atmosphere, as it's always busy. When you arrive, park in the back lot, and don't forget to grab a parking ticket from the machine to enjoy free parking for a certain duration. Now, let's talk about the food - my personal favorite is their delectable banana pancakes. Imagine the delightful flavors of banana bread infused into fluffy pancakes - it's sheer perfection! These pancakes are so irresistible that I simply cannot leave Nashville without indulging in them.

input:
Yes, there are vegan options in University City, you just have to know where to look for them. MexiCali has a number of great options.

Many options here can be made vegan by holding the cheese. I absolutely adore the marinated tofu burrito. The tofu has a wonderfully chewy texture, and along with the black beans, the meal packs a protein-filled punch that will leave you full well past dinner-time, should you choose to finish it.  The sweet potato and plantain burrito is purportedly dairy-free, and it's another delicious, filling vegan option. The veggie tacos come with a spicier version of the sweet potato, the marinated tofu and some cabbage on doubled corn tortillas. The tacos are not as filling as the burritos, but they're a delicious lighter option. Finally, a fourth option for vegans: the guacamole burrito. They homemade guac is to-die-for delicious. 

I end up at MexiCali about once a week. I've been going since they were just a lunch truck 8 years back. There's often a line at the restaurant, but this place has been around for years and they have a great system to get you your burrito in a very timely manner.
Refine this for me please:
Yes, there are vegan options available in University City if you know where to find them. MexiCali is a great choice with several delicious options to choose from.

One of my absolute favorites is the marinated tofu burrito, which is packed with protein from the tofu and black beans. The tofu has a satisfying chewy texture that I love, and this dish can definitely keep you satisfied past dinner-time if you can finish it. Another fantastic vegan option is the sweet potato and plantain burrito, known for being dairy-free and equally filling and flavorful. If you prefer something lighter, the veggie tacos are a great choice. They feature a spicier version of the sweet potato, marinated tofu, and cabbage, all served on doubled corn tortillas. While not as filling as the burritos, they are still incredibly delicious. Lastly, there's the guacamole burrito, a must-try for vegans. The homemade guacamole is absolutely delicious and makes this dish a winner.

Personally, I find myself visiting MexiCali at least once a week. I've been a loyal customer since their early days as a lunch truck, and I can vouch for their efficient system that ensures you get your burrito in a timely manner, despite occasional lines at the restaurant.

input:
Great breakfast fare and all. Eggs provençale was pretty good; all kinds of herbs and seasonings, but cooked inconsistently. Tomato on the side was awesome.

Omelets were executed well, and the pastries were pretty impressive.

But the coffee was horrendously bad. And without good coffee, what's the point of breakfast?

And I still can't trust restaurants that have misspellings on their menus. Even if the misspelling is from another language.
Refine this for me please:
The breakfast options were generally enjoyable. The Eggs provençale had a delightful mix of herbs and seasonings, although the preparation was inconsistent. The accompanying tomato was a standout.

The omelets were skillfully prepared, and the pastries left a favorable impression.

However, the coffee was disappointingly awful. It detracted from the overall breakfast experience.

In addition, I find it difficult to place my trust in restaurants that have misspellings on their menus, regardless of whether they are in another language.

input: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs.  I wouldn't call it a sports bar.  Nothing wrong with the place.  Cool location, good beer selection.  The food - delicious, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game.  Got the game.  The grub-- eclectic.  Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experience.  Don't go here if you want  a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.
Refine this for me please: Another Yelper gave an accurate description of this restaurant - it is noisy and crowded with big screen TVs, but I wouldn't necessarily classify it as a sports bar. However, there is nothing wrong with the place. It has a cool location with a good beer selection. The food is delicious, but it doesn't align with the typical pub grub you'd expect at a sports bar. My sons and I were looking to enjoy some pub grub while watching a hockey game, and while we did get to watch the game, the food options were more eclectic. This place is perfect if you're looking for a lively and energetic atmosphere with tasty and flavorful food, accompanied by thumping music. However, if you're in the mood for a simple burger, a beer, and the opportunity to engage in sports conversations while watching a hockey game, this may not be the ideal spot for you.

input: Fabulous, quick, stress free windshield repair. .. didnt cost a penny out of pocket. I would definitely use this company again and would recommend to anybody!!
Refine this for me please: Effortless and efficient windshield repair services that are truly outstanding, with zero out-of-pocket expenses. I am highly satisfied and impressed by this company and would undoubtedly utilize their services again and wholeheartedly recommend them to everyone.

input: I was so excited about this meal, I came home to review it immediately. The service was outstanding and the food I'd say was some of the best in New Orleans. Even the freshly made bread was piping hot and delicious. We started with the oysters good enough, which were four fried oysters with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon- a must get. Then we both got scallops and swine with a butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. All of the entrees sounded phenomenal, but we both couldn't resist getting that dish. The best part I have to say was the dessert. We got cafe au lait panna cotta with mini glazed donuts, which reminded us of beignets at cafe du monde. Finally, I sampled their house made 'cellos, including ginger and limecellos, and they were unique and delicious. An amazing experience!
Refine this for me please: I was extremely excited about this meal and couldn't wait to come home and write a review. The service exceeded my expectations, and I believe the food is among the best in New Orleans. The freshly baked bread was particularly impressive, being both piping hot and incredibly tasty. To start, we ordered the oysters, which consisted of four fried oysters served with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon - an absolute must-try. For our main course, we both went with the scallops and swine, accompanied by a delightful butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. Although all the entrees sounded phenomenal, we simply couldn't resist this particular dish. The highlight of the meal, in my opinion, was the dessert. We indulged in the cafe au lait panna cotta paired with mini glazed donuts, which instantly reminded us of the famous beignets at cafe du monde. To top it all off, we had the opportunity to sample their unique and delicious house-made 'cellos, including flavors like ginger and limecellos. Overall, it was an exceptional dining experience that I highly recommend.

input:
Absolutely amazing!!! My girlfriend and I went on a Wednesday night for Restaurant week and didn't know what to expect but we were overly satisfied. We ordered blood orange margaritas and they were strong and delicious. For our appetizers we had meatballs and let me tell you they weren't your average meatballs. They were veal and beef meatballs that melted in your mouth. Our other appetizer was some sort of grilled cheese that was amazing as well. For our entree we had the fishermen stew that was full of flavor and well balanced. Initially I did not think I was going to like it but it was to die for. Every element of the stew had it's own flavor and it was properly cooked. My girlfriend ordered the steak that came with cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley that was delicious as well. This was the first time we had ever ordered our steak to be medium-well and ever since we've been hooked. The steak was so juicy, tender and seasoned so eloquently and the puree was seasoned beautifully as well. 
The service there was amazing!! I forget the waitors name but he was great with the menu. He helped us order and came back frequently to check on us. 
Overall I think BARRA is amazing. It's not expensive and it is very intimate.  If you are looking for good food and great service at a reasonable price, BARRA is the place to go!!!!
Refine this for me please:
BARRA exceeded our expectations during our visit on a Wednesday night for Restaurant week. The experience was absolutely amazing! We were pleasantly surprised by the delicious and strong blood orange margaritas we ordered. The appetizers, particularly the veal and beef meatballs, were far from average. They simply melted in our mouths. The grilled cheese was another standout dish. Moving on to our entrees, the fishermen stew was bursting with well-balanced flavors that I initially had doubts about. However, it turned out to be a truly exceptional dish. The carefully cooked stew ingredients each had their distinct flavors. My girlfriend ordered the steak, accompanied by cauliflower puree and a flavorful vegetable medley. This was our first time trying medium-well cooked steak and it left us craving for more. The steak was juicy, tender, and perfectly seasoned, while the puree was also beautifully seasoned. 

The service at BARRA was outstanding! Although we forgot the waiter's name, he was fantastic at guiding us through the menu and checking in on us frequently. In terms of ambiance, BARRA offers an intimate setting that doesn't break the bank. If you're searching for reasonably priced food coupled with excellent service, BARRA is undoubtedly the place to visit.

input:
We went here hoping for a good breakfast,  and we weren't disappointed.  We went on Valentine's Day, not because we wanted to, but because we had to.  In doing so,  we knew the wait would be long, which it was (an hour and a half), though i hear there's always a wait. 

The place is buzzing with servers and busboys. The tables around the edges of the room are a bit close to one another,  so seating is tight.  The service was though, considering how busy it was.  I ordered the famed cornmeal pancakes with a side of hash browns and a fried egg.  My girlfriend ordered the banana pancakes with a side of bacon.  Everything was amazing.  The pancakes were hearty but fluffy... The side of bacon only comes with three pieces which is disappointing,  but it was cooked to her liking.  The cornmeal pancakes had just the right amount of everything... Bacon,  peppers... Salsa, sour cream,  syrup... Yes,  all of that.  If you're looking for good coffee,  this is not the place, which was surprising. 

The only question is do you go with the homemade syrup or the maple.... Or both
Refine this for me please:
We arrived at the restaurant with high hopes for a satisfying breakfast, and we were certainly not let down. Our visit took place on Valentine's Day, not out of choice but out of necessity. As expected, the wait time was lengthy, lasting an hour and a half, although I have heard that this is common regardless of the occasion.

The establishment was bustling with diligent servers and busboys attending to the needs of the customers. However, the closeness of the tables along the room's perimeter resulted in limited seating space. Despite the hectic atmosphere, the service managed to be commendable.

For my order, I indulged in the renowned cornmeal pancakes accompanied by a side of crispy hash browns and a perfectly fried egg. My partner opted for the delightful banana pancakes partnered with a side of bacon. Each dish surpassed our expectations. The pancakes struck the perfect balance between heartiness and fluffiness. 

It is worth noting, however, that the bacon served only amounted to three strips, which was slightly underwhelming. Nonetheless, it was cooked to perfection to suit my partner's preferences. The cornmeal pancakes, on the other hand, were a delectable medley of flavors, incorporating bacon, peppers, salsa, sour cream, and syrup – an unexpected but delightful combination. 

Regrettably, if you are seeking a satisfying cup of coffee to accompany your meal, this establishment may not meet your expectations, which came as a surprise to us.

Now comes the ultimate dilemma – should one opt for the homemade syrup or the classic maple syrup? Or perhaps, the ideal solution lies in enjoying both simultaneously.

input: Went on a Monday to have a daiquiri and watch a little bit of the NBA basketball game.  Asked the young lady working if she would be willing to turn on the game and was told she was watching Netflix.  I guess customer service is not important anymore.  Won't ever go back.
Refine this for me please: On a Monday, I decided to visit a bar for a refreshing daiquiri and catch a glimpse of an NBA basketball game. I approached the young lady working there and politely requested if she could switch the TV to the game. Unfortunately, she informed me that she was engrossed in a Netflix show. It left me disheartened, realizing that customer service may not hold the same importance it once did. Regrettably, this experience has deterred me from returning to the establishment in the future.

input: There  aren't  enough  stars  to  review  The  Pearl ! Food , service  and  ambiance . I  enjoy  every  minute  of  every  visit ! Not  just  dinner , a genuine  dining  experience  ! Pamper  yourself !
Refine this for me please: There aren't enough stars to accurately convey how amazing The Pearl is. From the delicious food, exceptional service, to the cozy ambiance, every visit is an absolute delight. It's more than just a dinner outing; it's an authentic dining experience that indulges all your senses. Treat yourself and bask in the luxurious pampering that The Pearl offers.

input: Pretty good bagels, be sure to ask for extra cream cheese if you like a lot. The people are always pleasant which is unique to Dunedin. The bad thing is the guy doesn't wash his hands or wear gloves. He took a previous customers money, my money,  used the phone and wiped his nose, then he made my bagel. I won't go back. If this doesn't bother you, the bagels are pretty good.
Refine this for me please: The bagels at this place are pretty good, but if you're a fan of extra cream cheese, make sure to ask for it. One standout feature of this place is the consistently pleasant staff, which is something unique to Dunedin. However, it is worth noting that there is a concerning hygiene issue. The staff member handling the cash, phone, and even wiping their nose subsequently made my bagel without washing their hands or wearing gloves. Personally, I find this unsettling, and as a result, I won't be returning. But if the lack of hygiene doesn't bother you, you might still enjoy the bagels.

input: Had great reviews. Tried someone new..my husbands cut looks great. My sons cut does not.
Refine this for me please: My husband's haircut received excellent reviews, so I decided to try a new stylist. Fortunately, his cut turned out amazing. However, I am disappointed with the haircut my son received as it did not meet our expectations.

input:
Good, but expensive. 

We both had steak, and it was pretty darn good. 

The guacamole is nothing special. Yes, it gets made in front of you, but it gets made wrong in my opinion.
Refine this for me please:
The quality of the steak was excellent; however, the price was quite steep. 

We opted for steak and both found it to be incredibly satisfying. 

Although the guacamole is prepared in front of you, I personally didn't find it to be particularly exceptional. There were some aspects of it that were not to my liking.

input: I've been to New Day Meadery quite a few times, and every time I come I'm never disappointed! Normally when I come here I order the South Cider or the Shelby Blue Ribbon, but on my last trip I decided to taste one of their seasonal items. I tasted the Paulding Light which has cranberry, honey, and a touch of lime. It was pretty good, but was not as sweet as Shelby Blue Ribbon in my opinion. But that is what I like about New Day, they always have a variety of meads and ciders that everyone can enjoy, not just sugar fans like myself. All in all it is one of my favorite places in Fountain Square! Their service is always prompt and their staff always friendly.
Refine this for me please: I have visited New Day Meadery multiple times, and without fail, I have always been impressed! Typically, I would order the South Cider or the Shelby Blue Ribbon, both of which never disappoint. However, during my last visit, I decided to be adventurous and try one of their seasonal offerings, the Paulding Light, which combines cranberry, honey, and a hint of lime. While it was enjoyable, I found it to be less sweet compared to the Shelby Blue Ribbon. Nonetheless, this is precisely what sets New Day apart - they consistently offer a diverse range of meads and ciders that cater to various preferences, not solely those who prefer sugary beverages like myself. Overall, New Day stands out as one of my favorite spots in Fountain Square. Their service is always efficient, and their staff is consistently welcoming and friendly.

input: I think this is better than the Philadelphia location. Nevertheless, Szechuan house in Hamilton, NJ is still the best.
Refine this for me please: I personally find the Szechuan house in Hamilton, NJ to be superior compared to the Philadelphia location. However, it is important to note that this is subjective and others may have differing opinions.

input: The food and service is fantastic.  Everything is fresh and bursting with flavor. I will come back.
Refine this for me please: The food is exceptional, and the service is outstanding. Every dish is prepared with fresh ingredients that are bursting with an incredible array of flavors. Without a doubt, I am definitely planning to return.

input:
Recently went to Make Up For Ever at KOP. Initially had a great experience and bought $75 worth of products. After trying them for 5 days I didn't really like them. I went to return and was told I couldn't because they were opened. Thankfully they let me exchange but I ended up having to shove more money out! Then they stamped a big FINAL SALE on my new receipt. Overall, still not in love with the products and definitely won't be buying from there again.

The Sephora in KOP sells the same Make Up For Ever products and their return policy is unopened or gently used can be returned, so I'll just keep shopping there.
Refine this for me please:
I recently visited Make Up For Ever at KOP and initially had a positive experience. I ended up purchasing $75 worth of products. However, after using them for just 5 days, I realized that I didn't really like the products. When I attempted to return them, I was informed that I couldn't do so because they had been opened. Thankfully, they allowed me to exchange the products, but I had to spend even more money. To add to my frustration, they stamped a big "FINAL SALE" on my new receipt. Overall, I am still not satisfied with the products, and I have decided that I will not be purchasing from Make Up For Ever again.

On the other hand, the Sephora in KOP also sells the same Make Up For Ever products and offers a return policy where unopened or gently used items can be returned. Due to this convenient return policy, I have decided to switch my shopping to Sephora instead.

input:
My favorite happy hour spot. Discovered how amazing all the appetizers are back in summer 2011 center city sips (great time to check out all the different center city happy hour spots). The mac & cheese is great!

They have a great selection of beers on tap and bottles. The food is superb! If you're looking for a private party space, they have a cozy basement space with a personal bar. Only thing is occasionally you'll have some crashers who want to use the ATM and restroom (even though there is one on the second floor and 2 on the 3rd)

Just go! You won't be disappointed
Refine this for me please:
My favorite happy hour spot is a hidden gem that I discovered in the summer of 2011 during center city sips, a fantastic event where you can explore different happy hour spots in the area. This place blew me away with its delicious appetizers, and ever since, it has become my go-to spot.

The menu here is fantastic, especially the mac & cheese which is an absolute must-try. Alongside the amazing food, they offer an impressive selection of beers on tap and in bottles. Whether you're a beer connoisseur or just looking for a refreshing drink, they have you covered.

One of the things that sets this place apart is its private party space. Located in the cozy basement, it offers a personal bar and creates the perfect ambiance for any celebration. However, it's worth mentioning that occasionally there are crashers who try to use the ATM or restroom, despite there being two restrooms on the third floor and one on the second floor.

Trust me when I say, you need to give this place a try. I guarantee you won't be disappointed.

input: There's been three times that I've ordered a green tea lemonade and got a peach tea lemonade and had to turn all the way back and go inside and have theme remake it.
Refine this for me please: On three separate occasions, I ordered a green tea lemonade only to receive a peach tea lemonade instead, which necessitated me to return to the establishment and have it remade.

input:
This was mine and my fiancé's first time eating here because it not only just opened up, but I got a coupon for a free pizza, so why not right?

We weren't blown away with the experience or the pizza, but liked that it was fast and efficient. The staff that made that pizza was very friendly, but the cashier wasn't sharing that same enthusiasm. 

Wouldn't drive out of my way to go here, but if we are in the neighborhood and feel like some pizza, we may go back.
Refine this for me please: My fiancé and I decided to try this restaurant for the first time as it had recently opened and I had a coupon for a free pizza. While our experience and the pizza itself did not surpass our expectations, we appreciated the quick and efficient service. The pizza-making staff was friendly and accommodating, although we found the cashier to be lacking the same level of enthusiasm. Although we would not make a special trip to dine here, we would consider returning if we happen to be in the area and have a craving for pizza.

input: My husband son and I went in for dinner last Friday night. Upon entering we were greeted by a friendly hostess. As we stood there waiting for her to grab the menus I couldn't help but to notice a strong dirty mop water stench. Thankfully when we left the entry way it didn't carry into the dining room. The remodel is impressive looking. We were sat at a booth. Looking over the menu I was surprised at how limited it was. As long as you make what you offer well no biggie. I ordered the mushroom swiss burger and a beer. My husband ordered the "knuckle sandwich", ( tri-tip sandwich served French dip style). My son ordered the chicken strips and we all got French fries as our side. Jesse, our server was nice enough but in the loud dining room you couldn't hear a word he said. I was more annoyed that he didn't take the initiative to speak up than about the noise. The beer came out, although tasty it wasn't cold enough at all. The food came out within a reasonable amount of time. My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was delicious! That is what the two stars are for. My burger was shockingly small and probably the blandest burger I have ever eaten. My son's chicken strips tasted like they floured them...and that was it... also, no hint of seasoning. The fries are your run of the mill freezer to fryer. I hope they step it up and are successful.
Refine this for me please: My husband, son, and I went to a dinner last Friday night. When we arrived, a friendly hostess greeted us. However, we were immediately struck by a strong, unpleasant smell of dirty mop water as we waited for her to bring us menus. Luckily, once we entered the dining room, the odor did not linger. The restaurant's remodel looked impressive. We were seated at a booth and began looking over the menu. I was surprised to find that the options were quite limited. Nevertheless, I thought if they could make what they offered well, it wouldn't be a big issue. I decided to order the mushroom swiss burger and a beer, while my husband chose the "knuckle sandwich" (a tri-tip sandwich served French dip style). Our son went for the chicken strips, and we all ordered French fries as our side. Our server, Jesse, was pleasant, but due to the loud ambiance, it was difficult to hear him. I was more annoyed that he didn't make an effort to speak up than about the noise itself. The beer arrived, and although it had a good taste, it was not cold enough. Thankfully, the food arrived in a reasonable amount of time. My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was a delight, earning the restaurant two stars. However, I was disappointed to find that my burger was surprisingly small and incredibly bland. In fact, it was possibly the most tasteless burger I had ever eaten. As for my son's chicken strips, they seemed to be only coated in flour without any seasoning, leaving them lacking in flavor. The French fries were the average frozen variety found in most places. I sincerely hope that the restaurant steps up their game and finds success in the future.

input: I had a delicious breakfast at Tuttini a few months ago.  I went back for lunch recently and was excited by their sandwich offerings, however, I was not served.  It was 1:45 PM, and their sign states that they serve lunch until 2:30 PM.  I waited in line for 7 or 8 minutes before a woman came out to tell me that the kitchen was closing.  Closing over 30 minutes early!  She said she might be able to make something to go.  So, if you can make something to go, doesn't that mean the kitchen is not yet closed?  Besides, I wanted to have a few minutes to relax in the cozy restaurant and enjoy my sandwich, not gulf it down on the street, so I left.  I got a sandwich at North Star Coffee around the corner and gave them my $10 instead.
Refine this for me please:
A few months ago, I had a delightful breakfast at Tuttini. Recently, I decided to give their lunch offerings a try and was excited by their sandwich menu. However, my experience was disappointing as I was not served. Despite arriving at 1:45 PM, which is well within their stated lunch serving hours until 2:30 PM, I waited in line for approximately 7 or 8 minutes before a woman informed me that the kitchen was closing. To my surprise, this was over 30 minutes earlier than their advertised closing time.

In an attempt to accommodate my request, she mentioned the possibility of making something to go. This left me perplexed – if they were able to prepare a takeout order, shouldn't the kitchen still be operational? Moreover, my intention was to enjoy my sandwich in the cozy restaurant and have a few moments to relax, not to hastily consume it on the street. Frustrated with the situation, I decided to leave.

Feeling disappointed by my experience at Tuttini, I decided to visit North Star Coffee, located around the corner. There, I purchased a sandwich instead and happily spent my $10 at their establishment.

input: Quick& friendly service, great portion size for the price and the pancakes I ordered were the perfect consistency.
Refine this for me please: The service provided was quick and friendly, the portion size in relation to the price was great, and the pancakes I ordered were of the perfect consistency.

input: I've eaten here numerous times and every time it's been absolutely fantastic. Great food, nice people, calm and quiet place. Their crepes are the best crepes I have ever had. Amazingly delicious. I recommend this place to my friends all the time. I've always heard great things from them as well.
Refine this for me please: I have dined at this establishment on numerous occasions and each time has been an absolutely fantastic experience. The food is exceptional, the staff are kind and welcoming, and the ambiance is calm and tranquil. In particular, their crepes surpass any others I have ever had - they are amazingly delicious. I consistently recommend this place to my friends, and without fail, they too have nothing but positive feedback to share.

input: I have purchased tires from Tires Plus in Flourtown at least 4 times. On this visit they mounted 4 new Michelins that I supplied. My car was worked on as soon as I arrived for the scheduled appointment at 9:00 and was returned to me within one hour.
Refine this for me please: I have been a repeat customer at Tires Plus in Flourtown, having purchased tires from them on at least four different occasions. During my recent visit, I brought in four new Michelins which they promptly mounted on my car. I had a scheduled appointment for 9:00, and upon arrival, they wasted no time in working on my vehicle. input:
Its a great place for Brunch.
We tried the Wildflower Triple where you can substitute any of the 3 items with sausage or biscuit or anything else. We couldn't figure out which one we wanted to try, so this choice was easy! 
The food was spectacular and the service was very friendly! 
We are here for two more days, so we might come back tomorrow or the day after.
Refine this for me please: This place is an excellent spot for brunch! We had the Wildflower Triple, which allows you to customize any of the three items with options like sausage or biscuit. With so many choices, it was a breeze to decide! The food was absolutely amazing, and the service was incredibly friendly. We have two more days here, and we're seriously considering coming back either tomorrow or the day after.

input: We had a great experience enjoying happy hour here! Vaughn and Mark are so kind, we will absolutely be back to get that same service. It's truly one of a kind. The free appetizer was awesome and the slot machines at the bar brought us luck. What a fun happy hour with amazing service!! It's a must!
Refine this for me please: We had an absolutely fantastic experience during happy hour here! Vaughn and Mark were incredibly kind and provided exceptional service. We were so impressed that we definitely plan on returning for that same level of service. The free appetizer was amazing, and the slot machines at the bar even brought us some luck. Overall, it was a very enjoyable and fun happy hour with outstanding service. This place is truly one of a kind and a must-visit!

input: Finally warming up for yogurt!!! They have crepes here too! It's awesome come try them
Refine this for me please: Exciting news! We're finally introducing yogurt to our menu and we can't wait for you to try it! But that's not all – we also have delicious crepes available. The combination is absolutely amazing, so why not come over and give them a try? You won't be disappointed!

input: The event started at 1 and we got there about 1:30. It was so packed you could not enjoy yourself. Most of tents were not even wine, either advertisment, beer, or food you had to pay for. By 3 o' clock most of the tables were out of everything... It was suppose to go till 5?! Definitely was not worth the money and probably will not be back next year.
Refine this for me please: The event began at 1, and we arrived around 1:30. However, it was incredibly crowded, making it challenging to have a good time. Most of the tents were not even offering wine; they were either promoting advertisements, selling beer, or offering paid food options. To make matters worse, by 3 o'clock, many of the tables had run out of everything. It was supposed to continue until 5, but it was clear that it wasn't worth the money we paid. I doubt we'll be returning next year.

input:
I've only eaten here twice and my experience has been great overall. The first time I went, they had just opened. There were some kinks but not anything I would complain about. After all, our group had 8 people so it was understandable. Second time was probably a month later and I noticed they figured out some of the kinks. Their servers are nice and I genuinely felt like they wanted to make my experience great. I know this because every time I made a request the waiter would literally run to get it. I've never seen a server so dedicated, kudos! Honestly most of the stars I'm giving them is because of their genuine service. Added bonus, they were playing Star Trek, hunger games, and iron man. Nice movie selections haha.

The seafood was ok. It's not their fault; it's Tucson so you know you really can't get fresh seafood. That's why I took off a star. They have 1 type of sauce with mild, medium, hot spiciness. It's similar to angry crab's "trifecta" or boiling crab's, "the whole shabang" but with an Asian twist. It was good in my opinion.

Lastly, if anyone has ever gone to angry crab, hot n juicy, boiling crab, should know that the price range is similar. Heck, if anyone has ever bought raw seafood at the store should know that it is on the expensive side. Expensive? Yes. Overpriced? No. I have been to many seafood places similar to this and it's a decent price for what you get. My advice for the Dungeness crab, since it did happen to me at other places and I saw a review on it here, is to share it or get their other selections that they can measure out. The dungeness crab is a full crab so finding a 1 lb dungeness crab is not common. 

Would recommend and go again.
Refine this for me please:
I've only dined at this restaurant twice, but my overall experience has been great. During my first visit, the restaurant had just opened, so there were a few minor issues, but nothing worth complaining about. Considering we had a group of 8 people, it was understandable. When I returned about a month later, I noticed that they had addressed many of the initial issues. The servers were friendly and truly seemed dedicated to ensuring a fantastic experience. I was impressed by their attentiveness, as they would swiftly fulfill any request I made. Their genuine service is a major reason why I am giving them such high praise. Additionally, they had a nice selection of movies playing, including Star Trek, Hunger Games, and Iron Man, which was a pleasant bonus.

Now, onto the seafood. It was decent, but I can't fault the restaurant for this. Tucson isn't known for its fresh seafood options, so I deducted one star for that reason. They offer one type of sauce with various spice levels: mild, medium, and hot. This sauce reminded me of Angry Crab's "Trifecta" or Boiling Crab's "The Whole Shabang," but with an Asian twist. In my opinion, it tasted good.

Moving on to price, it is similar to other seafood establishments like Angry Crab, Hot N Juicy, and Boiling Crab. Considering that buying raw seafood at the store can be expensive, their prices are fair. While it may seem pricey, I have been to many similar seafood places, and this one offers decent value for the money. Regarding the Dungeness crab, I have noticed this issue at other establishments and even saw a review mentioning it here. My advice would be to either share the Dungeness crab or opt for their other menu selections, which they can portion out properly. It's important to note that finding a 1 lb Dungeness crab is not common, as it is typically served as a whole crab.

To conclude, I would absolutely recommend this restaurant and would gladly dine here again.

input: Food was well prepared and fresh. I had the oso bucco ravioli. The ravioli were definitely homemade, they were a little light on the filling which made them less flavourful then they should have been. Service was great,  the place was so loud the wait staff had a hard time hearing us unless we raised our voice. Good place. Extremely tiny and tables are jammed in. Not recommended for a date night. With so many great places to eat in this neighborhood the only thing that would bring me back is the fact it's bring your own bottle. Otherwise I know I could find something as good or better with less noise, a tad more elbow room, and more flavor
Refine this for me please: The food at this restaurant was well prepared and fresh. I ordered the oso bucco ravioli and although they were homemade, I found them to be a bit lacking in filling, resulting in less flavor than expected. The service, however, was great. The only drawback was that the place was very noisy, making it difficult for the wait staff to hear us unless we spoke loudly. Additionally, the restaurant is extremely small and the tables are quite cramped. For these reasons, I would not recommend it for a date night. Despite these issues, the fact that it's bring your own bottle is a positive aspect that might make me consider going back. However, considering the wide variety of excellent dining options in this neighborhood, I believe I could easily find another place with less noise, more space, and additional flavor.

input:
I moved to Philadelphia from the midwest as a wide eyed 19 year old full of wonder. Yuengling lager was the first beer I've ever truly enjoyed and remains in my top five favorites of all time. Smooth, sweet, cheap, it's like me in a bottle. I love that the bottlecaps can be rusty, I like that the taste varies per batch, I even like its relatively low alcohol content. 

The tour was pretty great, the British tour woman was funny in a non canned way. She took a shine to my grandpa and was constantly begging him to sell her his hat (signed, sports, I haven't a clue).
