input:
This place has a great location for the hungry tourist. It manages to be edgy yet chill at the same time. My reason for stopping in was to try the ahi fish tacos with avocado relish, which sounded awesome. At around 3 there was still a healthy amount of people attesting to its popularity and eatability. They had a selection of local microbrews (bottle, not draft) for those interested in getting a taste of Philly in beer form. Alas, I ordered my tacos, but had a little Scooby Doo moment when the arrived. Somehow the chef decided that it was okay to put such a delicate fish in premade taco shells...enough to makes this SoCal girl wince a little and question whether I should consume. Luckily the flavor of the fish was great. I only saw one half inch cube of avocado, but at least the sauce was yummy! 
I got a glimpse of the brunch menu...looks pretty tasty I must say...
Refine this for me please: This place is in a great location and perfect for hungry tourists. It has a cool and relaxed vibe. I came here specifically to try the ahi fish tacos with avocado relish, which sounded amazing. Even at around 3 o'clock, there were still plenty of people there, showing how popular and delicious the food is. They also offer a selection of local microbrews in bottles for those interested in trying Philly beer. However, I was a bit disappointed when my tacos arrived. The chef had decided to use premade taco shells for the delicate fish, which made me question whether I should eat them. Thankfully, the flavor of the fish was still delicious. I did wish there was more avocado in the tacos, but at least the sauce was really tasty! I also caught a glimpse of the brunch menu, and it looks really appetizing.

input: OMG! Breakfast pizza and bottomless mimosas and bloody marys. Is there anything better in this world? Even got a handshake on the way out the door. Service like that seems scarce these days
Refine this for me please: Wow! Is there anything better in this world than indulging in breakfast pizza, accompanied by bottomless mimosas and bloody marys? The experience was made even more memorable by the thoughtful gesture of a handshake as we left. Such exceptional service is becoming increasingly scarce in today's world.

input: I love Bing's boba!!!!!!!!! The Taro snow is my go to drink. Definitely the best boba spot in Tucson! The place is always clean. They have board games for you to play. The staff is helpful and friendly. My husband ordered a drink that unfortunately was not at the right flavor level. He told the staff and they made him a new drink that was to his liking.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore Bing's boba! Their Taro snow drink is my absolute favorite. Without a doubt, it is the top boba spot in Tucson. Not only is the place always immaculately clean, but they also have board games available for customers to enjoy. The staff is incredibly helpful and friendly as well. On one occasion, my husband ordered a drink that didn't meet his flavor expectations. However, after informing the staff, they promptly made him a new drink that perfectly matched his preferences.

input: Venus nail is great. I was looking for a new salon and googled some in my area. I've been 3 times now and they've been amazing. Great atmosphere and service. Ask for Ivy she's fantastic. I told her I was going on a trip for my bday and to come up with something. I walked out with this and loved it all.
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend Venus Nail. I was in search of a new salon in my area, so I decided to do some Googling. After going there three times now, I can confidently say that they offer an amazing experience. The atmosphere is fantastic and the service is top-notch. Specifically, I would recommend asking for Ivy as she is truly fantastic. I once mentioned to her that I was going on a trip for my birthday and asked her to come up with something special for me. She did not disappoint - I walked out of the salon absolutely loving the result.

input:
Not really the town you would expect to find a great Indian restaurant, but figured I'd give it a shot.
I'm picky about Indian food, and all I can say is WOW it's good!
The Naan with peach chutney was amazing.
The Lamb Korma was perfect. Perfect amount of spice (too many Indian restaurant set your mouth on fire and you can't enjoy the taste). Not too much, not too little.
The rice and lamb was perfectly cooked. Very authentic.

The decor is very nice (those chairs in the front are impressive) and staff very friendly. Service was also very quick.

I'm relocating to Tampa, and might actually have to make the drive from there a few times to come back. Very impressive!

I would definitely recommend this place, even if it's a bit of a drive.  It's worth it.
Refine this for me please:
I was pleasantly surprised to discover an exceptional Indian restaurant in an unexpected town. Despite my pickiness when it comes to Indian food, I was blown away by the quality of the dishes here. The Naan with peach chutney was absolutely amazing, leaving me craving more. The Lamb Korma was the perfect balance of spice, allowing me to savor its flavor rather than just endure heat. The rice and lamb were flawlessly cooked, resulting in an authentic and satisfying meal.

In addition to the fantastic food, the restaurant boasts a pleasant ambiance with impressive chairs at the front. The staff were friendly and the service was brisk, adding to the overall enjoyable experience. In fact, I was so impressed that I am willing to make the drive from Tampa to this place multiple times even after my relocation.

I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone, even if it requires a bit of a drive. The quality of the food and the overall dining experience make it more than worth it.

input:
Have you ever tried a new lunch place and liked it so much that you went back for dinner that night and lunch the next day. I have done the back to back to back only once, at Greko. 

I've love the rotisserie chicken pita with fries. If you are in the mood for something healthier, they have great salads. Definitely try the Horta Greens (you can substitute fries for Horta Greens or have them on the side). The perfectly cooked and seasoned greens are delicious. 
I also love the Athenian Chicken (half a rotisserie chicken). 

As a quick, casual, food-first restaurant, Greko has hit the sweet spot.
Refine this for me please:
Have you ever tried a new lunch place and enjoyed it so much that you returned for dinner the same night and lunch the following day? Well, I've only had that kind of immediate repeat experience once, and it was at Greko. This spot offers a delightful variety of food, but what I particularly adore is their rotisserie chicken pita with fries. It's a heavenly combination that always leaves me satisfied. 

For those seeking a healthier option, their salads are outstanding. The Horta Greens, in particular, are worth trying. If you're not a fan of fries, you can substitute them for Horta Greens or simply have them on the side. The greens are flawlessly cooked and seasoned, resulting in a scrumptious dish.

Another highlight at Greko is the Athenian Chicken, which consists of half a succulent rotisserie chicken. This dish never disappoints, and the flavors are absolutely fantastic.

Greko has managed to find the perfect balance as a quick, casual, and food-centric restaurant.

input:
Brother Rabbit you are young, hip, and tasty!

Met friends for drinks and an early dinner. I was the first to arrive so I sat at the bar and ordered the house cider which is great and I followed that with the Oban 18 which is phenomenal so try it while you're there. 

Our dinner kicked off with the most amazing house biscuits and butter that will have you begging for the recipe.

The rest of our dinner was comprised of several selections from the First course menu. We had the daily oysters which were great. Followed by the Brussels sprouts, delicious but the crispy chicken skins were a bit of a let down, they needed more flavor. 

The smoked tuna tartar is great but the sweet chips can overwhelm the dish. Definitely get the marinated shrimp and jalapeño jus it is a wonderfully fresh and bright dish. 

To close thing up we had the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream, as if that wasn't enough they pour this amazing chocolate sauce on it when it arrives that will have you just dying as you wait to dig in.

Overall Compere Lapin is a great addition to the New Orleans food scene, great for groups or date night with your significant other.
Refine this for me please:
Met friends for drinks and an early dinner at Compere Lapin, a great addition to the New Orleans food scene. I arrived first and enjoyed the house cider at the bar, which was great. Then I had the Oban 18, a phenomenal choice that I highly recommend trying while you're there.

Our dinner started off with the most amazing house biscuits and butter. They were so good that you'll be begging for the recipe.

For the main course, we ordered several selections from the First course menu. The daily oysters were great, and the Brussels sprouts were delicious. However, the crispy chicken skins were a bit disappointing as they lacked flavor.

The smoked tuna tartar was fantastic, but the sweet chips can overpower the dish. I highly recommend getting the marinated shrimp with jalapeño jus, as it is a wonderfully fresh and bright dish.

To end the night, we indulged in the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream. As if that wasn't enough, they pour an amazing chocolate sauce on top when it arrives, making you eager to dig in.

Whether you're going with a group or on a date night with your significant other, Compere Lapin is a must-visit spot for its excellent food and atmosphere.

input:
Here for convention and Imo's was suggested as "The Best" St. Louis Style pizza by hotel staff. 

I opted for delivery which was good and efficient. The food arrived still hot. I ordered a medium pepperoni and an order of toasted ravioli. 

Now, I knew the cheese on the pizza was provel so it would taste different. I was really not impressed. It may just be a matter of taste preference. It was hard to separate each piece of pizza too.  Like, it wasn't cut all the way through. Not really a fan. So thumbs down on the pizza. 

What bumps the stars up are the T-Ravs!  I was hoping for cheese ravioli but the staple is a meat mixture. Boy...do they do it justice. They were the bomb!  The sauce with it was too watery but still tasty. I would order just the ravioli next time!
Refine this for me please:
During my convention stay, the hotel staff highly recommended Imo's as the ultimate spot for the renowned St. Louis Style pizza. Opting for delivery, I was pleasantly satisfied with the prompt and efficient service, as the food arrived piping hot. My order consisted of a medium pepperoni pizza and an enticing side of toasted ravioli.

Considering that Imo's uses provel cheese on their pizza, I expected a distinct flavor. However, it failed to impress me; perhaps it's simply a matter of personal taste. Moreover, the pizza slices were poorly separated, making it difficult to enjoy each individual piece. Unfortunately, I cannot say I am a fan of their pizza, resulting in a thumbs down.

On a brighter note, the real stars of my order were the glorious T-Ravs! Although I was initially hoping for cheese ravioli, I was pleasantly surprised by the meat mixture they utilized. Imo's truly excelled in this aspect, as the T-Ravs were absolutely fantastic! The accompanying sauce, although a bit watery, still possessed a delightful taste. If I were to reorder from Imo's, I would undoubtedly focus solely on the ravioli.

input: I have groen up eating Italian food and i have not come across a more legit place than Mazzaros! Love their sauce and meatballs.
Refine this for me please: Having grown up eating Italian food, I have yet to discover a more authentic place than Mazzaros. Their sauce and meatballs are absolutely outstanding.

input: Okay, so it's a dance club. It's trendy and offers higher-end cocktails and beers while still offering your run-of-the-mill wells and domestic bottles. On certain nights, guys have to pay a door charge (but that's not really uncommon in the industry). There is a huge patio and, even in the winter, almost the entire patio is still available because they enclose it. The music is pretty hit-or-miss...sometimes you're dancing away to classic hip-hop, pop, and even rock, and other times you're standing there while the DJ spins out an un-danceable tune. If you're on the patio, you can chat...but if you're inside it's (not shockingly) too loud to really talk. If you're in the CWE and you're looking to dance, at least give the Mandarin a shot; it's not going to be for everyone, but it's pretty great if you're in the mood for it.
Refine this for me please: The Mandarin is a trendy dance club that caters to a diverse crowd. It prides itself on offering a wide selection of cocktails and beers, including high-end options as well as more standard choices. While there may be a cover charge for men on certain nights, this is common in the industry and should not come as a surprise. One of the standout features of the club is its spacious patio, which is enclosed during the winter months, providing ample space for patrons to enjoy. The music played at the club can be hit or miss, ranging from classic hip-hop, pop, and rock to occasionally less dance-friendly tunes by the DJ. Inside the venue, the volume is loud making it difficult to hold conversations, whereas the patio offers a more relaxed environment for chatting. Located in the CWE area, if you're in the mood to dance, the Mandarin should definitely be considered. While it may not appeal to everyone, it has the potential to be a fantastic experience if it aligns with your preferences.

input:
Another gem on Frenchmen.  We made it in just in time to grab the corner tall table and enjoyed the piano player playing some nice tunes.

Order at the bar and they'll bring you the food.  What we had:
pork pot stickers - pretty good - $4 HH price
smoked hanger steak w/ chimichurri sauce on toastones - tasted much better than it looked - $4 HH price
lobster eggrolls w/ sweet chile lime sauce - $8 - didn't look promising but it was tasty
Hopitoulas - $4.5
UFO - $4.5

One of the owners/chefs is Korean, thus the Asian food.

HH everyday from 4-6:30pm, $4 tapas, $5 wines, $3 beers.

We will definitely return.
Refine this for me please:
We discovered another hidden gem on Frenchmen Street. Luckily, we arrived just in time to secure a tall table in the corner, where we could enjoy the delightful melodies played by the piano player.

To order food, simply head to the bar, and the staff will bring it right to your table. Here's what we indulged in:

- Pork pot stickers: These were quite tasty, especially considering the happy hour price of $4.
- Smoked hanger steak with chimichurri sauce on toastones: Despite its underwhelming appearance, this dish surprised us with its delicious flavors. Again, a steal at $4 during happy hour.
- Lobster eggrolls with sweet chili lime sauce: Although they didn't look appealing at first, these eggrolls turned out to be surprisingly flavorful. They cost $8, but definitely worth it.
- To complement our meal, we enjoyed a Hopitoulas and a UFO beer, both priced at $4.5.

It's worth noting that one of the owners/chefs is Korean, hence the presence of Asian cuisine on the menu.

Happy hour is offered every day from 4-6:30pm, featuring $4 tapas, $5 wines, and $3 beers.

Overall, we had an excellent experience, and we will definitely be returning to this spot.

input: food is ok, felt rushed, too many tables and not enough space.  its very crowded and frequently had other servers and customers bumping into our chairs.

She's styling my hair for my upcoming wedding plus 6 bridesmaids and I have no doubt it'll be picture perfect. Deseree is accommodating, dependable,and experienced (oh, and hilarious too )!!
Refine this for me please: Deseree has been my hairstylist for more than ten years, and I absolutely trust her expertise. With my upcoming wedding approaching, Deseree is going to style not only my hair but also that of my six bridesmaids, and I am confident that it will be flawlessly picture perfect. input:
Four of us had dinner at the Sockeye Grill this weekend.  Service was terrible.  Super slow.  Salads were warm and tasteless.  Dressing was watered down. 

Salmon was excellent.  Nachos were okay. Finger steaks were mushy and drab. 

Waitress  knew her beer. The dark lager was excellent.  The lighter beers we had were too warm. 

Looks like this restaurant need some fine tuning.  The atmosphere was like a warehouse, more like being in a barn than a restaurant. 

Tvs everywhere but the news was on. Huh? How depressing is that? 

We won't be back.
Refine this for me please:
Four of us had dinner at the Sockeye Grill over the weekend, but unfortunately, we were greatly disappointed with the overall experience. The service was exceptionally slow, leaving us waiting for extended periods of time. To make matters worse, the salads we ordered were warm and tasteless, with the dressing being disappointingly watered down.

Although the salmon we had was truly excellent, the same couldn't be said for the nachos, which were only okay. Unfortunately, the finger steaks we ordered were mushy and lacked any distinct flavor.

On a positive note, our waitress was knowledgeable about the beer selection, and the dark lager she recommended was simply fantastic. However, to our disappointment, the lighter beers we tried were served at a warm temperature, deterring from our enjoyment.

In terms of the restaurant's ambiance, it left much to be desired. The atmosphere felt more like a warehouse or barn rather than a cozy dining establishment. Adding to our dissatisfaction, televisions were scattered throughout the restaurant, yet they were all tuned to the news. This choice of programming only added to the less-than-pleasant vibe of the place.

Overall, our dining experience at the Sockeye Grill fell short of our expectations. Due to the slow service, subpar salads, lackluster finger steaks, and underwhelming atmosphere, we have decided that we will not be returning in the future.

input:
We had a very nice dinner here on St. Patrick's day, which happens to be my sister's birthday.  The server was super sweet and served the cake we brought to celebrate.  The bartender was so kind and gave my sister a complimentary St. Patty's cocktail, which was incredibly yummy.  

We ordered various dishes:  tri-tip, rotisserie chicken, pulled pork and a veggie burrito.  All was wonderful, except for the veggie burrito, which was lackluster (but who orders a veggie burrito at a rotisserie grill???).  My father-in-law has visited many more times, raving about the moist, flavorful rotisserie chicken.  

The prices were reasonable, portions adequate and service super!  We will definitely visit again, minus the resident vegetarian.  :)
Refine this for me please:
We had a delightful dinner at this establishment on St. Patrick's day, coinciding with my sister's birthday celebration. Our server provided exceptional service by graciously serving the cake we brought along. The bartender also went above and beyond by offering my sister a delectable complimentary St. Patrick's Day cocktail.

Our group decided to try a variety of dishes including tri-tip, rotisserie chicken, pulled pork, and even a veggie burrito (though it may have been an odd choice at a rotisserie grill). Overall, the food was exceptional, with the exception of the lackluster veggie burrito. However, it's worth mentioning that my father-in-law, who has frequented this restaurant before, always raves about the moist and flavorful rotisserie chicken.

In terms of value, the prices were reasonable, and the portion sizes were satisfactory. Additionally, the service provided was outstanding. As a result, we certainly plan on returning in the future, with the exception of our resident vegetarian. :)

input: Went to see Anders Osborne play here & it was a highlight of my trip to NOLA.  Streetcar went straight down to Bourbon after the show but I wish I'd stayed longer! Food smelled awesome, drinks were very reasonably priced  & the crowd was mellow.
Refine this for me please: During my trip to NOLA, I had the pleasure of attending a live performance by Anders Osborne, which turned out to be one of the highlights. After the show, I hopped on a streetcar that conveniently took me straight down to Bourbon Street. However, in hindsight, I regret not prolonging my stay. The tantalizing aroma of the local cuisine permeated the air, and the drinks were affordably priced. Moreover, the atmosphere was calm and relaxed, making it even more enticing.

input: I have been told by numerous native philadelphians that Ralph's is one of the best Italian restaurants in the city and is a must to experience. We did not think so. We started off with a grilled calamari appetizer that was soaked in salty red sauce. The amount of sauce overwhelmed the palate to the point where we couldn't even taste the calamari. I got the pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips. Again, the red sauce was very salty. The filet mignon tips was really just average quality beef. My wife ordered the black lobster ravioli which were decent but overly salty. We expected much more from the oldest Italian restaurant in the country.
Refine this for me please: Numerous native Philadelphians highly recommended Ralph's as one of the best Italian restaurants in the city, but our experience did not align with their praise. Our meal began with a grilled calamari appetizer drenched in a salty red sauce, overpowering our taste buds and obscuring the flavor of the calamari itself. The pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips featured a similarly salty red sauce, while the filet mignon tips were disappointingly average in quality. My wife opted for the black lobster ravioli, which, although decent, suffered from excessive saltiness. Considering the historic significance of being the oldest Italian restaurant in the country, we were left with higher expectations.

input: We get high on the beauty of this amazing high desert oasis! Nature's drama in the Catalina Mountains. We come here to run or hike. We're #MCLifeTucson - we love it in the canyon!
Refine this for me please: Experience the intoxicating allure of the breathtaking high desert oasis! Immerse yourself in the captivating landscape of the Catalina Mountains where nature's theatrical displays unfold. Whether seeking an adrenaline rush through running or hiking, we, the proud #MCLifeTucson community, find solace and exhilaration in the enchanting canyon.

input:
Beer service was lackluster. The first beer I ordered had an off flavor (sour). I ordered a taste of another similar dark beer to see if the problem was endemic but it wasn't. I would have appreciated it more if the bar tender looked into the off flavor when I sent my beer back. This tells me the bar tender doesn't know beer. I assume that particular draft line needs to be cleaned but maybe the problem was with the keg. 

Another thing that killed me was their use of glassware. They serve beers in the classic American "Shaker" pint glass and serve water in the far superior English Nonic Pint glass. I also saw the bar tender pour a white ale with normal ABV in a stemmed tulip glass.

The shaker pint glasses are kept refrigerated and are too cold in my opinion. I would much rather see them kept at room temp and rinsed in cold water (which they do here). 

All in all, the beer knowledge is not up to par for a place that advertises as a burger joint with a large craft beer selection (30 taps).
Refine this for me please:
The beer service was disappointing. The first beer I ordered had a sour and off flavor, suggesting a problem with its quality. To investigate further, I requested a taste of another similar dark beer, which turned out to be fine. However, it would have been better if the bartender had looked into the off flavor issue when I sent my first beer back. This lack of attention to detail indicates a lack of knowledge about beer on the bartender's part. It is possible that the draft line or the keg needs to be cleaned to prevent such issues.

Another aspect that bothered me was their choice of glassware. Instead of using the superior English Nonic Pint glass for serving beer, they opt for the classic American "Shaker" pint glass. Additionally, I observed the bartender pour a white ale with a normal ABV into a stemmed tulip glass, which seemed inappropriate.

Furthermore, the shaker pint glasses are unnecessarily refrigerated and become too cold for my taste. I would prefer if they were stored at room temperature and rinsed with cold water, as they currently do.

Overall, the beer knowledge at this place falls short of expectations for a burger joint that prides itself on a wide selection of craft beers on tap (30 taps).

input: Love love live Orangetheory!! Best full body workout ever!!! And so many classes.... always convenient!
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore Orangetheory! It's hands down the ultimate full body workout I have ever experienced. The variety of classes is simply amazing, making it incredibly convenient for anyone's schedule.

input: Great tour! Very informative  (our tour guide Raymond was awesome!) and the food stops along the way were very delicious. Definitely worth the time and money.

input: Rons still a regular stop for me.  Usually some good craft beers  (excellent this week) and tasty food  (if you know what to stick with on menu).
Refine this for me please: Rons remains a consistent favorite spot for me, with their selection of craft beers always impressing, especially this week. Additionally, they offer tasty food options, as long as you know which items to stick with on the menu.

input: This place is amazing!  They make the donuts fresh with each order.  In fact, I had to wait 10 minutes for them to cool down before I could eat them.  This location is clean and never super busy.  Its a really great addition to the neighborhood and people with cars are sure to appreciate the parking lot.  Best donuts in Philly and the Delaware Valley.
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely incredible! Not only do they prepare the donuts fresh for each order, but they even make you wait for a short while to let them cool down. The cleanliness of this location is impeccable, and it never gets overwhelmingly crowded. It's truly a fantastic addition to the neighborhood, and those with vehicles will especially appreciate the convenience of the parking lot. Hands down, the best donuts you can find in both Philly and the Delaware Valley.

input: This is the worst. My first time at an Econo anything. Playing nice for group purposes. We get here. They check us in like the rooms are clean. The rooms are dirty. The lady comes to clean the room because apparently they dont have any others clean or available. Go figure. So the manager comes outside to look as if we are lying about dirty rooms. It's hot as hell outside, wasps everywhere and we're standing here. I asked about other clean rooms and he (a-hole manager) (neil Patel) sarcastically states check in is at 2. It's 1:45 though. If you're going to check guest in at least make sure the rooms are clean or let them know it will be a few. So I'm standing outside in the heat as they apparently clean the room. Refine this for me please: This has been a terrible experience for me. It's my first time staying at an Econo Lodge and I am very disappointed. When we arrived, the staff checked us in as if the rooms were clean, but they were actually dirty. In addition to all of this, the manager came outside, seemingly doubting our claims about the dirty rooms. It was incredibly hot outside, there were wasps everywhere, and we had to stand there dealing with this situation. When I asked about other clean rooms, the manager (Neil Patel, who is quite rude) sarcastically mentioned that check-in time is at 2, even though it was already 1:45. If they insist on checking guests in early, they should ensure that the rooms are clean or inform them in advance that it will take some time. So instead of being inside the air-conditioned room, I'm stuck outside in the heat while they supposedly clean it. However, from what I observed, they only checked the microwave and fridge for cleanliness. They didn't wipe anything down or clean the counters or bathroom. It's just disgusting. input: Finally got to check out Cafe Soleil. One word: Delicieux!! Being from France, I had high expectations, I don't play with my pastries! Boy do they deliver, the croissants were buttery, nice and flaky, and melt in your mouth...even better then some of the ones I had in France. Not surprisingly, the baker "Nico" is french, and you could taste the difference in the food.  The fact that the products are imported does make a big difference in the taste, it's definitely authentic.  Nico was very personable and friendly, it was fun chatting with an ex-parisian :). The one negative thing is they are too far from me, 45 mins drive, but to satiate my sweet tooth, I will definitely be back! I highly recommend this bakery.
Refine this for me please:
I recently had the chance to visit Cafe Soleil, and let me tell you, it was an absolute delight. As someone from France, I hold my pastries to high standards, and this place definitely exceeded them. The croissants were simply heavenly - they were buttery, flaky, and melted in my mouth. I dare say they were even better than some of the ones I've had back in France. It's no surprise that the talented baker, Nico, is French himself, as you can truly taste the authenticity in every bite.

One thing that sets Cafe Soleil apart is that they import their ingredients, which undoubtedly contributes to the exceptional taste. You can really tell the difference in quality. Nico himself was incredibly friendly and personable, and it was a pleasure to chat with him, especially considering he used to live in Paris. 

The only downside is that the bakery is quite far from where I live, about a 45-minute drive. However, the trip is well worth it to satisfy my sweet tooth. I highly recommend paying Cafe Soleil a visit - you won't be disappointed.

input:
Not mediocre at all IMHO.  Makes me wonder if Daniel O. went to the same place we did.

This is a great neighborhood byob place that provides welcoming service and excellent food at a reasonable price.  We started going here because numerous South Philly friends recommended it.  This is not foo-foo Italian.  This is not pretentious Italian.  This is "let's go back and work our way through the menu" Italian.  We found the specials to be good choices.  My husband's broccoli rabe and sausage was excellent, as was a grilled romaine salad with bleu cheese and pine nuts.  Both were generous enough to share.  Last time, sausage & figs was a hit.  If you are in the mood for a basic plate of macaronis with red gravy, you won't be disappointed either.  We had a great time with the waitress because my BIL brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (that was the 2nd bottle we opened) and that started a whole crazy discussion.  She didn't know us from Adam, but we left there feeling like regulars.

It's a very doable destination if you are on your way to a sporting event at the Linc or the Cit, or to the Spectrum or Wachovia Center.  For those who rely on public transportation, you can get off the subway at Broad & Oregon, then walk back a block to Broad & Porter.  Make a reservation, though because it can be a popular place.  You also want to make sure you have time to have a relaxing meal and make your event in time.
Refine this for me please:
In my opinion, this place is far from mediocre. It's worth mentioning that Daniel O. might have gone to a different establishment altogether.

This neighborhood BYOB spot offers excellent food, welcoming service, and reasonable prices. We were initially drawn to this place upon multiple recommendations from our South Philly friends. It's important to note that this is not your fancy or pretentious Italian restaurant. Instead, it's the type of place where you want to come back and methodically explore the entire menu. The daily specials have proven to be delightful choices. We particularly enjoyed my husband's broccoli rabe and sausage dish, as well as the grilled romaine salad with blue cheese and pine nuts. Both portions were generous enough to share. On our last visit, the sausage and figs dish was a standout. If you're in the mood for a classic plate of macaroni with red sauce, you won't be disappointed either. 

Our experience with the waitress was fantastic. When my brother-in-law brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (which happened to be the second one we opened), it sparked a lively conversation. Despite not knowing us at all, the waitress made us feel like regulars by the time we left.

Conveniently, this restaurant is easily accessible if you're headed to a sporting event at the Linc or the Cit, or even the Spectrum or Wachovia Center. If you rely on public transportation, you can simply get off the subway at Broad & Oregon, then walk back a block to Broad & Porter. However, make sure to make a reservation ahead of time, as the place can get quite busy. Additionally, plan accordingly to ensure you have enough time to relax and enjoy your meal without rushing to your event.

input: Can't go wrong with some Todd Cobell!
Refine this for me please: You can never go wrong by listening to Todd Cobell!

input:
We are frequent patrons who enjoy their super fun bar, tv's and music selection.  The service is very good.  Nice, hard-working, mannerly people in a very cool atmosphere that appreciate the business.  Food is consistently fresh(seafood) and good.  Pizza is the best in South Jersey and my husband, the unofficial pizza 'officianado' makes me try them all, from NYC, to Trenton to Philly, Delaware, Chicago.  This is really the best pizza I've ever had. The crust is thin, crispy yet has a nice chew, and flavorful.

Last night I had a dinner special of chicken cutlet in a lobster, white -truffle oil, light cream sauce with asparagus, shallots and sundried tomatoes over angel hair pasta. On the Special's menu it is listed as a veal entree, but the kitchen was more than happy to substitute Chicken for me. The dish was so delicately seasoned with such a fine touch that I enjoyed smelling it almost as much as tasting it. In addition, it was such a generous portion that I enjoyed it two nights later for dinner and now want to go back tomorrow and order it again!!  What an absolutely fabulous recipe. Very fine, subtle flavor but also comforting and satisfying. 

Not to mention, Selena the Bar Manger, bartenders Jayna and Chris are just so pleasant, professional and helpful, it really is a great place to go!

Enjoy!!
Refine this for me please:
We are regulars at this fantastic bar, and we absolutely love everything about it. The atmosphere is cool and enjoyable, with great bar games, TVs, and an amazing music selection. The service is exceptional, provided by friendly, hard-working, and polite staff who truly appreciate your patronage. 

The food here is consistently excellent. I must mention their seafood, which is always fresh and delicious. However, the real star of the show is the pizza. As a self-proclaimed pizza connoisseur, my husband has made me try pizzas from all over South Jersey, including NYC, Trenton, Philly, Delaware, and even Chicago. We've concluded that this place serves the best pizza we've ever had. The crust is thin, crispy, and has the perfect amount of chew. Its flavor is simply outstanding. 

During my recent visit, I ordered their dinner special, which was a chicken cutlet dish served with a lobster and white truffle oil cream sauce, accompanied by asparagus, shallots, and sundried tomatoes over angel hair pasta. Although it was listed as a veal entree on the menu, the kitchen kindly substituted it with chicken for me. The dish was delicately seasoned, with a subtle yet captivating flavor that enticed not only my taste buds but also my sense of smell. The portion was so generous that I was able to enjoy it for another dinner the following night, and now I am already eager to go back and order it again. The recipe is absolutely fabulous.

I also want to mention the amazing staff. Selena, the Bar Manager, along with bartenders Jayna and Chris, are incredibly pleasant, professional, and always ready to assist. Their presence adds to the overall greatness of this establishment.

In conclusion, this place is a must-visit. You will have a fantastic time, enjoying the wonderful ambiance, delicious food, and top-notch service.

input:
Impeccable food and service! We figured if we were gonna do Sbraga, we needed the chefs counter 6 course with wine pairings. A pricy endeavor but no regrets. I loved having a front row view of the deliciousness about to be laid in front of me. The team behind the line on this particular Saturday night ran like a well oiled machine. 

The tone was set with the amuse Gruyere popover with foie gras soup. Heavenly! There were no duds on the menu, but other standouts were the saffron spaghetti with blue crab, the crispy Arctic char and the chicken liver mousse (btw I thought I hated chicken liver). The wines were matched very well. 

My friend was celebrating a birthday so I included that in the notes when making the reservation. To top off the experience, they gave her a note signed by Sbraga and a little goodie bag. Can't wait to return!
Refine this for me please:
The food and service at Sbraga were absolutely impeccable! We decided to go all out and opted for the chefs counter 6 course meal with wine pairings. Although it was quite expensive, we had absolutely no regrets. Sitting at the counter gave us a front-row view of the culinary magic that was about to be presented to us. The team of chefs working behind the line on that particular Saturday night ran like a well-oiled machine.

The evening started on a high note with the amuse Gruyere popover and foie gras soup, which was truly heavenly. Every dish on the menu was outstanding, but some notable highlights were the saffron spaghetti with blue crab, the crispy Arctic char, and the surprisingly delicious chicken liver mousse (despite my initial aversion to chicken liver). The wine pairings were also spot-on and complemented the flavors of each dish beautifully.

I had mentioned in the reservation notes that my friend was celebrating her birthday, and they truly went above and beyond to make the experience even more special. They surprised her with a personalized note signed by Sbraga himself, as well as a thoughtful little goodie bag. It was the perfect finishing touch to an already wonderful evening.

I can't wait to revisit Sbraga in the future.

input:
If you're looking for something different in this area, I highly recommend GlobalQ.  Their quesadillas and wraps are all very good, I've had at least half of the items on the menu and they've ranged from, at worst, just ok, to phenomenal.  The quesadillas are very big and are full of some pretty unique combinations.  The wraps are also huge, I usually only eat half a wrap and save the other half for the next day.  While they're all pretty good, I recommend going outside the box and getting the 'Montreal' or 'New Orleans'.  And their 'French Dip' quesadilla is also very good, but for some reason is not listed on their menu.  Check that one out if you like french dip sammies.  

Best part about this place: THEY DELIVER.
Refine this for me please:
If you're in the area and looking for something unique, I highly recommend GlobalQ. Their quesadillas and wraps are consistently delicious. I've tried numerous items on their menu and have found them to range from good to exceptional. The quesadillas are generously sized and feature interesting flavor combinations. The wraps are also quite large, often providing enough for two meals. Although everything is enjoyable, I suggest trying the 'Montreal' or 'New Orleans' options to step outside the usual choices. Additionally, the 'French Dip' quesadilla, which is not listed on the menu, is a hidden gem worth trying, especially if you enjoy French dip sandwiches. 

One of the best things about GlobalQ is their delivery service.

input: Celebrating our honeymoon over New Years week, we were lucky enough to score a few nights at the historic Monteleone. I'll forever want to stay there when visiting New Orleans. input:
