input:
I must say I'm very disappointed, my two stars are for presentation and prompt delivery. I ordered the rainbow roll, white tuna roll, calamari and chicken lettuce wraps. Where do I begin? ok with the bad. 

I strongly feel that when you are delivering food that should be served cold, you don't put it in a bag with hot food because that equals mushy, warm sushi, which is what I got. The rainbow roll, which normally is topped with raw fish was topped with mushy avocado????? which I ended up peeling off to salvage the sushi. The spicy white tuna roll was very good.

The calamari looked like chicken fingers all the breading was falling off and it was under cooked, I took one bite and tossed it. Now I've had lettuce wraps before but mines came with an actual head of lettuce in a bag and chicken filling in a plate. It was not described this way in the menu at all. All in all I don't think I'll be ordering from here again. I'll stick to Niji's on 5th.
Refine this for me please:
I must express my significant disappointment with my recent order. I would like to give credit for the presentation and prompt delivery, which warrant two stars. However, I encountered several issues with my order. 

Firstly, I was perplexed by the decision to store cold items with hot food. As a result, my sushi arrived mushy and warm, particularly the rainbow roll. Instead of the expected raw fish topping, it was crowned with mushy avocado. Consequently, I had to painstakingly remove this topping to salvage the sushi. On a positive note, the spicy white tuna roll was enjoyable.

Additionally, the calamari disappointed me greatly. Its presentation resembled chicken fingers, with the breading falling off, and it was clearly undercooked. After a single bite, I had to discard the rest. 

Furthermore, my disappointment extended to the chicken lettuce wraps. I was under the impression that I would receive a head of lettuce accompanied by a plate of chicken filling. However, the actual dish came in a different format, not accurately described in the menu. 

Considering these experiences, I am hesitant to order from this establishment again. Instead, I will opt for Niji's on 5th, which has consistently met my expectations.

input: Terrible service from the bar tender. Unless you are a regular she did not serve us. I was standing at the bar with money in my hand and she just kept going to the same old people. Very irritating!
Refine this for me please: Extremely poor service was received from the bar tender, as she chose to only serve regular customers. Despite being readily available at the bar with money in hand, she continued to prioritize the same individuals. This behavior proved to be highly bothersome and irritating.

input:
I came in here the other night for a  post-show snack after seeing a ESO performance at the Winspear. The main reason we chose this location was because it was close to the Winspear, and open late (until 11:30pm on Friday and Saturday). I don't have any strong criticisms of the restaurant. I suppose, if anything, the menu may have seemed a little bit over-priced - at least for what I ordered. I had a Caesar salad with three 'jumbo' shrimp on it, which cost $15. The portion size did not seem to justify the cost and the jumbo shrimp were fairly average in their size, but the flavours were good and the ingredients were fresh. My friend had a soup, which looked and smelled absolutely amazing, and at $6 it didn't seem too unreasonable. She also had the smoked salmon Carpaccio, which looked very appetizing with its thick slices of dark rye bread and generous slices of smoked salmon and capers. The also had a couple of interesting beers on their menu that we were keen to try.

I think if you're going to a show in the area and looking for a spot to get a drink or a snack afterward, this is not a bad option. Their menu at that time of night had an interesting mix of appetizers and desserts that seemed to provide something to suit most tastes.

I'm assuming Normand's Bistro must be connected to the Normand's restaurant which is on Jasper Avenue. Of interest, I have heard that Normand's took over the brunch menu that had formerly been offered at the Glenora Bistro.
Refine this for me please:
I visited this restaurant after an ESO performance at the Winspear. We chose it because of its close proximity to the Winspear and its late opening hours until 11:30 pm on Fridays and Saturdays. Overall, I don't have any major complaints about the restaurant. However, I did find the menu to be slightly overpriced, especially for the dish I ordered. I had a Caesar salad with three 'jumbo' shrimp priced at $15. The portion size didn't justify the cost, and the shrimp were average in size. Nonetheless, the flavors were good, and the ingredients were fresh. My friend had a soup, which looked and smelled amazing and was reasonably priced at $6. She also enjoyed the smoked salmon Carpaccio, which was appetizing with thick slices of dark rye bread, generous amounts of smoked salmon, and capers. We were also enticed by the interesting beer options on the menu.

If you're looking for a place to grab a drink or a snack after attending a show in the area, this is not a bad choice. Their late-night menu offers a variety of appetizers and desserts that cater to different tastes.

I believe Normand's Bistro is connected to Normand's restaurant on Jasper Avenue. Interesting to note, I've heard that Normand's took over the brunch menu previously offered at the Glenora Bistro.

input: The people at the store amazing! We came in to exchange a shirt from a few days before they had had some damage, and the managers were so helpful with our situation. Tonya is the best. Without hesitation she is going to help us out.
Refine this for me please: We were amazed by the incredible service provided by the store staff. We visited to exchange a shirt that had been damaged a few days earlier and the managers displayed exemplary assistance in resolving our situation. Tonya, in particular, stood out as the absolute best! She immediately offered her assistance without any hesitation.

input: My dogs and i love this place!   Always try to go when they have sales going on.  They have a wide variety of toys and are pretty well stocked.  They even allow your pets to come in with you.  The staff is very caring and friendly.  Whenever I have a question about a certain product, they give me a great answer or find someone who knows more about it.  Even though it's a chain store, I feel like it's a nice neighborhood pet store.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore this place with my dogs! We make sure to visit whenever they have their sales going on. The store has an amazing assortment of toys and is always well-stocked. The best part is that they welcome your pets to accompany you inside. The staff here is incredibly caring and friendly. Whenever I have a query about a specific product, they provide me with excellent guidance or connect me with someone who has more expertise. Despite being a chain store, it truly feels like a charming neighborhood pet shop.

input: Gets two stars because the service was great and staff was very friendly, food was not very good.. maybe we came on a bad day. I ate there and ordered a togo item for my husband. I asked the girl working the counter to pick the most popular thing out of the German section for him and it was literally just a pretzel and a piece of sausage in a box.
Refine this for me please: I would rate it two stars due to the excellent service and friendly staff. Unfortunately, the food quality was subpar. However, it's possible that we visited on an off day. For our visit, I dined in and ordered a to-go item for my husband. When I asked the girl at the counter to recommend the most popular item from the German section for him, she handed us a box with merely a pretzel and a piece of sausage inside.

input:
I have been a fan of Charlie's for many years and I recently came back because I didn't have any jeans that fit.  I'm so happy I came back.

The girl who helped me was extremely attentive.  She pulled about 20 different pairs for me to try and explained all the nuances in the different fits and washes.  She was very patient despite my incredible indecision.  I ended up purchasing two pairs of Sebastian McCalls and I am really happy that I discovered this brand.  They are super cute and comfortable.  I love this place!
Refine this for me please:
I have been a fan of Charlie's for several years now and recently returned because I needed to find new jeans that fit me well. Coming back to this store made me incredibly happy.

The young lady who assisted me during my visit was exceptionally attentive. She took the time to pull around 20 different pairs of jeans for me to try on and provided detailed explanations about the various fits and washes. Despite my hesitation and indecisiveness, she remained incredibly patient throughout the process. In the end, I ended up purchasing two pairs of Sebastian McCalls jeans, and I couldn't be happier about discovering this fantastic brand. Not only are they incredibly cute, but they are also remarkably comfortable. I absolutely adore this store!

input: Went there on a Tuesday with my minivan, which ended up being Senior Discount Day. They didn't tell me before I paid that they won't clean or vacuum 3rd rows on Senior days. I got the Super wash, which included wax. They handed it over with large dirt smudges on the side, like it hadn't been wiped at all. A couple cup holders were barely touched and Some not at all in the front. The rest of the vacuuming wasn't good, with paper scraps still on the floor. I talked with the manager about the 3rd row and why didn't they tell me upfront when I pulled in. He said, "I won't do your 3rd row on Senior Day. That's the way we've been doing it for 15 years." I said I was new to the area and he said, "That's too bad." What kind of customer service is that?!? I usually don't write reviews, but this place was that bad.
Refine this for me please: I visited this car wash on a Tuesday with my minivan, unaware that it was Senior Discount Day. Unfortunately, I was not informed before payment that they do not clean or vacuum the 3rd rows on Senior days. Despite purchasing the Super wash with wax, the car was handed back to me with noticeable dirt smudges on the side, as if it hadn't been wiped at all. The cup holders in the front were also poorly cleaned, with some not touched at all. Additionally, the vacuuming job was subpar, as there were still paper scraps left on the floor. Dissatisfied with my experience, I spoke to the manager about the issue with the 3rd row and questioned why they didn't inform me beforehand. To my surprise, the manager responded, "I won't clean your 3rd row on Senior Day. That has been our policy for 15 years." When I mentioned being new to the area, the manager simply responded with, "That's too bad." This kind of customer service is unacceptable. I rarely write reviews, but this car wash was exceptionally disappointing.

input: i had the seafood combo-catfish (and im talkin like 5 pounds of it), red beans and rice and coleslaw.  the food was pretty damn good.  well, the real reason we walked in to this place was due to the big sign out front: "happy hour, mon-sat, 4pm-7pm, 2 for 1"  Now THAT is what im talkin about.  i ordered a margarita...and being that i'm from California, i have extremely high standards for marg's.  wasn't bad, but really wasn't great... but food made up for it!
Refine this for me please: I indulged in the seafood combo, specifically the catfish, which came in a substantial portion of about 5 pounds. Alongside, I savored red beans and rice and a side of coleslaw, all of which were incredibly appetizing. Our decision to dine at this particular establishment was primarily influenced by the prominent sign outside advertising their enticing happy hour deal: "2 for 1, happy hour, Monday to Saturday, 4 PM to 7 PM". Needless to say, that's precisely what I was looking for. Furthermore, I decided to complement my meal with a margarita, as I have notably high expectations for this particular beverage given my Californian background. Although it didn't quite meet those elevated standards, it wasn't terrible either. Nonetheless, the exceptional quality of the food fully compensated for any shortcomings in the drink department.

input:
Have been here many times and always had a great experience. When we moved to Rita Ranch 6 months ago my husband and I did a lot of rehab work on our new house and would go almost once a week to recover from the week's "work-out". It's always clean, they never gyp you on time, take the time to work on problem areas. Felicia is the best. Highly recommend them! 

Update...neck really bothering me so I went in and had the best therapeutic massage with Felicia. It was amazing! She is truly talented.
Refine this for me please:
I have been to this place numerous times and have always had a fantastic experience. Since moving to Rita Ranch six months ago, my husband and I have been doing extensive rehab work on our new house. As a way to recover from the physically demanding tasks, we have been going to this place almost every week. The cleanliness is always on point, they never skimp on the amount of time they spend working on you, and they take the time to address any problem areas. I must say, Felicia is absolutely phenomenal. I highly recommend them!

In an update, my neck has been bothering me a lot lately, so I decided to visit them again and received an incredible therapeutic massage from Felicia. It was truly amazing! Her talent is exceptional.

input:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is an old style diner that has a very small-town, homey feel.   Service is prompt and super friendly.

I had a Monte Cristo sandwich per the waitresses recommendation and I won't lie, it was pretty disappointing.  Take a stack of turkey and a couple thick slices of ham out of their respective industrial packs, microwave them with some swiss cheese on top and serve on limp french toast.  Somebody out there might like it.  I didn't. 

It came with a salad and fries, both of which were good.  The fries were thick steak fries cooked to a perfect golden brown.   

I have a feeling there are some good items on the menu.  I would especially be interested in trying breakfast.  I'll be back.
Refine this for me please:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is a charming, nostalgic diner that exudes a warm and inviting ambience, reminiscent of a quaint small-town atmosphere. The service provided is exceptionally prompt and accompanied by an incredibly friendly staff.

During my visit, I followed the waitress's recommendation and opted for a Monte Cristo sandwich. However, I must admit that it failed to live up to my expectations, leaving me somewhat disappointed. The dish essentially consisted of turkey and thickly cut slices of ham, which seemed to have been taken directly from commercially packaged sources. These were then microwaved with a layer of swiss cheese, before being served on relatively limp French toast. While this concoction may appeal to some palates, unfortunately, it did not resonate with mine.

On a brighter note, the meal did come with a side of salad and fries, both of which were commendable. The fries, in particular, were perfectly cooked steak fries, boasting a delectable golden-brown hue.

Despite the slight letdown of the Monte Cristo sandwich, I am confident that there are undoubtedly other delectable options available on the menu. In particular, I am intrigued to sample their breakfast offerings, which I have heard promising things about. Consequently, I am inclined to give the Sunrise Family Restaurant another chance in the future.

input: First time at Butcher & Bee with my husband who joined me and my co-workers for lunch one day. I love the place, it so cute with the farmhouse feel. It's really open and cute booths that offers some privacy. We had a group of 7 and it was a bit tight, but we were able to be sat right away. I ordered the pork belly gnocchi, and it was good, but not great. I felt it lacked texture. If the pork belly was crispy, it would have sealed the deal. My husband ordered the trout sandwich, unfortunately, he was disappointed that it was basically a 'tuna salad' sandwich. He did not enjoy it. For dessert, we ordered coconut macaroons, which were good. Co-workers had mixed reviews, but one ordered the KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sandwich, and he liked it. Will definitely have to give this place another try. Also, the use books for bill holders, so cute!
Refine this for me please:
During my first visit to Butcher & Bee, my husband decided to join me and my co-workers for lunch. I instantly fell in love with the adorable farmhouse ambiance of the place. The open dining area and cute booths provided a sense of privacy, although the space felt a bit tight for our group of seven. Thankfully, we were promptly seated upon arrival.

I opted for the pork belly gnocchi, which was good but not outstanding. I found it lacking in texture, and felt that the dish would have been elevated if the pork belly had a crispy finish. On the other hand, my husband ordered the trout sandwich and was disappointed to discover that it essentially resembled a "tuna salad" sandwich. Unfortunately, he did not enjoy it.

For dessert, we decided to try the coconut macaroons, which turned out to be quite tasty. Among my co-workers, opinions were split, but one person had better luck with the KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sandwich and enjoyed it.

Overall, we felt that Butcher & Bee was worth a second visit to try out more of their offerings. It's worth noting that the use of books as bill holders added an extra touch of cuteness to our dining experience.

input:
This is a really fun event for those who enjoy beer in all its forms. The drinks themselves were relatively cheap ($2-4 for a 4 oz. sample. Most were $2, some were $3, and very few were in the $4 range), however the food was really over priced ($6 for a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese? really?). For the beer lover, however, there is a wide variety of tried and true along with the new kids on the block from local, national and international lines. Also, if you like what you tasted, you can buy it on site, with a Sobeys/Safeway liquor store right on site doing specials on the sampled brews. 

We went VIP for this event, however I don't think it's worth it. What you get: a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class ($2 value) and a beer seminar ($2 value). If you do it all, or really value the glass mug, go for it! But for me, who just did the beer and food class, it wasn't worth it. 

My only complaint is for the venue, but for an event that size, you need the space. $16 for parking on top of your entry fee (though I guess most people would cab or Uber it there so you don't have to have a designated driver), and then you have to buy sample tickets on site. It gets quite expensive.
Refine this for me please:
This event is perfect for beer enthusiasts with a variety of options available. The drinks themselves are fairly priced, ranging from $2 to $4 for a 4 oz. sample. While most are $2, some are $3, and only a few are in the $4 range. However, the food is overpriced, with a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese costing $6. 

For beer lovers, there is a wide selection ranging from local, national, and international brands, including both established favorites and new arrivals. If you enjoy a particular brew, you can conveniently purchase it on-site from the Sobeys/Safeway liquor store, which offers specials on the sampled beers. 

Although we opted for the VIP experience, I don't believe it is worth the extra cost. The VIP package includes a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class (valued at $2), and a beer seminar (also valued at $2). If you truly value the glass mug or plan on participating in all the offerings, then it may be worth it. However, I found that just attending the beer and food class didn't justify the additional expense. 

One issue I had was with the venue. Given the size of the event, it's understandable that ample space is required, but the parking fees were quite steep at $16 on top of the entry fee. However, it's worth noting that most attendees would likely opt for a cab or Uber to avoid the need for a designated driver. Additionally, sample tickets must be purchased on-site, which can add up and make the overall cost quite expensive.

input: I've been here a handful of times and it's always because I don't have time to go to VN Nails near Costco where I prefer to go (they get 5 stars from me).  Kiwi Nail has always done a cheap job trying to take shortcuts wherever possible.  But today I've had it and will never go back!  After getting the typical shabby job on a fill with French tips,  I accidentally smudged two nails really badly.  They needed to be repainted and I asked her to do so... I even offered to pay extra.  The nail tech came over to look and she pressed the clumps back down and painted right back over the mess (didn't even keep the paint in the lines) then slathered so much varnish over the train wreck that it was literally dripping down my finger. After my nails were dry enough to leave,  another tech rang me up and the receipt had no place for a tip.  When I asked,  he told me I had to pay tips in cash... Well it's lucky for me I didn't have any cash.  He said I will have to tip her next time.  NEXT TIME??!!  yeah right!  There will be no next time! Save yourself the hassle and don't bother with this d@mn place!
Refine this for me please: I have frequented this establishment a few times due to time constraints, as my preferred salon, VN Nails near Costco, consistently earns a five-star rating from me. Unfortunately, Kiwi Nail consistently provides subpar services in an attempt to take shortcuts whenever possible. Today, I have reached my limit and will never return! Not only did I receive a shoddy fill with French tips, but I accidentally smudged two nails severely. I requested the technician repaint them and even offered to pay extra for the service. To my dismay, the nail tech simply pressed the clumps back down, haphazardly painted over the mess (without staying within the lines), and applied an excessive amount of varnish, causing it to drip down my fingers. Once my nails were sufficiently dry, another technician handled the payment process, but the receipt did not provide an option for tipping. When I inquired about this, the technician informed me that tips must be paid in cash. Fortunately, I did not have any cash on me. He suggested that I leave a tip during my next visit. However, their suggestions of a "next time" are far-fetched as I have no intention of returning. Spare yourself the inconvenience and avoid this dreadful establishment!

input: I'm not really into the fast food scene BUT Chick fil A is a step above. Great quality food! I don't feel like I'm eating a ton of fillers!
Refine this for me please: While I typically steer clear of fast food, Chick-fil-A stands out for its exceptional quality. Their food doesn't feel loaded with fillers, and I appreciate the high standards they maintain.

input: Square 1682 is a hotel bar I frequent. I've been there for lunch, brunch, dinner and happy hour. The food is great, the service is excellent, and the space is upscale. There is always a nice group of people that go there. Whether they are staying at the hotel or live or work in the area, you'll always find someone nice to chat with at the bar. The very best thing about the bar is the bartender that works on Mondays. His name is Dan and he is the man! He's my favorite bartender in the city and I've been to a lot of places. He always knows just what I want and remembers my name when I go there. The only reason I go to Square 1682 on Monday's is because Dan is working. If I walk by and he's not on, I keep going. He's that good! Love him and have so many great memories at this fine establishment.
Refine this for me please: Square 1682 is an upscale hotel bar that I frequently visit for lunch, brunch, dinner, and happy hour. The food is consistently great, the service is top-notch, and the ambiance is refined. It attracts a pleasant crowd, whether they are guests of the hotel or locals who live or work in the area. The highlight of this establishment is the bartender named Dan, who happens to be my absolute favorite in the entire city. His personalized service is unparalleled as he always knows exactly what I want and even remembers my name. I have created many fond memories at Square 1682, thanks to Dan's exceptional skills behind the bar. On Mondays, specifically, I make it a point to visit solely because Dan is working, as I have yet to find a bartender who compares. Walking past the bar when he is not on duty is an easy decision for me, as his expertise and friendliness are truly unmatched. I adore Dan and cherish my experiences at this remarkable establishment.

input: This is a must try, we come here frequent and we are never disappointed. Get there early so you get right in and don't have to wait. Decent selection of coffees, they have french press as well. Menu isn't huge which is nice so you can figure out what you want quickly. Food comes how in a decent time. I seem to always get the same thing (wilburt skillet) everytime I go cause it is amazing. Food just seems so fresh as well, friendly staff. You will leave full and a smile on your face.
Refine this for me please: This place is a must-try! We visit frequently and are always impressed. It's a good idea to arrive early to avoid any wait time and get seated right away. They offer a decent selection of coffees, including french press. The menu isn't overwhelming, making it easy to decide what you want. The food arrives promptly and consistently tasty. Personally, I can't resist ordering the Wilburt skillet every time because it's truly amazing. The food feels fresh, and the staff is friendly. You'll leave feeling satisfied and with a smile on your face.

input:
I tried to like this place... I really did. So much so that I went back to try it after a less that satisfactory first wax.

Wax 1- I had Despina, I think her name was. I waited a good 15 minutes after my appointment time for her to come and get me from the front. Ironic they have a 9 minute policy that if you don't show they'll cancel/charge you or whatever. Anyway, as for the experience with Despina, she did not speak to me. Like at all. Made me feel super awkward the whole time, and missed a fair few chunks of hair. She didn't ask me anything about myself, didn't tell me where to sit or how she wanted me positioned etc. Luckily I got this one half price as it was my first time at EWC.

Wax 2- I booked 3-4 weeks later with Amy Jo (based on previous Yelp reviews). She was a lot friendlier (literally the only reason why I'm giving this 1 star) BUT way too sloppy. I think it's safe to say this is the worst wax I've ever had. She left half of my hair on right before Valentine's Day! I understand they can't get all the hairs all the time but a lottttt of hair right on top was left clearly visible to my waxer. My apt was at 3.45, I walked out of the building at 3.53. Really. This includes the time spent undressing, redressing, and paying. 8 minutes is not long enough for all of this. It went so quick that when she said she was done I was actually shocked.  
I'm about to go to CVS and get some at home wax strips to finish the job... For $47+ I expect way way more. 

The staff- Another reason why I won't be returning. The ladies at the front desk are generally rude and disinterested in showing any glimpse of good customer service. ALSO, I don't like being asked if I'm going to tip - can't you give me the card machine so I can do it myself rather than make me announce if I would like to tip and how much? 

The hunt for a decent Brazilian wax in Philly continues- someone help me PLEASE!
Refine this for me please:
I made an effort to like this place, but unfortunately, I was left unsatisfied even after giving it a second chance.

During my first wax with Despina, I experienced a 15-minute delay past my appointment time before she welcomed me from the front. Interestingly enough, they enforce a 9-minute cancellation/charge policy if the customer doesn't arrive on time. In terms of the actual waxing experience, Despina did not engage in any conversation, making me feel extremely uncomfortable throughout the session. Additionally, she missed quite a few patches of hair and failed to provide any instructions on where to sit or how to position myself properly. Fortunately, I received a discount for this session since it was my first visit to EWC.

For my second wax, I scheduled an appointment with Amy Jo based on positive Yelp reviews. While she was comparatively friendlier (hence the one-star rating), her technique was extremely sloppy. I can confidently say that this was the worst wax I have ever had. She left a significant amount of hair untouched, right before Valentine's Day. I understand that it can be challenging to remove every single hair, but there was an unmistakable amount left right at the top. Furthermore, my appointment was at 3:45, and I exited the building at 3:53, including the time spent changing in and out of my clothes and settling the payment. Eight minutes is simply insufficient for all of these tasks. The process felt so rushed that I was genuinely taken aback when she claimed to have finished.

Considering the unsatisfactory experiences with the aestheticians, the front desk staff also left a poor impression. They consistently displayed rudeness and disinterest in providing good customer service. Furthermore, I found it uncomfortable when they directly asked if I was going to tip. It would be preferable for them to simply provide the card machine, allowing me to make the decision discreetly.

This disappointing encounter has left me on the quest for a reliable place for Brazilian waxes in Philly. Any assistance would be greatly appreciated.

input: Amazing and comfortable atmosphere with extremely unique flavor combinations in the dishes. The Cuban Lamb Frita is a must (add the egg! It's worth it). All of the side items are delicious, you literally can't go wrong. The staff is friendly and they are extremely efficient with the coffee refills. This has quickly become my new regular brunch spot!
Refine this for me please: The atmosphere at this restaurant is truly amazing and comfortable, creating the perfect backdrop for the incredibly unique flavor combinations found in their dishes. When visiting, be sure to try the Cuban Lamb Frita – adding the egg is definitely worth it! Additionally, all the side items are absolutely delicious, making it impossible to make a wrong choice. The staff is incredibly friendly and they excel at efficiently refilling coffee throughout your visit. All in all, this restaurant has swiftly become my go-to brunch spot!

input:
This place is good. For the lofty prices the proportions were very small. However the drinks were cheap and the service was very good. The piano is a nice touch as well. 

The cheesecake is incredible, just get it and don't look back.
Refine this for me please: This place is highly recommended. Although the prices are on the higher side, the portion sizes are disappointingly small. However, the drinks are reasonably priced and the service is exceptional. Additionally, the presence of a piano adds a pleasant touch to the ambiance. One thing you must not miss is their incredible cheesecake - simply order it without any hesitation.

input: If you beat the crowd you're in. Small but that's the only negative. Everything I've tried on the menu is AMAZING! They even have vegetarian/vegan items. I always get whatever french toast special they have. I always take people who stay with me for Mardi Gras here for breakfast before we hit the parades.
Refine this for me please: If you arrive early, you'll secure a spot in the crowd. The only downside is that the place is small. However, everything on the menu is absolutely splendid! They offer a variety of vegetarian/vegan options as well. Personally, I highly recommend trying their french toast specials. Whenever I have guests staying with me for Mardi Gras, I never miss taking them here for breakfast before we head out to enjoy the parades.

input: Butch did a great job. The tour was relaxing, informative but 2 good stops to eat and see the cemetery. I recommend going on this trip the beginning of your stay so you know where to go during your trip. He'a also pretty fun.
Refine this for me please: Butch did an excellent job delivering a satisfying tour experience. The trip was both relaxing and informative, with two notable stops to enjoy delicious meals and explore the captivating cemetery. I highly recommend embarking on this journey at the start of your stay to gain valuable insights on where to visit throughout your trip. Additionally, Butch's entertaining personality adds an extra touch of enjoyment to the adventure.

input: I love this food truck. They have the tastiest street foods like their captain crunch tilapia burrito. Who would've thought of that? The fried fish is so flakey and delicious, paired with fresh cabbage, tomatoes, avocado and Sriracha mayo. I have also tried their katsu and curry chicken which are so rich in flavor. Their Thai tea is also on point! So much to offer from a small food truck. I live in Jersey and I have driven here many times just to get food. They are so friendly and provide great food at a great price.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore this food truck! They serve the most mouthwatering street foods, including their innovative captain crunch tilapia burrito. It's truly a surprising combination, but it works wonders. The fried fish is incredibly flakey and scrumptious, complemented perfectly by the fresh cabbage, tomatoes, avocado, and Sriracha mayo. I've also had the pleasure of trying their flavorful katsu and curry chicken dishes, which are simply delightful. And let's not forget their impeccable Thai tea - it's definitely a must-try. It's astonishing how this small food truck offers such a diverse and impressive menu. I reside in Jersey, and I've made numerous trips solely to indulge in their delectable offerings. The staff is incredibly friendly, and their prices are unbeatable.

input: I was having an bad migraine and felt terrible. When woke up I had a sinus infection and my day was just going awful. I called a few places to try to get a massage in today because I knew indeed it badly. No one had any availability and I stumbled across massage envy on Google and thought to give them a try. Not only were they able to fit me in with the exact specific type I needed, but they also were able to fit my father in at the exact same time. Jen was understanding and nice, she asked me questions and checked up on me constantly. She even showed me some at home techniques I could use. She took her time, obviously did not rush. Carrie, I believe, was the name of the woman who did a foot massage on my father. He was very pleased and recommended I try it sometime. They also informed me about the membership program which not only is very cost-efficient, but also adheres to my busy schedule. I signed up on the spot with no hesitation. Friendly staff, great atmosphere, comfortable building and very calming environment! Would recommended! I feel so much better already and am going back in a month to get a 90 minute massage.
Refine this for me please:
I woke up feeling terrible with a bad migraine and later discovered that I had a sinus infection, making my day even worse. Desperate for relief, I called multiple places to find a massage appointment, but nobody had any availability. Thankfully, I stumbled upon Massage Envy through a Google search and decided to give them a try. To my surprise, they were not only able to accommodate my specific needs, but they also managed to schedule my father for a massage at the same time.

Jen, my massage therapist, was incredibly understanding and kind. She consistently checked on me and asked relevant questions. Additionally, she took the time to show me some helpful at-home techniques. It was evident that she didn't rush through the session.

Meanwhile, Carrie, the therapist who performed a foot massage on my father, did an excellent job, leaving him quite satisfied. He even recommended that I try it sometime.

In addition to the great service, the staff informed me about their membership program, which not only offers cost-efficiency but also fits my busy schedule perfectly. Without any hesitation, I signed up immediately.

The friendly staff, pleasant atmosphere, comfortable building, and calming environment made my experience at Massage Envy truly enjoyable. Already, I feel significantly better, and I am looking forward to returning in a month for a 90-minute massage.

Overall, I highly recommend Massage Envy for their exceptional service and rejuvenating experience.

input: This place is good~  The chicken is moist, the skin is crispy, the flavor is nice and smokey, this is the best kind of roast chicken I have tried. The smells (smokey, bbq) is so good and hypnotizing, just make my mouth water.  I got the double chicken family which is 2 whole chickens, literally a bed of fries underneath them, and cole slaw.  It was more than enough to feed a family of four.  The dipping sauces that come with it are also real good, i really like the mustard base one, its kinda mustardy with a chipotle flair, and there is also a green sauce that is like a salsa.  The fries are wedge fries and they make you real full because there are plenty to go around. We had leftovers because the meal was that big.  I would rather eat here than popeyes or kfc, because you get more, its healthier, and you get better service. The owners are real nice and friendly. I will be back because I know I will be craving this chicken.
Refine this for me please:
This place is amazing! The roast chicken here is absolutely delicious - the chicken is juicy, the skin is crispy, and the flavor has a delightful smokiness. It's hands down the best roast chicken I've ever tasted. The aromas of smoky and BBQ essence are so tantalizing that they make my mouth water.

I ordered the double chicken family meal, which comes with two whole chickens resting on a bed of fries, alongside a serving of cole slaw. The portion size is incredibly generous - it easily fed my entire family of four. The meal also includes dipping sauces, which are fantastic. I particularly enjoyed the mustard-based sauce with its delightful chipotle twist, and there's also a green sauce that resembles salsa.

The fries are wedge-shaped, and they're so filling that we had leftovers despite the generous portion sizes. I personally prefer this place over Popeyes or KFC because not only do you get bigger portions, but the food is also healthier overall, and the service is superior. The owners of this establishment are genuinely friendly and welcoming.

Without a doubt, I will be returning here soon because I know I'll be craving this incredible chicken again.

input:
This is as close to Japanese cuisine I get! I'm not a big fan of sushi, sashimi or maki, but I really enjoy their rice bowls and tempura. This location is not terribly busy so you won't have to wait in line for too long. 

They also provide catering options so you can have sushi and maki platters at your functions.

input:
Went to Amigos on our 40th anniversary citing the great reviews. Near to no atmosphere. Food was bleeeeah and the price was kinda high for what you get. Can't figure why people like their salsa so much as I think the stuff from "NEW YORK CITY!!" is as good and the chips are just the giant bag variety.

Gawd... all I want is some decent Mexican fare here in Boise!! Used to love Gloria's though not nearly as clean as one would like.  $47.00 with drinks and tip though I think one would do much better at one of the taco trucks as far as flavor goes.
Refine this for me please:
We decided to celebrate our 40th anniversary at Amigos based on its positive reviews, but unfortunately, the restaurant lacked atmosphere. The quality of the food was disappointing and overpriced compared to what was served. I couldn't understand why people raved about their salsa, as I believe the salsa from "NEW YORK CITY!!" is just as good, if not better, and the chips were generic and lackluster.

Honestly, all I want is to find decent Mexican food in Boise. I used to enjoy Gloria's, despite its cleanliness not meeting standards. input:
5 STAR FOOD! 
For sure one of if not the best place to get a sandwich on the beach anywhere between St Pete Beach & Clearwater Beach. All orders cooked to order. Super Size, gourmet servings and great very friendly service from the owner. Artison sandwiches for the price of Subway. Great cook with well seasoned sauces and dips usually. I always go for the daily special. Today was 3 Shrimp taco's for $6.00 The shrimp were cooked perfectly and served on fresh corn tortillas with a Kiwi sauce with some fresh peppers. Just enough spice and fruit with the shrimp. DELICIOUS. I could have had 6 they were so good. Only drawback is this place is walk up with only bench seating outside. Not a problem given the food quality for me personally but some may p[refer to sit at a table. It's on the bench or to go. A great place if you are staying at one of the local hotel to walk to. I hear they will start delivering soon. This is a local favorite for me.
The only reason I did not give 5 stars overall as the seating may be an issue for some.
Refine this for me please:
5 STAR FOOD! 

This place is undoubtedly one of, if not the best spot for sandwiches along the beach, spanning from St Pete Beach to Clearwater Beach. All orders are cooked to order, ensuring freshness and quality. The servings are generously sized, resembling gourmet meals, and the owner provides exceptionally friendly service. What's remarkable is that their artisanal sandwiches are priced comparably to Subway. The cook excels in infusing well-seasoned sauces and dips into their dishes. Personally, I always opt for the daily special, such as today's offering of three delectable shrimp tacos for only $6.00. The shrimp boasted a perfect texture and were nestled in fresh corn tortillas, accompanied by a Kiwi sauce and fresh peppers. The combination of spice and fruit complemented the shrimp seamlessly, resulting in a truly delicious experience. I was so impressed by their taste that I could have easily devoured six of them. The only minor inconvenience is their walk-up setup with only outdoor bench seating available. However, considering the exceptional quality of the food, this is not a problem for me, although some individuals might prefer sitting at a table. It's either bench seating or takeout from here. Additionally, it is convenient for those lodging at local hotels, as it is within walking distance. I've heard that delivery services will soon be offered. Overall, this establishment remains a favorite among locals. I withheld one star in my rating due to the limited seating, which might be an issue for some individuals.

input:
We had dinner here after a long day at the convention center.  We asked to sit in a quieter area, and they found us a nice table in a side room.  Service was attentive and professional.  Our waiter recommended the aged ribeye steak--"best steak ever."  I didn't think I wanted an entire 18-ounce boneless, so he suggested we split it.  We did--certainly one of the "best steaks ever"--cooked perfectly medium rare and it was plenty for both of us.  Of course, we also had the signature shrimp cocktail (horseradish) and the iceberg lettuce wedge with crumbled bacon (very pancetta-like).   OK, iceberg wedge isn't the most exciting salad, but it's great when done well, which this was.  
   My only disappointment was a wine list that had a very limited choice of medium-priced wines by the bottle, so wine selection took a while.  A small complaint, so I would rate H & I  4.5 stars if possible.
Refine this for me please: We enjoyed our dinner at H & I after a tiring day at the convention center. Upon requesting a quieter area, the staff promptly seated us in a pleasant side room. The service was attentive and professional. Our waiter highly recommended the aged ribeye steak, claiming it to be the "best steak ever." Initially hesitant about the large portion, he kindly suggested that we split it. The steak turned out to be truly outstanding, cooked to a perfect medium rare and more than enough to satisfy both of us. Additionally, we couldn't resist trying the signature shrimp cocktail with a hint of horseradish and the iceberg lettuce wedge topped with crumbled bacon that tasted similar to pancetta. Despite the simple nature of the iceberg wedge, it was prepared exceptionally well. However, the only letdown was the limited choice of medium-priced wines by the bottle on the wine list, which took some time to decide. Nevertheless, this minor setback would only slightly detract from our overall dining experience. If possible, I would rate H & I 4.5 stars.

input: The worst Italian food I have ever tasted!!! I'm far from Italian, but I can make a MEAN lasagna & spaghetti myself compared to this place. 1st of all, we waited 45mins patiently w/ a hungry Hubby, 2yr old, 7yr old, & myself. When we finally got seated, the waitress was very polite, but forgetful at times. Didnt drink any alcohol or sodas but the lemonade was very tart & the garlic bread was not-so-fresh...had to request for some fresh bread after my family devoured the 1st basket from starving & waiting for so long. I ordered the stuffed shells & chicken parmagiana. The salad was very tasty; however, they only have Italian dressing...no ranch or anything else. I am not a picky eater & rarely complain, but the stuffed shells & parmagiana chicken tasted HORRIBLE!! The chicken was very bland & the stuffed shells were hard & overbaked. The meranera sauce tasted like it was old or aged too long (if there's ever such a thing, lol). I could not bring myself to eat my entree. I had to send it back. I heard the lady at the table next to ours say the salmon was good, so I figured the salmon might be safe. It was actually very good! I was still very disappointed after this restaurant was referred to me by many. I felt like they got an easy $50 bucks out of me. I would have rathered gone to the olive garden or macaroni grill. If u r looking for an awesome authentic Italian cusine restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. The only reason we didn't go there is b/c it was out of the way from where we were going.  It's pretty far from where we live but always worth the drive. Everything is freshly made & u can definite tell the difference! I'm sorry Caruso, but I don't think my family will be coming here ever again!
Refine this for me please:
The Italian food at this restaurant was the worst I have ever tasted. Despite not being Italian myself, I can make a much better lasagna and spaghetti compared to this place. Firstly, we had to wait for 45 minutes with a hungry husband, a 2-year-old, a 7-year-old, and myself. Once we were finally seated, the waitress was polite but forgetful. We didn't order any alcohol or sodas, but the lemonade was overly tart and the garlic bread was not fresh. We had to ask for fresh bread after finishing the first basket due to our hunger and the long wait. 

I ordered the stuffed shells and chicken parmigiana. The salad was tasty, but they only had Italian dressing, no ranch or any other options. I am not a picky eater and rarely complain, but the stuffed shells and chicken parmigiana were absolutely terrible. The chicken was bland and the stuffed shells were hard and overbaked. The marinara sauce tasted old or aged for too long, if that's even possible. I couldn't bring myself to eat my entree and had to send it back. While sitting there, I overheard the lady at the table next to ours say that the salmon was good, so I decided to try it. Surprisingly, the salmon was actually very good.

Even though this restaurant was recommended to me by many people, I was still extremely disappointed. It felt like they easily took $50 from me. I would have rather gone to Olive Garden or Macaroni Grill. If you're looking for an authentic and delicious Italian cuisine restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. It's a bit far from where we live, but it's always worth the drive. Everything there is freshly made and you can definitely taste the difference. I'm sorry Caruso, but my family will never be returning here again.

input:
If you are looking to be impressed by French-German dishes in New Orleans, please go to Luke Restaurant, I know I was. 

The restaurant is located in the Central Business District, next to the Hilton and in the former Masonic Temple Building, so there is that historic vibe to the restaurant. The front room is a lot more grand than the back room (where we were seated), but that is offset by views of the open kitchen. 

Apparently they only want to seat people with reservations, so since we did not have one, we were refused seating until 9:15pm (it was 6:45pm) but with a little back and forth, we ended up waiting only 15 minutes before we were seated. However, as we walked through the restaurant to the back room, way too many tables were empty that it made no sense that they acted that way. A lot of tables still remained empty throughout the meal.

I decided to start out my meal with a cocktail. I originally wanted the Mint Julep but they were out so I had the Riverbend (vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries & ginger ale) at the recommendation of the server. It was a relatively sweet cocktail, with the ginger ale being the most powering flavor, but you could still taste the alcohol.

My friend choose a regular starter and ordered a cup of the Crawfish Bisque. She ate all of it so I am assuming she liked it, but she did complain of a sour aftertaste.

My boyfriend skipped the appetizers and went straight for the entree. He always seems to find the most basic item on the menu and order it. He had the Luke Burger (bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, Swiss cheese) and was raving about it. One thing I can tell you, it was a very good size. 

My friend had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages. She loved it.

I have an obsession with mussels so I had the classic Moules et Frites. Although only having two simply ingredients (garlic & thyme) in the broth, the flavors stood out and the taste was a lot bolder than others I have had with a lot more ingredients. The house-made fries were scrumptious. These are the best kind.

Even with all that food, we still made room for dessert. We first had the Bread Pudding which was delicious but quite sweet. I am also not a fan of over sauced foods.

One wasn't enough so we also ordered the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It was superb and not too sweet which is a plus for me. The little cookies on top added nothing to the dessert and if anything could have been left off.

All that good food, I still have to give props to our server. He was amazing and engaging. The front desk soured the mood a little bit a first but he more than made up for it. I couldn't have asked for anyone better.
Refine this for me please:
If you want to experience impressive French-German cuisine in New Orleans, I highly recommend dining at Luke Restaurant. Situated in the Central Business District, this restaurant is housed in the historic former Masonic Temple Building, giving it a unique and charming ambiance. While the front room exudes grandeur, the back room offers views of the open kitchen.

It's worth noting that Luke Restaurant primarily caters to patrons with reservations. As we arrived without one, we were initially denied seating until 9:15pm despite it only being 6:45pm. However, after a bit of negotiation, we managed to secure a table within 15 minutes. Interestingly, we noticed several empty tables throughout the restaurant, which made their seating policy seem unnecessary. This remained the case during our entire meal.

To begin our dining experience, I decided to try a cocktail. Although my first choice, the Mint Julep, was unavailable, the server recommended the Riverbend cocktail (vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries, and ginger ale). It proved to be a moderately sweet concoction with the ginger ale dominating the flavors, though the alcohol was still detectable.

My friend opted for a traditional starter and ordered a cup of the Crawfish Bisque. She thoroughly enjoyed it, finishing the entire cup. However, she did mention a slightly sour aftertaste.

Bypassing appetizers, my boyfriend selected an entree and went straight for the Luke Burger (bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, Swiss cheese). He couldn't stop praising its taste and sizable portion.

Meanwhile, my friend indulged in the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" paired with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille, and green onion sausages. She absolutely loved it.

As a lover of mussels, I ordered the classic Moules et Frites. Despite the simple broth containing only garlic and thyme, the flavors were robust and outshined other versions I've tried with more ingredients. The homemade fries served alongside were irresistible.

Despite already enjoying a filling meal, we couldn't resist trying the desserts. We started with the delectable Bread Pudding, which, although delicious, leaned towards being overly sweet for my taste. I also prefer dishes with less sauce.

Unable to stop at just one dessert, we also ordered the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It proved to be superb, striking a perfect balance of sweetness. The addition of small cookies on top did not enhance the dessert and could have been omitted.

Lastly, I must commend our server. He provided exceptional service and was highly engaging. Although the front desk initially dampened our experience, he more than made up for it. I couldn't have asked for a better server.

Refine this for me please:

input:

A co-worker told me about Gemological Resources Inc (GRI) and the wonderful experience he and his now wife had with them. Since it was a local shop I gave them a shot not knowing what to expect. Wow.... What a great experience! 

From the moment we (my girlfriend and I) walked into GRI, it felt right. We met with Terry initially to get a feel for GRI's work, as well as to discuss ring options.Terry is an encyclopedia of knowledge; it was a true lesson on everything we needed to know about diamonds, rings, etc. Very much worth taking the time to meet with him. He not only shared much of his knowledge, but also listened and got a good feel for what my girlfriend liked. The initial meet was a success and I felt confident that GRI would be the right place to go once I was ready to make the decisive move solo.

When the time came I met up with GRI again, this time with Nirali who works closely with Terry. Because I wanted a unique, special, one-of-a-kind engagement ring I decided on a custom design ring. The CAD images and designs were perfect! To top it off, Nirali found me a high quality and very well priced diamond; this after I spent weeks personally searching for the right diamond. After a reasonable deposit and a couple of weeks, the ring was finally ready. And let me tell you, it exceeded all expectations! It was a hundred times better than anything I had seen before. GRI truly hit it out of the park! Fast forward a few months, and my wife is head over heels in love with her ring. We also had our wedding bands created by GRI, and they too are perfect. input:

input:
I love it!  The reviews were great and I was desperate for good carry out, so we decided to try Pizzaville (is anyone else picturing JT singing - Bring it on down to Pizzaville?).  The prices are a bit high, but the quality of the food is great!  The pizza crust is between a hand tossed and thin crust.  Perfectly crunchy ends and just chewy enough in the middle.  Good quality cheese and tangy tomato sauce. I ordered it with just mushrooms and they put on a lot!   I also asked for heavy sauce.  They put extra sauce on the pizza and even gave me an extra container of sauce in case I needed more. 

I can't decide which was better, the pizza or "breadsticks."  I say "breadsticks" because they were really more like garlic bread strips.  So buttery and garlicy, they were great even without sauce.  I'm ashamed to say I ate nearly the entire order myself.  

The employees are very nice and helpful.  The store is clean. I need to go back and try their lunch buffet.
Refine this for me please:
I absolutely love Pizzaville! After hearing great reviews and craving some good take-out, my friends and I decided to give it a try. Admittedly, the prices are a bit on the higher side, but the quality of the food definitely makes up for it.

The pizza at Pizzaville is simply fantastic. The crust strikes the perfect balance between hand tossed and thin crust. It has crunchy ends and just the right amount of chewiness in the middle. The cheese used is of good quality and the tomato sauce has a delightful tang. I opted for a pizza with just mushrooms, and they did not skimp on the toppings at all. It was loaded with mushrooms, exactly how I like it. Additionally, I had requested extra sauce, and they went above and beyond by not only generously putting extra sauce on the pizza but also providing an extra container of sauce in case I needed more.

Now, let's talk about the "breadsticks." I put the term in quotes because they were more like garlic bread strips, but boy were they delicious! Each strip was buttery, garlicky, and satisfying on its own, even without any sauce. I must admit, I ended up devouring almost the entire order by myself. They were simply irresistible.

Not only is the food top-notch, but the employees at Pizzaville are also incredibly friendly and helpful. The store itself is clean and well-maintained, creating a pleasant dining experience.

I am already planning my next visit to Pizzaville, especially to try out their lunch buffet. I have a feeling it will be just as amazing as their other offerings.

input: The service was good and the staff was polite, but the food was bland and lacked flavor. The drinks were ok about what you would expect of a chain restaurant. If you are looking for somewhere to sit Down for a quick lunch this might be your place.
Refine this for me please: The service provided was satisfactory and the staff exhibited politeness. However, the food lacked flavor and was quite bland. The drinks, while not exceptional, were in line with the average quality expected from a chain restaurant. If you're seeking a place to sit down and have a quick lunch, this venue might be suitable for your needs.

input:
I thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance. The decor was modern and cozy. The lighting was appropriate for dinner but terrible for selfies lol. Our waiter was OK. He seemed to be very hyper and impatient. I almost felt like he was rushing to take care of us instead of genuinely trying to give us an experience. I ordered the Shrimp Breaux Bridge and it was tasty. Nothing to phone home about but it was good. My friend ordered the Balsamic Salmon and it was good as well. It kind of reminded me of an Asian dish. Another friend had the Pesto Crusted Idaho Trout. It was cooked and flavored very nicely. 

I also ordered the Zangria White which is a sangria that was supposed to include strawberries, blueberries and diced apples... and i only got apples. IF there is an item on the menu that contains SEASONAL FRUITS AND VEGGIES ETC.... DISCLOSE SOMEWHERE ON THE MENU THAT THOSE THINGS ARE OUT OF SEASON. It definitely wouldve made a difference in my drink order. But overall the sangria was OK. 

I would go back because Im sure the service is better that what I experienced and I have heard amazing things about the menu.
Refine this for me please:
I thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance of the restaurant. The decor was a perfect mix of modern and cozy, creating a comfortable atmosphere. The lighting, although great for dinner, wasn't ideal for taking selfies, but that was not a big issue. 

However, I have mixed feelings about our waiter. While he was energetic, he seemed somewhat impatient and in a hurry, which made me question his dedication to providing us with a memorable dining experience. 

When it came to the food, I ordered the Shrimp Breaux Bridge, which was tasty but nothing extraordinary. It was a good dish, but didn't leave a lasting impression. On the other hand, my friend's choice of the Balsamic Salmon was good, with flavors reminiscent of Asian cuisine. Another friend had the Pesto Crusted Idaho Trout, which was excellently cooked and seasoned.

Unfortunately, my drink order didn't meet my expectations. I opted for the Zangria White, a sangria that promised strawberries, blueberries, and diced apples, but I was only served apples. I believe it would have been helpful if the menu had mentioned that certain ingredients were out of season. Despite this disappointment, the sangria was still decent overall.

Despite the inconsistencies in my experience, I would be willing to give this restaurant another chance. I believe that the service might be better than what I encountered, and I have heard great things about the rest of the menu.

input:
Despite being a spin-off at the burgers from Rouge, I actually think that the burgers here are, dare I say it, better then flagship restaurants.
Over the last year they keep expanding their burger and toppings options by editing the little placard next to the registers, instead of changing their giant menuboard every time  they decide to add a new cheese or vegetable you can put on the burger.

I've been here a few times, trying the 500 (lettuce, bacon, cheddar, special sauce) delicious, and also making my own combos with their Kobe Beef burger (I think its worth the extra few bucks). I like it with truffle cheese and grilled onions. The brioche bun also really makes these burgers something special.

Their fries are also extremely delicious. As a huge fan of truffle oil, I can never resist getting their truffle oil fries. When they come warm out of the fryer, coated in truffle oil, there is just no better taste known to man.

Most important of all, they are open late on weekends.
Refine this for me please:
Refined version: Despite being a spin-off of Rouge, I honestly believe that the burgers here are better than those served at the flagship restaurants. In the past year, they have continuously expanded their burger and toppings options by simply updating a small placard near the registers, eliminating the need to change their large menu board every time a new cheese or vegetable is added.

During my visits, I have tried their 500 burger (consisting of lettuce, bacon, cheddar, and special sauce) and found it to be absolutely delicious. Additionally, I have enjoyed creating my own combinations using their Kobe Beef burger, which I believe is worth the additional cost. My personal favorite includes truffle cheese and grilled onions, and the brioche bun elevates the overall burger experience.

Their fries are also exceptionally tasty. As a passionate fan of truffle oil, I simply cannot resist their truffle oil fries. When these fries are served straight out of the fryer, coated in truffle oil, there is simply no better taste in the world.

Furthermore, one of the most advantageous features of this place is that they remain open late on weekends, making it a convenient option for those seeking a late-night meal.

input: Tried this place the other day the pizza was not very good at all the place before this one was so much better all home made food with it would've stuck around
Refine this for me please: I recently tried this place and unfortunately, the pizza was quite disappointing. I had previously visited a different place that was far superior, with delicious homemade food. If only I had stayed there instead.

input: Stopped in for a quick lunch. Jalapeno burger was great.  Sittin' on the patio's pretty cool.  Definitely be back.
Refine this for me please: I stopped by for a quick lunch and was impressed with the jalapeno burger. The experience of sitting on the patio was enjoyable, providing a cool and relaxed atmosphere. I will definitely return in the future.

input:
I really, really, really like so much about this hotel. For starters, it's BEAUTIFUL!!  Everytime I go to Reno, this is where I stay and I will continue to stay here when I go!!

PRO's:

1. The Spa is amazing! The staff working there are so friendly and helpful.The pools in the spa area are so clean. There were plenty of towels, water, juice, etc. 

2. The rooms were very clean and organized. 

3. The front desk staff was very nice and helpful. We didnt like the location of our room, so they moved us to another location with no problems.

4. They have a little diner that is there open 24 hours and has good food. Granted its a bit expensive, but it's a casino, what do you expect?


CON's:

1. The bathrooms in the hotel rooms didnt have fans, so when you're in the shower it gets so steamy, so fast!

2. We ordered rooms services and we ordered coffee as well, and they didnt bring creamer.
Refine this for me please:
Refined version:

I absolutely love this hotel for so many reasons. Firstly, it is absolutely stunning! Whenever I visit Reno, this is always my first choice and I will definitely continue staying here in the future.

Here are the pros:

1. The Spa is fantastic! The staff is incredibly friendly and helpful. The pools in the spa area are always clean and well-maintained, and they provide plenty of towels, water, juice, and other amenities.

2. The rooms are impeccably clean and well-organized.

3. The front desk staff is very kind and accommodating. When we didn't like the location of our room, they graciously moved us to another location without any issues.

4. They have a charming diner that stays open 24 hours and serves delicious food. It may be slightly pricey, but given that it is a casino, it is to be expected.

Now for the cons:

1. The hotel rooms' bathrooms lack fans, which leads to a quick buildup of steam when showering. It can get quite uncomfortable.

2. We ordered room service, including coffee, but unfortunately, they forgot to bring creamer.

Overall, despite these minor cons, I still highly recommend this hotel for its beautiful aesthetic, amazing spa, cleanliness, friendly staff, and convenient amenities.

input: It was great. The your was interesting if you're in to tours. The beer was good. The atmosphere was the best part. A couple of Tvs for sports, board games, live music, and yours every hours. input: This place is terrible. Terrible service, terrible food, and the place is dirty beyond reason.  Really hope I don't have food poisoning after eating here, but I wouldn't bet on it.
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely dreadful. The service is abysmal, the food is unspeakably bad, and the overall hygiene is shockingly poor. I sincerely pray that I don't end up with food poisoning after dining here, although I have little confidence in that outcome.

input:
My personal favorite wine and liquor store in Nashville.  The staff is usually very friendly and helpful without being pretentious.  You can ask for a $10 dollar bottle of wine recommendation without being scoffed at.  The selection is good and the prices are comparable with other liquor stores in town.

They readily offer recommendations for affordable choices, even if you're looking for a $10 bottle of wine, without any condescension. input: When my daughter was about a year-and-a-half old, Linda, the owner, helped me out by taking her for a drop in a couple times. My daughter is now four and a half and I have a one-and-a-half-year-old son. I switched school districts from Carson to Washoe and I kept going to all of these other daycare places and not getting a great feel, as well as the fact that they were totally booked for having an infant\toddler. I needed a place for both of my kids and there was just no where for my son..... My gut kept telling me go back to Circle of Friends. I've been extremely happy. Are there always going to be kids who attended daycare that I do not agree with their behavior? absolutely! There is no way to get around that whether it is in school, daycare, or a sports team or some other organized deal. I try the best of my ability to not let those other children's behaviors influence my own and we talk about it. Well the best you can for a 4 year old! I really like Linda and the whole staff. She has a little turnover and I really like that. The first place that my kids were at in Carson had turn over all the time..... The second place was a home daycare so she didn't turn over herself, and the other place was a mother and daughter run joint as well. They had very little turnover. That's important to me that employees stick around. So, my kid has been flourishing both emotionally and academically. She's picking up things that I'm totally surprised about.... Like starfish have two stomachs and octopus have 9 brains.... I didn't believe her and I had to Google them! I didn't read the Yahoo review, but people are always going to have mixed situations with whatever's going on for them. All I know is that Linda and her daughter helped me out greatly when I was in need several years ago, and she helped me out greatly this time and it's been a great fit. I'm very happy and content.
Refine this for me please:
When my daughter was around 18 months old, Linda, the owner of Circle of Friends daycare, kindly helped me out by watching her on a couple of occasions. Fast forward to now, my daughter is four and a half years old and I also have a one and a half year old son. After switching school districts and visiting various other daycare options, I couldn't find a suitable place that would accept my infant/toddler son and gave me a good feeling about their care. My gut instinct kept telling me to go back to Circle of Friends. I have been extremely satisfied with their services.

Of course, there will always be kids in daycare whose behavior I don't necessarily agree with. This is something I have come to accept as part of any group setting - whether it's school, sports, or any other organized activity. However, I make a conscious effort not to let other children's behavior influence my own kids, and we have open discussions about it, to the best of my ability to explain things to a four year old.

What I really appreciate about Circle of Friends is the consistency in its staff. Linda ensures that her employees stick around, which has been a rarity in my past experiences with daycare. This stability has contributed to my child's positive growth, both emotionally and academically. It's amazing to see her learning things that surprise me, like starfish having two stomachs and octopuses having nine brains. I initially doubted her, but had to resort to Googling to confirm her knowledge!

I haven't read the Yahoo review, as I understand that people's experiences can vary. All I know is that Linda and her daughter have been a great help to me in the past and present, providing a wonderful fit for my children. I am genuinely pleased and content with the care they receive at Circle of Friends.

input: Great new location on Central. Great staff and atmosphere! Looks like they have found a place where they will thrive.
Refine this for me please: Exceptional new location situated right in the heart of Central. The staff members are truly outstanding and the atmosphere is absolutely fantastic. It appears that they have discovered the perfect setting where their success is guaranteed to flourish.

input: First time here and I'm not disappointed. Great seasoning on the seafood. I ordered oysters and their $45 combo and some garlic chicken wings for a family of six. It was more than enough for us. Only thing I can complain about is she messed up on our order.

input: Chicken was salty, I ordered 1/2 chicken, rice and plantains to go for lunch. With the chicken and rice, I only received 2 pieces of plantains & paid I've $8 for this meal. input: Pretty average take-out chinese. Not bad, not the best, but id definitely eat there again. ***update--- just ate there again and they got our complex delivery perfect and the food was excellent! 5 stars now!!

input:
We've been going to the Rib Cook-Off for a few years now, but apparently I've never taken the time to review it. We have our day pretty much planned out before heading down there. 

We walk to the bus stop by our house, the bus takes us directly to the Sparks bus station for a whopping $2 each. No parking, no driving through crowds, and no paying for parking. Winning.

From the bus station, we head immediately to Great Basin to get a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. Beer is a must for battling these crowds and the large beers are worth the price!

If you have the JA Nugget mobile app, it will tell you where every vendor is and show it on a map. No more mindless wandering looking for your favorite vendor. I don't have a favorite, but go off of recommendations from friends, co-workers, etc.

Some vendors take cards, but we always make sure to bring plenty of cash. 

Be sure to walk through the non-rib vendors too. We got a couple of hats this year, which are nice to have at the event, but are also great beach hats for next year.

Saturday was a whole day affair and required us taking a cab back home. But because there was practically no crowd on Monday, we were able to get a beer, some food, and still use our bus transfer to get back home. Food stops being served at 5:00 pm on Monday and the vendors also start selling off extra food at crazy cheap prices.
Refine this for me please:
We have been attending the Rib Cook-Off for several years now, but surprisingly, I have never taken the time to write a review about it. Before heading to the event, we already have our day planned out.

To avoid the hassle of parking and driving through the crowds, we opt for walking to the nearby bus stop from our house. For just $2 each, the bus takes us directly to the Sparks bus station. It's a convenient and cost-effective way to reach the event.

Upon arriving at the bus station, our first stop is always Great Basin to grab a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. It's essential to have a beer in hand to tackle the busy crowds, and the large beers are definitely worth the price.

If you have the JA Nugget mobile app, it becomes effortless to locate any vendor and see their location on a map. No more aimless wandering in search of your favorite vendor. While I don't have a personal preference, I rely on recommendations from friends and co-workers.

While some vendors accept cards, we always make sure to bring plenty of cash to be on the safe side.

Don't forget to explore the non-rib vendors as well. This year, we purchased a couple of hats which not only came in handy during the event but also make great beach hats for the following year.

On Saturday, the event consumed the entire day, and we had to take a cab back home. However, Monday had significantly fewer crowds, allowing us to enjoy a beer, some food, and still utilize our bus transfer to return home. Food stops being served at 5:00 pm on Monday, and vendors often sell off excess food at incredibly low prices.

input:
Excellent food and bar. Slow service.

A friend and I stopped here during an evening of bar hopping in the CBD. We were seated promptly and given our menus, which are half-French, half-English. Not a big deal for anyone who can read French and/or has been living in Louisiana for a reasonable amount of time, but definitely something tourists should be wary of. I didn't have any alcohol because I was the designated driver, but I can say that their drink menu is extensive, and the bar was packed from the moment we arrived until the moment we left. 

This restaurant's biggest strength is it's food. I tasted their crab bisque, and had Poulet Grand-Mère as my entrée. Both were excellent. The latter arrived in a wide cast-iron bowl, which I'm sure has a more proper name, but was an interesting touch nonetheless.

The service was why I gave this restaurant 4/5 instead of 5/5. Most of the wait staff seemed to be interns from culinary school. The handful we dealt with were very friendly, but would do well to be a little more attentive. For example, the server who brought us our desserts ran off before we could ask for spoons to eat the dessert with. 

In summary, a good dining experience, but I think I would rather continue exploring new restaurants in the area before returning.
Refine this for me please:
This restaurant offers excellent food and has a well-stocked bar, but the service is slow. My friend and I decided to dine here during a night of bar hopping in the CBD. We were quickly seated and handed menus that were a mix of French and English. While not a major issue for those familiar with French or Louisiana culture, it could be confusing for tourists. As I was the designated driver, I didn't have any alcohol, but I noticed that their drink menu was extensive and the bar was filled with patrons throughout our visit.

The highlight of this restaurant is undoubtedly its food. I had the pleasure of trying their delectable crab bisque and opted for the Poulet Grand-Mère as my main course, which was superb. The presentation of the latter dish in a wide cast-iron bowl added an interesting touch.

However, I found the service to be lacking, which is why I gave this restaurant a rating of 4/5 instead of 5/5. Most of the wait staff seemed to be culinary school interns. While they were friendly, they could benefit from being more attentive. For instance, one server hastily left after delivering our desserts, neglecting to provide us with spoons to enjoy them.

In conclusion, this restaurant offers a positive dining experience, but given the abundance of other eateries in the area, I would prefer to explore new options before considering a return visit.

input:
I had just moved to Nashville and one of my friends told me I HAD to come here. We're not both from here originally so technically we were still tourists at this point. Anyways, I went around 9:15 and the line wasn't too bad - I'd say a 5-10 minute wait. The food was awesome. I had the chocolate chip pancakes which were to die for. The sausage side I had didn't rock my world then again it's not the Side Dish Pantry. You don't pay at the table - they ring you up by the door to try and get people in and out fast which seems to work because the line is always moving fairly fast. 


Rip : I drive by it almost every morning - if you want to avoid the line go either RIGHT when they open to around 7:15
Refine this for me please:
Refined: After recently relocating to Nashville, one of my friends strongly recommended a visit to this place. Being newcomers ourselves, we were technically still tourists. So, one morning at around 9:15, I decided to check it out. Surprisingly, the line wasn't too long, with a wait time of about 5-10 minutes.
