input:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, one can only expect they want some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been here a couple of times, but they were the ones that wanted to go, due to their lunch special. It's a nice, well know restaurant that offers a 17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a 4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I got the Bloody Mary and it was a great size for the price. It was spicy and hit the spot.
They text message you when your table is ready, so were able to walk around the quarter while we waited. Thank god a lot of restaurants are getting rid of the those buzzers that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 
We sat down to a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, were ok. They were busy, but forgot a couple of things we asked for. It was still a great experience though!
I got the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was one of the best I have had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection and the read beans were seasoned very well. It came with cornbread, but it was very dry. After this lunch at noon, I didn't find myself hungry till it was basically time for bed. It was a very generous portion and well worth the money.

Muriel's is a great way to get a classic, good quality New Orleans meal at a decent price. The location is spectacular, and the history behind the restaurant made for great conversation at the table.
Definitely check it out if you are in the Quarter!
Refine this for me please:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, it is expected that they would want to try some classic New Orleans dishes. On a couple of previous visits, my friends had insisted on going to a well-known restaurant that offers a $17.00 lunch special, which includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a $4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I decided to try the Bloody Mary, which was reasonably priced and satisfyingly spicy.

While we waited for our table, we received a text message notification, allowing us to explore the Quarter. It was a relief that the restaurant didn't give us those annoying buzzers that make you feel like you're under house arrest. Our table was conveniently located near open shutters, providing a lovely atmosphere. The servers were decent, although they seemed occupied and forgot a few of our requests. Nonetheless, it was still a memorable experience.

For my meal, I chose the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was hands down one of the best I've ever tasted, and the pork chop was perfectly cooked and seasoned. Unfortunately, the cornbread that came with the meal was quite dry. After this hearty lunch at noon, I didn't feel hungry again until it was practically bedtime. The portion was incredibly generous and definitely worth the price.

Muriel's is an excellent choice for those looking to enjoy a classic, high-quality New Orleans meal without breaking the bank. The location is breathtaking, and the restaurant's rich history provides interesting conversation topics at the table. Don't miss out on the opportunity to visit Muriel's if you find yourself in the French Quarter!

input: We stopped here's on the recommendation of our shuttle driver.  The red velvet ice cream is wonderful!! Pieces of cake. Creamy goodness.  Yum!
Refine this for me please: We made a pitstop at this place on our shuttle driver's suggestion, and boy were we delighted! The red velvet ice cream they serve is absolutely divine, with heavenly chunks of cake mixed in. Its irresistibly creamy texture is pure bliss. Simply yum!

input:
I ate here for the first time today.  The woman that works behind the counter is really friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount ($7), since I work nearby.

The food itself is pretty average for American-Chinese food.  Nothing great, but not bad either.  My sauce was greasy, but the food in general doesn't seem to be (e.g. fried rice).  They do have some vegetarian options which are of the tofu variety as opposed to fake meat. 

I would go back since they have lunch specials that come with rice and either a drink, soup, or egg roll ($5.75).

EDIT: I got super sick after leaving this review, and I'm 99% sure it was food poisoning.  Will not be returning.
Refine this for me please:
Today, I had my first dining experience at this establishment. The courteous woman behind the counter pleasantly surprised me by offering to waive the minimum credit order amount of $7, recognizing that I work nearby.

In terms of the food itself, it can be categorized as average for American-Chinese cuisine. While it did not exceed expectations, it also did not disappoint. I did find that the sauce I had was slightly greasy, although the overall dishes, such as the fried rice, did not exhibit the same greasiness. Furthermore, they do provide vegetarian options, primarily featuring tofu rather than imitation meat.

I am inclined to revisit this place due to their lunch specials, which comprise a serving of rice accompanied by a choice of drink, soup, or egg roll, all priced at a reasonable $5.75.

UPDATE: Unfortunately, after writing this review, I fell severely ill and strongly suspect it was due to food poisoning. Consequently, I have decided not to return to this establishment.

input:
Delicious! 

I wish they took reservations, but my friend and her fiance go there nice and early so that we could snag a seat inside (it was cold out!). 

We ordered the bianco salad ( to share between 2) and the western addition (to share between 4).

I thought the salad was tasty but nothing special, despite the white chocolate shavings. Cute idea, but not enough crunch or pizazz to make the salad seem really fabulous.

The pizza, however, was pretty darn good. We ordered it deep dish to try their special cornmeal crust and were pretty impressed. 
The crust tastes a little bit like cornbread, a little bit like pizza dough, a tiny bit like grease (the good kind) and a lot like YUM!

I don't know if it was the best pizza I've ever had, but it was very good. It would be even better if it were a tad cheaper, and didn't get so crowded! But definitely worth a visit if you're in the area!
Refine this for me please:
Delicious! Although it would have been better if they accepted reservations, my friend and her fiance were kind enough to arrive early to secure us a seat inside since it was chilly outside. We decided to order the bianco salad, meant to be shared between the two of us, and the western addition, which we split between four people. 

To be honest, the salad was tasty but didn't quite stand out, even with the addition of white chocolate shavings. Although it was a cute idea, it lacked the desired crunch and pizazz to truly make it fabulous. 

On the other hand, the pizza was undeniably delicious. We opted for the deep dish with the special cornmeal crust and were pleasantly surprised by how impressive it was. The crust had a delightful combination of cornbread and pizza dough flavors, with just a hint of satisfying greasiness (the good kind). It was definitely a YUM-worthy experience. 

While I can't say it was the absolute best pizza I've ever had, it was certainly very good. I do wish it were a bit more affordable and less crowded, but it's definitely worth a visit if you happen to be in the area!

input: A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without... I don't know I lost the metaphor. It's just sad is what it is. You need books, you need a place to browse, talk with other book lovers, and listen to book readings. Indy Reads is that place. And it's more than that because all proceeds support a great cause, adult literacy. Most of the books are used so donate a book and pick up a new (used) one. You may be surprised at all the books they have that you didn't even know you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you're looking for, you can order it. The one thing I don't really like is that the $1 children's books can be jammed so tightly that it's hard to look through them. The kids books are also arranged by color, which makes it harder for me to distinguish between titles as I glance through. Prices are excellent throughout, and the space is really nice. Check it out!
Refine this for me please: A downtown without a bookstore is like a barren landscape, devoid of a crucial cultural hub. It's a void that leaves a community without a place to escape, explore, and engage with literature. However, Indy Reads emerges as a beacon of hope and enlightenment. Not only does it offer a sanctuary for book enthusiasts to browse, bond, and revel in the magic of written words, but it also serves as a formidable force in promoting adult literacy through its charitable endeavors. The majority of books at Indy Reads are pre-loved, creating an opportunity for individuals to donate their own books while discovering hidden literary gems. Its vast collection leaves patrons pleasantly surprised, presenting them with books they never knew they desired. While there is also a small assortment of new books available, it is worth noting that the children's section can be quite cramped and disorganized, making it challenging to peruse. The pricing, on the other hand, is consistently reasonable, and the atmosphere within the store is undeniably pleasant. In essence, Indy Reads is a gem waiting to be explored in the heart of downtown—definitely worth a visit.

input: Wish I would have came on Yelp and read the previous reviews, it would've saved me a lot of time and frustration. I ran in today to see if someone could take a look at my right passenger front wheel. My tire pressure light was on and I noticed a piece of tire was lifted. I go in and he tells me it's a couple hours wait. Ok, I'll give you that I just showed up so the wait thing is to be expected. I ask the guy if I can make an appointment to come back. He says its first come first serve. Really? When I've made appts previously with other Just Tires? Why not just say you don't want my service? Bottom line? Guy was rude and lacked any customer service. Went down the street to Mr. Tire and was in and out with a replaced new tire in half an hour. Oh, and they appeared WAY busier based on the waiting area and cars in the garage.
Refine this for me please: I wish I had read the previous reviews on Yelp before coming here. It would have saved me a lot of time and frustration. I visited this place today to have my right passenger front wheel checked as my tire pressure light was on and I noticed a piece of tire was lifted. When I walked in, the technician told me there would be a couple of hours wait. I understand that since I hadn't made an appointment, but I asked if I could schedule one for a later time. Surprisingly, he replied that it's a first come first serve basis. This was confusing as I've been able to make appointments at other Just Tires locations before. It felt like he didn't want my business. In summary, the technician was rude and lacked basic customer service skills. I decided to go to Mr. Tire down the street instead, where they promptly replaced my tire in just half an hour. Additionally, Mr. Tire seemed much busier based on the number of cars in their garage and the waiting area.

input: Fantastic experience! I own a flower shop so I am kind of a hard one to please when I send flowers to others but this shop did a GREAT job! I called this afternoon and told the woman that answered the phone to do whatever they would like for x amount of money. My only request was that it was bright and cheery. They hit the nail on the head and delivered it quickly. THANK YOU :)
Refine this for me please: I had a truly fantastic experience with this flower shop! As the owner of a flower shop myself, I have high standards when it comes to sending flowers to others. However, this shop exceeded my expectations by doing an absolutely GREAT job! When I called this afternoon, I simply asked the woman who answered the phone to create a floral arrangement for a specified budget, leaving the design up to them. All I requested was that it be bright and cheery. I must say they absolutely nailed it, delivering a beautiful arrangement that perfectly captured the desired ambiance. Moreover, the delivery was swift and efficient. I am extremely grateful and satisfied. Thank you so much!

input:
I gave it one star because it doesn't give me an option to give it zero. This place sucks. Where should I start?? Okay, arrived at 7 pm with reservations and was seated in the dungeon. Fine. We ordered queso fundido with chorizo and got a weird looking cheese skillet with tortillas NOT chips. Odd! So had to ask for chips. Should've asked for a trash can. So we asked for some salsa to dress it up a bit -- that took an hour and I'm not exaggerating! The salsa was a thick mushy mess. Could turn the bowl upside down and nothng would've come out. Our food took an hour and a half, too. By that time, we were full on chips -- which were the only good thing on the menu! Oh... My favorite part... I ordered a side of beans and rice to go with my carne asada tacos -- which were more like unseasoned beef tips -- and I got a bowl of hard WHITE rice with refried beans on top. WHITE rice??? Seriously?!

Terrible! Dont waste your time. Taco Bell serves better food than this and that isn't saying much! Service was just as bad!!
Refine this for me please: I gave this place a one-star rating because there was no option to give it zero stars. Overall, my experience here was very disappointing. Upon arrival at 7 pm with reservations, we were seated in an unfavorable location that felt like a dungeon. We decided to order the queso fundido with chorizo but were surprised to receive a strange-looking cheese skillet with tortillas instead of chips. We had to specifically ask for chips, which was an inconvenience. It would have been better to ask for a trash can instead. Furthermore, it took an incredibly long time, about an hour, for us to receive some salsa to accompany our food. The salsa itself was of poor quality, with a thick and mushy consistency. Our main dishes took around an hour and a half to arrive, by which point we were already full from eating the chips – the only decent thing on the menu. The worst part was when I ordered a side of beans and rice to go with my carne asada tacos, but was served a bowl of hard white rice with refried beans on top. It was a complete disappointment. Quite frankly, I would not recommend wasting your time at this establishment – even Taco Bell offers better food, and that is not saying much. The service was equally as terrible.

input: This is a small coffe place own by Karyn, a blond sweet lady with a big smile! Great coffee and they have drive through
Refine this for me please: This is Karyn's small coffee place, owned by a kind-hearted and cheerful blond lady who always welcomes everyone with a warm smile. They take pride in serving exceptional coffee, and for the customers' convenience, they offer a convenient drive-through option as well.

input:
This used to be Red's but they knocked of the "R" and re-launched as Ed's, although when I see the sign from outside I keep forgeting it's called Ed's - cause it just looks like part of the sign fell off. Ed's is huge. If you've ever been on a cruise ship, Ed's has a variety of activity spaces, restaurant, bars and lounges under one roof. 

It's endless entertainment. You could probably float around here for a whole week and never get bored. There is a pool room, video games, bowling, a dance area, restaurants, lounges, a stage and much more around every corner you turn. It's a good place for young kids and birthday parties once you're too old for Chucky Cheese. 

Although I've personally never seen a band here my partner has, and it's not that expensive to see good bands like Ween, Jurassic Five or Interpol. The venue's neither big or small, so Ed's can host lesser known but interesting musicians as they can sell upwards of 600 tickets. So for bands that aren't popular enough to fill the Coliseum, Ed's still helps them establish a presence in E-town.
Refine this for me please: This establishment used to be known as Red's, but they recently rebranded as Ed's after removing the letter "R" from their sign. However, from the outside, it still looks like part of the sign fell off and it's easy to forget its new name. Ed's is a massive entertainment venue that offers a wide range of activities, including restaurants, bars, lounges, and various spaces for different types of events. It's reminiscent of being on a cruise ship, with endless entertainment options that can keep you engaged for an entire week without getting bored. There are numerous amenities like a pool room, video games, bowling, a dance area, multiple dining options, lounges, and even a stage for live performances. It's an ideal place for young children and hosting birthday parties for those who have outgrown venues like Chuck E. Cheese. While I haven't personally seen a band perform at Ed's, my partner has and it's surprisingly affordable to see well-known acts such as Ween, Jurassic Five, or Interpol. The venue is neither too big nor too small, allowing Ed's to support lesser-known yet interesting musicians who can sell up to 600 tickets. This gives these bands a chance to establish themselves in E-town, even if they aren't popular enough to fill larger arenas like the Coliseum.

input: I've had the fortune of eating my way across Asia Pacific, so I might be biased in saying I don't understand the rave reviews. I will say though that the conversation and company I was with more than made up for this!
Refine this for me please: Having had the opportunity to indulge in the diverse culinary delights of Asia Pacific, I must admit that I may be biased when I say that I fail to comprehend the enthusiastic praise regarding certain dining experiences. However, I must confess that the captivating conversations and delightful company I had the pleasure of sharing definitely compensated for any lackluster food encounters.

input: Very disappointed they no longer have the salad & pizza bar! Used to go to other location all the time, moved away & thought they closed. Then I realized they relocated & was excited about having salad there; I loved the salad bar. Was hoping for a piece of pizza for dinner and some salad. Not anymore:-(  Not unless you want to order a whole pizza!
Refine this for me please: I'm extremely disappointed to discover that they have discontinued their salad and pizza bar. I used to frequent their other location regularly but moved away, mistakenly assuming that they had closed down. I recently discovered they had relocated and was thrilled about having their delicious salad again - I was particularly fond of their salad bar. I was looking forward to enjoying a slice of pizza for dinner along with some salad. Unfortunately, that won't be possible anymore unless I want to order a whole pizza. It's quite disheartening.

input:
They used to make an Amiga bowl that had an abundance of shredded grilled chicken on the bottom of a flour tortilla bowl, a layer of rice topped with grilled onions and peppers with a queso sauce drizzeled over the top.
Tonight there was no rice nor any shredded chicken, it had been replaced with chicken crisps. They are the outer parts of a grilled chicken breast with no moisture and very few of them.
Having met the owner in the past and having his wife wait on me I knew something wasn't right.
I explained to the waitress that this dish had changed and wasn't good! She politely offered something else. What to order...if they had modified a basic dish what was next?
To my surprise a male manager came out and "informed" me that this is exactly what they had been serving for 10 years and I must have either special ordered something or was mistaken.
I said this is not what they had served me for the past 5 years and I never had requested a special order before. 
I also asked what they had done to the phenominal soft tacos? They were usually served in a soft warm flour tortilla and had moisture and flavor. Tonight they were stale and crisp and the filing was bland.  Again he informed me I was mistaken while he held my order that had been sent back to the kitchen in front of me.
I apologized and said I didn't wish for anything else, thank you.
Another manager came out a few moments later apologizing and stated that they are unfamiliar with what I had ordered and would "special order" anything I wanted. I declined.
Apparently their cook walked out tonight and they were winging it.
Too bad it was a good place to get a good mexican meal.
Two thumbs down on Poblano's.
Refine this for me please:
Please refine this for me: 
The Amiga bowl at Poblano's used to be a delicious combination of shredded grilled chicken, rice, grilled onions and peppers, and a queso sauce drizzled on top, served in a flour tortilla bowl. However, when I visited tonight, I was disappointed to find that they had changed the dish. Instead of rice and shredded chicken, they had replaced them with dry chicken crisps. Knowing the owner and having been served by his wife before, I knew this wasn't right. I informed the waitress about the change, and she kindly offered me another option. I was unsure about what to order, as I wondered if they had modified other dishes as well. To my surprise, a male manager approached me and insisted that this was the same dish they had been serving for the past 10 years, suggesting that I must have either made a special order or mistaken it for something else. I explained that in the past five years, this dish had never been served to me like this, and I had never requested any alterations. I also asked about the soft tacos, which were usually soft, warm, and flavorful, but tonight they were stale, crispy, and lacking in taste. Once again, the manager argued that I was mistaken, even though he had my returned order in front of him. Feeling frustrated, I politely declined any further options and thanked them. Shortly afterward, another manager approached me and apologized, admitting that they were unfamiliar with my usual order and offering to "special order" anything I wanted. However, I declined their offer. It turned out that their cook had walked out that night, and they were improvising in the kitchen. It's a shame because Poblano's used to be a reliable place for a good Mexican meal. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I would give Poblano's two thumbs down.

input:
I like Deweys's primary because it's close to my house.  The pizza looks great and the crust is good.  My gripe with Dewey's is that the pizzas are just so salty.  We had the pepperoni, socrates revenge, and bronx bomber.  It's like a eatting a brick of salt.  I'm not sure if it's the amount of salt sauce combined with the salty meat, but the combo so overwhelming, I tastebuds are numb to any other flavor.  Otherwise, if they fix that, I would love it.  

As for the salads, they're a good size, but seems like something you can toss together yourself.  I usually not get because don't want to spend the money on it.
Refine this for me please:
I enjoy going to Dewey's primary because of its convenient location near my house. The overall appearance of the pizza is appealing, and the crust is particularly good. However, I do have a complaint about Dewey's in that their pizzas tend to be excessively salty. This was particularly evident in the pepperoni, socrates revenge, and bronx bomber pizzas that my party ordered. The saltiness is overpowering, making it difficult to taste any other flavors. I suspect that it may be a combination of the salt in the sauce and the saltiness of the meat. If they were to address this issue, I would absolutely love Dewey's.

Regarding the salads, they are a decent size, but they seem like something that can easily be thrown together at home. Personally, I usually avoid ordering them because I don't believe they justify the expense.

input:
I came in with high hopes and left with slight disappointment. 

Our server was super attentive, and very friendly; however I feel like the food was disappointing. Our egg drop soup came out right away at a nice piping hot temperature and when the rest of our food came out it was practically room temperature. 

Feeling adventurous, I had ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice while he ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. I like the idea of sharing food, but my food was too busy all on its own without adding something else to the mix. The brown rice was cold and very bland while the shrimp was overly sweet and I didn't feel like the candied walnuts and melon balls were complementary flavors.

The chocolate cake we had for dessert was amazing though; 6 layers of chocolate on chocolate. It was so sweet and rich, we ended up sharing a slice.

So to sum up, service was great, dessert was great, but the food needs some work. Sorry PF Changs, I just am not impressed.

One thing I will note (that our server told us) is that they are very big on catering to food allergies (especially gluten).
Refine this for me please:
I entered the restaurant with high hopes but left slightly disappointed. Although our server was extremely attentive and friendly, the quality of the food fell short of expectations. While the egg drop soup arrived promptly and at the perfect temperature, the remainder of our dishes was disappointingly lukewarm.

Being adventurous, I opted for the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree accompanied by brown rice, while my companion chose the Sesame Chicken platter. However, my dish felt overwhelming even without any additions. The brown rice lacked flavor and was unpalatably cold, while the shrimp tasted excessively sweet, and the combination of candied walnuts and melon balls did not create harmonious flavors.

On the bright side, the chocolate cake we indulged in for dessert was exceptional. With six layers of rich, sweet chocolate, it was a truly enjoyable experience that we were happy to share.

In summary, the service provided by our server was outstanding, and the dessert exceeded our expectations. However, the overall quality of the food left much to be desired. Unfortunately, I cannot say that PF Changs impressed me. Nonetheless, it is worth noting that the restaurant prides itself on accommodating food allergies, particularly gluten-related ones, as informed by our server.

input: We ordered the rib dinner, pork on a bun, Mac n cheese, baked beans, and cole slaw.  Mac n cheese is worthwhile to prostitute yourself out for! The meat on the ribs had great flavor but was as tender as the bottom of my nikes.  Pulled pork had a sweet taste and was overall very good.  Baked beans were okay, cole slaw was very creamy and I would not gets those again (they have an after taste like lake water). The overall experience of getting BBQ in an abandoned car wash is special, worth a try!
Refine this for me please: We ordered a variety of dishes including the rib dinner, pork on a bun, Mac n cheese, baked beans, and cole slaw. The Mac n cheese was mind-blowingly delicious. It’s so good that you might consider selling yourself just to have another bite. The meat on the ribs had a fantastic flavor, but it was a bit tough—definitely not as tender as I had hoped. The pulled pork had a delightful sweetness and was overall very tasty. The baked beans were decent, nothing exceptional, and the cole slaw had a very creamy texture. However, I would advise against trying the cole slaw again as it had an unpleasant aftertaste reminiscent of lake water. Despite its unconventional location in an abandoned car wash, the unique experience of getting BBQ here is definitely worth a try.

input: I love the fries (wow, I'm still thinking about them because they're that good!) but I was not impressed by the beef kebob sandwich.  The sandwich was heavy on the onions and light on the meat, so it could have been better.  I do think that may have been an off sandwich, so I'm thinking of going back to give it a second chance (and to have another helping of fries!).  Smoothies also tasted like syrup and ice.  Prices are fair and service is great.  I love the mom and pop feel of the restaurant :).
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore their fries (I'm still daydreaming about them, they are just that incredible!). However, the beef kebob sandwich left much to be desired. It was overloaded with onions, lacking in meat, and overall, it could have been improved. Although, I do believe that my experience with the sandwich might have been an exception, so I am contemplating giving it a second chance (and of course, indulging in more of those amazing fries!). On another note, their smoothies tasted overly sweet and melted-ice-like. Nonetheless, the prices are reasonable, and the service is excellent. I genuinely appreciate the cozy, charming atmosphere of this family-owned restaurant :)

input: It is under new ownership and now called Taqueria Burrito's Grill. Absolutely delish! I love it! The green sauce rocks! I love it on cheese enchiladas. I'm picky about mexican rice and I love theirs. I recently moved back to New Orleans from Houston and one thing I miss is those little Taquerias that most people don't know about. Truly authentic mexican and they recently moved from Houston as well so I knew I was at the right place. It's the only mexican food that I can find in New Orleans East. I'll be a frequent customer. I think I am going back today! Open 7 days a week. Breakfast served 9a-11a. Open past 5PM. There # is 504-242-0573 to call for take out. YUMMY!!!!
Refine this for me please: Under new ownership and now known as Taqueria Burrito's Grill, this establishment is a must-try! Their food is absolutely delicious, and I can't get enough of it. The green sauce they serve is amazing, especially when paired with their cheese enchiladas. As someone who is particular about Mexican rice, I can confidently say that theirs is excellent. Having recently moved back to New Orleans from Houston, one thing I miss is the hidden gem taquerias that not many people know about. Thankfully, this place offers truly authentic Mexican cuisine and they have relocated from Houston as well, so I knew I had found the right place. It's the only Mexican food option available in New Orleans East, making it even more special. I definitely plan on becoming a regular customer and might even visit again today! They are open 7 days a week and serve breakfast from 9am to 11am. Additionally, they are open for dinner past 5pm. To place a take-out order, you can reach them at 504-242-0573. Trust me, their food is YUMMY!

input: Had the Mexican Roll and Philadelphia Roll for take-out. Very disappointed with the portion size of the rolls. There was nothing special with the taste and overall bland.
Refine this for me please: I recently ordered the Mexican Roll and Philadelphia Roll for take-out and I must say, I was quite disappointed with the portion size. Additionally, the taste of both rolls was underwhelming and lacking any distinct flavors. Overall, I found them to be rather bland and nothing out of the ordinary.

input:
I love going into this place to just browse and see what trendy item I can blow my money on. Living near mass ave shopping can be limited but also very competitive. Between silver in the city, boomerang boutique, global gifts, and homespun you pretty much can find whatever you are looking for as far as gifts go. 

Silver in the city is always my go to first. They are always on top of the newest "it" items for your home and style. They also allow dogs in their store so that's a huge plus because I'm typically walking my dog when I stop in. 

The only reason I am not giving them five stars is that although their employees are super friendly, they definitely watch you. I understand the need for this because they have little items that probably get stolen a lot but I always feel like I have no privacy to browse and debate any purchases. 

Cheers!
Refine this for me please:
I thoroughly enjoy visiting this place to casually browse and discover the latest trendy item I can indulge in. Living near mass ave shopping area provides a unique mix of limited options with intense competition. However, when it comes to finding gifts, you can't go wrong with establishments like Silver in the City, Boomerang Boutique, Global Gifts, and Homespun. 

Silver in the City always tops my list due to their ability to consistently stay up-to-date with the newest and most coveted items for both home decor and personal style. The added bonus of allowing dogs in their store is a huge plus for me, as I usually have my furry companion with me during my visits. 

The only slight drawback that prevents me from rating them five stars is the feeling of being closely observed by their staff. I understand the necessity for this precaution, considering the presence of small items that are frequently targeted for theft. However, it does leave me with a sense of limited privacy while browsing and contemplating potential purchases. 

Overall, I cherish the experience and will continue to visit these establishments for my shopping needs. Cheers!

input: I had takeout because it was about 45 min prior to closing . I ordered the puttanesca. It was delicious . Perfect combo of salty spiciness. There was such a wide variety of menu combos or you could get the fold and creat your own . Genius ! My only gripe is they need to come up with a gluten free dough option. My tummy will pay for this gluttony later .
Refine this for me please: I chose to have takeout as it was approximately 45 minutes before the restaurant's closing time. I opted for the puttanesca dish, which turned out to be absolutely delicious. The blend of salty and spicy flavors was perfect. The restaurant provided an extensive range of menu combinations, and customers could also customize their own pizzas. This flexibility was truly impressive. However, I do have a minor complaint regarding the lack of a gluten-free dough option. Unfortunately, indulging in this meal may result in some discomfort later.

input: Food was great!!!! I had the crab cake Benedict and it was delicious! Great service and smoothies
Refine this for me please: The food at this place was absolutely fantastic! I couldn't resist trying their crab cake Benedict, and it exceeded my expectations in terms of taste and flavor. Not only was the food delicious, but the service provided was also outstanding. The staff was attentive and friendly, ensuring a great dining experience. To top it off, their smoothies were incredibly refreshing. Overall, I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a satisfying meal with excellent service and delightful beverages.

input:
The one thing I really wanted for breakfast while in New Orleans was Grillades. I have made them at home from a recipe but never had them in a restaurant. When Yelp searching this place popped up so it was a must for breakfast. 

The restaurant has a diner style atmosphere. We were seated by the window so we got to watch traffic pass by on Canal Street. Our service was quick and our server was great. 

Of course I ordered the Grits and Grillades. Slow roasted beef with peppers and onions in a brown gravy over creamy Gouda cheese grits sounded perfect. It did not disappoint as it was so delicious!  I get excited when I go to a restaurant and order something I've cooked before and it tastes better than mine. This will be a must on any future New Orleans trips.
Refine this for me please:
During my time in New Orleans, there was one breakfast item that I simply had to try: Grillades. Even though I had previously made them at home using a recipe, I had never experienced the joy of savoring them at a restaurant. Upon conducting a Yelp search, I came across a restaurant that seemed like the ideal spot for enjoying this delicacy.

Upon entering the establishment, I was greeted by a cozy diner-style atmosphere. Luckily, we were seated by a window that offered a delightful view of the passing traffic on Canal Street. The service we received was prompt, and our server was genuinely attentive.

Without a moment's hesitation, I placed an order for the Grits and Grillades. The description of slow-roasted beef, combined with peppers and onions in a delectable brown gravy served over creamy Gouda cheese grits, made my mouth water. When the dish arrived, it exceeded all expectations – every bite was an explosion of flavors that left me wanting more. That feeling of ordering a dish that you have prepared at home, only to find that it surpasses your own efforts, is truly remarkable.

Needless to say, Grillades will forever be a staple on my future trips to New Orleans.

input: If I could select less than one star I would. Completely awful. After calling multiple times and no one answering, I finally was able to talk to a very unhelpful employee. He emailed me a specific unit, price, move in date and application. I filled out the paperwork but was unable to find the specific unit he indicated. When trying to call about my problem no one answered for 2 full business days. Then when talking with another very unhelpful employee, she told me that unit was already gone & suggested other units more expensive & not in the move in date discussed. When asking if they would honor the price originally discussed in email correspondence, they would not. Long story shorter, I cancelled my application & just wasted $50. This business only cares about money & does not care about the tenants at all.
Refine this for me please:
If I could rate this business lower than one star, I definitely would. My experience with them was completely awful. It was incredibly frustrating to call multiple times and not receive any answer, but eventually, I did manage to speak to an employee who turned out to be very unhelpful. He emailed me specific details regarding a unit, including the price, move-in date, and application. However, when I proceeded to fill out the paperwork, I couldn't locate the unit he had mentioned. I made several attempts to contact them about this issue, but no one answered for a full two business days. Eventually, I spoke to another unhelpful employee who informed me that the unit had already been taken. She then proceeded to suggest other units that were more expensive and had different move-in dates than what we had initially discussed.

When I asked if they would honor the price that had been agreed upon in our email correspondence, they flat out refused. It was clear to me at this point that this business only prioritizes money and doesn't care about their tenants at all. To cut a long story short, I decided to cancel my application, resulting in a wastage of $50. My experience with this business has made it evident that their primary concern is financial gain, with no regard for their customers.

input: Sierra and her sidekick, India, took impeccable care of my family last weekend during a family reunion.  We came to Santa Barbara from all over the world, and Sierra not only took care of purchasing everything we needed ahead of time, but she also thought of things we didn't think of, and went out multiple times to replenish drinks and food we went through.  They were flexible, fun, thorough and all-around fabulous.  I hope I have another event in Santa Barbara in the future, just so I can use JOTSB!
Refine this for me please:
Sierra and her amazing sidekick, India, provided exceptional care for my family during our recent family reunion in Santa Barbara. From the moment we arrived from various parts of the world, Sierra went above and beyond to ensure that we had everything we needed. Not only did she skillfully handle all the pre-event purchases, but she also proactively anticipated our needs, making multiple trips to replenish drinks and food throughout the weekend.

Their flexibility, sense of fun, and meticulous attention to detail made our experience truly unforgettable. Sierra and India truly were the epitome of fabulousness. In fact, I am secretly hoping for another opportunity to host an event in Santa Barbara just so I can have the pleasure of utilizing JOTSB's services once again.

input: Meh...I wasn't impressed with this spot. Looking past the array of hand written signs and lack of available bagels, the food was ok. I got the pastrami, egg, and cheese. There was hardly any pastrami and the cheese wasn't melted. My wife also had the pleasure of adding spoiled creamer to her coffee. I think we'll just stick with Einstein's or St Pete Bagel.
Refine this for me please: I wasn't impressed with this place. Despite the numerous handwritten signs and limited bagel options, the food was just alright. I ordered the pastrami, egg, and cheese sandwich, but it was disappointingly low on pastrami and the cheese wasn't even melted. On top of that, my wife discovered spoiled creamer in her coffee. Overall, it didn't meet our expectations, and we'll probably stick with Einstein's or St Pete Bagel instead.

input: Very nice employes very resonable price. Excellent homemade salad dressing. Good food, an all around good italian resturant.
Refine this for me please: The restaurant has incredibly friendly and accommodating employees, and offers reasonably priced dishes. They also serve outstanding homemade salad dressings that perfectly complement their delicious food. Overall, it is a fantastic Italian restaurant that guarantees a great dining experience.

input: I love their breakfast burritos. I usually get bacon, egg, cheese and potatoes. The potatoes are  well seasoned and cut small, so you don't end up getting a burrito that is about 95% full of overdone, mushy potatoes. You can actually taste the eggs, bacon and potatoes. Could use a bit more cheese, but that's a minor complaint. Nice selection of salsas at the salsa bar and the staff has always been friendly and welcoming. Very glad that they are located about a mile from my house! Hopefully they will be here for a long time.
Refine this for me please: I absolutely adore their breakfast burritos, specifically the bacon, egg, cheese, and potatoes combination. What sets these burritos apart is the perfectly seasoned and finely chopped potatoes, ensuring that you don't end up with a burrito that overwhelms you with mainly overcooked and mushy potatoes. Instead, you can genuinely savor the flavors of the eggs, bacon, and potatoes together. Although a touch more cheese would be ideal, that's just a minor quibble. Additionally, the salsa bar offers a nice variety of salsas to accompany your burrito, and the staff consistently goes above and beyond by being friendly and welcoming. Having their location conveniently within a mile from my house brings me immense joy, and I sincerely hope they remain a fixture in the community for years to come.

input:
I'm still new to Tucson, but having tried a large sample of the various pizza places near the U of A, I have to say that this is the best so far. 

In fact I'd say it's the best I've ever had. Better than the places I tried in NYC even. The crust is just magical. The five alarm (which I tried) is the perfect amount of spicy for those of us who crave that extra spicyness in our food. 

If you decide to try it, I doubt you'll be disappointed.
Refine this for me please:
As a newcomer to Tucson, I have explored numerous pizza places near the U of A, and I must admit that the one I am about to mention stands out as the top contender. I dare say, it surpasses any pizza joint I have ever encountered, including those in the revered city of NYC. The crust is nothing short of enchanting, possessing a quality that sets it apart from the rest.

Specifically, I highly recommend trying their five alarm pizza, a personal favorite of mine. It strikes the perfect balance of spiciness, catering to individuals like myself who crave that fiery kick in their meals.

Should you decide to give it a go, I have every confidence that disappointment will not befall you.

input: I heard alot about Honey's and how the food is so good here. I chose today my birthday to be my first visit .I read earlier reviews about how crowded it gets and they were not lying but I didn't wait no more than 20 minutes. Now let's get down to the food it was delicious. I had french toast, home fries, sausage and for dessert a slice of Jewish apple cake and it was to die for! I will be back most definitely.
Refine this for me please: I had heard a lot of good things about Honey's and their delicious food, so for my first visit, I decided to go on my birthday. I had read some reviews beforehand mentioning how crowded it can get, and I can confirm that they were not lying. However, the wait was manageable and I didn't have to wait longer than 20 minutes. Now, let's talk about the food – it was absolutely delicious! For breakfast, I ordered French toast, home fries, and sausage, all of which were cooked to perfection. To top it off, I indulged in a slice of Jewish apple cake for dessert, and it was simply divine! Needless to say, I will definitely be coming back for more.

input: Tria's employees are very knowledgeable about the selection of beers and wines they offer. This is probably why I look forward to going to Tria. This location has outside seating during the warmer months and is a real treat if you can get a table out there. It always seems to be busy, which is a good thing. I've never had any of the food items at Tria, because the real treat here are the drinks.
Refine this for me please: Tria's employees possess extensive knowledge about their diverse selection of beers and wines, which undoubtedly contributes to my excitement when visiting the establishment. With outside seating available in the warmer months, securing a table in this area adds an extra layer of delight to the experience. The constant buzz of activity at Tria reflects its popularity, which is a positive attribute. While I cannot speak to the quality of the food items offered, the true highlight at Tria lies in their exceptional drink selection.

input: Mae's is the best Chinese restaurant on this east side. We tried Mae's due to some rude pricks across the street. Lol! But, luckily things happen for a reason. The environment, the decor, the air inside is so much better to start. The food taste so much more fresher, like it was not frozen or reheated. No greasy/oily after taste. The service is very good,  always right there when you need something, staff is very friendly. My family and I love Mae's and what makes it better are the prices. We're large family and we can do really well with just $60. Lunch specials are awesome! I encourage you to try Mae's.
Refine this for me please: Mae's is undoubtedly the finest Chinese restaurant located on the east side. Initially, we ventured into Mae's as a result of encountering some discourteous individuals across the street - quite amusing, to say the least! However, it turned out to be a fortunate occurrence as everything about Mae's exceeded our expectations. The ambiance, decor, and atmosphere inside the restaurant are exceptionally pleasing. The food, in particular, is noticeably fresher, devoid of any frozen or reheated taste. Moreover, there is no unpleasant greasy or oily aftertaste. The service at Mae's is truly commendable, with the staff always readily available when assistance is required, and their friendly demeanor adds to the overall positive experience. My family and I are ardent supporters of Mae's, and the icing on the cake is the affordability of their offerings. Even as a large family, we can indulge in a satisfying meal with just $60. The lunch specials are truly amazing! I wholeheartedly encourage you to give Mae's a try - you won't be disappointed.

input: This place is my absolute fave! The flavors are spot on, they taste exactly the way you imagine, but better! The strawberries & champagne, toasted marshmallow, and cheesecake  are a few of my personal favorites. I moved to Phoenix a few years back and was ecstatic when I found out they opened locations in the valley. This is a Tucson gem that I will continue to visit over and over!
Refine this for me please: This place is without a doubt my favorite! The flavors here are absolutely incredible, accurately capturing exactly what you expect and taking it to a whole new level of deliciousness. Personally, I cannot get enough of their strawberries & champagne, toasted marshmallow, and cheesecake flavors - they are simply exceptional. Having moved to Phoenix a few years ago, I was overjoyed when I discovered that they had opened new locations in the valley. This incredible ice cream parlor truly is a Tucson gem that I will continue to visit time and time again!

input: This location used to be good, several years ago. About 3 years ago it started to go downhill and now it is just terrible. There were 2 people working on a Saturday evening. Nearly all the tables were full and there were people waiting to order and to pay. The sandwich that was made for me was on hard bread, burnt and barely edible. They need to either shape up or ship out.
Refine this for me please: This location was once excellent, but unfortunately, it has drastically declined over the past few years. Currently, it is in a deplorable state. On a recent Saturday evening, there were only two employees handling a packed house. The restaurant was nearly full, with customers waiting in line to order and settle their bills. Regrettably, the sandwich I received was made with rock-hard, burnt bread, and it was barely palatable. Ultimately, the management of this establishment must either drastically improve the situation or consider closing down.

input:
The girly loves this cemetery for photographing angels and such. Personally, I think she's a little creepy.

On the plus side, it's quiet, no zombies and the witches doing spells took time out to photobomb a bit.

So there's that.

Seriously, a well laid out cemetery and some of the better made stones and angels.

And no zombies. Remember that part.
Refine this for me please:
The girl really enjoys visiting this cemetery to capture photographs of angels and other subjects. Personally, I find it a bit unsettling. However, one positive aspect is that the cemetery offers a tranquil atmosphere devoid of zombies. Additionally, there were moments when witches, who were engaged in performing spells, amusingly inserted themselves into some of the photographs. 

In all seriousness, the cemetery is aesthetically appealing, with well-arranged tombstones and beautifully crafted angel sculptures. And let's not forget about the absence of zombies. That aspect is worth mentioning.

input:
On a recent trip to Port Richey, I selected Holiday Inn Express for a couple of reasons.  The main reason was the option of two beds (as I was sharing the room with my brother).  The other reasons were:  price, vicinity to my aunt's home and complementary breakfast. 

My family and I typically stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we're traveling.  However, since it was just my brother and I, I figured we'd give Holiday Inn a shot. 

+  The staff were very friendly and helpful.
+  Free wifi.
+  Breakfast was very good, offering both hot and cold entrees. 

-  Sadly, the beds were WAY TOO soft.  It felt as if the mattresses were past their life expectancy.  As a result, I didn't really sleep well for most of my three nights there.
-  The a/c was hit and miss with the lack of reliable thermostat controls. 

There was a pool and hot tub, but since I didn't utilize either, it wouldn't be fair to rate them.  There also a small gym that I didn't use either. 

All in all, it was just ok.  Hyatt has spoiled me.
Refine this for me please:
During my recent trip to Port Richey, I chose to stay at the Holiday Inn Express for a few specific reasons. Firstly, I needed a room with two beds as I was sharing with my brother. Additionally, the hotel offered a competitive price, was conveniently located near my aunt's house, and included a complimentary breakfast.

Normally, my family and I prefer to stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we travel. However, as it was only my brother and me on this trip, I thought it would be worth giving the Holiday Inn a try.

There were several positive aspects of our stay. The staff at the hotel were extremely friendly and helpful, ensuring we felt welcomed throughout our visit. Furthermore, the availability of free wifi was a convenient and appreciated amenity. The breakfast served at the hotel was also quite satisfactory, offering a variety of both hot and cold options.

Unfortunately, there were a couple of drawbacks that impacted our experience. Firstly, the beds in our room were excessively soft, giving the impression that they were past their prime. Consequently, I struggled to get a good night's sleep for the majority of the three nights we were there. Additionally, the air conditioning in the room was unreliable due to a lack of dependable thermostat controls.

While the hotel did offer a pool, hot tub, and a small gym, I did not have the opportunity to make use of these facilities, so I cannot provide a fair assessment of them.

Overall, I would describe our stay at the Holiday Inn Express as adequate. However, my past experiences at the Hyatt have set a higher standard, leaving me slightly underwhelmed.

input: The staff wasn't too interested in helping customers, instead focused on the TV in the lobby, flirting with each other and just standing around. I found the food to be ok, not great, not terrible. I'll round up from the 1.5 I give them.
Refine this for me please: The staff lacked enthusiasm in assisting customers as they seemed more engrossed in watching the TV in the lobby, engaging in flirtatious interactions with each other, and idly standing around. As for the food, it was passable but did not leave a lasting impression - falls in the mediocre category. Nonetheless, I would generously rate it slightly higher, rounding up from the 1.5 I initially intended to give.

input:
The food is excellent. The customer service and quantity over time has continued to go down. I've been going to this place every couple weeks for two years. The portions over time have continued to gradually get smaller and smaller. I commented on this, because my take out dish is now to the point where it is less then half full when I order, when it used to go to the top. When I commented on this I was told I was wrong.  I proceeded to explain my case. I was told if I didn't want to take the food, I didn't have to pay for it. I said ok, and was the berated for not taking the food I ordered. 

Long story short, these people have lost my business. I am not going back.
Refine this for me please: The food used to be excellent, but unfortunately, the quality of customer service and portion sizes has consistently declined over time. I have been a loyal customer of this place for the past two years, visiting every couple of weeks. However, the portions have gradually decreased in size. Recently, my takeout dish was less than half full, whereas it used to be filled to the top. When I brought this up, the staff denied it and dismissed my concern. I tried to explain my case, but they responded by saying I didn't have to pay if I didn't want the food. This response was disheartening, and I decided to stop patronizing this establishment. They have lost my business, and I have no plans to return.

input: Food was great. Staff was nice, friendly and helpful with menu suggestions. The Happy Hour is a good deal and the house margaritas tasted better than many other restaurants I've visited. I had the chicken poblano which was great. My friend enjoyed his enchiladas and they allowed him to have 3 different types on one plate.
Refine this for me please: The food was absolutely fantastic. The staff went above and beyond to provide excellent service, offering friendly and helpful menu suggestions. Their Happy Hour is definitely worth it, and their house margaritas surpassed those of many other restaurants I've been to. Personally, I tried the chicken poblano and it was outstanding. Additionally, my friend thoroughly enjoyed their enchiladas, and we were delighted that they accommodated the request for three different types on one plate.

input: Try the salted caramel chocolate cake. It was the best we ever had. I also tried the Apple Brown Betty  - awesome. Good beer selection.
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend trying the salted caramel chocolate cake, as it is truly the best we have ever had. Additionally, the Apple Brown Betty is absolutely awesome. They also have a great beer selection to complement your dining experience.

input:
A laid back bar for the college crowd. Cheap drinks.  They have projectors so u can watch the big game that day. However the screen needs to be two feet wider so the picture doesn't go off into the wall.

I came here during the day so it was really spacious, but I can only imagine how it is at night.
Refine this for me please: Please refine this for me: A casual bar catering to college students, offering affordable drinks. They have projectors for viewing the big games, but the screen should be expanded by two feet to avoid distortion on the wall. I visited during the day and found the place to be quite roomy, leaving me curious about its atmosphere at night.

input: Terrible service. Called in an order for pick up and completely butchered my order. I asked for a half sausage half cheese pizza and felt like he had no clue what i was saying as i had to constantly repeat myself. i had my boyfriend call back to make sure the order was right and he repeated back the order that i ordered half sausage half BEEF??? So after we corrected him and picked up or pizza, we got back and opened it up and it was ALL SAUSAGE. This is the second time in the past month i have had terrible service. The first time i got there for pickup and they had completely forgotten to put my order in. Terrible.
Refine this for me please: Extremely poor service. I placed an order for pickup and my order was completely mishandled. Specifically, I requested a half sausage and half cheese pizza, but the person taking my order seemed confused and I had to constantly repeat myself. To ensure accuracy, I had my boyfriend call back and confirm the order, but even then, he misunderstood and repeated back a half sausage and half beef pizza. After correcting the mistake, we picked up our pizza and to our disappointment, it turned out to be an all sausage pizza. This incident marks the second time within a month that I have experienced such horrendous service. The first time, I arrived to pick up my order only to discover that they had completely forgotten to process it. This level of service is absolutely unacceptable.

input:
do not eat here. my husband, two friends and i went out for restaurant week to marmont steakhouse on saturday, january 26, 2013; our experience was horrific.  the four of us ordered the crab bisque soup for our first course, it was cold and we sent it back to be reheated.  my second course was the calamari it was bland, fried too hard and rubbery.  finally two ppl from our party ordered the lobster ravioli for an entree.  it was not lobster ravioli but beef. i asked our waiter and one other waiter to please double check with the chef because this is not lobster, i expressed that i have not eaten beef or pork since 1994, and that it would make me ill. they both came back separately and argued that it was in fact lobster. another party of maybe 6 ppl ordered the lobster ravioli, they had the same problem and sent their dishes back to the kitchen too.  the server finally came over after i'd eaten two of the ravioli to apologize for the kitchens error and telling us that was in fact beef. 
i have been in the bathroom all day with diarrhea from the beef ravioli! the staff was very nonchalant about it and offered an insincere apology.
Refine this for me please:
Please avoid this restaurant at all costs. My husband, two friends, and I had the misfortune of dining at Marmont Steakhouse during restaurant week on Saturday, January 26, 2013. Our experience was absolutely horrific.

To start with, all four of us ordered the crab bisque soup as our first course. However, it arrived cold and completely ruined our appetites. We had to send it back to be reheated, which was already a disappointing start to the evening.

Next, I had the calamari for my second course. Unfortunately, it was incredibly bland, over-fried, and rubbery. I was extremely disappointed with the quality of the dish.

To make matters even worse, two members of our party ordered the lobster ravioli for our main course. Shockingly, what arrived on our plates was not lobster ravioli, but beef. Despite my clear dietary restrictions and express statement about avoiding beef and pork since 1994, the waitstaff initially insisted that it was indeed lobster. I had to ask both our waiter and another waiter to check with the chef, hoping they would rectify the mistake. However, they both returned separately, adamantly arguing that it was lobster. 

Shortly after, another group of about six people also ordered the lobster ravioli, only to encounter the same issue and send their dishes back to the kitchen. Finally, our server approached us and offered an apology for the kitchen's mistake, acknowledging that it was, in fact, beef. By that point, I had already consumed two ravioli and ended up suffering from severe diarrhea for the entire day as a result of the beef. 

The nonchalant attitude of the staff in handling the situation and their insincere apology were truly disappointing and distressing.

input: It simply does not get any better than Tako for sushi. Everything is fresh & delicious. The private rooms are so fun for a festive night out, it's BYO & when my girls get together we enjoy the feast & atmosphere! Some personal favorites are the jalapeño yellowtail(a must!!), kani salad, bird's nest roll & the naruto (served in cucumber instead of rice. Honestly, you can't go wrong when ordering. And so reasonable!! I rarely spend over $35 including tip when we go, and we do not hold back at all when ordering. Highly, highly recommend Tako!
Refine this for me please: Tako is unrivaled when it comes to sushi. Their selection is always fresh and delectable. The private rooms add an extra touch of excitement to any night out, especially with the convenience of BYO. Whenever my girlfriends and I gather, we indulge in the mouthwatering array of dishes while reveling in the vibrant atmosphere. Amongst my personal favorites are the must-try jalapeño yellowtail, delightful kani salad, tantalizing bird's nest roll, and the unique naruto, presented in a refreshing cucumber wrap instead of rice. Honestly, any choice you make when ordering is a winner. What's even better is the affordability! Rarely do I exceed $35, tip included, no matter how lavish our feast may be. I cannot stress enough how highly I recommend Tako!

input: Very good local ice cream. Expresso chip. Moose tracks. Graham Slam are all custom made flavors.
Refine this for me please: Exceptionally delicious, our local ice cream presents a delightful array of custom-made flavors including Expresso Chip, Moose Tracks, and Graham Slam.

input:
My hubbie and I have been taking our trucks here for a few years and can't complain. Every Wednesday is ladies day, so you get a discount on any of their wash options. (Firemen also get a discount on Mondays) . This isn't a hand-wash, so it's not perfect  but a good $5 carwash if your "baby" needs a quick bath.

They do run a special every now and then on auto detail packages 2 for 1. My husband and I always buy when they're running this special, since they have always done a nice job.
Refine this for me please:
My husband and I have been bringing our trucks to this car wash for several years now and we have no complaints. Every Wednesday, they have a ladies day promotion where you receive a discount on any of their wash options. Additionally, on Mondays, they offer a discount to firefighters. While it is not a hand-wash service, it still provides a decent $5 car wash for those times when your vehicle needs a quick clean.

Occasionally, they also have special deals on their auto detail packages, such as a 2 for 1 offer. My husband and I always take advantage of these promotions because we have consistently been pleased with the quality of their work.

input:
Everything about this place is average. The food is just ok, the service sort of depends on your luck - sometimes good sometimes not so good. 

Had the drunken noodles once and Thai green curry once. Both were average.
Refine this for me please: This place can be described as quite average overall. The food, including the drunken noodles and Thai green curry that I had, was just okay. Similarly, the quality of service can vary, depending on your luck—sometimes it's good, while other times it's not so great.

input:
This is a milestone review for me on Yelp.  I had been struggling with which one to chhose.  I decidede to make it Redemption.  This was seriously one of the best meals of my ENTIRE life.  

This review was from about 2 months ago.  Sorry it is a little dated.  Such as life.  

The setting is an old church.  It is really a beautiful surrounding for a restaurant.  Although I am an old church architecture nerd.  It was really cool to look around.   

The service was incredible.  I was hear as part of a group of 7 other characters, several were part of the NOLA restaurant scene.  We wanted a good time with the meal and they provided it!   

Paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian.  I was not fortunate enough to have enjoyed the original.  I can not comment on the faithfulness to the founders recipe.  I can say this there is no highe calling for a soft shell crab than to be cold smoked and fried in preparation for this dish.  On to your 77 virgins and mecca for you!  But I experienced heaven eating this.  

Seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's - This was superlative.  Again did not try the original, but the mirliton and seafood stuffing was heavenly, and more importantly improved the taste of the fresh flounder rather than competing for the spot light!   

The combination was quite possibly one of the 10 best meals of my life.  If you have been here, you should try it!
Refine this for me please:
This is a milestone review for me on Yelp, as I have been struggling to decide which restaurant to choose. In the end, I decided on Redemption, and I must say, it was one of the best meals I have ever had in my entire life.

I visited about 2 months ago, so please excuse the slightly dated review. The restaurant is set in an old church, which provides a beautiful and unique surrounding. As someone who appreciates old church architecture, it was a really cool experience to look around while enjoying my meal.

The service at Redemption was outstanding. I was part of a group of 7 other individuals, some of whom are well-known in the NOLA restaurant scene. We were seeking a good time along with our meal, and the staff definitely delivered.

One of the standout dishes for me was the Paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian. Unfortunately, I didn't have the opportunity to try the original version, so I can't comment on its faithfulness to the founder's recipe. However, I can confidently say that there is no better way to prepare a soft shell crab than by cold smoking and frying it for this dish. It was truly heavenly, making me feel like I had reached cloud nine.

Another dish that impressed me was the Seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's. Again, I didn't try the original, but the combination of mirliton and seafood stuffing elevated the taste of the fresh flounder, rather than overpowering it. It was truly divine.

Overall, the combination of dishes at Redemption possibly ranks among the top 10 best meals I've ever had. If you have the opportunity to visit this restaurant, I highly recommend trying it out.

input:
I love this place. It's just down the street from me so I'm there probably every other week... don't judge me! They rotate their flavors regularly and if at first you don't see a topping you'd like be sure and ask if they have it because they keep some under the counter!

This place also busts out some pretty intense EDM music over their sound system, which is somewhat bizarre but wholly awesome!
Refine this for me please:
I absolutely adore this place, located just down the street from me. I find myself visiting it almost every other week, although I hope you won't judge me for my frequency! One of the things I appreciate about this place is that they frequently rotate their flavors, ensuring there's always something new to try. If you don't initially spot a topping of your preference, it's worth asking if they have it since they often keep some hidden under the counter.

What truly sets this place apart is the unexpected choice of intense EDM music that blares through their sound system. It may seem a bit unusual, but I find it to be incredibly cool and captivating!

input:
Amazing. We had; Steak Tartare, Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot and the Curried Goat. Everything was really wonderful. Tartare maybe the best i've had. The goat with the sweet curry and gnocchi was very different and I loved it. I had a bite of the lime cheesecake and it was top notch, too. 

No drinks, because it's 2 days after Mardi Gras and I'm still in recovery mode. The service was among the best I've had in this town, which is know for it's hospitality industry. Great great great!
Refine this for me please: We had an incredible dining experience at this place. We tried the Steak Tartare, Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot, and the Curried Goat, and everything exceeded our expectations. The Tartare was possibly the best I've ever had. The combination of sweet curry and gnocchi with the goat dish was unique and absolutely delicious. We couldn't resist trying a bite of the lime cheesecake, and it was truly outstanding. Despite not ordering any drinks as we were still recovering from Mardi Gras, the service was exceptional, rivaling the renowned hospitality industry in this town. Overall, it was an outstanding experience.

input:
I went here on a Wednesday night and, though it wasn't busy, there were no open tables without a reservation,  except the tall tables in the bar area. It still seemed to be a very quiet place anyway. 

The location is not attractive, the street is dark and mostly empty at night, but the inside is stylish in a masculine, refined sort of way; dark wood, low light, maps on the walls and prints of watercolors depicting old Missouri scenes. It was a great place for a quiet, intimate dinner. They've got a couple of TVs up above the bar. 

They seemed very well staffed, as if each table had its own server. 

The menu is one page but very intriguing, I had so many questions for our server about "what is this?" and "what is that?" and he was totally nice and knowledgeable about the menu items. He seemed nervous and unsure at first, but he was friendly and made sure to check on us frequently. 

We decided to split 3 small plates and a side dish between the two of us and, honestly, it was a little too much food for just two people. Perhaps we don't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is so varied and interesting, it's really all over the map in terms of seasonings and ethnic origins but the main focus seems to be rustic and warming - at least at this time of year. I have a feeling they may change it up from time to time. I'm sure you'll get things here you won't find anywhere else. The prices are very reasonable, considering the planning and good execution of the food. You'd certainly find more expensive, and less original places in Clayton and down town. 

We ordered the smoked trout, the venison hot dogs, the mini monte cristo sandwiches, and the french fries. 

The venison hot dogs and the smoked trout were fantastic and interesting. The french fries were very well made, and the dipping sauces delicious. I was so impressed with these that I was then a bit underwhelmed by the mini monte cristos. Since everything else there seemed to have a unique spin on it, I expected them to do something original here as well, but they were just like any monte cristo you might have. They were very tasty of course, but nothing new. 

With the food plus two draft beers, our total was $52.05 before tip and we were stuffed and satisfied. I applaud them!
Refine this for me please:
I visited this restaurant on a quiet Wednesday night and despite not being busy, all tables were reserved except for the tall ones in the bar area. However, the overall ambiance was still peaceful. Despite the unattractive location with dark streets, the interior exuded a stylish, masculine charm with its dark wood, low lighting, and wall decorations of maps and watercolor prints depicting old Missouri scenes. It provided an ideal setting for a quiet and intimate dinner. There were a couple of TVs mounted above the bar area.

The restaurant seemed to be adequately staffed, with each table having its own dedicated server.

The menu, although concise, offered intriguing options that left me with plenty of questions for our server. He was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu items, although initially seemed a bit nervous and unsure. However, he made sure to check on us frequently.

We decided to share three small plates and a side dish between the two of us, but it turned out to be more food than we anticipated. Perhaps, our appetites were not hearty enough.

The menu at this restaurant is interestingly diverse, incorporating a variety of seasonings and ethnic origins. However, there is a prevailing rustic and comforting theme, especially during this time of the year. I suspect that they may change their menu periodically, offering unique and exclusive dishes. The prices are reasonable, considering the well-thought-out and executed food. In comparison, other places in Clayton and downtown tend to be pricier and less innovative.

For our meal, we ordered the smoked trout, venison hot dogs, mini Monte Cristo sandwiches, and French fries.
The venison hot dogs and smoked trout were outstanding and offered an interesting twist. Additionally, the French fries were expertly prepared, and the accompanying dipping sauces were delightful. However, I was slightly underwhelmed by the mini Monte Cristo sandwiches. Though tasty, they lacked the originality I had come to expect from the rest of their menu.

We also enjoyed two draft beers along with our food, and the total bill came to $52.05 before gratuity. Overall, we left the restaurant feeling full and satisfied. I commend them for their excellent service and quality of food.

input: "High Score!"...unfortunately I wasn't playing a video game with my friends, but rather wracked up the highest weight for my frozen yogurt. Refine this for me please: "High Score!" Unfortunately, this "victory" was not achieved in a video game with my friends, but rather by piling on the highest weight of frozen yogurt. input: I went last night with a few friends and let me say I was impressed, not necessarily with the quality of the food (nothing wrong with it by any means) or the decor, but the servers: how they don't kill every 4th customer is beyond me. I heard tables on both sides of us giving the most ridiculous of complaints to our/their server. Both tables were demanding as hell and already said loudly to eachother that they weren't tipping because of x, y and z reasons, and then were dumbfounded that there's a gratuity on their bill (it says it in the menu, anything over $50) their server, smaller girl so with purple hair, carried upwards of 4 plates at once, explained the menu perfectly and had an eagle eye for every table in her section and dealt with ridiculous complaints like a true professional. Thumbs up and five stars to the staff, customers, learn how to be basic humans, or stay home.
Refine this for me please:
I went out last night with a group of friends and I have to say, I was thoroughly impressed. Not necessarily with the food or the decor, although there was nothing wrong with either, but with the exceptional service provided by the servers. I couldn't help but wonder how they manage to handle demanding customers without losing their cool. At the tables neighboring ours, I overheard the most absurd complaints directed at our server and theirs. Both tables seemed to be extremely demanding and even made a point to loudly declare that they wouldn't be leaving a tip for various reasons. However, they seemed to be unaware that there is a gratuity automatically added to the bill (as clearly stated in the menu for bills over $50). 

Our server, a smaller girl with purple hair, skillfully carried multiple plates at once, explained the menu with precision, and attentively attended to every table in her section. She handled all the ridiculous complaints that came her way like a true professional. I must applaud the entire staff for their outstanding performance. As for those complaining customers, they really need to learn basic manners or perhaps just stay home. I give a thumbs up and five stars to the staff, but it's about time the customers learn how to behave.

input:

Refine this for me please: Although I ultimately didn't purchase a vehicle from this dealership, I must say that the overall shopping experience was exceptional compared to most others. The prices they offered were both reasonable and competitive, and their certification and warranty options for used vehicles were noteworthy. It just so happened that I decided to go with a different car make/model than the ones available at Hallmark. The salesman and sales manager were genuinely friendly and not at all pushy, which made the whole process much more enjoyable. I was also pleased with how quickly I was able to receive assistance and test drive the specific car I was interested in. If the car had captured my interest more than the one I was comparing it to, I would have likely made my purchase here. Based on my negative experiences elsewhere, I would highly recommend giving this dealership a chance if you're in the market to buy locally.

input: Gross, just gross. I ordered the white meat fried chicken with Mac and cheese and garlic mashed potatoes as my sides. Chicken was slimy and salty.
