Overall, the dining experience was decent. The sushi roll was enjoyable, although there were not many options to choose from. At the hibachi grill, I ordered the steak and despite the chef asking me twice for my preference of medium, it ended up being well done. Additionally, the rest of my group ordered chicken which all lacked seasoning according to their feedback.

One thing to note is that their advertised late happy hour from 8-11pm on their website was misleading. When we inquired about it, the staff informed us that it was only available at a different location. The website does not indicate that the happy hour is exclusive to a specific branch, nor does it mention the existence of multiple locations at all.

input:
I saw a deal on Groupon for Lee How Fook recently and after I read the reviews on Yelp, I was really excited to check this place out.  Unfortunately, I just didn't enjoy this restaurant and was pretty disappointed.

Lee How Fook is pretty small, but that didn't make it lose any points in my book.  I could see it getting really busy (especially since there are only about 10 tables available), so I would definitely suggest making reservations if you're going on a weekend.  The service wasn't bad, but when I asked some questions about some dishes on the menu, I had a hard time understanding what she was trying to say.  

Okay now to the main course - food!  For appetizers, we ordered the pan seared pork dumplings and sui mai.  Both appetizers were delicious and the dipping sauce was really good.  For the entrees, we ordered the sweet & sour chicken, pan fried noodle with shrimp, and pan fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce.  The sweet & sour chicken was awful - more sweet than sour - and the vegetables in it were really undercooked (pretty much raw).  (I do have to admit that I like things spicy, so maybe this dish just wasn't for me.)  For both pan fried noodle dishes, they were blah with a side of blah.  The beef dish was supposed to be spicy, but I just didn't taste any heat.  I left here full, but unsatisfied.
Refine this for me please:
After spotting the deal for Lee How Fook on Groupon, I eagerly checked out the restaurant following the positive reviews on Yelp. However, my experience left much to be desired, as I found myself disappointed with the overall visit.

Despite its small size, Lee How Fook didn't lose any points in my book. However, due to the limited seating (around 10 tables), I highly recommend making reservations, especially on weekends when it can become quite crowded. Although the service wasn't terrible, I did encounter difficulties understanding the server when I asked about certain menu items.

Moving on to the main event - the food. We began with the pan-seared pork dumplings and sui mai as appetizers, and both were delicious with a flavorful dipping sauce. As for the entrees, we opted for the sweet and sour chicken, pan-fried noodles with shrimp, and pan-fried noodles with beef and black bean sauce. Unfortunately, the sweet and sour chicken was a disappointment; it leaned more towards being overly sweet rather than offering the expected sour flavor, and the vegetables were undercooked, bordering on raw. (Given my preference for spiciness, it's possible that this dish simply wasn't suited to my taste.) The pan-fried noodle dishes were lackluster and failed to impress in terms of flavor. Despite leaving the restaurant feeling full, the overall satisfaction fell short.

input: The hot chicken is probably one of the best fried chickens I've ever eaten, and I'm from the South/NC and have had quite a bit of it. However, the price for the small portion size is really expensive. The drinks here are fantastic too.
Refine this for me please: The hot chicken at this place is hands down the best fried chicken I've ever had, and believe me, being from the South/NC, I've had my fair share. The only downside is the steep price for the small portion size. On the bright side, the drinks they serve here are absolutely fantastic.

input: I could write a lengthy review, persuasive and layered to hit all the right points. But why do that when Lee How Fook makes food that does it for you? Long story short they have some of the best general tso chicken I have eaten to date. Try it for yourself and get back at me. - Coolie
Refine this for me please:
Let me provide a refined version of your text:

Why spend time writing a lengthy review, persuading and layering it with all the right points, when Lee How Fook's food speaks for itself? In short, their General Tso chicken is undoubtedly one of the best I've ever tasted. Give it a try and let me know your thoughts. - Coolie

input:
Thank you Chef John Besh!  My husband and I stayed at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles. One of my main goals was to find some delicious New Orleans grinds.  I was starving when we arrived and didn't want to do any research on Yelp for a place to eat.  Thank God Luke was connected to our hotel!!!  We ended up eating here 3 times over 5 days.  It's usually full of business suits, but that doesn't bother me when the food is so good.

All the traditional dishes were good, but the huge surprise was the burger.  I was against ordering a burger while I was in New Orleans, because I wanted to try as many local eats as possible... and you can find burgers anywhere.  I overheard this lady raving about how delicious her burger was, so I had to order it the next time we ate there.  She was absolutely right!  It was one of the best burgers I've ever had!  It was huge, juicy, and packed with flavor.  I also highly recommend getting their bread pudding a la mode.  It was mouth-watering good and straight out the oven!
Refine this for me please:
Thank you Chef John Besh! My husband and I recently stayed at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles during our visit to New Orleans. Among our main goals was to discover the city's delicious cuisine. Upon our arrival, feeling famished, I decided to skip researching on Yelp for dining options and instead relied on the fact that Luke was conveniently connected to our hotel. Little did we know, it would become our go-to spot, as we ended up dining there three times over our five-day stay. Despite the restaurant often being filled with business-suited patrons, I wasn't bothered since the food was simply outstanding.

While all the traditional dishes exceeded our expectations, the true surprise came in the form of their burger. Initially, hesitant to order a burger in New Orleans where there were countless local dishes to try, I overheard a lady passionately raving about the mouthwatering burger she had just devoured. Intrigued, I couldn't resist ordering it on our next visit. And boy, was she right! It turned out to be one of the most delectable burgers I have ever had the pleasure of sinking my teeth into. Juicy, flavorful, and generously portioned, it surpassed all expectations. Additionally, I highly recommend indulging in their bread pudding a la mode, which was simply divine and served warm from the oven.

input: Came down here for some of their tasty fish tacos to find out that they have closed this location.
Refine this for me please: I came down here specifically for their delicious fish tacos, only to discover that this location has sadly closed down.

input:

I looked up "locksmith" on my phone's Google Maps app and Alpine came up (their Truckee office). Jacob had obviously dealt with the situation before. We enjoyed a nice happy hour in the meantime and when he got to the parking lot, I think it took him less  than 4min to get our key code and create us some new keys. Thanks for saving the day! Honest, quick service. Hope I never need to call them again under the same circumstances, but they'll be the first I call I make if I lose another set of keys. (Alpine accepts AAA).
Refine this for me please: I am extremely grateful to Jacob from Alpine for the exceptional service he provided. Uncertain about my options, I considered reaching out to Toyota or having the car towed back to SF. In a desperate attempt, I searched for a locksmith on my phone's Google Maps app and found Alpine's Truckee office. Thankfully, Jacob was experienced in handling such situations. Within just 30 seconds, he provided me with a price quote and an accurate timeframe for his arrival at Squaw. Impressed by his professionalism, Jacob even called me when he was running a few minutes behind schedule. While waiting, my companions and I enjoyed a nice happy hour. When Jacob finally arrived in the parking lot, it took him less than 4 minutes to obtain our key code and create a new set of keys for us. His timely and efficient service saved the day! I truly appreciate their honest and quick assistance. Although I hope to never find myself in the same predicament again, if I ever lose another set of keys, Alpine will be my first call. input: Service was so poor we didn't even get to the food. New Years Day 2017 around 7:30 and we get seated. input:
I finally made it to Farmhaus last Saturday, and it was worth the wait.  

As expected for a weekend, it was crowded.  We arrived about 15 minutes early and had to wait on the bench back by the bathrooms for a few minutes.  However, as I said, we were earlier than they anticipated, and they got us to the bar as soon as seats opened up.  They wisely gave us a copy of the menu to be prepared once we were seated, and we did indeed plan our entire meal in advance.  This was helpful, because we were actually seated about 20 minutes late, and I was about to eat the menu itself as I drooled over the descriptions!  

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were fantastic- the standouts of the meal.  The mushroom salad and tapenade were also very good.  The meatloaf was good, but a little on the dry and bland side.  I wanted to get the nachos, but there were no other takers in my group....next time....

Service was good.  It was a bit shaky at times, but it was slammed the whole time we were there and that small space must be tough to work in.  

I would love to go back and check out their blue place special lunches...I have heard amazing reviews.  I think I will head back for dinner when there is outdoor seating, as I think that would add to the experience.
Refine this for me please:
Last Saturday, I finally had the chance to visit Farmhaus and it certainly lived up to the hype. Despite it being a busy weekend, we managed to arrive a few minutes ahead of our reservation time. While we had to wait briefly by the restrooms, the staff quickly accommodated us at the bar as soon as seats became available. To our delight, they handed us a menu in advance, allowing us to plan our meal while waiting. With a slight delay of about 20 minutes in being seated, I was so famished that I practically considered devouring the menu itself, which had me salivating with its tempting descriptions.

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were absolutely phenomenal, undoubtedly the highlights of our meal. The mushroom salad and tapenade also impressed with their flavors. Although the meatloaf was decent, it leaned towards being on the dry and bland side. Regrettably, I yearned for an order of nachos, but my companions weren't as enthused, so I reluctantly passed this time.

Considering the circumstances, the service was commendable. Despite being somewhat shaky at certain moments, the staff coped well with the constant rush of customers in the limited space of the restaurant. I'm eager to return and try their highly acclaimed blue plate special lunches, as I've heard rave reviews. Additionally, I'd like to visit for dinner when outdoor seating is available, as I believe it would enhance the overall experience.

input: This restaurant is seriously lacking in customer service!  We have dined many times at Dish.  We like the food.  We made a reservation two weeks ahead for 3 people.  When we arrived we were seated at the smallest table in the restaurant which barely fits two people.  The table next to us had an extra person added at the end, his back was literally a couple of inches from our table.  We asked for a table that would accomdate three people and not involve eating with someone's large back at our very tiny table.  We were rudely informed that it was a take or leave it situation.  It was very frustrating since we booked this as a special night out weeks earlier.  Unfortunately, we are writing this restraurant off our list.
Refine this for me please: This restaurant severely lacks customer service. Despite being regular customers at Dish and appreciating the food, our recent experience was disappointing. Despite making a reservation for three people two weeks in advance, we were seated at an exceptionally small table that can hardly accommodate two individuals comfortably. Moreover, the adjacent table had an extra person squeezed in, resulting in their back being only a couple of inches away from our table. Hoping for a more suitable table that can comfortably fit three people without having to eat next to someone's large back, we politely requested a different arrangement. However, we received a rude response stating that it was a take-it-or-leave-it situation. This encounter was incredibly frustrating, especially considering we had planned this night out well in advance. Regrettably, we have decided to remove this restaurant from our list of preferences.

input: This restaurant was pretty good; i'll admit it! I went here in the late evening with my boyfriend to have a nice date! He insisted on us ordering a milkshake and i'm SO GLAD that he did. The milkshake was probably one of the best ones i've had in my lifetime. The food was pretty good and so was the service but something was a little off. I couldn't tell what it was but i just got a really strange vibe from the restaurant. Maybe i'm just being crazy!
Refine this for me please:
I must admit, this restaurant was actually quite good. I visited here in the late evening for a delightful date with my boyfriend. He insisted on trying their milkshake, and I am incredibly grateful that he did. Undoubtedly, it was one of the best milkshakes I have ever had.

The food and service were both fairly commendable. However, there was a vaguely unsettling atmosphere that I couldn't quite put my finger on. Perhaps I am merely overthinking it, but there was something peculiar about the overall ambiance of the restaurant. Then again, maybe it's just my imagination running wild!

input:
I was so disappointed when this opened; I was hoping for Nashville's first real authentic Greek restaurant (Athens notwithstanding).  This isn't Greek; it isn't even Mediterranean. It's pseudo-Americanized versions of Mediterranean classic cuisine. The corporate chefs got so many things wrong:  Skordalia is a classic Greek dip made out of potatoes and garlic (not bread).  Avgolemono is chicken soup with egg, lemon and rice -- not this thin, awful broth they are currently serving. If one wants true Greek cooking, one should go to Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. 
Just say no.
Refine this for me please: I was greatly disappointed when this establishment opened, as I had hoped for Nashville's first truly authentic Greek restaurant (except for Athens, of course). However, this restaurant falls short in delivering genuine Greek cuisine, and doesn't even manage to capture the essence of Mediterranean flavors. Instead, it offers watered-down, Americanized versions of classic Mediterranean dishes. The corporate chefs have overlooked several crucial elements: for example, skordalia should be made with potatoes and garlic, not bread. Likewise, their rendition of avgolemono is far from the traditional chicken soup with egg, lemon, and rice, as they serve a thin and disappointing broth. If you desire authentic Greek cuisine, I recommend visiting Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. In light of all this, I strongly advise against dining here.

input: Best meal in New Orleans!!! I was in a group of 4 and we were served by Travis, Susan & Caroline. I had the set price menu: strawberry salad appetiser, chicken entrée & chocolate cake dessert. The salad was fresh and a great start. The chicken is the best chicken I have ever eaten anywhere. It had crispy skin, but was the meat was extremely moist and the corn bread stuffing was superb. The cake was yummy, but very rich. One of our party is vegetarian and she LOVED her vegetable selection plate. The other 2 members had the pork with sweet potato mash and said it was excellent. The staff were wonderful and very attentive. Excellent location and definitely the best meal we had in New Orleans.
Refine this for me please: The best meal in New Orleans! Our group of 4 had an amazing experience at this restaurant, thanks to the exceptional service provided by Travis, Susan, and Caroline. I opted for the set price menu and started with a refreshing strawberry salad. The chicken entrée surpassed all my expectations - it had a perfectly crispy skin, exceptionally moist meat, and the cornbread stuffing was truly superb. For dessert, the chocolate cake was absolutely delicious, although quite indulgent. Our vegetarian companion was delighted with her vegetable selection plate, and the other two members of our group raved about the pork with sweet potato mash, describing it as excellent. The staff were outstanding, providing attentive and friendly service throughout our meal. The restaurant's location was fantastic, and without a doubt, this was the best dining experience we had in New Orleans.

input:

input: Although the term is often overused, "farm fresh" truly applies here. Inventive, flavorful dishes and just-right portions amaze. A cozy dining room, friendly atmosphere and attentive service make it the perfect setting to catch up with friends and loved ones (BYO, so grab a good bottle). Try the Bloody Beet Steak!
Refine this for me please: The term "farm fresh" may be frequently used, but it genuinely applies to this establishment. Here, you can expect inventive and flavorful dishes that are served in just-right portions, leaving you amazed. The cozy dining room, along with its friendly atmosphere and attentive service, create the perfect ambiance for catching up with friends and loved ones. Don't forget to bring along a good bottle of wine since it's a BYO spot. Make sure to try their specialty, the Bloody Beet Steak; it's a must-try!

input:

input:
Dayum, that was a good burger. Juicy, glistening melting with cheese - simplistic yet tastes completely different from other burger joints due the quality of the ingredients. Bacon looks good in pictures, but it was a too thick of slice of puuuure white fat, if it would have melted in my mouth it would have worked but it didn't therefore just felt sinful, in a bad way. 

Unfortunately, this communal table trend has got to go. 
I hate it, it's a crap shoot on who your going to get to sit next to and basically listen to a complete strangers stupid conversations. Terrible idea.
Refine this for me please:
Wow, that burger was absolutely amazing. It was incredibly juicy and the cheese was perfectly melted, giving it a unique and satisfying taste compared to other burger places. However, I have to admit that the bacon was a bit disappointing. Its thick slice was mostly pure white fat, which didn't have that delightful melt-in-your-mouth sensation. Instead, it felt indulgent in a negative way.

On another note, I have a strong dislike for the communal table trend. I find it inconvenient and unpleasant to have to sit next to complete strangers and be subjected to their annoying conversations. It's simply a terrible idea.

input:
i've been a member of this gym for a couple of weeks now, and i'm enjoying it.  conveniently located, very reasonably priced, and all the basic amenities -- plenty of cardio machines, plenty of weights, a lap pool, a spin class room, and a big aerobics studio.  the staff are all really nice as well, and you get a free personal trainer session when you sign up.  and your membership fee allows you to use all of their area locations for no extra money.  and if you have kids (i don't), they offer babysitting for limited hours.

the only things i'm a bit bummed about are:  1. they don't open until 8am on the weekends (i'm an early riser and would prefer to go a bit earlier than that), and 2. the only group fitness class they offer before work is a 5:45am spin class (i'm sorry, i just can't do spin that early in the morning).

this isn't the gym for you if you want all sorts of foo-foo stuff like a smoothie bar and massage and lots of high-tech equipment.  but if you just want a place to come and work out with nice people on good equipment, then you'll save some money by joining LA fitness.
Refine this for me please:
I have been a member of this gym for a few weeks now and I am really enjoying it. It is conveniently located and reasonably priced. They provide all the basic amenities I need, including plenty of cardio machines, weights, a lap pool, a spin class room, and a big aerobics studio. The staff members are all very friendly and welcoming. In addition, when you sign up, you get a free session with a personal trainer. Another great perk is that your membership allows you to use any of their locations without any extra charge. They also offer babysitting for limited hours for those who have kids.

The only downsides for me are that they do not open until 8am on the weekends, which is a bit late for me as an early riser. Additionally, the only group fitness class offered before work is a 5:45am spin class, which is too early for me personally.

If you are looking for a gym with fancy extras like a smoothie bar, massages, and high-tech equipment, this may not be the right fit for you. However, if you just want a friendly gym with a good atmosphere and adequate equipment, joining LA Fitness will save you some money.

input: I'm very picky when it comes to Sushi. Quality of the fish and ingredients are very important but so is the chef, maybe the most important. Hiro San is absolutely amazing at what he does. His skills are hands down the best and he's also a really great human being to talk to. If you are in the Santa Barbara area looking for a great Sushi experience come here and sit in front of the master, you won't regret it.
Refine this for me please: I have extremely high standards when it comes to Sushi. The quality of the fish and ingredients is paramount, but equally important is the expertise of the chef, who I believe is the key factor. Without a doubt, Hiro San surpasses all expectations in his craft. His skills are unrivaled, making him the absolute best in his field. Moreover, he is a delightful person to engage with. If you find yourself in the Santa Barbara area and seek a remarkable Sushi experience, I highly recommend visiting Hiro San's establishment. Take a seat in front of this master chef, and I assure you that you will not be disappointed.

input: This theater is dated but you can't beat the cheap prices.  Staff is always very friendly and that alone keeps me dividing my time between here and the Loft.  It is never even close to being crowded and you can always see any of the major movies on top of lots of Indie films they show here and hardly anywhere else.  I would much rather wait out a movie til it comes here.
Refine this for me please: Despite its dated appearance, this theater offers unbeatable prices. The staff's friendly demeanor alone makes it worth frequenting, along with the nearby Loft. Thankfully, it is never crowded, allowing for easy access to both mainstream and unique indie films that are rarely shown elsewhere. Waiting for a movie to arrive at this theater is a preferable option for me.

input: Fun place, inviting interior and a pleasure to hang outside with the couches, etc. brunch food was very good, and beer selection exceptional.  Waiter, however, was a disaster.  Was jerky to us from the beginning, (we were all sitting around asking each other why he was being such a jerk to us), did not know the menu at all, constantly disappeared on us, and was argumentative when he brought out the wrong order (twice)...and there were only 2 other tables at the time). Otherwise, would have gotten 4 stars.
Refine this for me please: This place is a lot of fun with an inviting interior, and it's great to hang outside on the couches. The brunch food is very good, and the beer selection is exceptional. Unfortunately, the waiter was a complete disaster. Right from the start, they were rude and unfriendly, making us wonder why they were treating us so poorly. They seemed unfamiliar with the menu, constantly disappearing, and when they brought out the wrong order (not just once, but twice), they actually started arguing with us about it. It's a shame because without this terrible service, I would have given this place 4 stars.

input: Great restaurant, and creative menu. We also love La Mulita next door, which shares the same kitchen. The only downside is that they do not take reservations, so it can be a bit of a gamble on a weekend. You also need your whole party to sit, so if you have a late friend, you could be stuck for a bit.
Refine this for me please: This establishment is a fantastic restaurant offering a diverse and imaginative menu. Additionally, we have a strong affinity for La Mulita, an adjacent restaurant that operates from the same kitchen. However, it is important to note that reservations are not accepted, which could potentially pose a challenge on busy weekends. Furthermore, it is essential for the entire party to be present in order to secure seating, meaning that if one member arrives late, there may be a slight delay in getting seated.

input: For Cool Springs on a Thursday when Bonefish grill was packed this place had a comfortable wait of 15 minutes. Also the food is always amazing, but that's a given
Refine this for me please: During Cool Springs on a busy Thursday at Bonefish Grill, while it was packed with customers, this place offered a pleasant wait time of only 15 minutes. Furthermore, it is worth noting that the food consistently exceeds expectations, although such excellence is to be expected.

input:
Yum-O! We spend the day in Tarpon Springs, and headed here around 3:45 for lunch / dinner. We waited for about 10 minutes for our table and were seated. 

This restaurant has a TON of staff and they are always running around. Our waiter was nice and quick.

We ordred:
Gyro - yum
Chicken Slouvaki - yum
Spanokopita - YES (this is what I ordered, good, but the top filo dough crust was a bit harder than I like)
Hotdog (this is what the 5 year old got)

We also got an order of the cheese, opa!

Yes, this will be our go to spot when we visit Tarpon Springs.
Refine this for me please:
Yum-O! Our day in Tarpon Springs was fantastic, and we decided to head here for lunch/dinner around 3:45. After a short 10-minute wait, we were seated at this bustling restaurant with a large and attentive staff.

Our waiter was friendly and efficient. We couldn't resist ordering some delicious dishes:
- The gyro was absolutely delicious.
- The chicken slouvaki was equally mouthwatering.
- I tried the spanokopita, which was good, although the top filo dough crust was a bit crunchier than my preference.
- Our 5-year-old enjoyed a hotdog, their favorite.

On top of that, we indulged in an order of the cheese - opa! It was incredible.

We've already decided that this will be our go-to spot whenever we visit Tarpon Springs.

input: Simply put, the Grypon Cafe makes me feel infinite.  It's about two minutes away from the Wayne Starbucks, but believe me when I say that all the cool informed coffee connoisseurs flock to Gryphon Cafe.  Its setting is quiet and intimate.It exudes a chill and serene vibe, from its very dim lighting and small (in a good way!) space.  The lattes are very good- made with strong espresso.  In addition, it provides various baked goods, although I've had a really dry, stale brownie from there (A big no-no! As a result, I don't care too much for the baked goods).  In addition, Gryphon supports a lively local music scene; music begins at 9 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.
Refine this for me please: In short, Gryphon Cafe is my go-to place for a limitless experience. Located just minutes away from the Wayne Starbucks, it attracts the coolest and most knowledgeable coffee enthusiasts. The cafe offers a quiet and intimate atmosphere that emanates a serene and laid-back vibe, enhanced by its dim lighting and cozy space. Their lattes are excellent, boasting strong espresso. While they also offer a variety of baked goods, I must admit I had a disappointing experience with a dry and stale brownie, so I don't usually indulge in their baked treats. However, what sets Gryphon apart is its support for the local music scene, with live performances starting at 9 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.

input:
Its a rarity that i give five stars for anything. But in comparing this tattoo shop to the others around Indy and how they've jacked me around i decided its simply worth it to give 5. The other places have cancelled on me at the last moment, even when i was en route to go get the tattoo, one guy didnt even remember me when i called the day before to make sure we were on schedule for the tat and yet another had the inks set out and asked me to sit down when he got a call that he needed to go pick up the kids at school - all of these places i scheduled months out in advance as well. So, here we are back at Metamorphosis where they actually like to run a business the way it should be. Honestly i have only had one tat done here by Trevor and at the time it was the most fun 4 hour rib tattoo experience i could have had. They act professional, not like the rock star wanna be's i tried to check out at other places. Just cool chill people who want your business here. Trevor gave me the tattoo i wanted in the place i wanted it even though i feel he would have given me honest advice if it were needed. When it came time to get the tat, he held his appointment and i was treated with respect and as though a customer should be treated. Honestly i dont think this place cost more than any other place where youll get good work. Prices are about average in my opinion for the quality of work done. Dont waste your time going to the other places and getting jerked around - ive already done the work for you. Its a shame too that they may have good artwork at other places but youll feel like less of a human going anywhere else. The artists are just as good here and youll be respected for your $.  And by the way, yes they do ask for a non refundable deposit so they know your serious which is no different than any tattoo place ive ever been to.
Hopefully they dont change up anything, especially their roster as i believe they have a good thing going here. Yes its in hoity toity popular town but its a diamond in the rough and there are no rock star attitudes here. Cant wait to go back to Trevor again.
Refine this for me please:
I rarely give five stars to anything, but after comparing this tattoo shop to others in Indianapolis and the negative experiences I've had elsewhere, I believe it's worth it to give them five stars. The other tattoo places have frequently canceled on me, even when I was on my way to get the tattoo. One artist didn't even remember me after I called the day before to confirm our appointment, and another had me sit down to start the tattoo only to leave abruptly to pick up their kids from school. All of these appointments were scheduled months in advance. 

Metamorphosis, on the other hand, maintains professionalism and runs their business the way it should be. I've only had one tattoo done here by Trevor, but it was a fun and enjoyable four-hour experience for my rib tattoo. The staff here are not pretentious rock star wannabes like the others I've checked out. They are cool, laid-back people who genuinely appreciate your business. Trevor gave me the exact tattoo I wanted in the desired location, and I believe he would have given me honest advice if necessary. He honored his appointment and treated me with respect as any customer should be treated.

In terms of pricing, I don't believe this place is any more expensive than other reputable tattoo shops. The quality of work justifies their average prices. Don't waste your time getting jerked around at other places - I've already done the research for you. Although other places may have good artwork, the way they treat customers makes you feel devalued. The artists at Metamorphosis are just as skilled, and they respect and value their customers.

It's worth noting that this tattoo shop requires a non-refundable deposit, which is standard practice for any tattoo place I've been to. I hope they don't make any changes, especially to their roster, as I believe they have something great going here. Despite being in a popular and upscale area, this place is a hidden gem without any big egos or attitudes. I can't wait to go back to Trevor for my next tattoo.

input: Had the lengua burrito. It was non greesy and plated neatly. Simple food that was easy on the wallet. Think I will try the flan next time
Refine this for me please: I enjoyed the lengua burrito as it was both delicious and not overly greasy. Additionally, it was presented neatly on the plate. The affordability of this simple yet satisfying dish was another plus point. I am already contemplating tasting their flan during my next visit.

input: Poor lighting very dark can't even see your food all the food was average. Sorry I really wanted to like it more.
