input: Banana pudding is amazing. You can get the extra toppings but just plain no nana is great. They care about their customers and are always welcoming. I love supporting their shop and hope it's around for years.
Refine this for me please: Banana pudding is absolutely delightful. While additional toppings can enhance the experience, enjoying the plain version is equally delightful. The establishment truly values their customers and consistently provides a warm and welcoming atmosphere. Personally, I take great pleasure in supporting their shop and sincerely hope it continues to thrive for many years to come.

input:
I mistakenly left my organizer/wallet on my table when eating at Shepard's yesterday (6/24/12). I realized the mistake early this morning and called Shepard's. I was told that no one turned in anything resembling my organizer. 

I called back a few hours later to try and determine who bussed my table and what management was on duty and was told that my organizer had indeed been found and was in the "safe". I asked about the contents of the wallet and discovered that everything was present except for a $100 bill that I had just gotten the night before. I have witnesses to the $100 bill being in the organizer. 

I went today to retrieve the organizer and met with the assistant manager, who told me it was not their responsibility to keep track of guests belongings and would not investigate the issue whatsoever. She would not approach the server, would not ask who turned the organizer in, would not ask who stored it in the safe and essentially told me it was not her problem. 

This is customer service at it's worst... I have no recourse at this establishment to even try to get my money back. I am incensed that they won't even conduct an investigation for me.
Refine this for me please:
I accidentally left my organizer/wallet on the table while dining at Shepard's yesterday (6/24/12). Upon realizing my mistake this morning, I promptly called Shepard's to inquire about it. Unfortunately, I was informed that no one had turned in anything resembling my organizer.

However, a few hours later, I decided to call again to gather more information. To my surprise, I was informed that my organizer had indeed been found and was being kept in a secure location. Curious about its contents, I inquired further and learned that everything was intact, except for a $100 bill that I had received just the night before. To validate my claim, I have witnesses who saw the $100 bill in my organizer.

Seeking resolution, I made a trip to Shepard's today to retrieve my organizer. I met with the assistant manager and explained the situation. However, to my disappointment, she stated that it was not their responsibility to keep track of guests' belongings and that they would not be conducting any investigation into the matter. She refused to approach the server, inquire about the individual who turned in the organizer, or identify the person who stored it in the safe. Essentially, she brushed off the issue, indicating that it was not her problem.

I am extremely dissatisfied with the level of customer service displayed by Shepard's in this situation. Their refusal to conduct an investigation or assist me in any way prevents me from seeking any recourse or attempting to recover my lost money. I am infuriated by their lack of willingness to address my concerns.

input: As usual, this restaurant doesn't seem to heed the bad reviews and fix the problems. Dinner here last night was abysmal. The prime rib was 40% fat with tons of gristle. My dog wouldn't even eat the left overs!  Who wants cold fries? I asked for regular butter (not cinnamon) and never got it. Hey, Jeanne, do you not even TRY to fix your problems?
Refine this for me please: Once again, it is disappointing to see that this restaurant continues to neglect negative feedback and fails to address its issues. Last night's dinner experience was truly dreadful. The prime rib dish I ordered was overwhelmingly fatty, with an excessive amount of gristle. To put it into perspective, even my dog refused to eat the leftovers. Adding to the disappointment, the French fries served to me were cold. Furthermore, despite specifically requesting regular butter instead of cinnamon butter, it never arrived at my table. Jeanne, I can't help but wonder if any effort is being made to rectify these recurring problems.

input:
I'm only giving them 4 stars because I haven't tried out enough of their menu. But in regards to previous reviews saying the pizza was soggy, they must have listened! The pizza I ordered today was a personal specialty pie. Vegan general tso's pizza. It was so good! No skimping on the "chicken" either. The crust was crisp and fluffy, not greasy at all but still packed with flavor. The chicken had that delicious general tso's sauce coated on each piece, as well as a slight kick at the end. 

I will definitely be ordering from there again. When I called to see if it was possible to veganize an online order, they instructed me to simply write vegan in the comments section. And they called me back to iron out a pricing discrepancy as well! The delivery came within the time they quoted and was hot. I'd definitely recommend giving them a try. They make the seitan themselves and wow, it is good.
Refine this for me please:
I'm giving them 4 stars because I haven't tried enough of their menu yet. However, I must say in response to previous reviews mentioning soggy pizza, it seems like they have taken the feedback into consideration. The personal specialty pie I ordered today, the Vegan General Tso's Pizza, was absolutely delicious! The "chicken" topping was generously portioned, and the crust was perfectly crisp and fluffy without any greasiness. Each piece of chicken was coated with the flavorful General Tso's sauce, with a slight spicy kick at the end.

I was impressed with their customer service as well. When I called to inquire about veganizing an online order, they instructed me to simply mention it in the comments section. They even called me back to resolve a pricing issue. The delivery was right on time and the food arrived hot.

Overall, I will definitely be ordering from them again. Their homemade seitan is truly remarkable. I highly recommend giving them a try.

input:
This restaurant is attached to the Drury Plaza hotel, so it was conveniently located for dinner when you're not really familiar with the area. There were 20+ in our party each night and the service was pretty good. Only a few forgotten drinks, which was to be expected with such a large group. 
Portions are huge and food was good. I had the Cuban sandwich one night and it was massive but delicious. The shandy is good. The margaritas are not and I don't recommend their patron one. I forget the name but it wasn't that good. Their shrimp tacos have a kick but they're good too.
Refine this for me please:
The restaurant which is conveniently attached to the Drury Plaza hotel makes it a convenient choice for dinner, especially if you are unfamiliar with the area. Despite our large party of over 20 people, the service provided was generally good, with only a few instances of forgotten drinks, which is understandable for such a large group.

The portions at the restaurant are generously sized and the food itself is of good quality. One night, I opted for the Cuban sandwich, which was not only massive but also delicious. In terms of drinks, the shandy is enjoyable, however, I do not recommend their margaritas, especially the Patron one which I found to be lacking. Unfortunately, I cannot recall the exact name of the margarita I had, but overall it was not up to par. Lastly, for those who enjoy a little spice, the shrimp tacos pack a flavorful kick while still being enjoyable.

input:
You know how those 5 stars mean, "Woohoo!  As good as it gets!"?

Each one of those stars is well deserved by Tanti and the rest of the crew at Papertini.  They specialize in wedding flowers but these aren't just your clump of red roses.  These are creatively and artistically designed masterpieces speckled with striking elements like papers, wires, luxe fabrics, and more.  As an added bonus, they're just great, friendly people.  A true asset to your wedding team.

If you want traditional wedding flowers, Papertini can do it but I think it would kill their soul - go elsewhere.  If you want something more unique without being artsy-fartsy, I can't recommend them highly enough!
Refine this for me please: Papertini and their team deserve each of those 5 stars because they go above and beyond in their specialization of wedding flowers. Unlike the typical bouquet of red roses, their designs are true works of art, creatively adorned with elements like papers, wires, and luxe fabrics. And it doesn't stop there - they also happen to be friendly and wonderful people, making them a valuable addition to your wedding planning team. Though they can certainly handle traditional wedding flowers, that's not where their true passion lies. If you're seeking something truly unique and special without being overly artistic, I cannot recommend Papertini highly enough. Look elsewhere for the traditional, but trust me, they are the perfect choice for a non-traditional and extraordinary experience.

input:
Looking for a delicious New Year's Day brunch was hard this year in New Orleans. We didn't want to wait in line and wanted instant gratification. Although we may have felt tired, my bf and I were appropriately dressed to go to Mr. B's. As soon as we walked in, I felt transported into a different world. Jazz music was playing and I felt at home. 

First of all, I could not have been more grateful for the fresh loaf of bread we were given. We devoured it in a matter of minutes. Then came the gumbo ya-ya. It was spicy and savory and everything I expected from a gumbo. Finally came the bbq shrimp. We had been warned that these shrimp did come with their heads and tails on. Bibs were placed around our necks and we were off. The shrimp were some of the most rich and delicious ones I have ever tasted. The sauce they were served with was divine. Although it was messy, there is no other dish on the menu I would have traded for this.

Overall, service was friendly and quick at Mr. B's. The food was delicious, although a little pricey. Definitely try the brunch if you are able to.
Refine this for me please:
Finding a delicious New Year's Day brunch in New Orleans proved to be challenging this year. We were determined to avoid waiting in line and desired instant gratification. Despite feeling tired, my boyfriend and I dressed appropriately for Mr. B's. Upon stepping inside, I instantly felt transported to a different world, with jazz music playing and a familiar ambiance.

I cannot express enough gratitude for the fresh loaf of bread we received. It was devoured within minutes. Subsequently, the gumbo ya-ya arrived, meeting every expectation of spiciness and savory flavor associated with a gumbo. Finally, the BBQ shrimp made their entrance, accompanied by a warning that they would come with heads and tails intact. Bibs were placed around our necks, and we eagerly delved into the rich and flavorful shrimp. The sauce they were served with was divine, making any messiness worth it. I wouldn't have traded this dish for any other option on the menu.

Overall, the service at Mr. B's was friendly and efficient. The food, while slightly expensive, was undeniably delicious. I highly recommend trying their brunch if you have the opportunity.

input:
Nice Steakhouse in St. Louis. We went here for a client dinner and was pleasantly surprised. You get a nice view of the arch on the way in to the restaurant as well. 

The Apps were OK. We ended up getting the Carmine's trio (crab cakes, scallops and toasted ravioli). Crab cakes were above average. The scallops were a little saccharine for my tastes but the ravioli was good; and let's face it...one doesn't come to St. Louis for the scallops. Thankfully the filet mignon was exceptional. It was the perfect size, not too salty and rare just like I had requested. 

This was partnered with an above average wine list to make a great night out.
Refine this for me please:
I had a pleasant surprise dining experience at a nice steakhouse in St. Louis when we went here for a client dinner. The restaurant offers a nice view of the arch as you enter. 

The appetizers, particularly the Carmine's trio consisting of crab cakes, scallops, and toasted ravioli, were decent. The crab cakes stood out as above average, while the scallops were a bit too sweet for my liking. Nonetheless, the ravioli was good. However, it's worth noting that when it comes to St. Louis, the scallops are not the main attraction. 

Fortunately, the filet mignon was exceptional. It was perfectly sized, not overly salty, and cooked rare as I had requested. Additionally, the restaurant had an above average wine list which added to the overall experience, making it a great night out.

input: Three from my office had lunch delivered from San Antonio Taco today.  It was our first time from there.  The food did not live up to the reviews.  Three of us ordered sides of refried beans and rice.  All 3 thought the beans were much too salty and the rice was clumpy.  I had beef enchiladas.  The beef was cut with the grain instead if against it so it was stringy and inedible.  I will generally give a restaurant a second try but not sure I will this time.
Refine this for me please: Three colleagues from my office decided to have lunch delivered from San Antonio Taco today, marking our first opportunity to try their food. Unfortunately, the overall experience did not match up with the positive reviews we had heard. Specifically, the three of us who ordered sides of refried beans and rice found them to be disappointingly subpar. The beans were excessively salty, while the rice had formed into unappetizing clumps. Personally, I opted for the beef enchiladas, only to find that the beef was improperly cut with the grain, resulting in a stringy and practically inedible texture. While I am typically open to giving a restaurant a second chance, I am uncertain if I will do so in this particular case.

input:
Cousin's is the place to go if you live in North Philly. I take this joint any day over Fresh Grocer. 

The only complaints I have is with the produce (which is expected considering it is COUSIN'S after all) and the hours (like many others have said, they have awful and inconvenient hours post-5pm).

That being said, I can get most essentials here and for much cheaper than anywhere else. 

This is only a two minute bike ride from my apartment so there's no reason not to shop here. Matter of fact, I'm headed there tomorrow.

When it's too cold or you're feeling to cheap to go to Trader Joe's, Cousin's is the place to head to.
Refine this for me please:
Cousin's is the go-to spot in North Philly, surpassing Fresh Grocer in my book. However, I do have a couple of gripes. Firstly, the produce is not top-notch, but that's not surprising given the name - COUSIN'S. Additionally, the store has inconvenient hours after 5pm, echoing the sentiments of many others.

Nevertheless, I can find most of my essentials here at significantly lower prices compared to other options. It's just a quick two-minute bike ride from my apartment, so there's really no excuse not to shop here. In fact, I'll be heading there tomorrow.

When it's too chilly outside or you'd rather save a few bucks than go all the way to Trader Joe's, Cousin's is the ultimate destination.

input:
I've been here twice now and sampled a bunch of what they have to offer - I feel like what you order will really dictate how much you like this place.  i.e. they do some things great and other things just so-so.

The two things I will surely go back for more of is the Sausage and Pepper Pizza (capitalized - because I mean business) and some sort of puff pastry that has a white cream in the middle - I'm sure it has a name but it escapes me.  The pizza was perfectly flavored and the sausage/peppers had a nice kick to it.  Im sure it would make for great leftovers but unfortunately (fortunately?) for me it was gone well before it found the refrigerator.  The cream puff cream was just awesome - couldn't pin-point the flavor (vanilla?) but I would prefer it to top every dessert I get from this point forward.

I also got a bunch of the other sweets (salted brownie, blondie, red velvet crumb-cake) and a few bagels.  All were good, but not great.  Was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels - whole wheat bagels usually suck.

What I didn't really like was the pepperoni pizza.  It was pretty bland for my liking - in complete contrast to the sausage and pepper pizza - and the pepperoni was pretty sparse. I also didn't like being told 25 minutes, showing up in 25 minutes and then standing there for 25 minutes waiting for the pizza.  The small shop + no chairs = awkwardly standing there for almost a half hour.  

Since it's close to me and has so many tasty looking treats yet to try - I'll surely be back.  Hopefully I'll get more 'great' than 'so-so'.
Refine this for me please:
I have visited this place twice now and have tried a variety of their offerings. However, I have noticed that your experience here largely depends on what you order. Some items are executed exceptionally well, while others are just average.

Out of everything I have tasted, there are two items I will definitely return for. Firstly, the Sausage and Pepper Pizza is a standout. Its flavors are perfectly balanced, and the sausage and peppers provide a delightful kick. I was so impressed with it that I wished I had leftovers, although it disappeared before I could save any. Secondly, there is a puff pastry with a creamy white filling that I cannot recall the name of, but it was absolutely amazing. I couldn't quite pinpoint the flavor, perhaps vanilla, but I would love to have it as a topping on every dessert I have in the future.

I also tried a variety of their other sweet treats, such as the salted brownie, blondie, and red velvet crumb cake, as well as a few of their bagels. While they were all good, they didn't quite reach the level of greatness. However, I was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels, as I usually find whole wheat bagels to be disappointing.

Unfortunately, I did not enjoy their pepperoni pizza. It lacked flavor, especially in comparison to the amazing sausage and pepper pizza, and the amount of pepperoni was quite sparse. Additionally, I was disappointed with the service. Despite being told it would take 25 minutes to prepare my order, I arrived on time only to find myself waiting an additional 25 minutes. The lack of seating in the small shop made it an awkward experience standing there for close to half an hour.

Since this place is conveniently located near me and there are still many tempting treats to try, I will definitely be back. Hopefully, my future visits will yield more "great" experiences than "so-so" ones.

input:
It is an actual speakeasy! Very cool and chill place. The ambience is classy but the vibe of the place is casual. Highly recommend if you just want to have good cocktails/drinks with good music. 
Warning: They literally serve one dish of appetizer (which is not that tasty). Don't go empty stomach and with expectation of good food (or any food). As I mentioned, it is true to its speakeasy status.
Refine this for me please:
This place is an authentic speakeasy with a cool and relaxed atmosphere. The ambiance is classy, yet the overall vibe is casual. I highly recommend it if you're looking for a great selection of cocktails or drinks accompanied by good music.

However, it's important to note that they only serve one appetizer dish, which may not be particularly tasty. So, it's best not to come here on an empty stomach or with high expectations for food. As mentioned earlier, the establishment stays true to its speakeasy status.

input: Spent way too much money to get actually spoiled food delivered to us. Ordered a huge order, over 50% of it was incorrect. Will never return to this location.
Refine this for me please: We had a disappointing experience with this establishment. Despite spending a considerable amount of money, we received spoiled food upon delivery. To make matters worse, more than 50% of our order was incorrect. As a result, we have no intentions of returning to this location.

input: This is actually a 3 1/2 star review for me. Only because everything that I wanted they did not have or weren't willing to do. Firstly, I came here specifically for the chicken slider because from the picture it showed that you can get it on a biscuit and when I told the lady taking my order, she said they don't do that -__-. Then I wanted that buttermilk bites and they weren't available, however, my brother ordered the brown buttered cream sundae and got the buttermilk bites in that!! Oh yes, and the glazed donuts are so thick and dry. I liked the sliders I had though: fried chicken, beef belly and catfish(okay). And the sundae is pretty tasty. Good for a first try but not to continue coming.
Refine this for me please: This is a 3.5-star review for me due to some disappointments in the menu options. I came specifically for the chicken slider on a biscuit, but was informed that they do not offer it. Additionally, the buttermilk bites I wanted were not available, yet my brother received them in his brown buttered cream sundae. The glazed donuts were thick and dry, which was not enjoyable. However, I did enjoy the fried chicken, beef belly, and catfish sliders, as well as the tasty sundae. Overall, it was a decent first experience, but not enough to make me want to return.

input: A short walk from my apartment I was told about a small, welcoming cafe very popular for breakfast and brunch. It did not disappoint! I had a salmon scramble with egg whites the first time i went. The second time i went i got the tofu with brown rice breakfast plate. Both meals were great!! And i was seated quickly
Refine this for me please: Just a short walk from my apartment, I had heard about a cozy and highly-regarded café that specializes in delectable breakfast and brunch options. To my delight, it certainly lived up to its reputation! During my first visit, I couldn't resist ordering the salmon scramble with egg whites. The flavors were absolutely fantastic. On my subsequent visit, I opted for the tofu with brown rice breakfast plate, which did not disappoint either. Both meals were exceptional, and I was promptly seated upon arrival.

input: Went for Dinner at 6pm on a Friday and expect it to be packed, luckily for us, it wasn't. The staff is very friendly and the atmosphere is straight out of Magnolia Journal. The food was pretty dang good and drinks are too. The only reason I left off a star was the fact it took a little while to get our cocktails and our appetizer came at the same time as our food. But, they're new and I've been in hospitality before, so I get it!
Refine this for me please: We went for dinner at 6pm on a Friday, anticipating a packed restaurant. Fortunately, it wasn't crowded. The staff was exceptionally friendly, and the ambiance exuded the charm reminiscent of Magnolia Journal. The food surpassed our expectations, and the drinks were enjoyable as well. The only reason I deducted a star is because it took slightly longer than expected to receive our cocktails, and our appetizer arrived simultaneously with our main course. However, considering the establishment is relatively new, and having experience in the hospitality industry myself, I understand and empathize with their situation.

input: This is a great quiet place to eat very 1960's business style.  You can have the food of Tony's or eat off the bar menu.  I had the Risotto which was excellent.  Other people at the table had the special, linguine with shrimp and lobster, and strip steak.  Everyone loved their meals.  Of course the service here is fantastic.  They are not overbearing but attentive as well.
Refine this for me please: This establishment offers a fantastic dining experience characterized by a peaceful ambiance reminiscent of 1960's business style. The menu options include delectable dishes available at Tony's or from the bar menu. Personally, I highly recommend the Risotto for its exceptional taste. Moreover, other individuals at our table savored the special of linguine with succulent shrimp and lobster, as well as the perfectly cooked strip steak. The entire group thoroughly enjoyed their meals. The impeccable service provided by the staff here strikes a perfect balance between attentiveness and not being overly intrusive.

input: My go to place for sushi rolls! Their rolls are huge and the service is excellent. My favorite is heat attack appetizer( korean style jalapeno poppers) sapporo roll and honey roll. They also have a section of deepfried rolls on the menu! Their food always look so  fresh and appetizing. Great presentation. Try the spicy sashimi bowl if you wanna try something new!
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend this place as my ultimate destination for sushi rolls! Notably, their rolls stand out for their immense size, leaving customers more than satisfied. Furthermore, the service provided here is truly exceptional. Personally, I'm fond of their heat attack appetizer (Korean style jalapeno poppers), as well as their delectable Sapporo roll and honey roll. It's worth mentioning that they even offer a selection of deep-fried rolls on their menu, which adds an extra element of variety to their offerings. The food at this place always appears fresh and alluring, boasting an impeccable presentation. For an adventurous palate, I suggest trying their spicy sashimi bowl - it's a unique experience you won't want to miss out on!

input:
Ok. I am not the type to complain, but I have been here twice and both times I have had terrible service at the bar. The first bartender served me but acted as if I was bothering him.  This second time, with a completely different bartender mind you, it was worse. I am not dressed like a street person or anything, and I am not pan-handling. But you would think that I was the way he acted. First, I sit at the bar and I am waiting for service. So, the bartender walks by me, pours a glass a water, turns in front of me, puts the water down, gives me some stupid half-grin then walks off. Not one audible word of greeting or a grunt passed between his lips. Then, he gets a menu, drops that down and walks off again! Not a sound. Is it me, but when a customer enters an eating establishment, shouldn't they be greeted in some manner?  Not looked at like "why are you here. I have better things to do"?  I am not looking for a royal salute or anything. Just "Hey man, what can I get ya?"  or something to that affect.   Anyway, I start to look at the drink and food menus. Then, a group of anywhere from 10-15 people come in behind me and say, to what looked like a manager, "We don't want to eat, is it ok if we just have a few drinks at the bar?". The manager says "Sure." The guy then says, "Can we get few beers down here"? (paraphrasing). The bartender says "Sure!" and proceed to service this group, one-by-one, as they order drinks. Ok, fine technically, I was looking at the menu when this started. But still, he walked back and forth, right in front of me, for about 10-12 minutes. Not once did he say, "Hey, just shout and I will get you something", or "Hey man, just give me a few minutes and I will be right with you". Nothing!  It was obvious it was a big group, but I mean, he gave no acknowledgement to the fact that I was sitting there waiting! 

Long story short - after this 10-12 minutes of waiting, I just walked out and went somewhere else. Now this place has about 4\5 stars with around 500 reviews. So, I guess people like it. But their bartenders are as unfriendly as I have ever encountered.  Maybe if you get a table it's different.
Refine this for me please:
I visited this establishment twice and unfortunately, both experiences at the bar were extremely disappointing. During my first visit, the bartender seemed annoyed and uninterested in serving me. On my second visit, with a different bartender, the service was even worse. Despite being appropriately dressed and not causing any trouble, I was treated as if I didn't belong there. As I sat at the bar waiting for service, the bartender walked past me without acknowledging my presence, poured a glass of water, placed it in front of me, and gave me a half-hearted grin before walking away without a word of greeting or assistance. He returned briefly to drop off a menu before disappearing once again. I couldn't help but feel ignored and unwelcome. It's common courtesy for customers to be greeted upon entering an eating establishment, and it seems as though I was seen as an inconvenience rather than a valued patron. I don't expect a grand display, but a simple "Hey, what can I get you?" would have sufficed. 

As I started perusing the drink and food menus, a large group of about 10-15 individuals arrived and asked the apparent manager if they could just have a few drinks at the bar instead of dining. The manager approved their request, and the bartender promptly attended to their orders with enthusiasm. Although I understand that the group's arrival may have diverted the bartender's attention momentarily, it was disheartening to see him serve them attentively while completely disregarding my presence. I patiently waited for approximately 10-12 minutes as he passed back and forth in front of me, never acknowledging my existence or offering any explanation for the delay. Eventually, I decided to leave and find another establishment to enjoy a drink. 

It's worth noting that this place has received generally positive reviews with a rating of around 4/5 stars from approximately 500 customers. However, based on my personal encounters with their bartenders, I found them to be exceptionally unfriendly. Perhaps the experience differs when sitting at a table, but I cannot recommend their bar service.

input:
Love it here

The atmosphere is great the options are more than average and the lunch bento boxes are great.  If you have the opportunity always try the boba as well.

Those complaining are just picky and should go back to eating at home.  

Try their beef braised soup as it is hearty and delicious.
Refine this for me please:
I absolutely love it here. The atmosphere is fantastic, the variety of options is well above average, and their lunch bento boxes are simply amazing. I highly recommend trying their boba as well - it's a must. 
As for the complaints, I believe they're just being overly picky. They should probably stick to eating at home if they can't appreciate the wonderful experience this place offers. 
Additionally, you should definitely give their beef braised soup a try. It's a hearty and delicious dish that you won't regret ordering.

input: Beautiful decor, great atmosphere, amazing food! My husband and I were thinking how it's NY prices but better quality than most we have had at this price point. He had udon noodles and I had a few rolls (Spicy Salmon is a must!) Flavors were great- not too strong but tasteful! :) We enjoyed our experience!
Refine this for me please: The restaurant has beautiful decor and a great atmosphere, making it the perfect setting for a memorable dining experience. The food is truly exceptional, surpassing the quality typically found at this price point in New York. My husband opted for the udon noodles while I indulged in a few rolls, with the Spicy Salmon being an absolute must-try. The flavors were balanced and tasteful, not overpowering in any way. Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our experience at this restaurant.

input: Hotel is lovely. The front desk staff is extremely friendly and helpful. We were lucky enough to get a room away from the club so we had no problem sleeping. If you are looking for quiet stay somewhere else if you looking for fun this is perfect!
Refine this for me please: The hotel is absolutely lovely, boasting charming accommodations and a pleasing ambiance. Notably, the front desk staff is exceptional, displaying an impressive level of friendliness and unparalleled helpfulness throughout our stay. We were fortunate enough to be allocated a room situated away from the club, ensuring a peaceful environment that facilitated uninterrupted sleep. It is worth mentioning that if you aspire for tranquility, it might be advisable to seek accommodation elsewhere. However, if your objective is to have a joyous and entertaining experience, this hotel proves to be an excellent choice.

input: I loved loved loved the pizza here. I returned and got their gnocchi and it was amazing as well. Really fresh ingredients nice variety on the menu. Really felt like a small family restaurant in Europe. Best pizza in middle Tennessee.
Refine this for me please: I simply adored the pizza at this place - it was absolutely incredible! In fact, I loved it so much that I decided to revisit and try their gnocchi, which turned out to be equally amazing. The restaurant offers a fantastic range of dishes made with the freshest ingredients, and the menu variety is delightful. It truly felt like dining in a cozy family restaurant, reminiscent of those found in Europe. Without a doubt, it serves the best pizza in middle Tennessee.

input: For a $16 haircut, I was expecting an OK-looking trim (all I really needed was some damage control - just someone to lop off my split ends and maybe add a few layers).  What I got was a very professionally looking haircut that works well with my face shape and made my hair a lot healthier and happier.  My expectations were far exceeded - and it definitely surpassed my last 'professional' hair salon experience.  Plus, the shampoo smelled amazing and the girl was really thorough.  I wish I had brought more cash to tip her!!!  The only thing you should keep in mind before going is time.  I had to wait an extra half an hour and it was the longest haircut I've ever had.  I would much rather have the student take the time to make sure it looks good, however, than have someone do a half-ass job.  I think it's important that the school has a series of steps and checklists their students have to go through to ensure they are giving you the best experience possible.  Just make sure you have a decent block of time in your schedule to relax in the chair!
Refine this for me please:
I had initially expected a basic trim for my $16 haircut, mainly to fix the split ends and possibly add a few layers. However, I was pleasantly surprised to receive a professionally done haircut that complemented my face shape and significantly improved the overall health and appearance of my hair. It exceeded my expectations and surpassed my previous salon experience. Additionally, the shampoo used smelled amazing and the stylist was very thorough. I regret not having brought more cash to tip her generously. 

Before visiting this salon, it is important to consider the time factor. I had to wait an additional half an hour, making it the longest haircut I have ever had. Nevertheless, I appreciate the student taking their time to ensure a satisfactory result rather than rushing through the process. The school's emphasis on step-by-step procedures and checklists to guarantee the best experience for customers is commendable. Just be sure to allocate a decent amount of time in your schedule to fully enjoy your time in the chair.

input: My daughter was married at the Presidio Chapel in May, 2015. The wedding was magical and we were all treated really well by Rain Longo(she coordinates special events in the Chapel). She was very patient, supportive and enthusiastic. The chapel itself made for an outstanding and very authentic venue. My daughter and bridesmaids were able to get ready in a beautiful adjoining room. The rental of the Chapel included use for 6 hours and it was very affordable. Thanks to all for making this special day so perfect. Thanks!!!!
Refine this for me please: My daughter's wedding at the Presidio Chapel in May 2015 was truly magical. We were incredibly impressed with the service provided by Rain Longo, the coordinator for special events at the Chapel. Rain showed great patience, support, and enthusiasm throughout the process. The chapel itself was a stunning and authentic venue, creating the perfect atmosphere for the ceremony. Additionally, there was a beautiful adjoining room where my daughter and her bridesmaids could prepare. The rental package for the Chapel, which included 6 hours of use, was affordable and well worth it. We would like to express our sincere gratitude to everyone involved in making this day so perfect. Thank you all for everything!

input:
I'm not a regular waxer, but went in for a pre-vacation treat. The wax specialist Miriam was prompt and knew what she was doing. She spent much of our hour together telling me why my regular shaving is bad and waxing is good, and seriously marketing the EWC products to me. 
Brows and lower legs were done well. Underarms were left with a decent number of stray hairs which she told me I could tweeze out later. Little bits of wax were left on my skin here and there. Overall I felt like I did not walk out of there ready to hit the beach.
Refine this for me please:
I recently visited a wax specialist named Miriam for a pre-vacation wax, despite not being a regular waxer. Miriam was punctual and demonstrated expertise in her work. Throughout our appointment, she spent a significant portion of our time discussing the drawbacks of regular shaving and advocating for waxing as a superior option. Additionally, she actively promoted various products from the EWC line.

Regarding the actual treatment, Miriam did a satisfactory job on my brows and lower legs. However, there were a noticeable amount of stray hairs remaining on my underarms, which she advised me to tweeze later. Furthermore, I noticed small remnants of wax left on my skin in certain areas. These factors led me to feel that my beach readiness was not fully achieved upon leaving the establishment.

input:
The food was very good. The reason for the three stars is the noise level. I was with three other people in a corner table and we had to shout to hear each other. If the restaurant could work on the noise level, it would absolutely get more stars. The pad see ew got great reviews from the person who ordered it. I got The King and I (veg/chicken/shrimp stir fry) and it was excellent. Nice heat and curry flavor. The pad thai was a bit sweet I thought, but the person who ordered it really liked it.

Portion sizes are not enormous. We had some leftovers but also didn't come in starving.

Good service, very attentive. The noise level was the only negative.
Refine this for me please: The food at this restaurant was very good, but the reason for the three-star rating is the high noise level. Despite being seated at a corner table with three other people, we had to shout to hear each other. If the restaurant could address this issue, it would certainly earn more stars. One person who ordered the pad see ew had great reviews for it. As for me, I ordered The King and I (a stir fry dish with vegetables, chicken, and shrimp) which was excellent, with a nice blend of heat and curry flavor. However, I found the pad thai to be a bit too sweet for my taste, although the person who ordered it enjoyed it. The portion sizes were not huge but reasonable. We had some leftovers but didn't arrive famished. The service was good, with attentive staff, but the noise level was the only downside.

input:
***Please note that if you lose something valuable you may not get it back. The person who may clean the vehicle may be a thief. I left in the car my radar detector complete with a case not logged in to their lost and found. When I check in my rental on 12/21 and returned 01/02/2018 to visit the counter they told me nothing was found. They also told me that for something with a case go missing was very unlikely. Yet they found nothing. Hmmm, I wonder how it can go missing when it was the only place I left it? I filed a lost ticket with them; Reference Number: 4355421, Reported: 12/21/2017.

They may think their employees may be honest but my $300 radar detector is nowhere to be found at their location. So? Yes, one of their employee's stole it. 

I'm a fan of the concept of picking your car. As someone who has been using the same rental place in St. Louis Airport for 8 months and counting. I can tell you they do lousy job at cleaning the cars. I'm always finding plastic bottles underneath the back seats.

I'm also finding a lot un-wiped of front seat and dashboard areas full of sticky substances. The cars are never fully clean as someone who rents from them weekly.

This location does a shitty job of making cars ready for travel. As someone who has access to the execute cars due to the amount of travel I do. They fail to meet some simple travel requirements you expect when you rent. 

Next time you rent look underneath the seats in the passenger areas and you may find plastic bottle under them.

I would love for them to review the cameras and see who cleaned the car so they can fire them on the day I returned the rental! I brought them thousand of dollars and I do expect a refund for the stolen item.
Refine this for me please:
Please be aware that there is a risk of losing valuable items, as the person responsible for cleaning the vehicle may be dishonest. In my recent experience, I left my radar detector, which was securely stored in a case, in the car. However, upon checking with the rental counter on 12/21 and returning on 01/02/2018, they informed me that nothing was found. Despite being assured that it was unlikely for an item with a case to go missing, it remains inexplicably lost. I have filed a lost ticket with reference number 4355421 on 12/21/2017.

Considering the circumstances, it appears that one of their employees may have taken my $300 radar detector. I have been a loyal customer of this particular rental place at St. Louis Airport for 8 months and have noticed that they do not adequately clean the cars. I frequently find plastic bottles under the back seats and encounter uncleaned areas, including sticky substances on the front seat and dashboard. It is disappointing that they consistently fail to meet the basic cleanliness standards one expects when renting a vehicle.

I encourage future renters to thoroughly inspect the passenger areas, particularly underneath the seats, as plastic bottles may be hidden there. It would be greatly appreciated if the rental company could review their security footage to identify the employee responsible for cleaning the vehicle on the day I returned the rental. This employee should be held accountable for the missing item. Considering the substantial amount of money I have spent with this company, I expect a refund for the stolen item.

input: This place is so great. I love the laid back atmosphere. Walked right in with our dog and were seating on the cozy wrap around porch outside. We ate here the last morning of our trip and it was the perfect ending. I stayed full long enough to get me through and 8 hour car ride home! I had the bananas foster French toast which was amazing but super rich. I couldn't eat it all because of the portion size and richness. My fiancé opted for the healthier choice of a vegetable omelet which was delicious as well. I can't wait to come back here and try something else on the menu. I will definitely try one of their famous juices next time.
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely amazing, with a laid-back atmosphere that I adore. We were able to easily bring our dog in and got a cozy spot on the wrap-around porch outside. On the last morning of our trip, we decided to dine here and it was the perfect way to end our vacation. The food was so satisfying that it kept me full for the entire 8-hour car ride home. I ordered the bananas foster French toast and it was absolutely incredible, although quite rich. The portion size was generous, so I couldn't finish it all. Meanwhile, my fiancé made a healthier choice and opted for the delicious vegetable omelet. I'm already looking forward to returning to try something else from their menu. Next time, I definitely want to sample one of their famous juices.

input: The food here is delicious and the portions are amazing for the price.  The girl who works behind the counter is an absolute sweetheart.  Always smiling and happy.   I wish I worked closer so I could come more often.
Refine this for me please: The food at this place is incredibly tasty and the portions offered for the price are truly impressive. Moreover, the girl who works behind the counter is an absolute gem - she consistently wears a bright smile and exudes genuine happiness. If only my workplace were closer, I would gladly frequent this place more often.

input: Nice scenery of nature. Great trail for running, walking, hiking and biking. Plenty of places to sit for a short break along the way.
Refine this for me please: Immerse yourself in breathtaking natural scenery, featuring a diverse range of landscapes. Discover an exceptional trail suitable for running, walking, hiking, and biking enthusiasts alike. Enhance your adventure with various scenic spots where you can conveniently pause and rejuvenate.

input: Really truly slow service.  Not the waitress. The kitchen. 40 min to get a pasta and salad.  Recommended if you want to really drag that date out.
Refine this for me please: The service at this establishment is exceptionally slow, particularly in the kitchen. It took a staggering 40 minutes to receive a simple order of pasta and salad. This place might be worth considering if you desire an exceptionally extended date experience.

input: This place is wonderful! Obviously the chips, salsa and beans are yummy, but get the guacamole too! The chimichanga bites are fantastic, whatever the sauce is that comes with them is super good! For dinner, the street tacos are amazing, so are the enchiladas. They don't have a full bar, but you can still get a real margarita, and they pack a punch! They make them at their other location and bring them over, which is clever, because this location doesn't yet have its liquor license. Overall 4 out 5 stars because it's a good Mexican restaurant, but 5 stars is reserved for my most favorites only. Close second though, and we love that it's right downtown. Oh, and the service... very good! We usually always have the same server, and she is very nice and attentive.
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely amazing! The chips, salsa, and beans are delicious, and let's not forget about the guacamole which is a must-try! The chimichanga bites are incredibly tasty, especially with the flavorful sauce they come with. For dinner, the street tacos and enchiladas are out of this world. While they don't have a full bar, their real margaritas will definitely pack a punch. It's impressive how they make them at their other location and bring them over since this one doesn't have its liquor license yet. Overall, I would give this place a solid 4 out of 5 stars as it's a fantastic Mexican restaurant, but I reserve 5 stars for my absolute favorites. That being said, it's definitely a close second, and the fact that it's conveniently located downtown adds to its appeal. Oh, and let's not forget about the service, which is top-notch! We usually have the pleasure of being served by the same friendly and attentive server each time we visit.

input:
I LOVE JONES. Honestly.....

For dessert? I had the Duncan Hines slice of yellow cake and glass of milk. Genius.

We came back AGAIN a few weeks ago when a friend was visiting from LA. I had the Seared Ahi Tuna. The husband had the Halibut. Our friend had the Roast Beef Dinner. Our friend won when it came to food selection. My belly was so warm and happy after one bite of his roast beef. The meat was succulent, juicy, the perfect medium rare. The mashed taters were creamy with a slight hint of garlic. Mmmm.

I preferred my husband's halibut over my tuna. The tuna was good, but the halibut had more flavor, IMO.

Can't wait to go back again. Yum yum yum.

I fell in love with Jones at the YEE earlier this year. The food was absolutely divine, offering comforting and indulgent dishes. From the mac and cheese that I could've eaten with a ladle, to the sliders, pigs in a blanket, and delicious cocktails, every bite was a delight.

My love for Jones was reaffirmed when I visited with my mother. The calamari surpassed my expectations, perfectly crispy and bursting with flavor. And for dessert, the Duncan Hines slice of yellow cake paired with a glass of milk was pure genius.

Recently, we returned yet again when a friend from LA was in town. Our food choices varied, but it was our friend who won the selection game with the Roast Beef Dinner. Each bite of his succulent, juicy meat was a delight, and the creamy mashed potatoes with a hint of garlic completed the amazing experience.

Although my tuna dish was good, I have to admit that I preferred my husband's halibut. It had a bolder flavor which I found more enjoyable.

I am eagerly anticipating our next visit to Jones. The food is simply irresistible.

input:
I purchased a used 09 Rav4 from Glanzmann Subaru last month. Coming from TN, I chose to purchase this vehicle from Glanzmann due to its limited availability and attractive price. I communicated with sales on numerous occasions before committing to purchase from Glanzmann nearly 1000 miles from home.

The process was overall quite simple, though I felt we could have gotten alot more done regarding interstate complications prior to completing travel plans to purchase the vehicle. My only actual complaint stems from the vehicle's description. As an out of state buyer, I was at the mercy of the sales team to accurately describe and depict any conditional issues that might be of interest to a prospective buyer. Unfortunately, none of the issues with this vehicle were highlighted, depicted, described, or otherwise demonstrated throughout the entire sales process. I even asked the sales agent to, while on the phone, inspect the vehicle and describe any possible imperfection so that I could have no surprises upon arrival. I spent several hundred dollars in travel expenses to collect this vehicle, only to discover there were a number of aesthetic defects that deserved attention (large dents, cracked paint, cuts in leather). I had limited time and opportunity to react to these conditional flaws and purchased the vehicle - I had already flown from Nashville to Philadelphia! 

This is obviously a small family-owned dealership. I expected a considerably more honest and direct interaction and was disappointed with the outcome. The automobile is a fine machine, but the defects certainly take away from the value. Mr. Jeff Glanzmann, I implore you to make honesty your #1 policy.  I had the opportunity to purchase the same vehicle, with honestly similar defects, from a dealership in Atlanta for the same price. I opted to purchase yours, incurring not-insignificant travel expenses, because of it's immaculate description.
Refine this for me please:
I recently purchased a used 2009 Rav4 from Glanzmann Subaru, located nearly 1000 miles away from my home in Tennessee. I chose to buy from Glanzmann because of the vehicle's limited availability and attractive price. Before committing to the purchase, I communicated with the sales team multiple times.

While the overall purchasing process was relatively simple, I believe that more could have been done to address the complications of buying from a different state before finalizing my travel plans. However, my main complaint lies in the vehicle's description. As an out-of-state buyer, I relied heavily on the accuracy of the sales team's description and depiction of the car's condition. Unfortunately, none of the vehicle's existing issues were highlighted, described, depicted, or demonstrated throughout the entire sales process. Even when I requested the sales agent to inspect the car and disclose any imperfections, nothing was mentioned. 

When I traveled to collect the vehicle, I was disappointed to discover several aesthetic defects, including large dents, cracked paint, and cuts in the leather. Due to limited time and options, I had no choice but to purchase the car despite these flaws, after having already flown all the way from Nashville to Philadelphia.

As a small family-owned dealership, I had expected a more honest and transparent interaction. Although the car itself is in good working condition, these defects significantly diminish its value. Mr. Jeff Glanzmann, I kindly urge you to prioritize honesty as your number one policy. I had the chance to purchase a similar vehicle with honestly disclosed defects from a dealership in Atlanta for the same price, but I chose yours based on its seemingly impeccable description.

input:
My girlfriends and I ate at the Creole House for dinner. Our decision to dine here was largely based on the fact that it was pouring raining and this restaurant is next door to our hotel. We started with the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. The bacon garlic oysters were average, at best. The oysters were overpowered by the cheese and bacon, which was disappointing. The buffalo wings were pretty good and seasoned well. For entrees, we ordered: 1) jumbalaya pasta, 2) blackened red fish and 3) canal street red fish. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite (would not order again). The blackened red fish was just okay and the skimpy side of sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were VERY salty (would order again as a LAST resort). The canal street red fish wasn't great but my friend would order it again. Her biggest complaint was that it had very little garlic sauce. We also ordered paddle boat drinks, which tasted good but were more juice vs alcohol (had to order an extra shot).

So, overall, we were underwhelmed with the food, making it a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, was great...very hospitable and tried his best to make sure we were satisfied.
Refine this for me please:
My girlfriends and I decided to have dinner at the Creole House due to its proximity to our hotel during the heavy rain. We began our meal with the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. Unfortunately, the bacon garlic oysters were average, as the cheese and bacon overwhelmed the flavor of the oysters. On the other hand, the buffalo wings were enjoyable with a well-balanced seasoning. 

For our main courses, we ordered three dishes. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite, leaving us unimpressed and unlikely to reorder it in the future. The blackened red fish was decent, but the small side of sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) was excessively salty, making us hesitant to choose it again except as a last resort. The canal street red fish didn't stand out, but one of my friends would consider ordering it again, although there was a noticeable scarcity of garlic sauce. 

Furthermore, we decided to try the paddle boat drinks, which were flavorful, but they contained more juice than alcohol, leading us to order an extra shot. Overall, the dining experience left us feeling underwhelmed with the food, resulting in a solid 3-star rating. However, our server, Alexander, provided exceptional service, displaying great hospitality and making efforts to ensure our satisfaction.

input:
Okay, don't jump on me for this, but its partially my fault because I held them to such high expectations (due to the hype and anticipation of them opening up here) before actually eating at this location. I read so much about it on Facebook and the likes......so reading and seeing the yummy pics; well I just knew it would be all that.....untill yesterday.....

Me and my bf Vince went to BlackFinn for Sunday lunch yesterday. The atmosphere was cool and it was really nice inside. The staff was pleasant as well, so I'm thinking "hum...I like...". We ordered  a couple of mojitos and we also had another drink, which was okay.  Time to order; I ordered the Cuban sandwich, hold the mustard, and add mayo instead....with Black Finn fries and my bf ordered the Prime Rib sandwich with au jus and the same fries.  We got our order, which took a bit of time but it was okay. Everything looked so yummy and I knew they were going to meet my expectations. Now mind ya, my bf put off going to BlackFinn since they day they opened and I've been on him to go here. So anyway, the fries were a bit salty, but good. I had a choice of two dipping sauces, which I believe were ranch and barbeque. Delicious! I bit into the sandwich and what did I taste? A mouth full of mustard!!! Eeewww!! Okay, did I not say "hold the mustard"? So lo and behold, my food had to be returned while my bf ate his food. His beef about his sandwich (no pun intended) was that there was more bread than meat. I looked at it and I noticed the same thing. Also, the au jus was a bit low as well and wasn't enough for the sandwich.  So I'm like the little old lady from the back-in-the-day commercials saying "Where's the beef?" LOL. Wow! 

Finally, after he finishes his sandwich, my food finally comes out and guess what? They left the swiss cheese off the sandwich. WTF! Okay, so at this point I'm like "forget it, just take it back." How many times must I send my sandwich back to get it right? Now I must say that the manager on duty was accommodating and she took care of the check and apolgized for the errors. So for her professionalism and the fact that the staff was very polite, I give them two stars. Will I go back....yes I will give them another chance to redeem themselves, but all in my ear is my bf saying that there must have been a reason why he hesitated to come here and this is why.  Oh well......
Refine this for me please:
I apologize for any inconvenience, but I take partial responsibility for this experience as I had high expectations for this restaurant before actually trying it. I had read a lot about it on social media and seen appetizing pictures, so I was confident it would meet my expectations - until yesterday.

My boyfriend Vince and I decided to have Sunday lunch at BlackFinn. The ambiance was pleasant and the interior was nice. The staff was friendly, which left a good impression on me. We ordered a couple of mojitos and another drink, which was decent. When it was time to order our food, I requested a Cuban sandwich without mustard and with mayo instead, along with Black Finn fries. My boyfriend ordered the Prime Rib sandwich with au jus and the same fries.

Our order took a bit of time, but that was acceptable. The presentation of the food looked appetizing and I was hopeful that it would live up to my expectations. However, the fries were a bit salty, though still tasty. There were two dipping sauces, possibly ranch and barbecue, which were delicious. As I took a bite of my sandwich, I was surprised to taste a mouthful of mustard - despite specifically requesting to hold it. Disappointed, I had to return my food while my boyfriend continued eating his sandwich. He also had a complaint about his sandwich, namely that there was more bread than meat. I noticed the same issue when I looked at it. Furthermore, the au jus was insufficient for the sandwich. I couldn't help but think of the old commercials saying, "Where's the beef?".

Finally, after he finished his sandwich, my food arrived, only to find that they had forgotten to include the swiss cheese on the sandwich. Frustrated, I decided to give up and asked them to take it back. How many times should I have to send my sandwich back to get it right? However, I must commend the accommodating manager on duty, who took care of the bill and apologized for the mistakes. Due to her professionalism and the overall politeness of the staff, I am giving them two stars. I will give them another chance to redeem themselves, although my boyfriend is skeptical, considering this experience and his initial hesitation to try this restaurant. Oh well, we will see how it goes next time.

input:
I have to start out by saying, why do those who like hookah not know about this place?! It was such a wonderful experience! Please hear me out!

My mission on this review is to get the word out! A friend and I went spur of the moment and I'm glad we did. From the outside of the building you wouldn't know it was a hookah bar (except the giant sign of course lol). The moment you open that giant wooden door, the decor and paint color gives it that authentic look. Warm yellow paint with evil eyes and giant metal wall lamps with cutouts shining red surrounding all the walls.
When you go up a few steps there's a gift shop, a table, and the register. They ask you to take a seat upstairs and they follow you shortly after. (There's even another upstairs that I barely peaked at).
This is the amazing part: cushions on the floor with giant metal mandala tables!!!! It was so authentic I could barely handle my excitement. They have a menu with drinks, food and hookah. Water was only a dollar which was amazing because hookah bars are usually pretty pricy.
We smoked "sex on the beach" flavored shisha. It was smooth! Very smooth! We even brought bubbles for the trip to have a little fun :)
What I like about this place compared to other loud hookah bars is that it wasn't even close to being hectic. I felt like I should have whispered at first, but after awhile I was more comfortable. Only one other couple was there and they were very nice to talk to as well. The older man and the young guy was extremely nice. The younger dude checked in on us and was sociable which was really kinda nice but not overbearing. 

If you want a low key, quiet and chill hookah bar, this should be at the top of people's lists.
Refine this for me please:
Let me start by expressing my amazement and surprise that more people who enjoy hookah aren't aware of this incredible place! Trust me when I say that it was an absolute delight! I urge you to listen to what I have to say!

My goal with this review is to spread the word about this hidden gem. A friend and I decided to visit on a whim, and I'm incredibly grateful that we did. From the exterior of the building, you wouldn't suspect it to be a hookah bar, except for the obvious giant sign, of course (lol). The moment you swing open the massive wooden door, the authentic decor and paint colors transport you into another world. The warm yellow walls adorned with evil eye motifs, and the grand metal wall lamps casting red light, completely immerse you in the ambiance.

As you ascend a few steps, you'll find a gift shop, a table, and the register. They kindly ask you to take a seat upstairs, where they promptly join you shortly after. (There's even another floor upstairs that I only briefly glimpsed). Now, here comes the truly amazing part: the seating consists of comfortable floor cushions surrounding exquisite metal mandala tables! It felt so authentic that it was almost overwhelming. The menu offers a variety of drinks, food, and, of course, hookah. I was pleasantly surprised to find that water was only a dollar, which is quite a steal considering hookah bars are usually quite pricey.

We opted for the "sex on the beach" flavored shisha, and let me tell you, it was impeccably smooth! In fact, we even brought along some bubbles to make our experience even more enjoyable :) 

What sets this place apart from other bustling hookah bars is its serene and tranquil atmosphere. Initially, I felt as though I should speak in hushed whispers, but as time passed, I grew more comfortable. To my delight, there was only one other couple present, and they were incredibly friendly and engaging. Both the older gentleman and the young man were extremely cordial. The younger patron even made sure to check on us and engage in friendly conversation without being overwhelming.

If you're in search of a low-key, peaceful, and relaxed hookah bar, this establishment absolutely must be at the top of your list.

input: I'm not from this area and trusted good 'ol Yelp to find a salon to get a gel manicure and I think I definitely found the best one in this area. input:

input: Solid cheesesteaks.  Cheese fries are also good.  Not worth venturing far for, I'd say you can get similar in most of Philly.

input:
hmm deep fried balls. This was my first venture with takoyaki and I love Japanese food of any kind, so needless to say I was excited. I ordered the original and was served 6 deep fried balls of goodness. They were tasty, albeit doughy, but left a greasy aching not so fresh feeling. I needed to be drunk to really appreciate the grease. Since it was my first venture I'll say its worth a try, but buyer beware they're super heavy for being small balls of dough. 

The curry chicken I had was a bit disappointing. I scarfed it down thanks to my near state of starvation, but found the roux too rich for my taste. Its worth another trip for japanese fast food- one of my faves and sorely lacking in the city, but its certainly not the best I've had...
Refine this for me please:
hmm deep fried balls. This was my first experience trying takoyaki, and as a lover of all kinds of Japanese food, I was eagerly looking forward to it. I ordered the original flavor and was served a plate of 6 deep fried balls that were bursting with flavor. They were undeniably tasty, although the texture was slightly doughy, and I couldn't shake off the greasy aftertaste that left me feeling a bit less than fresh. In order to truly appreciate the grease, I found that I needed to be in a slightly intoxicated state. Since it was my first time trying takoyaki, I would say it's worth giving it a shot, but be forewarned that these small balls of dough can be surprisingly heavy.

On to the curry chicken I ordered, it didn't quite live up to my expectations. I quickly devoured it due to my extreme hunger, but I found the roux to be too rich for my personal taste. However, this place is still worth another visit for its selection of Japanese fast food, which is one of my favorites and unfortunately not easily found in this city. Nevertheless, I must admit that it's not the best Japanese fast food I've ever had...

input: Nice wines and great location. Too bad they don't have food. But you can bring food up and enjoy the view with your pup so they get big points for being dog friendly! Lovely!

input: I truly enjoyed the atmosphere, the service (Connor) and my dinner meal. I had the cakes for an appetizer, a cup of barley soup and the shrimp ravioli. Malbec glass of wine was perfect. input: I have eaten here mainly for breakfast, but the juevos rancheros was amazing.  We did stop in and eat chips and salsa and my wife got one tamale for a snack.  Both were great.  The salsa was a little spicy, which I enjoy and the tamale was home made and delicious.  We'll be back.

input:
3.50 stars.  

Gabby's wasn't open.  I knew that.  Neither was Rotier's.  But my handy Yelp app had assured me that Fido's was open.  Imagine the disappointment when I realized there was a very real possibility that no burgers would happen on this trip down to the Deep South.  Would I really have to wait two more weeks when I would find solace in East Texas?   

"We can try Burger up," I mentioned.  

"Why don't you just call them?" hissed the appropriately nicknamed Viper.  

True.  We didn't have to keep driving around aimlessly.  So I call Burger Up, and a very pleasant, sweet voice assures me they are indeed open.  

Viper: "What was her name?  She sounded hot."
  
Me: "Paige."

Viper: "Yeah, she's definitely hot.  Have you ever met an unattractive Paige?"

Me: "Good point.  At least we have that going for us."

Paige was indeed attractive, but this review isn't about a photogenic individual who happens to work at Burger Up.  It's about what ended up being a visit to our fourth choice for burgers in Nashville.  

Burger Up follows a national trend towards upscale burgers.  My particular order consisted of a medium rare patty served with aged cheddar, Benton's bacon (very good), and ketchup served on an artisan bun.  Basically, it was a gussied up bacon cheeseburger, but it was a rather tasty one.  My major complaint is that I wish the actual meat itself exhibited more flavor.  Having said that, the burger was cooked properly and the flavors worked well together.  I ordered some wilted spinach on the side (mediocre) and truffle fries.  Let's talk about those truffle fries for a bit.  I know more people are apparently into the sweet potato fries here, but I think they are missing the boat.  Burger Up's truffle tries have pleasant aroma, taste great, and are the perfect texture for soaking up oil.  If you are on a diet, it is true you should skip these delightful fries.  But if that were the case, why are you at a burger joint in the first place?  Seriously, if you get nothing else out of my review, please do yourself a favor and order the truffle fries.  

Burger Up also boast an interesting beer menu with semi-obscure breweries from the Deep South included in the list.  I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi - not bad.  I could imagine Burger Up could be a decent place to drink for a bit after eating.  

If I attended Vanderbilt, I would probably go here on a moderately frequent basis.  If you want a change from the dive bar hamburger, Burger Up is a decent change of pace.
Refine this for me please:
Burger Up in Nashville, with a rating of 3.50 stars, was our fourth choice for burgers after finding that Gabby's and Rotier's were closed. As I called to check if they were open, I had the pleasure of speaking with a friendly and attractive staff member named Paige. However, this review is not about her but rather about our experience at Burger Up.

Burger Up aligns with the popular trend of upscale burgers, and my order consisted of a medium rare patty with aged cheddar, delicious Benton's bacon, and ketchup on a well-crafted artisan bun. While the burger was flavorful and the ingredients worked well together, I found the actual meat lacking in taste. The burger was cooked properly, though. On the side, I ordered wilted spinach, which was mediocre, and their standout truffle fries. These fragrant, perfectly-textured fries are definitely worth indulging in, unless you're on a diet, in which case, why are you at a burger joint in the first place? Seriously, order the truffle fries!

Burger Up also boasts an interesting beer selection, featuring lesser-known breweries from the Deep South. I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi and found it to be quite enjoyable. This makes Burger Up a suitable spot to grab a drink after a meal.

If I were a Vanderbilt student, I would likely visit Burger Up fairly regularly. For those seeking a change from the typical dive bar hamburger, Burger Up offers a decent alternative.

input: Mandala has everything you need for massage at great prices! Lisa is extremely helpful, knowledgeable, and friendly. input: If you want beignets in Metarie, for my money Morning call is better than this shop.  If you're dead set on Cafe Du Monde, you're only twenty minutes including parking to Decatur.

input: Beautiful new nail Salon on West Chester Pike .. staff Is friendly.. the salon is brand new .. prices are good .. very serene colors ..  pedi chairs have phone chargers .. definitely recommend it!

input: Not just for feet. All I can say is....Wow! Worth the extra $$ for an hour full body massage. Simon has the most talented hands to coax your muscles to relax, taking the kinks out with skill. The atmosphere is incredibly desirable and comfortable, making your experience even more enjoyable. While they do offer walk-in services, I highly suggest scheduling an appointment, especially during the early evening, to secure your massage session. We initially went for a foot massage, and it was absolutely fantastic! Additionally, their prices are very reasonable and the quality of the massage is worth every indulgent penny. I cannot emphasize enough how much I recommend this heavenly place.

input: Stopped in to check out this new spot around the corner from us, as my boyfriend has been anticipating its opening for quite some time. Can I say it- FINALLY! We were there for what they were calling their soft opening, where apparently they are testing out menu and cocktail items for their "official" opening sometime soon. This is a must stop if you're a sushi/Asian fusion fan. We look forward to seeing what's in store for Tuna Bar and are thrilled to have this a two minute walk away!

We visited during their soft opening phase, where they are fine-tuning their menu and cocktail selections before their official grand opening. We can't wait to see what the future holds for Tuna Bar, and we're thrilled to have such a fantastic dining option just a short two-minute walk away.

input: I'm all for a dive bar but this place takes it to another level. The walls are old wood panel, the whole place smells disgusting, the drinks are tiny...I don't feel any need to ever go there again.

With these underwhelming experiences in mind, I have no desire or inclination to ever revisit this establishment.

input: Really like this place. The food is amazing, great atmosphere and the hostess has such a positive energy. It was my friend's first time and he definitely enjoyed it and wants to come back. The shrimp salad with the lime chili dressing was refreshing.
Refine this for me please: I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at this place. The food is absolutely incredible, and the atmosphere is fantastic. input:

The one positive aspect is that the service was still good, as it has been in the past. However, based on my recent experience, I don't think I will be returning to this place.

input: Excellenet Professional Service ! Loved my experience here today...unfortunately didn't get name of stylist who did my haircut but she was incredibly good !! U earned my confidence

The Greek salad, prepared right at our table, was outstanding. I opted for the Dolmades, while my coworker had the combo plate featuring moussaka, dolmas, and lamb, which he couldn't stop raving about. input: Good on the 'getting away from straws' for environmental reasons! Not so good on ingredients in ur mixers! Not so impressed with bar girlZzzz energy Saturday eve... Her Margarita getZ 2 thUmbs DOWN...  ItZ kind of an easy drink...

input:
I went to my first BarreAmped class at the Music Row location (I've also been to bounce class - on a trampoline - at the Nations location), and it was a great class: definitely a better workout and a better experience than some of the barre classes I've taken in town since moving to Nashville in July. Had a very family vibe - everyone knew each other in my class except for me (a Class Pass-er trying it out for the first time). Great instructor - very hands on. 

The room is TINY, but luckily there were only six or seven of us in the class (it was a random class in the middle of the day on a weekday). The room is oddly shaped and very small, so if the class was full, I'm sure I would have been hitting everyone else with my arms and legs every 30 seconds. Another frustrating thing? BarreAmped is located within a house on 16th that is also a gym. The building does not say BarreAmped on it! No sign at all! It was my first time coming to this location, and I drove right past it and had to circle around to find it. Then, when I walked inside, no one was at the welcome desk, so I wasn't even sure I was in the right building! Finally someone came in (looked like something using the gym rather than working there), and she told me the BarreAmped room was the up the stairs. A bit confusing. I wish that information had been on Class Pass and that they had a sign on the building.

Still it was a great class, and I think I'd go again!
Refine this for me please:
I recently attended my first BarreAmped class at the Music Row location, following a previous experience at the Nations location for a bounce class on a trampoline. Overall, I found the BarreAmped class to be a superior workout and a more enjoyable experience compared to other barre classes I have taken since relocating to Nashville in July. The class had a welcoming and familial atmosphere, with everyone acquainted except for me, as I was trying it out as a Class Pass-er for the first time. The instructor was excellent and provided hands-on guidance.

However, I must mention that the class space was extremely cramped. Fortunately, there were only a few of us in attendance during this particular session, which took place on a weekday in the middle of the day. If the class had been full, the confined space would have made it difficult to avoid accidentally hitting other participants with my limbs. Additionally, I found it frustrating that the BarreAmped studio is located within a house on 16th Street that also functions as a gym. The building itself lacks any signage indicating the presence of BarreAmped. This lack of clear signage caused me to drive past the location initially, leading to a frustrating experience of circling around to locate it. Upon entering the building, there was no receptionist present, which further added to my confusion about whether I was in the correct place. Eventually, someone who appeared to be using the gym, rather than working there, informed me that the BarreAmped room was upstairs. It would have been helpful if this information had been provided on Class Pass and if there was a visible sign on the building.

Despite these minor inconveniences, I thoroughly enjoyed the class and would consider attending again in the future.

input: When I called she put me on hold 3 times. Was very rude. Then when delivery came received wrong order. She wouldn't fix this, and hung up on me 3 times. Very rude and horrible service. Don't go there

input:

input: Kudos to this place for providing a much needed late night snack while I was visiting Nashville! Didn't have to wait on delivery because they allowed pick-up at 2 AM!
