input: Terrible delivery service & food order was incorrect once received an hour over what I was told.  All the food was under or over cooked.  Never again!  Sad
Refine this for me please: Extremely disappointing experience with the delivery service. Not only was my food order late by an hour from the promised time, but it was also incorrect. To make matters worse, all the food I received was either undercooked or overcooked. I have no desire to repeat this experience ever again. Feeling quite disheartened.

input: Great spot to come to if your in Nashville. The have one the best drink deals you can find on thursdays and Saturday's and Sunday's. Food is okay.
Refine this for me please: If you're in Nashville, this is a great spot to visit. They offer some of the best drink deals on Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays. While the food may be decent, the main draw here is definitely the drinks.

input: I like their salads, tea, and french fries! The servers were great...I've been here a few times and I'd come back!
Refine this for me please: I absolutely love their salads, tea, and french fries! The servers provided exceptional service during all of my visits, and I have been here multiple times. Without a doubt, I would definitely return in the future!

input: This was a great place to have brunch with the family. It is very clean and the staff were great. I love the decor!! Plus, my four year old actually ate here!!! That is a HUGE deal. He doesn't like anything.
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely fantastic for a family brunch! It was impeccably clean, and the staff were incredibly welcoming and helpful. The charming decor added to the overall experience. What's even more remarkable is that even my four-year-old, who is extremely picky, actually enjoyed the meal here. That speaks volumes about the quality of food and dining experience provided.

input: Very cute place with a great selection of loose leaf teas and other tea paraphernalia. The drinks and sweets are delicious and creative. Great relaxing ambience. As a tea lover, I loved reading the books about tea that the owner had. The owner is very nice and is very knowledgeable and passionate about tea. I would love to come back again!
Refine this for me please: This place is absolutely adorable, boasting an extensive selection of loose leaf teas and a variety of tea-related items. The drinks and sweets offered are not only delicious, but also creatively presented. The overall atmosphere is incredibly relaxing, making it a perfect spot for unwinding. As a fellow tea lover, I thoroughly enjoyed perusing through the owner's collection of books all about tea. The owner himself/herself is incredibly friendly, and their expertise and enthusiasm for tea are truly remarkable. I cannot wait to return to this charming establishment!

input: Great food and service. The antipasto was by far the best that I have ever had.  The pasta is all fresh and full of flavor. The Fisherman's stew was loaded with great tender fish in a saffron sauce.
Refine this for me please: The dining experience was exceptional, with excellent food and top-notch service. The antipasto surpassed all expectations, being the best I have ever tasted. The pasta dishes were truly remarkable, boasting freshness and immense flavor. The Fisherman's stew stood out, with an abundance of tender and flavorful fish perfectly complemented by a delightful saffron sauce.

input: Muriel's is a great stop in NOLA. The goat cheese and shrimp crepes are by far the best food I ate in the city (perhaps anywhere ever) and the rest of the meal lived up to the appetizer. Service is great, venue is quintessential French Quarter. It's a little distracting to see ghost tours outside the window at dinner- but the food is so delicious, you won't mind the audience. Rumor has it that Muriel's is haunted, but the only thing other worldly I encountered was the cuisine.
Refine this for me please: Muriel's in NOLA is an exceptional stop worth visiting. Undoubtedly, the goat cheese and shrimp crepes at this establishment are the epitome of gastronomic excellence, surpassing any other culinary experience I have had in the city (and possibly anywhere else). Remarkably, the quality of the main course matches the excellence of the appetizers. The service provided is impeccable, and the venue itself truly embodies the charm of the French Quarter. Although the presence of ghost tours outside the window during dinner can be slightly distracting, the delectable food is sure to overshadow any minor inconveniences. While there are rumors of Muriel's being haunted, the only supernatural encounter I had was with their extraordinary cuisine.

input: Went to this Taco Bell last night.  It was 1 30 and it said 30 minutes to close.  All the lights were on.  We backed up and forward twice and no one would wait on us.  We gave up and pulled up young man was at window closing  register.  Taco Bell was happy to serve us.
Refine this for me please: Last night, I went to this Taco Bell location, which had a sign indicating that it would close in 30 minutes at 1:30 am. Despite all the lights being on, my friends and I drove back and forth past the drive-thru window twice, but no one acknowledged us or took our order. Feeling frustrated, we decided to give up and pulled up to the window one last time. Surprisingly, a young man was at the window closing the register but happily took our order and served us at Taco Bell.

input: Cute place to eat at. Ate breakfast here and was dissappointed after seeing such good reviews. Breakfast menu is very limited. The omlet was just OK.  Biscuit didnt have much flavor to it. We were able to be seated really quick (during the week) but i imagine it getting really crowded during the weekends.
Refine this for me please:
Disappointingly Limited Breakfast Menu at This Otherwise Cute Eatery

Upon visiting this charming restaurant for breakfast, I was let down after reading all the great reviews. The breakfast options were quite limited, leaving much to be desired. The omelet I ordered was mediocre at best, lacking that "wow" factor. Even the biscuit failed to deliver on flavor. On the bright side, we were promptly seated without delays during the weekdays, although I can assume it might get considerably crowded on the weekends.

input:
Probably the most expensive game in town. But totally worth it for me. I upgraded myself to the executive locker rooms because that gives me zero excuses for why I can't go to the gym before work or after if I am going out later that night. I always have my makeup, hair stuff, etc in my locker. Just getting back to the gym after a long absence due to health issues so I'm taking it slow. I've seen one or two machines that are not quite working right but the facility as a whole is pretty sharp & welcoming. You have tons of options of what to do classes wise, equipment wise...
My only 2 down sides are that I wish they were open a little later on weekends, but that's just me moving slowly on my time off. I wish there was a bit more ritation with the class schedule. There are classes I'd like to take but they always run mid day, never really early, after work or weekends. So no option to try them. I'm sure it's an instructor issue so not likely something that will change. Overall I'm super happy that I joined.
Refine this for me please:
I recently upgraded myself to the executive locker rooms at the gym, and despite being the most expensive option in town, it is definitely worth it for me. The executive locker rooms provide me with no excuses to skip my workouts before or after work, and they also serve as a convenient storage space for my makeup and hair products. 

After a long absence from the gym due to health issues, I am gradually easing myself back into my fitness routine. While I have noticed a couple of machines that are not functioning properly, the overall facility is well-maintained and welcoming. There is a wide range of classes and equipment options available to cater to different preferences and fitness goals. 

However, there are a couple of downsides that I have encountered. Firstly, I wish the gym had longer operating hours on weekends, but this is mainly a personal preference as I tend to take my time off leisurely. Additionally, I would appreciate more variety in the class schedule. There are certain classes that I am interested in trying, but they always seem to be scheduled during mid-day, making it impossible for me to attend due to work or other commitments. Although I understand that this issue may be related to specific instructors, I don't foresee it changing anytime soon. 

Despite these minor drawbacks, I am extremely satisfied with my decision to join this gym.

input:
A++ 
I have to say, this place is great and one of the biggest reasons why is their bar staff. There is a bartender named "Ally". She is always kind and attentive. Everyone can be crammed at the bar, and the employees running around like their hair is on fire, and Ally still treats you like you're her only customer. 
Cool vibe, great indoor and outdoor seating. Great addition to the Funk Zone.
Definitely go!!
PS: Say hi to Ally for me :-)
Refine this for me please:
A++ 
I must say, this establishment is absolutely fantastic, and one of the primary reasons for that is their exceptional bar staff. One bartender, in particular, named "Ally", goes above and beyond to provide outstanding service. It doesn't matter if the bar is packed or if the employees are rushing around, Ally always treats you as if you're the most important customer. The atmosphere is cool, and they offer excellent indoor and outdoor seating options. It's truly a valuable addition to the Funk Zone. I highly recommend visiting this place, and don't forget to give my regards to Ally.

input: Not to bad. I sat at the bar and the bartender was awesome. The lunch menu here is very decent and the beer is ice cold.  I usually come during lunch when it isn't to congested. So, to get consistent service,  go when it isn't to congested. I will definitely go back?
Refine this for me please: It was a great experience. I had a pleasant time sitting at the bar with an awesome bartender. The lunch menu offered decent options and the beer was perfectly chilled. I prefer visiting during less busy times to ensure consistent service. Overall, I highly recommend this place and will definitely be returning in the future.

input: The only knock on this place is that they didn't have all the pools open during Memorial Day weekend. Other than that the hotel provides a very friendly environment that's good for adults and families as well plenty of places to eat inside the resort and the atrium was amazing and really fun to explore. Little far from town but a good middle point between music row and the airport. Hotel staff was top notch and the place was clean while still having that old charm. I'd stay here again in a heart beat next time I visit Nashville.
Refine this for me please: The only downside to this place was that not all the pools were open during Memorial Day weekend. Besides that, this hotel offers a very hospitable environment suitable for both adults and families. There are plenty of dining options within the resort, and the atrium is an incredible and enjoyable place to explore. While it may be a bit far from town, it serves as a convenient halfway point between music row and the airport. The hotel staff is exceptionally professional, and the establishment is clean while still retaining its old-world charm. Without hesitation, I would choose to stay here again on my next visit to Nashville.

input:
Great treat to beat the heat! I stopped in during the Manayunk Arts Festival yesterday to get a cold refreshing treat and I was very pleased with the service and the quality of the fresh frozen yogurt and toppings.

It is a self service fro-yo establishment with countless options of flavors and toppings. I enjoyed the toasted coconut yogurt and topped it with rainbow sprinkles, fresh strawberries, blueberries and raspberries. The fruit was very refreshing but it was hard to select what to put on it because everything looked so yummy. If you are a chocolate lover there are plenty of candy toppings to add to your fro-yo too. 

If you are not sure what flavor you will enjoy best you can sample them with small paper cups that so you don't have to find out if you like the flavor or not after you already purchase! 

Another plus is that the establishment is kept very clean and it still looks as new as it did when it first opening on Main Street just a couple of years ago!
Refine this for me please:
I had a fantastic experience at the Manayunk Arts Festival yesterday, where I discovered a delightful solution to beat the summer heat. The service and quality at this self-service frozen yogurt establishment exceeded my expectations. With an abundance of flavors and toppings to choose from, I savored the delectable toasted coconut yogurt topped with a medley of rainbow sprinkles, luscious strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries. The refreshing fruit toppings made it quite a task to decide among the mouth-watering options. For the chocolate aficionados out there, an assortment of candy toppings is available to elevate your fro-yo experience.

Notably, the establishment takes pride in maintaining a clean and immaculate environment. Despite being on Main Street for just a few years, it still maintains a fresh and inviting appearance. Additionally, the establishment offers a feature that allows customers to sample different flavors with small paper cups, guaranteeing satisfaction before purchasing.

input: I think the trendiness of this chain, in general, has sort of faded and what you have left is the basis of this chain, which is over-priced food of a questionable quality. I wouldn't call it bad, but it's a whole lot of fried food and most of the breadings, whether it's fried pickles or okra or calamari or shrimp, are the same across all of that. The batter is fine, but it gets wearing. The coconut shrimp and hush puppies were definitely overcooked, which was kind of disappointing. Coke Zero on tap, but the mix could be better. For the price, it is also worth nothing there is a ton of food here, definitely quantity over quality. Décor is pretty cool and this is parked right along the Boise river, though it's a bit tucked away and has to be more or less sought out...probably worth hitting at least once, but there are far better local places that are more worthy of attention.
Refine this for me please:
I believe the popularity of this chain has significantly diminished, leaving behind the core concept of overpriced food with questionable quality. While I wouldn't describe it as terrible, the menu consists mainly of fried dishes with similar breading, such as fried pickles, okra, calamari, and shrimp. Although the batter is satisfactory, it becomes unappealing after a while. Moreover, the coconut shrimp and hush puppies were disappointingly overcooked. Despite having Coke Zero on tap, the beverage mix could use improvement.

Additionally, it is worth mentioning that the price reflects the abundance of food rather than its quality. On a positive note, the restaurant's decor is appealing, and its location along the Boise River adds to its charm. However, it is slightly hidden and requires some effort to find. While it may be worth visiting once, there are definitely superior local establishments that deserve more attention.

input:
There are bars you can still smoke in?! Yuck. Sorry smokers (I used to be one so I get it) but yuck. The stink of smoke in my hair woke me up in the middle of the night after stopping in here and was so bad I had to get up to wash it before I could get back to sleep. That's not good.

Definitely a dive, this bar is very dim and smokey. The bartender was friendly and came to take my order as soon as I walked up to the bar. The bloody mary I ordered wasn't that great or strong, though.  That's not good either.
Refine this for me please:
Are there still bars where you can smoke? Gross. Sorry to all the smokers (I used to be one, so I understand), but gross. The smell of smoke in my hair woke me up in the middle of the night after visiting this place, and it was so terrible that I had to wash it before I could go back to sleep. That's not ideal.

This bar is definitely a dive. It's poorly lit and filled with smoke. On a positive note, the bartender was friendly and took my order right away when I approached the bar. However, the bloody mary I ordered wasn't impressive or strong. That's also disappointing.

input: Got there mid-morning today, the early rush was over. Two tables were full, each with three people. The family in one of the tables had just walked in ahead of me, so they were being attended to first. Still, I was immediately welcomed, and in a couple of minutes a friendly lady brought the breakfast menu and asked if I wanted coffee. A cup appeared a few moments later, and was kept full throughout my visit. Radio playing golden oldies from the 70s, my kind of music. The ham omelet with home fries and toast arrive a few minutes later, worth waiting for. Done just right and kept me filled for hours. A friendly family restaurant where you feel welcome and appreciated, just north of Gulfport.
Refine this for me please: I arrived at the restaurant mid-morning today, after the early rush had subsided. Two tables were occupied, each accommodating three people. Although a family had entered before me and were being attended to first, the staff promptly greeted me and provided a breakfast menu. Within a few minutes, a friendly lady served me a cup of coffee, which was consistently replenished throughout my visit. The pleasant ambiance was enhanced by the radio playing nostalgic hits from the 70s, catering to my personal musical taste. After a brief wait, my ham omelet with home fries and toast was presented, satisfyingly prepared and kept me satiated for hours. This amiable family restaurant, located just north of Gulfport, made me feel valued and welcomed.

input: This place is so lovely. It has everything!! Amazing wine selection, hookah's, Lebanese food which I think is the best in the city.
Refine this for me please: This place is incredibly charming and offers a wide range of amenities that cater to various preferences. From an extensive selection of exquisite wines to the option of enjoying a relaxing hookah session, it truly encompasses a diverse set of offerings. Moreover, the Lebanese cuisine served here is renowned and widely regarded as the best in the city.

input: This was recommended by a colleague who is local in the area. A group of us from work decided to go and give it a try.  As soon as we sat down, Chris, took care of us.  He was patient, understanding and extremely knowledgeable of the menu.  Well, our entire party enjoyed every part of the evening while at Red Mess!  From the chips & salsa to the drinks to each of our entrees ... just absolutely DELICIOUS!
Refine this for me please: I received a recommendation from a colleague who is familiar with the area, so a group of us from work decided to give it a try. From the moment we sat down, Chris, our server, took excellent care of us. He was patient, understanding, and had thorough knowledge of the menu. Our entire party had a fantastic experience at Red Mess! Everything, from the chips and salsa to the drinks and our entrees, was absolutely delicious.

input: This is my 3rd time and 3rd location at a Brick House across the country. This is by far one of the few chain restaurants I will regularly and happily eat at. The food is very unique and every selection is a good choice. This particular location I received better than average service. Will come back when back in town.
Refine this for me please: This is my third visit to a Brick House location, and it is located across the country. Without a doubt, this is one of the few chain restaurants where I genuinely enjoy dining on a regular basis. The food at Brick House is remarkably distinct, and every dish on their menu is a satisfying choice. What sets this particular location apart is the exceptional service I received, surpassing the usual standard. I definitely plan on revisiting this restaurant whenever I am back in town.

input: So... This place is the sh*t. By far the classiest spot on the block, Siam is nudging STL standards up and up. The sashimi:  top grade. The outdoor patio: perfect to enjoy a beer/conversation off the dance floor. The music: something for everyone -- and the last couple nights I've been, the guest dj's we're KILLING some deep house grooves that rival NYC and Miami.  The best thing, though, may be the crowd: a solid mix that don't need labels, don't want pretense, just want a solid, quality night out.  F*ck yeah, Siam!
Refine this for me please: Siam is absolutely incredible. It is without a doubt the most sophisticated place in the area, constantly raising the standards for St. Louis. The quality of the sashimi is unparalleled, while the outdoor patio creates the perfect atmosphere for enjoying a drink and engaging in conversations away from the dance floor. The music selection is diverse, catering to every taste. Lately, the guest DJs have been absolutely killing it with their deep house grooves, giving even renowned cities like NYC and Miami a run for their money. However, the true highlight of Siam has to be the crowd. It's a diverse mix of people who couldn't care less about labels or pretense; all they want is a fantastic night out. Siam, you truly rock!

input:
Worn down signs intrigue me.  I had biked passed 16th Street Seafood a ton of times, always wondering what was going on inside.  Now I know the answer, and the answer is- not much. At least in terms of decor. There is a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, plus a counter to order at and that's pretty much it. Also absent was the plethora of seafood over ice you would hope to see at a place specializing in seafood. There were some frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs- but not else. Still, I threw caution to the winds of Tasker Street and put in an order.

I didn't want to go for fried seafood, so the sandwiches and platters were out.

I got a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Mussels are one of those things I like making at home, but it is way too hot for that right now. . My main complaint is that the order came with an unacceptable amount of closed shells - 9!   It was still a good sized order with a big piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy, broth. As the place is to-go only- they know how to wrap up messy seafood orders, nothing was spilled.

Remember when I said I didn't want anything fried, well that's not ever actually true. So I ended up sneaking in 2 fried shrimps. Not bad, but not worth $1.25 each.
Refine this for me please:
I am intrigued by worn down signs, like the one at 16th Street Seafood. Having biked past it many times, I was always curious about what was happening inside. Finally, I satisfied my curiosity, only to find that there wasn't much going on in terms of decor. The interior consisted of a gumball machine, two empty candy machines, and a counter for ordering — that was pretty much it. Disappointingly, there wasn't the abundant display of seafood on ice that one would expect from a seafood-focused establishment. Instead, they had frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs; nothing more. Nevertheless, I decided to take a chance and place an order.

Given that I wasn't in the mood for fried seafood, I ruled out the sandwiches and platters. Instead, I opted for a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce, priced at $9.50. Mussels are something I enjoy cooking at home, but the weather was too hot to do so at the moment. My only complaint is that the order contained an unsatisfactory number of closed shells — a total of nine. However, the portion size was generous, and it came with a sizable piece of bread to dip into the unexpectedly spicy broth. As the establishment only offers take-out, they excelled at packaging messy seafood orders, ensuring that nothing was spilled.

Remember when I claimed not to want anything fried? Well, that wasn't entirely true. I couldn't resist sneaking in two fried shrimps. They weren't terrible, but certainly not worth $1.25 each.

input:
we had a groupon and so we went - great lobsters (although they were out of a few sizes this evening) but they were delicious and our waitress Jessica was very attending and nice - made some good suggestions.

not fancy but good lobster.
Refine this for me please: We used a Groupon and decided to try out this place. Despite being out of a few sizes of lobster that evening, the ones we did have were absolutely delicious. Our waitress, Jessica, was attentive and friendly, offering some great suggestions. Overall, the atmosphere may not be fancy, but if you're craving good lobster, this place is worth a visit.

input: Great little upscale but not overpriced cafe. Lots of options, but needs a lox bagel sandwich. :) One of my preferred places to lunch with someone.
Refine this for me please: Refined version: This charming upscale café offers a great selection of dishes at reasonable prices. While there are plenty of options to choose from, it could benefit from adding a lox bagel sandwich to its menu. Nonetheless, it remains one of my favorite spots to enjoy a casual lunch with someone.

input:
Animo juice is the best find in Haddonfield (after the Hadrosaurus, of course!)

I stop at Animo every time I go to Jersey to visit my family; or do I visit my family every time I stop at Animo?  Debatable.

Animo started with juice.  Not frozen juices with sorbet & yogurt added.  Real juice.  

Their menu has expanded & they now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!"  The burrito menu features 10 burritos, all under $10, f my favorite the "Haight & Ashbury" is stuffed with rice, beans, meat/roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole & sour cream.

Not that hungry, have a 'petito', a small version of the burrito, averaging $5.  Porky & Petunia - the name is as cute as the petito is yummy:  shredded lettuce, pulled pork & pineapple salsa.  

A breakfast petito & Animo MD juice destroy any hangover.  The MD is juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana & spirolina.   My BF loves the Chilly Palmer:  Acai, apple, banana, yogurt & flax seed.  

For a happy belly add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish.  The Border Salad is a perfect example: lettuce, guac, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vin, & sub quinoa for meat.   

Fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheat grass (cheaper than Jameson!) & yogurt/granola bowls!  

The city's juice bars have something to learn from Animo.
Refine this for me please:
Animo Juice is a beloved spot in Haddonfield, offering a refreshing and diverse menu of juices and burritos. With a range of options, including their famous Haight & Ashbury burrito packed with delicious ingredients, there is something for everyone at Animo.

As the name suggests, Animo began as a juice bar, focusing on real juice without any added sorbet or yogurt. However, they have since expanded their offerings and proudly operate as the "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar." Their burrito menu boasts ten affordable options, all priced under $10, making it an excellent choice for a satisfying lunch or dinner.

For lighter appetites, Animo also offers a "petito," a smaller version of their burrito, averaging around $5. One popular petito is the Porky & Petunia, with shredded lettuce, pulled pork, and a tasty pineapple salsa.

Animo doesn't just provide delicious food, but also offers a range of fresh and invigorating juices. Their MD juice, packed with juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana, and spirolina, is the ultimate hangover destroyer. Additionally, their Chilly Palmer juice, featuring Acai, apple, banana, yogurt, and flax seed, is a favorite among patrons.

For those seeking a wholesome and nutritious addition to their meal, Animo offers perfectly cooked quinoa that can be added to any dish or substituted for meat. The Border Salad, a delightful combination of lettuce, guacamole, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime dressing, can also be enhanced by the addition of quinoa.

Animo sets itself apart from other juice bars in the city. Their signature juices are fiber-rich and satisfying, while their offerings of frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheatgrass, and yogurt and granola bowls add a touch of variety to their menu.

In conclusion, Animo Juice is a must-visit spot in Haddonfield. Their range of juices and burritos, along with their dedication to using real ingredients, make them a standout destination. Other juice bars in the city could certainly learn a thing or two from Animo.

input: Had a very memorable birthday in SB and was so happy to have Wine Edventures be my gift! Sean picked us up Saturday morning and was super friendly (funny, too). It was just my husband and I along with a group of 10 - who happened to be all guys, having a bachelor party! Haha, so that was pretty funny. We stopped at 3 wineries and 1 brewery. Sean explained where we were as we were driving around and also gave us lessons at the tastings. He provided us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. We had lunch at the 2nd vineyard of the day, which was very good - choice of sandwich and a pasta salad side with chips and a cookie (the cookies are awesome). It was a fun day and I'd highly recommend this adventure to anyone looking for a fun day in the SB area.
Refine this for me please: I had an incredibly unforgettable birthday experience in SB thanks to Wine Edventures! Sean, our guide, was an absolute delight and made us feel extremely welcome and at ease. It was only my husband and I in the group, along with a lively bunch of 10 guys celebrating a bachelor party. The mix of people made it quite amusing! Throughout the day, we visited three wineries and one brewery, with Sean providing interesting information about each location as we traveled. He even gave us informative lessons during the tastings. Sean thoughtfully supplied us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses, which added a special touch to the experience. Our lunch at the second vineyard was excellent, consisting of a choice of scrumptious sandwiches, pasta salad, chips, and incredible cookies. Overall, it was an incredibly enjoyable day, and I highly recommend Wine Edventures to anyone seeking a fantastic time in the SB area.

input:
This is my favorite in Delaware.  The menu is simple and perfectly executed.  Rolls are reasonably priced, artfully made and are PACKED with fish!  I do believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste and smell are perfect.  Easily the best spicy tuna I have ever had.  I think the secret is the kewpie mayo along w/ the right amount of sriracha and sichimi powder.  Frankly, I can't get enough of this place and have at times, eaten it every day for lunch for weeks.  I've gone as far as to pick it up for dinner AFTER having had it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been great!

The Sushiman, YC Park is amazing to watch.  I've seen him skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in no time flat, in a single ribbon and then continue to shave it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll roll.  The temaki are as big as a carnival iced cream cone.  You can barely finish one of them, there is so much fish in there.  The nigiri are beautiful.  Uniform pieces of fresh fish, perfectly perched on the best sushi rice I've ever had (just the right amount of vinegar and sugar).

Skip the newly opened Kooma.  Save Mikimotos for a night out, but go to Tokyo for lunch!  The owners are lovely, so support them in this tough economy.  If you must eat sushi, eat it here!

Why not 5 stars?  I have to save it for places that serve the local fresh fish, plucked out of the water that morning.  Let me know if you find a place that does!
Refine this for me please:
This is my favorite sushi spot in Delaware. The menu is simple and impeccably executed. The rolls are reasonably priced, beautifully crafted, and generously filled with fish! While I suspect they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, the color, texture, taste, and aroma are all spot-on. Their spicy tuna roll is by far the best I have ever had. I believe the secret lies in their combination of kewpie mayo, sriracha, and sichimi powder. I am genuinely addicted to this place and have even eaten here daily for weeks on end. I've even gone as far as picking up dinner after having it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a fantastic addition.

Watching Sushi Chef YC Park, also known as The Sushiman, in action is truly astounding. I have witnessed him effortlessly skin a cucumber with his sushi knife, turning it into a single ribbon and then delicately shave it into a thin nori sheet for his tuna naruto roll. The temaki rolls here are enormous, reminiscent of carnival iced cream cones. The abundance of fish packed into each one is almost overwhelming. The nigiri pieces are nothing short of beautiful. Each slice of fresh fish is uniform and delicately placed on the best sushi rice I've ever tasted, with just the right balance of vinegar and sugar.

I wouldn't recommend trying the newly opened Kooma or saving Mikimotos for a special night out. Instead, opt for Tokyo for your lunchtime sushi fix. Not only are the owners delightful, but supporting them during these challenging times is truly worthwhile. If you must indulge in sushi, this is the place to be!

Why not a perfect 5-star rating? I reserve that accolade for establishments that serve locally caught, fresh fish straight from the morning's catch. Let me know if you come across a place like that!

input: So I'm super confused as to why everyone rags on this place. They're super nice, quick, and cheap.  People have complained about their chicken fingers being dry but I have no clue what they're talking about. They're great and their honey mustard is delicious. I've had salads from there too and they give you lots of veggies which I love. Their fries are delish as well and I love that they give you cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. All and all, I love that this place is literally a few steps away from my apartment and that they have decent food. I also don't understand the greasy spoon comments... you do realize it's a pizza joint right? You aren't going there for the ambiance, more for the cheap food.
Refine this for me please: I don't understand why everyone criticizes this place. The staff is friendly, service is quick, and the prices are affordable. Some people complain about the dry chicken fingers, but I disagree completely. In my opinion, the chicken fingers are delicious, especially when paired with their tasty honey mustard. I've also tried their salads which are packed with vegetables, and their fries are delightful. Another thing I appreciate is that they include cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. Overall, I love the convenience of this place being just a few steps away from my apartment and the fact that their food is decent. As for the comments about it being a greasy spoon, it's important to remember that it's primarily a pizza joint. We don't go there for the ambiance; it's more about the affordable food.

input: Great cheesesteak! Friendly and fast service. Lazo's really made my day.
Refine this for me please: Lazo's cheesesteaks are absolutely amazing! Their service is not only friendly but also incredibly fast, which made my day even better.

input: Ambience OK, too bad stuck in a mall in New Hope.  They were very understaffed (which thankfully they kept apologizing for) so there service was definitely slow, however very very pleasant.  We definitely felt it was worth the wait!  Vegetable Samosas were delicious, chicken were slightly dry.  I ordered chicken tikka masala which was so flavorful and rich and my husband had the chicken tagine...amazing!  Has the feeling of a place where "you get what you get and you don't get upset" but when you get it, it is really out of this world!  Loved the mix of cuisines, just enough choices on the menu.  Restaurant is BYOB so we were unprepared, but we will be back!
Refine this for me please: The ambience was alright, but it was unfortunate that we were stuck in a mall in New Hope. The staff was extremely understaffed, although they were apologetic about it, resulting in slow service. However, they were very friendly and pleasant. Despite the wait, we felt it was worth it. The Vegetable Samosas were delicious, but the chicken was a bit dry. I ordered the chicken tikka masala, which was incredibly flavorful and rich, while my husband had the chicken tagine, and it was amazing. The restaurant gave off a "take it or leave it" kind of vibe, but once you receive your food, it is truly exceptional. We appreciated the variety of cuisines on the menu, and there were just enough options to choose from. It is important to note that the restaurant is BYOB, which caught us off guard, but we will definitely be returning.

input: This is the cutest mom/pop local, high-quality ice cream joint in all of Tucson! Delicious... But definitely a bit pricey ($4.50 for a regular single scoop)- hence the 4 stars as opposed to 5.
Refine this for me please: This is the most adorable, family-owned local ice cream shop in Tucson, known for its top-notch quality! The ice cream is absolutely delicious, although slightly on the expensive side with a regular single scoop priced at $4.50. This is the only reason why it deserves 4 stars as opposed to a perfect rating of 5.

input: Cool ass brewery/bar. Very unique decor that suits the name of the place. We came on dat afternoon and it was packed but we got 3 seats easy. Beer selection was good especially for imperial stout lovers. No food there but you can bring your on or there are plenty of places across the street.

input: I definitely won't be coming back here. Long story short, I scheduled an appointment online to have the transmission and differential fluid changed on my pilot. When it was finally done and I was ready to check out, my advisor (Brandon) give me the total cost, which was double than what I expected and paid for in the past. input: We love, love M.L. Rose! I am a huge beer fan and the flights are so fun to choose and try. I love the neighborhood hangout feel, not too hipster, not too old....just right! We always have awesome service too. My hang up can be the food. Wings not quite crispy enough, burgers not cooked to taste, spinach artichoke dip just meh. The steak and Gouda was flat out gross - big fatty slab of undercooked steak on bread. We were told it is leaving the menu, but they should have removed it long ago. And no visit from the manager when the sandwich was returned, which was a little underwhelming. We will be back, we are big fans, but please get your kitchen together so I can have my fav burger in town cooked just right :-)
Refine this for me please: We absolutely adore M.L. Rose! Being a huge beer fan, I thoroughly enjoy selecting and sampling their flights. The cozy, neighborhood atmosphere strikes the perfect balance between being hipster and outdated. Moreover, their service is consistently exceptional. However, I must admit that I have some reservations concerning the food. The wings could use a bit more crispness, and the burgers often fail to meet my desired level of doneness. Additionally, the spinach artichoke dip falls short of my expectations. The most disappointing experience was with the steak and Gouda sandwich, as it was served as a thick, undercooked slab of fatty steak sandwiched between two slices of bread - flavorless and unappealing. We were informed that this item is being removed from the menu, but it should have been done so much earlier. On top of that, we received no acknowledgment from the manager when we returned the subpar sandwich, which was rather underwhelming. Despite these concerns, we remain loyal fans and will continue to patronize M.L. Rose. However, we sincerely urge the kitchen staff to improve the consistency and quality of their dishes, particularly their beloved burgers, so that we can enjoy them prepared to perfection.

input:
I normally wouldn't think Greek food for brunch or lunch; I'm way more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy.  But when my friends suggested to meet them here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their better judgement.  In the end, I'm glad I did.  This cozy Center City spot not only serves an amazing (and dare I say, a contender for the best) brunch in Philly, the staff really make you feel at home.  They really know how to wow their patrons: fresh food, delightful presentation, and so many delicious sounding choices it's hard to choose which dish you want from their one page menu for mains.

Their specialty, and they're not shy to tell you, is the Cyprus Breakfast.  It's a mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch.  The plate comes out with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsely.  It's served alongside a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and tomato, cucumber, and onion salad.  The menu also features a spread of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialities: Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa to name a few.  They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service may be a little over-attentive in an attempt to make you feel more than welcome, but it's much appreciated, especially when other restaurants fail to put as much effort into the service as they do the food.  One other tip: reservations are highly recommended, if not required.  Because of Kanella's small space, getting a table at brunch is nearly impossible if you're not on the list.  But if you can score seats here for brunch, then expect nothing less than a stellar way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities).  Can't wait to come back and try out the dinner menu.
Refine this for me please:
I typically prefer traditional American-style brunch, so I wouldn't usually consider Greek food for brunch or lunch. However, when my friends suggested meeting at this cozy Center City spot last weekend, I decided to trust their judgment. And I'm so glad I did. Not only does this place serve an amazing brunch (possibly the best in Philly), but the staff also creates a welcoming atmosphere that makes you feel right at home.

The menu is filled with so many delicious options that it's hard to choose just one dish from their concise one-page menu. They truly know how to impress their patrons with fresh food and delightful presentation. Their speciality, the Cyprus Breakfast, is a Mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch. It features two sunny-side-up eggs fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsley. Alongside the eggs, you'll find a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty and crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and a refreshing tomato, cucumber, and onion salad. But that's not all - the menu also offers a variety of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialties, including Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa. They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service at Kanella can be a bit overly attentive, but it's ultimately appreciated, especially when compared to other restaurants that prioritize food over service. One helpful tip is to make reservations in advance, as the limited space makes it nearly impossible to secure a table for brunch without one. However, if you manage to snag a spot here, you can expect a stellar way to kickstart your weekend morning or recover from the previous night's activities. I can't wait to return and try their dinner menu.

input:
I have always dreaded going to the hair salon.  I hated the phony atmosphere of most places and I really dreaded the small talk I would be forced to have with my stylist.  Maybe I am unusually insecure, but I always felt intimidated in most salons.  
Then, one day a couple of years ago, I wandered into Andre's salon and I never looked back.  
Andre is warm and personable and made me feel at ease immediately.  Right off the bat, we connected on a topic I care about--dogs--and I didn't feel uncomfortable at all.  Oh, and the cut and color were fantastic!  My highlights last longer than highlights I have received from any other salon.
For the past year or so, Christopher has been styling my hair and I LOVE him to death.  He is incredibly sweet, down-to-earth and talented!  My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it and, try as I might, I can never get it to look as good as he can.
The last time I was at the salon, Christopher, Leah and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion!  I can't remember a time when I enjoyed going to the hair salon (which is probably because I never have!).
Also, back in the spring, I asked Andre if he would be interested in donating a gift for a charity 5K I was helping to organize.  Being the wonderful person he is, Andre didn't hesitate and put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race!  Andre has a good heart and that it what I love about going to his salon!
I also love that clients can schedule appointments online through schedulicity!
Great prices, great cuts, great color, great space, convenient scheduling options and, most importantly, great people--you will not regret choosing Andre for your next cut or color!
Refine this for me please:
I used to dread going to the hair salon due to the phony atmosphere and forced small talk. Most salons made me feel insecure and intimidated. However, a couple of years ago, I discovered Andre's salon and it completely changed my outlook. Andre is warm, personable, and immediately put me at ease. We connected over a shared love of dogs, and for the first time, I felt comfortable during my salon visits. Not to mention, the cut and color were fantastic, and my highlights lasted longer than any other salon's. 
For the past year, Christopher has been styling my hair, and I adore him. He's sweet, down-to-earth, and incredibly talented. My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it, and I can never replicate the results myself. 
During my last salon visit, I had a great time reminiscing about '80s fashion with Christopher and Leah. It was a refreshing change, as I've never enjoyed going to the hair salon before. 
Another reason I love going to Andre's salon is because of his generosity. When I asked him for a gift donation for a charity 5K I was organizing, he didn't hesitate to put together a beautiful basket. It was a big hit at the race, and it showcased Andre's kind heart. 
I also appreciate the convenience of scheduling appointments online through schedulicity. The salon offers great prices, cuts, and colors. The space is inviting, and most importantly, the people are amazing. Choosing Andre for your next cut or color is a decision you won't regret.

input: Absolutely amazing and unique food. Love their bobba and pork pancake!
Refine this for me please: Their food is not only absolutely amazing but also unique. I particularly love their bobba and pork pancake, they are simply delightful.

input:
Nice, old school space with a long bar. It reminded me of some places I've been out west, which might be a little strange in the heart of Philadelphia. 

Not too loud at all - conversations were easy and a lot of the patrons were doing just that. There's a jukebox, so maybe it cranks up later in the evening. We were there pretty early. 

Great service from several people working behind the bar. 

Several beers on tap including a local CCCCC IPA, which was solid. Not many wines, though.

Small menu but very good food. The elote (corn) is quite good, as was the cucumber(?) salad. But the brat plate was the star. Wonderful brat, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel and a hot salsa/relish. Best brat plate ever. Served on a cool wood board.

Prohibition is located in or near a somewhat dicey neighborhood, at least to this non-resident's eye. I may very well be wrong about that. We had to walk a trashy, pissy street past what seemed like skid row coming from the hotel on Race St. If it was later at night we might have chosen not to walk back.
Refine this for me please:
Refined Version:

The atmosphere in this space is reminiscent of an old-school bar, with its charming interior and expansive bar area. It's a peculiar find in the heart of Philadelphia, evoking memories of similar western-themed establishments.

The noise level was pleasantly low, allowing for easy conversation among patrons. The presence of a jukebox suggests that the volume might increase later in the evening, but during our early visit, it was not an issue.

The bar staff provided excellent service, with multiple individuals attending to patrons' needs.

Though the drink options leaned heavily towards beers on tap, they had a decent selection, including a noteworthy local CCCCC IPA. However, the wine choices were limited.

The food menu may be small, but the quality is exceptional. The elote (corn) and cucumber salad are particularly delicious, but the real standout is the brat plate. Accompanied by German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel, and a spicy salsa/relish, the brat plate is hands down the best I've ever had. The presentation on a wooden board adds to the overall appeal.

Prohibition is situated in or near a neighborhood that may appear questionable to outsiders like myself. We had to traverse a somewhat unpleasant street, filled with trash and an unpleasant odor, akin to a skid row area, while walking from our hotel on Race St. If it had been later in the night, we might have opted for an alternative mode of transportation.

input:
On the Run is a convenience store chain and BP gas station. It is in a very convenient location for those who are returning rental cars at Lambert-St. Louis International Airport! How many times have you been on the way back into an airport, and not found a gas station nearby? Happens to me to any times - often you have to go out of your way to find one. Not so here!

Paid at the pump - I note that the pump had a hand scrawled note taped to the pumps - requesting you press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping your credit card. Never seen this before - this is the exact opposite procedure of other gas station pumps when using a credit card!

Refueled and was on my way to Hertz!
Refine this for me please:
On the Run is a convenience store chain and BP gas station located at Lambert-St. Louis International Airport, making it incredibly convenient for those returning rental cars. It can be frustrating to search for a gas station when heading back to the airport, often requiring you to go out of your way. However, with On the Run, this is not an issue!

One notable feature of this gas station is the hand scrawled note taped to the pumps, instructing customers to press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping their credit card. This is quite unique, as most other gas stations follow the opposite procedure when using a credit card.

After refueling at On the Run, I quickly made my way to Hertz!

input:
This is a pretty historical building that is well maintained. When we visited, we were the ONLY people there, which meant the Park Ranger gave us a private tour. Sweet!

Also - if you're into collecting National Park Stamps, you can get a few here! w00t!
Refine this for me please:
This captivating historical building is meticulously preserved and offers a unique experience. During our visit, we had the privilege of being the sole visitors, granting us an exclusive private tour led by the knowledgeable Park Ranger. It was truly a delightful surprise!

Moreover, for avid National Park Stamps collectors, this location presents a wonderful opportunity to obtain a few notable stamps. How exciting!

input: The service was great and the restaurant was clean, but the food was just okay. We had the linguine with marinara and the rotini primavera. The linguine was fine. The primavera, however, is not something anyone should order!!! The sauce had a great flavor, but the vegetables were actually from frozen. I mean, literally from FROZEN. Go to your local grocery store, look at the bag of Bird's Eye mixed vegetables and you will see what they use... right down to the ruffle cut carrots. There is so much wonderful fresh produce in Tucson, there is absolutely no reason to ever use gross frozen vegetables.
Refine this for me please: The service at the restaurant was excellent and the establishment was well-maintained. However, the food left much to be desired. We opted for the linguine with marinara sauce and the rotini primavera. While the linguine was satisfactory, the primavera dish was highly disappointing. The sauce had a delightful taste, but unfortunately, the vegetables were clearly taken straight from the freezer. To illustrate, they were identical to the Bird's Eye mixed vegetables found in local grocery stores, including the ruffle cut carrots. Considering the abundance of fresh produce available in Tucson, there is truly no excuse for resorting to subpar frozen vegetables.

input:
We  heard that Fresh Market was open and since we just got back from vaca we thought we would try it.  First of all, accolades to the staff they could not have been more helpful.  Especially Thomas in the meat section.  For these two things I would give them a five.  However, it does downhill from this point on:  ordered one pound of swiss cheese, after standing there waiting for about 5 minutes, and no one else was on line, the unfriendly clerk waited on us. The imported swiss cheese that we ordered was so poorly cut that in two days we had one clump of swiss cheese, rather than many slices.  I bought ricotta cheese for Easter and went to open it, and it was bad, although it was dated 3/28.  The tomatoes on the vine that I bought on Friday were bad by Sunday.  I have found their prices very high, selection, poor and at this point it is just not worth it. I also bought two pound cakes and their were not up to par.  Very dry and tasteless.. Overall a very disappointing shopping trip 
There is plenty of convenient parking and the store was immaculate, but it is not for me.  The final straw was that I asked for extra cash for Easter gifts, the clerk at the register said there was a $150 limit, the ATM terminal said $100 and the "manager" said $50...I thought they should get their act together.  Best to stay with Weaver's Way... or Whole Foods or Wegmann's.
Refine this for me please:
After hearing that Fresh Market had opened, we decided to give it a try upon returning from vacation. Firstly, we must commend the staff for their exceptional helpfulness, particularly Thomas in the meat section. Based on this aspect alone, we would rate them a five out of five. However, our experience took a downward turn from there.

When we ordered one pound of swiss cheese, we had to wait for approximately five minutes without any other customers in line. The clerk who eventually attended to us was quite unfriendly. To our disappointment, the imported swiss cheese we received was poorly cut, resulting in a clump rather than several slices within just two days. Similarly, the ricotta cheese we purchased for Easter turned out to be bad, despite its expiry date being March 28th. Moreover, the tomatoes on the vine that we bought on Friday had already gone bad by Sunday. 

In addition to these quality issues, we found the prices at Fresh Market to be exorbitant and their selection to be lacking. Consequently, we have come to the conclusion that it is not worth shopping there. Even the two pound cakes we bought were dry and flavorless, adding to our disappointment. Overall, our shopping trip was highly unsatisfactory.

On the positive side, Fresh Market does offer ample and convenient parking, and the store itself is immaculate. However, given our overall experience, it is clear that Fresh Market is not the right fit for us. The final straw occurred when we requested extra cash for Easter gifts. The clerk at the register informed us that there was a $150 limit, while the ATM terminal stated a limit of $100. To our surprise, the so-called "manager" contradicted both and stated a limit of $50. This inconsistency further reinforced our belief that Fresh Market needs to improve their organizational cohesion. In light of this, we believe it is best to stick with Weaver's Way, Whole Foods, or Wegmann's.

Overall, our shopping experience at Fresh Market left us thoroughly disappointed.

input:
I've only been once, but I'm ready to return.

Since moving to Fletcher Place, I've been looking for a bar near by that's similar to my neighborhood favorite, J Clydes. I think I've found it.

The Dugout is a simple hole-in-the-wall place. They have a decent selection, Sun King for $4.50, happy hour appetizers, and my favorite part: HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! No longer must I wait until my coveted Mug N' Bun trips for these fried morsels of tasty peppery goodness. Had a nice little piece form this joint, too. 

Really excited to return.
Refine this for me please:
After my first visit, I'm eager to go back to Fletcher Place. I've been searching for a bar nearby that captures the same vibe as my favorite spot, J Clydes, and I think I've finally found it.

The Dugout is a charming dive that offers everything I'm looking for. They have a satisfying selection of drinks, including Sun King for just $4.50. During happy hour, they also serve appetizers that hit the spot. However, my absolute favorite aspect of this place is their HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! I no longer have to wait for my treasured trips to Mug N' Bun to enjoy these delicious fried treats. I even had a pleasant conversation with someone I met at The Dugout.

I can't wait to go back and experience it all over again.

input:
I heard this ice cream parlour opened last summer, so upon my first trip home (sometime during the fall) I hustled over to try it. Since Friendly's closed a few years ago, Warminster has sorely needed a new ice cream place (DQ was our last one standing for quite some time). 

Much to my dismay, the Big Scoop had already closed for the season. I marked it in my calendar go return in March, when it reopened. Upon my next trip home in the spring, I was disappointed to see that I was just a few days early for their reopening, and would have to wait until my return in April.

After much anticipation, I made it to Big Scoop last weekend with my sister (who has been before). I was shocked to see what a range of products they serve - hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, pizza, you name it! I was tempted at the prospect of waffles and ice cream, but I wasn't that hungry so I settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous scoop of ice cream was tasty and packed with globs of cookie dough! I also tasted the birthday cake, which I enjoyed very much. 

The service was quick, and the shop crowded quickly. The interior was nicely remodeled and looks clean and family friendly. The man who helped me was extremely courteous and seemed to be doing most of the work. 

Especially given the lack of competition around here, the Big Scoop gets an easy four stars!
Refine this for me please:
Refined version:

When I first heard about the opening of this ice cream parlour last summer, I was eager to try it on my first trip home during the fall. With the closing of Friendly's a few years ago, Warminster was in desperate need of a new ice cream place, and for quite some time, Dairy Queen was the only option left.

To my disappointment, the Big Scoop had already closed for the season when I visited. Determined to try it out, I made a note in my calendar to return in March for their reopening. However, on my next trip home in the spring, I learned that I was a few days early for their reopening and would have to wait until April.

Finally, after much anticipation, I managed to visit Big Scoop last weekend with my sister, who had been there before. I was pleasantly surprised by the wide range of products they offered, including hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, and pizza. Although tempted by their waffles and ice cream, I wasn't too hungry and settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie ice cream with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous serving of ice cream was delicious, packed with flavorful globs of cookie dough. I also had a taste of their birthday cake flavor, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

The service was quick, and the shop quickly filled up with customers. The interior had been nicely remodeled, giving off a clean and family-friendly atmosphere. The man who assisted me was extremely courteous and seemed to be handling most of the workload.

Considering the lack of competition in the area, I would easily give the Big Scoop a four-star rating!

input: Aparently this review is for Saguaro East. I didnt realize there were two separate parks. This park is fine. We planned to do some hiking, but it just looked like flat average desert you can easily see and hike in the Phoenix area. The visitor center and staff were nice.
Refine this for me please: Apparently, this review is specific to Saguaro East, as I was unaware that there are two separate parks. Overall, I found this park to be satisfactory. Although our intention was to go hiking, the landscape appeared to be unremarkable and resembled the average flat desert that is readily accessible for hiking in the vicinity of Phoenix. On a positive note, the visitor center and its staff were pleasant and accommodating.

input:
Staff is amazing!  Coupons on their website are for 40 percent off a regular priced item... so that means... you are always getting something on sale!

We went in one evening at around 15 minutes before closing to grab some things very quickly... and all staff members were very helpful even so close to closing!  

Great store!
Refine this for me please:
The staff at this store is truly amazing! They offer fantastic coupons on their website that give you 40 percent off regular priced items. This means that every time you shop, you're guaranteed to find something on sale! 

Even when we went in one evening just 15 minutes before closing in a rush to grab a few things, the staff members were incredibly helpful and accommodating. It was a great experience overall. Highly recommend this store!

input:
This is another one of those anytime coffee shops. You can come get some work done, people watch, or just grab a drink to go. Either way, its open early and late.

For the quarter, its "off the beaten path" but in the busy area the locals hang out, and on the way to Fenchmen where everyone goes for good local music, Jazz, et al. 

They have food, not the cheapest, or local, but its better for you than the greasy, salty, fatty foods. Just make sure your service number is visible I got distracted hid my number, and had to stop the guy looking.  

Service varies. Since its a busy sidewalk, people stop in for that pick me up before work or party. One minute there is a like 12 long, and the barista is running ragged, the next its dead. 

Sometimes I'll sit for over an hour working or catching up on email. I'll order something every so often, and its no big deal for me to queue myself if they get busy. After all it helps those stopping in for a quick drink.

p.s. I love there tall cookies

oh and how many coffee shops can you get a shot in your coffee! That's right, its not a bar, but its New Orleans.
Refine this for me please:
This coffee shop is a versatile place that caters to different needs. Whether you want to work, people-watch, or grab a drink on the go, it's the perfect spot. It opens early and stays open late, making it convenient for everyone.

Although it may not be located in the center of attention, it's tucked away in a bustling area where locals hang out. It's also on the way to Fenchmen, known for its great local music and jazz. 

The food options are a bit pricier than the average, but they are healthier than greasy, salty, and fatty foods. Just make sure to keep your service number visible, as I made the mistake of hiding mine and had to search for the person delivering my order.

The quality of service varies here. Since it's located on a busy sidewalk, people often pop in for a quick pick-me-up before work or a party. Sometimes there's a long line of about 12 people, which keeps the barista running ragged, but then it can also be completely empty.

Personally, I often spend over an hour working or catching up on emails at this coffee shop. I order something occasionally, and I don't mind queuing up if they happen to be busy. It helps those who are in a rush to get their drinks quickly.

On a side note, I absolutely love their tall cookies. They are a must-try at this place. And by the way, how many coffee shops in New Orleans offer shots in your coffee? It may not be a bar, but it's a unique feature that adds to the New Orleans experience.

After I was shoved through I tried to explain to the bouncer what had happened so I could properly verify that I was actually on the list. Refine this for me please: I was included on the guest list for tonight's event because my high school friend was DJing. However, as I approached the front of the line, I was forcibly pushed through the entrance before I had a chance to present my ID and confirm my guest list status. Once inside, I immediately approached the bouncer to explain what had happened and ensure that I was properly authorized to be there. This unpleasant experience has left me with a strong aversion towards returning to this venue.

input: Salad portions are great. I always go with the Greek. One of the few Nick's spots that serves a rustic roast beef sandwich. Highly recommend that one. Pizza isn't that bad. I'd recommend an XL if having guests over. It's probably there better pizza, surprisingly.
Refine this for me please: The salad portions at Nick's are generous and satisfying. Personally, I always opt for the Greek salad. Additionally, Nick's offers a delicious rustic roast beef sandwich that is hard to find elsewhere. I highly recommend giving it a try. When it comes to pizza, it's actually quite decent. If you're having guests over, I suggest ordering an XL size as it is their best option and surprisingly tasty.

input:
Definitely dug this place...rather hipster-ish and way, way reminiscent of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake, but I liked it a lot despite all that...pizza here is definitely a lot better, as is beer selection. This may wind up being one of my more regular haunts as I slog my way through more of their menu (I think I may need to heavily modify next time I'm there), but so far, I have no cause at all for complaint and much to celebrate. It's interesting to me that the environments of the various locations are different, sometimes vastly, yet all have their own unique and innate charm. Whoever is running these is doing a phenomenal job, so props there.

One thing of note here...the ordering system is extremely clunky and seemingly disorganized and I sort of dislike it. Not enough to stop coming here, since I really dig the vibe of these, but on one of my less patient nights, that sort of thing may be enough to cut this out of the running. Definitely a good spot for pizza and a brew (or several), though. I back it.
Refine this for me please:
I thoroughly enjoyed this place. It has a cool, hipster vibe, reminding me a lot of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake. However, I still liked it a lot despite the similarities. The pizza here is definitely better, and they have a great selection of beers. I may become a regular here as I explore more of their menu, although I may need to make some modifications next time. So far, I have no complaints and plenty to celebrate. What's interesting to me is how each location has a different, unique charm. The person in charge of these places is doing an incredible job, so kudos to them.

One thing worth mentioning is that the ordering system here is really clunky and disorganized, which I kind of dislike. It's not enough to make me stop coming here, though, because I absolutely love the vibe. However, on nights when I'm feeling less patient, it might be a reason to consider going elsewhere. Nevertheless, it's definitely a great spot for pizza and beer. I highly recommend it.

input:
New St. Louis Wok is one of the few local Chinese places that deliver to our area.  Every time (but one), we've ordered, and gotten the food within an house.  In addition, they have a website where you can order the food (avoiding possible language barriers), and then they follow up with a call for your credit card number.

Food wise, it's the best Chinese delivery we've had here.  Nothing too greasy, and everything comes hot...with lots of sauces and fortune cookies.  For our rare Chinese cravings, it's the go-to place.
Refine this for me please:
New St. Louis Wok stands out among local Chinese restaurants for their convenient delivery service to our area. Without fail, except for one instance, our orders have been promptly delivered within an hour. They offer the added convenience of a user-friendly website for placing orders, minimizing potential language barriers, and follow up with a phone call to collect credit card information.

Furthermore, the quality of their food surpasses any other Chinese delivery options available in our vicinity. The dishes are never overly greasy and always arrive piping hot, complemented by a generous selection of delectable sauces and traditional fortune cookies. Whenever a craving for Chinese cuisine arises, New St. Louis Wok is consistently our top choice.

input: This is my go to sushi place. it's cheap and the rolls are AMAZING. if you want a new sushi place to try i highly recommend osaka
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend Osaka as my go-to sushi place. Their rolls are absolutely amazing, and the best part is, it's budget-friendly. If you're looking for a new sushi place to try, Osaka should be at the top of your list.

input:
Kelly's has changed hands and the menu has completely changed.  It's clear they've had to defend this and it seems to annoy them.  I mean the menu was epic - why change it?

In response, the new crew touted the place being cleaner and it was.

I got the  classic burger and fries.  I'll be honest, it was the worst $11 burger that I've ever had.  Dry and flavorless and made me envy a $2 McDonalds bacon burger flashing on the TV.  The fries were OK.

I was shocked to just walk in at dinner time.  This wasn't possible before.  Now I know why.

:
Refine this for me please:
Kelly's has recently undergone a change in ownership, resulting in a complete overhaul of the menu. It is evident that they have faced criticism for this decision, which appears to frustrate them. The previous menu was highly regarded, making it even more perplexing as to why they chose to make such drastic changes.

However, in response to the criticism, the new management emphasizes the improved cleanliness of the establishment, which is indeed noticeable.

Lured by the reputation, I decided to order the classic burger and fries. Unfortunately, I must admit that it was the most disappointing $11 burger I have ever had. The patty was dry and lacked any sort of flavor, making me wish I had opted for a $2 McDonald's bacon burger instead, as I saw it advertised on the television. On a positive note, the fries were decent.

To my surprise, I was able to walk into the restaurant during dinner time without any difficulty. This was an entirely different experience from before, and the reason behind this newfound ease became apparent later.

input: Great place to go everyday. I saw huge changes in my strength and flexibility there. All of the teachers are unique and teach beneficial classes. I highly recommend a monthly membership!
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend this place as a great destination for daily visits. It has made a significant impact on my strength and flexibility through considerable improvements. What sets this place apart are the individualistic and skilled teachers who conduct highly beneficial classes. Considering the immense benefits, I strongly suggest opting for a monthly membership.

input:
