I ordered a delivery for the first time today, and the driver's behavior towards me was insulting. Upon opening my door, she immediately questioned me about a car across the street with a man in the driver's seat. I honestly replied that I didn't know anything about it. In response, she insinuated that she didn't want to be a target for robbery. This unexpected behavior made me feel extremely uncomfortable, as I had already paid for my order beforehand with my visa. I handed her the tip I had prepared and politely thanked her, hoping that my politeness would change her negative perception of me. All I wanted was some pizza, and I didn't deserve to be judged or stereotyped based on my surroundings.

input:
First time here and I have to say it's pretty good! The bake shop fits well with the fishtown environment and it's very clean and welcoming inside. The display of beautiful cakes let's you know you have top quality bakers there. 

I got a few items to share such as a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. 

I had a taste of the Burbon Pecan Cookie. It was not too sweet and you get nice bites of pecan; a nice hot coffee is a perfect compliment.The cupcakes were good (cake wise) but, not a huge fan of the icings. The cake itself was sweet and moist. 

Didn't get to try the Chocolate chip cookie but the concensus was that it's delicious. 

I would definitely come back and I have taken a big interest in having Cake Life make a custom order!
Refine this for me please:
Upon my first visit here, I must say that I am thoroughly impressed. The bake shop seamlessly blends into the vibrant atmosphere of Fishtown and the interior is exceptionally clean and inviting. The stunning array of beautifully crafted cakes on display immediately conveys the expertise and skill of the bakers present.

During my visit, I indulged in several delectable treats, including a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. The Burbon Pecan cookie, in particular, struck a perfect balance of sweetness with delightful bursts of pecan. Pairing it with a steaming cup of coffee was an absolute treat. While the cupcakes themselves boasted a moist and pleasant taste, I personally found the icings to be less to my liking. However, it is worth mentioning that the consensus among others was that the Chocolate chip cookie was nothing short of delicious.

Overall, I am eager to return to this bake shop and have developed a keen interest in placing a custom order with Cake Life.

input:
Went here last Thursday and arrived early enough to take advantage of their $5 domestic pitchers during hh which includes mich golden light, my fave! It did take the server about 10-15 minutes to even notice we were there, but after that service was just fine. 

Started off with the wings which were delicious, although the bf was certain it was not actually a pound of wings which they claim on their menu.

I ordered the gyro and fries which were surprisingly really good! Gyro meat was tasty and the fries were awesome! Bf had the French onion soup and potato skins which he said were good as well.

We stayed for rock n roll bingo (which I guess is every Thursday, and free!) and we had a blast. They also have a pool table and darts in the back which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

We will definitely be back!
Refine this for me please:
Last Thursday, I visited this place and arrived early enough to take advantage of their happy hour, where they offer $5 domestic pitchers, including my favorite, Mich Golden Light. Despite initially being overlooked by the server for about 10-15 minutes, the service was satisfactory afterwards.

To start, we ordered their delicious wings, although my boyfriend believed that it was not actually a pound of wings, as it claimed on the menu. But regardless, the taste was great.

For my main course, I decided on the gyro and fries, which pleasantly surprised me with its fantastic flavors. The gyro meat was very tasty, and the fries were excellent. My boyfriend went for the French onion soup and potato skins, which he enjoyed too.

We stayed for their rock n roll bingo, a free event that apparently takes place every Thursday, and had a fantastic time. In addition, they also provided entertainment options such as a pool table and darts in the back, which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our experience and will definitely return in the future.

input: Johnny Tucci and his crew are the absolute best videographers, hands down. They are professional, prompt, and extremely talented. They made our wedding footage look like a movie production and brought everyone to tears that watched it. My advice is that if you are going to splurge in one area for your special day, spend it on a videographer. They do not disappoint.
Refine this for me please: Johnny Tucci and his crew surpass all expectations as videographers. Their professionalism, punctuality, and impeccable talent are unmatched. Transforming our wedding footage into a cinematic masterpiece, they evoked emotions that left everyone who watched it in tears. If you are looking to invest in one aspect of your special day, I highly recommend splurging on a videographer. The experience and results are truly unparalleled, leaving you utterly satisfied.

input:
One of the absolute best places to see a game in the entire country!

Get there early or if it's a blowout, stroll around the park. There are tons of interesting places to eat & drink (including a rooftop bar). Tickets are still amazingly reasonable even after all the success the Phils have had in recent years particularly when compared to the NY parks.

I used to go more often before the team became so prominent (right after the park opened), and I sat all over the joint. Not really anywhere I wouldn't recommend. The outfied is a great option. 

After starting with a 17 game pack many years ago & then buying season tix a few years back (which my company still has), the staff was great about recommending sections that would avoid direct sunlight , etc. (3rd base field level is awesome).

If you are visiting or considering a trip, don't buy the negative publicity about the Philly fans. The crowds are great. Sure, you have idiots and maniacs like you do at any park and for any professional sporting event, but they are by far the minority and Citizens Bank Park is policed pretty well for nonsense. 

I was once with a group of guys & we stood out in one of the open standing areas between 3rd base & the left field wall the whole night. At one point a very nice officer politely asked us not to curse because there were families around. We we were far from out of control, and we all thought that was pretty cool... so we had fun with some occasional lighthearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

Don't expect to be sheltered with your kids like you would be in your own living room, but there's no teens running onto the field getting tazed every night nor are there drunk idiots throwing up on people. 

It's a great atmosphere, a wonderful park & still a very fun team to watch.
Refine this for me please:
Citizens Bank Park is undoubtedly one of the absolute best venues across the entire country to catch a game! Whether you arrive early to soak in the atmosphere or take a leisurely stroll around the park during a blowout, there is plenty to explore. The park offers a multitude of enticing dining and drinking options, including a fantastic rooftop bar. Surprisingly, even with the recent success of the Philadelphia Phillies, ticket prices remain remarkably reasonable, especially in comparison to those at New York parks.

Having frequented the park more frequently in its earlier years, I can confidently say that there isn't a bad seat in the house. However, if I had to recommend a section, the outfield is particularly enjoyable. Personally, after starting with a 17-game package many years ago and eventually purchasing season tickets through my company, I received excellent guidance from the staff regarding sections that offer shade and other amenities. For instance, I highly recommend the third base field level for an awesome experience.

If you're visiting or contemplating a trip to Citizens Bank Park, don't let the negative publicity about Philly fans discourage you. The crowds are fantastic, and while there may be a few unruly individuals, they represent only a minority. Additionally, the park is well-managed and properly policed, ensuring a pleasant experience for all attendees.

During one memorable outing with a group of friends, we spent the entire night in one of the open standing areas between third base and the left field wall. At one point, a courteous officer kindly asked us to refrain from using profanity due to the presence of families. This interaction left a positive impression on us, as we engaged in light-hearted banter with the officer for the remainder of the evening.

While you shouldn't expect the same level of child-friendly environment as your own living room, rest assured that incidents like teenagers trespassing onto the field or intoxicated individuals causing disruptions are extremely rare occurrences. Overall, the park offers a fantastic atmosphere, combined with a wonderful facility and an entertaining team. It is sure to provide an enjoyable experience for all.

input: I love Cosi but this Cosi is going down hill fast. I always get a signature salad and lately they are made wrong and no dressing at all. How hard is it to make their own signature salad!? It's practically what they are known for!!! So angry.
Refine this for me please: I used to love Cosi, but recently I've noticed a decline in their quality. Specifically, when I order their signature salad, it's often made incorrectly and without any dressing. It's frustrating that they can't even get their own renowned dish right. I'm really disappointed and angry about it.

input: OMG!! what a disappointment today was, I have been so excited to see Rembrandt's reopen after a few months of remodel, what I was thinking is that the new owners would want to do more restorations of this Beautiful, Cozy, old Church, maybe try to find more space to add Tables, but NO, I walked into a Modern, Cold, Hospital Coffee Shop, the Charm is gone, so so disappointed and sad, we all love the Charm of Eagle, but it seems to be fading fast, Please People talk to all the other Eagle Shop Owners when your visiting them especially the old Original Buildings to keep Eagle's charm and quaintness and restore these Beautiful Buildings.
Refine this for me please: I can't believe how disappointed I am with today. I was eagerly looking forward to the reopening of Rembrandt's after a few months of renovations. I had expected the new owners to enhance the beauty of this lovely, cozy old church by adding more restorations and maybe even finding additional space for more tables. However, to my dismay, what I found was a modern, cold coffee shop that reminded me more of a hospital. The charm that we all love about Eagle seems to be rapidly disappearing. It's disheartening and saddening. I implore everyone to talk to the other shop owners in Eagle, especially those in the original buildings, and encourage them to preserve the town's charm and quaintness by restoring these beautiful structures.

input:
The service was lacking. The waiters and waitresses don't know the menu and when you ask for certain things to be brought to your table, it's constantly forgotten. The food is visually appealing but some of the most awkward and distasteful food I've ever had. The waffles are stale, the biscuits are hard as rock and their chorizo is not real chorizo.

The only thing this place has going for it is the atmosphere and their alcohol selection.
Refine this for me please:
Please, refine this for me: The service at this establishment was extremely disappointing. The waitstaff seemed to be unfamiliar with the menu, frequently forgetting requests to bring items to the table. Additionally, the quality of the food was highly underwhelming. Despite visually appealing presentations, the waffles were stale, biscuits were rock hard, and the chorizo did not live up to its name.

However, it is worth noting that the atmosphere of the place is pleasant and they do offer a commendable selection of alcoholic beverages.

input:
This restaurant is a nice place to go and sit down to have something to eat. I've ate just about everything they have on the menu and I'd say their burgers are great. Although their pizza is a bit on the tough side I still manage to eat the crust too. 

Very comfortable dining room area as well!
Refine this for me please: This restaurant offers a pleasant atmosphere for a sit-down meal. I have tried nearly every dish on the menu and I highly recommend their burgers, they are delicious. Although their pizza can be a bit tough, I still enjoy eating the crust. The dining room area is very comfortable and inviting.

input: We live in the neighborhood and have eaten here many times. I feel as if this restaurant is going downhill. This time we were there for dinner early on a Sunday. The bathrooms were filthy. There are 2 and one was not usable due to all of the paper towels that had been put into the toilet (there was no toilet paper). The other one was usable but also no toilet paper. Our server, Ashley, was not interested in providing any semblance of customer service...RUDE! We had a simple question about the beers on special and she became quite defensive. My daughter spilled her drink, which I realize is a pain in the ass for the restaurant and server (although we were outside so it wasn't that big a deal). We apologized profusely but she didn't even try to hide her annoyance. Finally, the chicken quesadilla should have been labeled the gristle quesadilla....more fat than actual meat...yuck. We love the proximity of this place to where we live and it was great in the past but not anymore...will likely not return...not with so many better quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown.
Refine this for me please: We are regular visitors of this restaurant in our neighborhood, but we have noticed a decline in its quality recently. On our recent visit on a Sunday evening, we were disappointed with the state of the bathrooms. One of the bathrooms was unusable due to paper towels being jammed in the toilet, and the other one also lacked toilet paper. Our server, Ashley, displayed a lack of interest in providing good customer service and was frankly rude. When we asked a simple question about the specials, she became defensive. Unfortunately, my daughter accidentally spilled her drink, and although we apologized, Ashley made no effort to hide her annoyance. Additionally, the chicken quesadilla we ordered was mainly gristle rather than meat, which was unappetizing. Despite the convenience of its proximity to our home, we feel that there are now better quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown, and we are unlikely to return to this particular establishment.

input: Pretty average bar/restaurant with the menu offerings you can expect from a place like this. The food was OK, and the service was excellent.
Refine this for me please: A fairly typical bar/restaurant with a menu that aligns with your expectations. The food quality was satisfactory, but the service provided was exceptional.

input: We came here based on the recommendation we received and from the street it doesn't look like much. But when you sit down and you scan the menu you will come to realize that this place serves nothing but home-cooked comfort food. We had the BLT and it was packed full of flavor, they didn't scrimp on the bacon and the vegetables for very fresh. With the sandwiches came some of the best french fries that we've had, and some of the best coleslaw that I've had in the state of Florida. We took a couple of pies home and they were delicious. We will definitely come back.
Refine this for me please: Based on a recommendation, we decided to give this place a try, though it didn't seem impressive from the outside. However, as soon as we sat down and scanned through the menu, we realized that this hidden gem specializes in delectable home-cooked comfort food. Our choice, the BLT, exceeded expectations with its flavorful combination of generous bacon and fresh vegetables. Accompanying the sandwiches were some of the most delectable French fries we've ever had and the coleslaw was unparalleled even within the state of Florida. Unable to resist, we also took home a couple of their scrumptious pies. Needless to say, we will certainly be returning for another satisfying meal.

input: I was greated by a nice friendly staff. There wasnt a long wait for my food. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipolte sauce. They cut it in half as requested and was served in maybe only 20 seconds after the time it took to cook. Food taste great
Refine this for me please: I was greeted by a friendly and welcoming staff who provided excellent service. I didn't have to wait too long for my food, which was a pleasant surprise. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipolte sauce, and they accommodated my request to have it cut in half. The food was promptly served, only taking about 20 seconds after it was cooked. Most importantly, the taste of the food was fantastic.

input: Excellent food! I am a Thai food junkie, and have travelled to Thailand and throughout Southeast Asia several times. There is ok Thai food in Nashville and then there is Great Thai food. This place was GREAT! The decor is a little dated but who cares...I was there for the food, which is fabulous!!!
Refine this for me please: The food here is absolutely excellent! As a self-proclaimed Thai food enthusiast who has visited Thailand and Southeast Asia multiple times, I can confidently say that the Thai cuisine offered here falls under the category of "Great Thai food." While the decor may appear somewhat outdated, its importance is overshadowed by the incredible taste of the dishes they serve. The food at this place is truly fabulous!

input: This place is absolutely fantastic. I honesty really don't even like sweets and am not all that into donuts but this place will make you a believer. The apple fritter is amazingly delicious and you can't go wrong with a chocolate long john. Don't even bother with any other donut shops in stl.
Refine this for me please: This place is truly exceptional. Although I am not particularly fond of sweets or donuts, this establishment has completely changed my preferences. The apple fritter is exceptionally delicious and the chocolate long john is simply outstanding. I highly recommend skipping any other donut shops in St. Louis and giving this place a try.

input: Of all the restaurants we tried in New Orleans, this was by far our favorite. I had both lunch and dinner on two separate occasions. The service was wonderful, the ambiance is cozy but alive. Make sure to call ahead and get a reservation over the phone if opentable looks booked. Their lunch special spicy fried chicken is a must have! If you are a party of two or three, ask for the corner booth by the window. Best table in the house.
Refine this for me please: This restaurant in New Orleans was unquestionably our favorite out of all the ones we tried. I had the opportunity to visit twice, once for lunch and once for dinner, and both experiences were exceptional. The service provided was outstanding and the atmosphere was cozy yet vibrant. It is advisable to call in advance and make a reservation over the phone if the availability on opentable appears to be full. Without a doubt, the lunch special of spicy fried chicken is an absolute must-try! And if you happen to be a party of two or three, I highly recommend requesting the corner booth by the window, as it is undoubtedly the best table in the entire establishment.

input:
City Parkの近くにある激安かき氷屋さん。シェーブドアイスっていったほうがいいね！
特に夏のニューオーリンズはジメジメして暑いから、公園に行った後にここでかき氷とか最高だと思う！

味の種類は半端なく多いです！50以上はあったはず！
そしてなんといっても安い！ぼくは一番安いチョイスのレギュラーかき氷のスモールを頼みましたが、スモールでも結構十分だと思います。そして値段はたったの$1.50. 安い！！

トッピングをしても５ドル以上はいかないはず。
夏のうだる暑さには、最高のチョイスだと思います！
Refine this for me please:
Refine: There's a super cheap shaved ice shop near City Park. I think calling it "shaved ice" is better! Especially in the hot and humid summer of New Orleans, I think it's the best to have shaved ice here after visiting the park!

There are countless flavors available! There should be over 50 options! 
And, most importantly, it's so affordable! I opted for the smallest size of regular shaved ice, called the Small, and it was surprisingly satisfying. And the price? Just $1.50. So cheap!!

Even with toppings, it shouldn't go over $5.
I believe it's the perfect choice for the scorching summer heat!

input: Mr. X has amazing flavor and overall a pretty friendly staff. The wait time for carry out is on average about 20 minutes, which is way better than a 45 minute wait at chain pizzerias. I get the hand-tossed crust comparable to traditional NY style pizza, and has excellent flavor and texture!
Refine this for me please: Mr. X is known for its outstanding flavor and exceptionally friendly staff. When it comes to carryout orders, the wait time is impressively short, averaging around 20 minutes, unlike the 45-minute wait commonly experienced at chain pizzerias. I personally love their hand-tossed crust, which is reminiscent of traditional NY style pizza. The flavor is unbeatable, and the texture is simply excellent.

input:
First time being here.  It was a nice place but empty.  Had one old man sitting in there, then us two 40 somethings, then another old man.  That was it.   We came during happy hour, basically waiting for Snake and Jakes to open up so we came here to kill some time.  

Beer selection was nice, Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, etc.  Prices were ok too.

Lotsa dark woods and a few TVs and a lonely but attractive bartender that was very nice.  

Nothing bad to say about this place other than it was kinda dead.  It was very clean looking and nicely decorated, just kinda boring.
Refine this for me please:
My first visit to this place was pleasant, despite its emptiness. All that occupied the establishment were an elderly man, my companion and I (both in our forties), and another elderly gentleman. We arrived during happy hour, simply passing time before Snake and Jakes opened, hence our decision to spend some time here.

The beer selection was commendable, offering options such as Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, and more. The prices were reasonable as well.

With its abundance of dark woods, a few televisions, and a solitary yet attractive bartender who was very friendly, the atmosphere was welcoming. The place appeared immaculately clean and thoughtfully decorated, but it lacked excitement.

Overall, there is nothing negative to say about this establishment, except for its lack of liveliness. It was undeniably a well-maintained and aesthetically pleasing place, albeit somewhat uneventful.

input:
i dont know what has happened to the in store service in this place!  We have been down here for a few weeks now and have been here 6 times.Only once was the order completed without a screw up!

Today 2 tall decaf coffees took close to 20 minutes.By then our bagels were cold.First i was told the decaf was "brewing' and then i was told there was something 'wrong" with the brewer? After 15 minutes i was offered a decaf americano.
Before we left i politely told a fellow behind the counter the service was abominable and he said 'well we can only store 2 vente size decafs at a time? HUH? I asked if the management knew about this and he just shrugged.
Clearly this staff has never been trained to make it right for the customer.No apology.No coupon.Just a convoluted story.
 
Amazing how you can have numerous people running around a store but you cant get the simplest order straight My next visit to a Starbucks will certainly not be this one.
Refine this for me please:
I am extremely disappointed with the decline in the in-store service at this particular place. Despite being here for a few weeks and visiting a total of six times, we have only had one order completed correctly.

Today, it took nearly 20 minutes to receive two tall decaf coffees, and by then, our bagels had become cold. Initially, I was informed that the decaf was "brewing," but later, I was told that there was something "wrong" with the brewer. After waiting for 15 minutes, the only alternative offered was a decaf americano.

Before leaving, I politely expressed my dissatisfaction to a staff member, who nonchalantly explained that they could only hold two vente size decafs at a time. This lack of storage capacity seemed baffling to me, and when I asked if the management was aware of this issue, the staff member merely shrugged.

It is evident that the staff working here have not been trained to prioritize customer satisfaction. There was no apology, no compensation, just a convoluted explanation. It is truly astonishing how a store can have multiple employees bustling around, yet fail to fulfill even the simplest order correctly. I can assure you that my next visit to a Starbucks will not be to this particular location.

input:
As a double date with a good long lost friend for a relaxing evening dinner, we were surprised in early august to not get reservations until 8. 
So we arrived an hour early and had drinks in the lobby while the piano man played beautifully. The bartender was a bit slow at first but kept us well tended. 
Our table in the corner against the glass was ready early and we enjoyed watching the rays chase fish around the bay as the sun set.  
I started with the tasty crab and corn chowder but was a bit disappointed with al dente potatoes in the bowl. 
Wife ordered the scallops which were superb as was my crab stuffed grouper. But my rice was also inadequately cooked. 
Creve brûlée was excellent as was Tim's attentive service. 
Worth going again, but they need to get all the parts of the dishes correct to get 5 stars.
Refine this for me please:
My long-lost friend and I decided to have a double date for a relaxing evening dinner, but we were surprised to find out that we couldn't get reservations until 8 in early August. Determined to make the most of our evening, we arrived an hour earlier and enjoyed drinks in the lobby. The piano man added to the ambiance with his beautiful music, although the bartender was a bit slow initially, he eventually took good care of us.

Fortunately, our table in the corner, with a view of the bay, was ready ahead of time. We delighted in watching the rays playfully chase fish as the sun set. For starters, I ordered the tasty crab and corn chowder, but was disappointed to find al dente potatoes in the bowl. On the other hand, my wife ordered the scallops which were absolutely superb, and my crab stuffed grouper was also delicious. The only letdown was the inadequately cooked rice that accompanied my dish.

To end the evening on a high note, we savored a delightful crème brûlée, which turned out to be excellent. Tim, our attentive server, added to our enjoyable dining experience. Overall, the restaurant is worth visiting again, but they should focus on improving the consistency of their dishes to earn a full 5-star rating.

input: My wife and I visited this hidden gem today and were not let down. The shop was clean, bright, colorful, and comfortable. We were able to sample all the flavors, listen to the story of how they came about, and walked off with many bags of deliciousness. The owners there were so kind. They took the time to understand exactly what kind of foods we enjoy to match us up with the perfect popcorn. Definitely coming back soon!
Refine this for me please:
My wife and I had the pleasure of visiting this hidden gem today and it exceeded all our expectations. The shop was impeccably clean, exuding a vibrant and inviting atmosphere. Its tasteful assortment of colors made it a visually pleasing experience. Moreover, we found the ambiance incredibly comfortable.

One of the highlights of our visit was being able to sample each flavor of popcorn available. Not only did this allow us to indulge in delightful treats, but it also provided us with an opportunity to learn the intriguing stories behind each creation. With our taste buds tantalized and our curiosity piqued, we left the shop with several bags of pure deliciousness.

The owners of the establishment deserve special mention for their exceptional kindness. They took the time to genuinely understand our preferences and meticulously matched us with the perfect flavors of popcorn. Their attentiveness further enhanced our overall experience, leaving an indelibly positive impression on us.

We are already eagerly anticipating our next visit to this extraordinary place. With such a delightful and memorable experience, it is without a doubt that we will be returning soon to explore their enticing array of flavors once more.

input: A really cute new coffee shop in town. We stopped here in the morning to get a much needed caffeine break. Who's warm day so we opted to get an iced coffee. We had many options on the type of milk and sweetener is available. They had limited food items available being mostly donuts this morning. We opted for a piece of the vegan banana bread to share. Iced coffee came out quickly and are banana bread and we went outside to sit with and realize there is no area connected to this restaurant for outdoor seating. The restaurant next-door however was not yet open so we sat at one of their tables thinking no one would mind. It would be nice if the coffee house itself had its own outdoor seating. Are iced coffee was very good and hit the spot. The vegan banana bread was good but seemed very dense to me. I'll be back another time to try some more of the fancy coffee they have available here. I'm hoping that they will add to the food menu as well as a try to not eat donuts most days. Maybe a breakfast sandwich or some other option than a pastry would be good.
Refine this for me please: We discovered a charming, newly opened coffee shop in town where we decided to indulge in a much-needed caffeine break in the morning. Since it was a warm day, we opted for refreshing iced coffees. The shop offered a wide variety of milk and sweetener options, which was quite impressive. As for food, they had limited choices and mostly focused on donuts. Nevertheless, we chose to share a piece of their vegan banana bread. Our iced coffees were served promptly, and we took our banana bread outside to enjoy. However, we realized that there was no designated outdoor seating area connected to the coffee shop. Luckily, since the neighboring restaurant had not opened yet, we decided to sit at one of their tables, assuming no one would mind. It would be even better if the coffee shop had its own outdoor seating area. Despite this inconvenience, the iced coffees were truly delicious and satisfied our cravings. The vegan banana bread, while tasty, felt a bit dense to me. Nonetheless, I plan to return to explore more of their extravagant coffee options in the future. It would be great if they could expand their food menu to include options other than pastries, such as breakfast sandwiches.

input: I went here after a recommendation that this is "the best coffee place in philly" and I'm so glad I checked it out! The cafe area itself is super nice & clean. They also offer tap and sparking water to customers which is awesome. Prices are very reasonable and the staff is super friendly. My friend and I chatted with one of the baristas for a few minutes and he gave us some pro-tips on how to make a killer espresso. I will definitely be coming back here again soon!
Refine this for me please: Based on a recommendation as "the best coffee place in Philly," I decided to visit and I'm thrilled that I did! The café's ambiance is impeccable, with a pleasant and well-maintained environment. What sets them apart is their thoughtful provision of tap and sparkling water for customers, which I found remarkable. Additionally, their prices are fair, and the staff is incredibly amiable. During my visit, my friend and I engaged in a brief conversation with one of the baristas who generously shared some valuable insights on how to craft an exceptional espresso. I can confidently say that I will definitely revisit this place in the near future!

input: It's a college-town bar, what do you expect? Lol. Alcohol, pub/bar food, good tap selection, good atmosphere and specials. A Villanova tradition. It's not an upscale bar, or a great place to grab lunch. It is what it is, a bar!
Refine this for me please: When it comes to this college-town bar, you can expect nothing less than a classic experience. With its lively atmosphere and rich traditions, it has gained a special place among Villanova students. Offering a selection of refreshing beverages on tap, mouth-watering pub/bar food, and enticing specials, this joint leaves no room for disappointment. However, keep in mind that it is not a high-end establishment or an ideal spot for a lunchtime feast. What it proudly represents is simply a bar, undeniably fulfilling its purpose. Cheers to that!

input: Great customer service! Mary was a great help- helped me pick out frames and she was extremely personable! From the time I walked in the store, I was greeted with smiles and hellos! I will be back in the future!
Refine this for me please: Exceptional customer service! Mary provided invaluable assistance in selecting frames and displayed unmatched personability throughout the entire process. The store staff warmly greeted me upon arrival with welcoming smiles and kind hellos. I wholeheartedly intend to patronize this establishment again in the future!

input:
Simply stated...They are true to their word as it relates to having discounted furniture that is less expensive than your name brand furniture stores. The staff was friendly, they definitely don't follow you around the store, however, they get a ding for customer service because they don't seem to be as knowledgeable about the furniture products.

Furniture quality is a mix ranging from low to moderate quality.  

At the end of the day, if you are looking for less expensive furniture or to get a good deal or to find a unique accent pieces this is the place to be!  I mean...I saw "the same" sectional for $1,000 less than the name brand store.   Now that's a deal!!!
Refine this for me please: In summary, this furniture store lives up to its promise of offering discounted furniture that is less expensive than name brand stores. The staff is friendly and not overbearing, but their lack of knowledge about the furniture products can be a downside in terms of customer service. The quality of the furniture varies, ranging from low to moderate. However, if you are seeking affordable furniture, good deals, or unique accent pieces, this store is a great option. In fact, I personally saw a sectional here that was priced $1,000 lower than what I found at a name brand store – now that's definitely a great deal!

input: I have been here numerous times for brunch, dinner and take out during lunch time hours. Staff is always friendly and the food is delicious.
Refine this for me please: I have frequented this place on multiple occasions for brunch, dinner, and lunch takeouts. The staff consistently exhibits a friendly demeanor, while the food served here never fails to please the taste buds with its delicious flavors.

input: Amazing dinner.  What a unique menu.  The service was top notch.  Adrian was our server and she was a delight.  I had the endive and beet salad - lovely.  And then the tongue.  Not what my grandmother made and that's okay.  This was spectacular.  Good wine list and yummy dessert.  The meal was wonderful and I'll be back next time I'm in town.  Bravo!!!
Refine this for me please: The dinner was absolutely fantastic. The menu was refreshingly unique, offering a delightful array of dishes. The service was exceptional, with Adrian as our server, who positively brightened our dining experience. Starting with the endive and beet salad, it was truly a lovely fusion of flavors. As for the tongue dish, it surpassed any expectations I had, not resembling my grandmother's recipe, but in the most incredible way. It was a truly spectacular culinary creation. Additionally, the wine list was impressive, providing a perfect pairing for our meal. To top it off, the dessert was simply scrumptious. Overall, this dining experience was nothing short of wonderful, and I eagerly anticipate returning the next time I'm in town. Bravo to the entire team!

input: Do not waste your time and money on this place. The "food" is what you might expect from a small town Chi-Chi's.
Refine this for me please:
I would suggest a refined version of your statement as follows:

"I would advise against investing your time and money at this place. The quality of the 'food' resembles that of a typical small-town Chi-Chi's restaurant."

input:
Cozy and family friendly restaurant. I came here for a private engagement party, where the bride and groom to be had arranged for special menus and baked all of their desserts. There were a few booth tables reserved for presents, wine, and desserts. No room for side tables like in an actual special events space.

The wait staff was nice. From the limited menu, I picked the Penne Fellini, which has prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and light cream sauce. The whole dish was literally this pasta swimming in sauce. It may have had a light cream flavor, but it was ladled heavily onto the pasta. I didn't have a desire to consume an entire meal of this, so I ended up not finishing.

It was a fun celebration, and we were really there for the friends and family, not the food. Oh, and we also had the bruschetta and salad, neither of which was very memorable. I wouldn't be thrilled to come back here, but I think it's awesome that they turned the whole restaurant into a venue for such a special occasion!
Refine this for me please:
Refined:

I attended a private engagement party at this cozy and family-friendly restaurant. The bride and groom had organized special menus and baked all the desserts themselves. The set-up included booth tables dedicated to presents, wine, and desserts, as there wasn't enough space for separate side tables like in a traditional event venue.

The wait staff was friendly and accommodating. I opted for the Penne Fellini from the limited menu, which consisted of prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and a light cream sauce. Unfortunately, the dish was overly saucy, drowning the pasta completely. While the sauce had a subtle cream flavor, it was excessive and made it challenging to enjoy a full meal. Consequently, I didn't finish it.

We primarily attended the celebration for the company of friends and family rather than the food. We also tried the bruschetta and salad, but neither stood out as particularly memorable. Although I wouldn't eagerly return to this restaurant, I do appreciate the efforts they made to transform the entire space into a special venue for such a significant occasion.

input: We are having a recall fixed on our 1999 Nissan Pathfinder. The staff is very friendly and they keep you updated. We were treated the same as somebody buying a new car. Highly recommend!

input:
This place is the epitome of a great hole in the wall find.  From  the  70s vintage floral upholstery  to the back entrance off the alley, it undersells it self and sets you up for a great surprise.  The food is good -- not fancy, not at all pretentious - but good. 

A group from work made the trek on the coldest day of the year and we were rewarded for our efforts -- the chicken hot pot was the best example this dish I have ever had.  The seafood dish with shrimp, scallops and squid was very generous for the price of about $10. The beef in black bean sauce was nice and spicy.  

I will certainly return, but only with adventurous companions.
Refine this for me please:
This place truly embodies the essence of a hidden gem. From its vintage floral upholstery dating back to the 70s, to its inconspicuous back entrance tucked away in the alley, this establishment humbly surpasses expectations and leaves you pleasantly surprised. The chicken hot pot presented the epitome of this dish - truly unparalleled in its taste and quality. The beef in black bean sauce provided a pleasing level of spiciness.

I will certainly make a return visit, but I am inclined to recommend it only to those who are open to exploring new flavors and experiences.

input:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're looking for quality meal that is quick and affordable, the Fountain has you covered. The menu isn't extensive, but it's got a good amount of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.  

Their Cuban Sandwich ($10 w/ side) was pretty excellent.  The bread wasn't the traditional panini-style, but a French baguette...it was still great and had a little crispness to it.  All the main ingredients (meat, mustard, pickles, cheese) were in good balance.  As a Florida boy who loves his Cuban sandwiches, I would definitely recommend this.

I also tried a bit of their Royal Grille, a grilled-chese sandwich with several cheeses, as well as apple slices, on whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 w/ side, extra to add ham/turkey).  It was damn good and hit the grilled cheese craving just right.  A side salad was also done well.

For my side, I chose their "spicy carrots" which sounded unique.  It consists of sliced raw carrots that have been marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served in a cup. The carrots were cold and crisp and the flavors were fantastic.  The spice was just enough to be pleasant.  I would definitely get these again.

Our food came out super quick and our service was great.  I'm looking forward to trying a couple more items and bumping this up to 5 stars.
Refine this for me please:
FOOD REVIEW: The Fountain

If you're in search of a quick and affordable quality meal, look no further than The Fountain. While the menu may not be extensive, it offers a satisfying selection of reasonably priced sandwiches, salads, and soups.

One standout item is their Cuban Sandwich ($10 with a side). Although it deviates from the traditional panini-style bread and opts for a French baguette instead, it is still exceptionally delicious with a satisfying crispness. The meat, mustard, pickles, and cheese are well-balanced, making it a must-try for any Cuban sandwich enthusiast.

Another option worth mentioning is the Royal Grille, a grilled cheese sandwich that features a delightful combination of multiple cheeses and apple slices, all sandwiched between whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 with a side, additional charge for ham or turkey). It perfectly satisfies any craving for grilled cheese, and the side salad is equally well-prepared.

As for the side dish, I opted for the "spicy carrots," which intrigued me with their unique description. These thinly sliced raw carrots are marinated in a tangy dressing infused with crushed red pepper and served in a cup. The carrots are refreshingly cold and crisp, and the flavors blend wonderfully. The spice level is just right, adding a pleasant kick. I would certainly order these again.

The service at The Fountain was outstanding, and our food arrived promptly. With such a positive experience, I am eager to venture back and try more of their offerings, confidently giving them a well-deserved 5-star rating.

input:
Burger Up is, by far, one of our favorite restaurants in the Nashville area.  It has a cool hipster vibe, without being annoying :)  The burgers are outstanding, and there are endless options, whether you prefer beef, chicken, seafood, or veggie!  I would recommend the Woodstock - the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is out of this world, and Benton's bacon is always delicious.  Upgrade to the truffle fries; they're to die for.  Or, if you're a vegetarian, the troyathalon is a great option.  Filling, with great texture and flavor.  As far as drinks go, 12 South Lemonade.

The customer service is also great.  They've always been attentive, but not "on top of you", and they're very knowledgable about their food.  Parking can be a bit difficult at certain times of the day, but it's worth a short walk if necessary.

I would definitely recommend checking it out!
Refine this for me please:
Burger Up is undoubtedly one of the standout restaurants in the Nashville area. The atmosphere exudes a cool hipster vibe that's refreshing without being overbearing. What truly sets this place apart is their exceptional burgers, offering a plethora of options to cater to everyone's tastes - whether you crave beef, chicken, seafood, or something vegetarian. My personal recommendation is the Woodstock - the extraordinary combination of Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup and delectable Benton's bacon is a taste you won't soon forget. To take it up a notch, indulge in the truffle fries which are absolutely divine. And for the vegetarians, the troyathalon is a fantastic choice, boasting incredible texture and flavor.

Aside from the mouth-watering food, the customer service at Burger Up is top-notch. The staff strikes the perfect balance of attentiveness without being overly intrusive, and they possess an extensive knowledge of their menu. While parking might pose a minor inconvenience during peak hours, a short walk will be more than worth it.

Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend giving Burger Up a try.

input:

I knew I couldn't eat the full-course meal so we decided to get cheese fondue and one of their entrees. Cheese fondue was delicious. If I go next time, I would probably just get the cheese fondue. =]

And the entree we had.. was some chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, etc. We decided to go with oil instead of broth because that's what our waitress suggested and I didn't really like it. Refine this for me please:
I have mixed feelings about this place. On one hand, the lack of reservation caused us to wait for approximately 50 minutes instead of the promised 15 to 20 minutes. In hindsight, I should have considered leaving and trying another time, as the wait left me in an unhappy state when we were finally seated.

As for the food, since I knew I couldn't handle a full course meal, we opted for cheese fondue along with one of their entrees. The cheese fondue was undeniably delicious, and if I were to visit again, I would likely stick to just the cheese fondue.

Regarding the entree we ordered, it consisted of chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, and other items. Following our waitress's recommendation, we chose to use oil instead of broth, but I personally did not enjoy it. If I were to return, I might give the broth a try to see if I prefer it. The only standout item was the mushroom with stuffing; the others were satisfactory at best.

On a positive note, we had a private booth that created a romantic and pleasant atmosphere. This place seems most suitable for individuals seeking privacy and ample time for a leisurely dinner. Our total time spent, excluding the waiting period, was approximately 2 and a half hours.

input:
Great Mexican BYOB! I went to Las Cazuelas for the first time for my birthday.  We had a wonderful time.  I was looking for a fun and festive place to go with friends.  This was the perfect choice. We brought our own bottle of tequila, and they made tasty margaritas for the table.  Those were a big hit with my friends, and a cool twist for a Mexican BYOB.  The restaurant is cute.  Plus, the food here is delicious. 

I'm surprised this place doesn't have higher reviews on Yelp, because it far exceeded my expectations... 

The guacamole appetizer was fresh and yummy.  I ordered the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, and asked for it spicy.  My entrée had an attractive presentation on the plate (i.e. looked classy), and was delicious, well seasoned, and very fresh. On my suggestion, my partner ordered one of their mole sauce dishes (i.e. a sauce usually made from unsweetened chocolate and pureed pumpkin seeds), and it was tasty too. 

I should also note that the waitress was very attentive.  When I placed my order, I explained to her that I have mild lactose intolerance and can't eat much butter or cream (but am okay with cheese), so she had the chef cook the veggies in olive oil, rather than butter.  Thanks for being so cool about accommodating that request!  

The prices are extremely reasonable for fancy and unusual Mexican food, and I love the fact they're a BYOB.  The chef serves creative and inspired cuisine, which has a traditional flair and style to it.  In other words: Don't come here for regular tacos or burritos.  Come here for a fun foodie experience at a reasonable price, and bring tequila for the perk of BYOB Margaritas!
Refine this for me please:
Las Cazuelas is a fantastic Mexican BYOB restaurant that exceeded my expectations. Perfect for a fun and festive night out with friends, this quaint establishment offers a unique twist by allowing patrons to bring their own tequila for delicious margaritas made by the staff. While it may not have the high Yelp reviews it deserves, I assure you the food and experience are top-notch.

Starting with the appetizer, the guacamole is fresh and delectable. For my main course, I opted for the shrimp dish with rice and vegetables, requesting it to be spicy. Not only did it have an appealing presentation, but it was also flavorful, well-seasoned, and incredibly fresh. After recommending it to my partner, they ordered one of the mole sauce dishes, which proved to be a tasty choice.

The attentive waitress deserves special mention for her accommodating nature. I informed her about my mild lactose intolerance, and she took the initiative to have the chef cook the veggies in olive oil instead of butter. This small gesture made a big difference, and I truly appreciated their consideration.

What sets Las Cazuelas apart from other Mexican restaurants is its reasonably priced fancy and unique cuisine, along with its BYOB policy. If you're seeking regular tacos or burritos, this may not be the place, but if you crave a thrilling foodie experience without breaking the bank, this is the spot for you. Don't forget to bring your own tequila for the added perk of BYOB Margaritas!

input: This was one of the greatest meals I have ever had.  The food was delicious and the hospitality was second to none. input:
I'm not really sure why I bother going to other restaurants. 

Every Valentine's Day I try to find some cute, new little BYO for me and my boyfriend to try out and I spend weeks scouring menus and Yelp reviews. 

Every year SOMETHING goes wrong and I get frustrated and pissed off and he always says "Let's go to Jones".

This year was no different. We went out last night (2/12/11...the weekend before Valentines Day) to the BYO I picked out and when I made our reservations, no mention was made that they had a special fixed menu that night consisting SOLELY of seafood, which I am allergic to. As I started to get upset at our table, my boyfriend said "Let's go to Jones".

We got there, were told there was a little bit of a wait, so we sat at the bar for a drink. About 5-10 minutes later they came and got us and sat us at our table. Our waiter (who was WONDERFUL and looked like Jared Leto - extra bonus-) came over and took our order and the food came out perfectly (as usual) and right on time.

We both got the filet, done rare and the spinach it came with was fantastic. The mac and cheese is also an app we get every time and is one of my favorites. I got the deviled eggs for the first time and holy crap they were amazing. I'm gonna say, possibly the best ones I've ever had (sorry, Dad). 

Everything about this restaurant leans towards comfort and it's always done so well. The atmosphere, the staff, the decor, the food, hell even the temperature. I've never had a bad experience at Jones and I don't think I ever will. 

Next year....we'll just go straight to Jones.
Refine this for me please: I can't seem to find anything to refine in this text. The text seems to convey the message clearly and effectively.

We started off with the chips, salsa, and bean dip, which were all delightful and greatly enjoyed by everyone. The tortilla soup also received unanimous praise for its excellent flavor. However, our satisfaction took a dip when the main courses arrived.

While our dining experience at Casa Garcia was not necessarily unpleasant, we found that there are better dining options in close proximity.

input:

My only drawbacks are:  no teeth cleaning; the price is the same regardless if the dog is 5 lbs or 40 lbs; and the feeling of judgement for not taking better care of my dogs (but that could just be me).
Refine this for me please:
I absolutely adore the convenience of having a groomer visit my home rather than having to transport all of my dogs to a salon. Not only is the price for grooming very competitive, but it may even surpass other local groomers. How can you possibly beat that?

For my smaller dogs, I pay $40, while I pay $60 for my 65lb dog. This fee covers essential services such as a bath, ear cleaning, nail grinding, and anal gland expression if necessary. Since my dogs have short hair, I don't require any elaborate grooming.

Secondly, the pricing remains the same regardless of whether the dog weighs 5 lbs or 40 lbs. Lastly, there is occasionally a feeling of judgment for not providing optimal care for my dogs, although this may simply be my perception.
